# RES-085: The tools of the MCP servers and the skills of frameworks and libraries

## Question
For the frameworks, packages and libraries that provide an MCP server or agent skills: which tools does each MCP server give to an agent, and what does each tool do? Which skills does each project provide, as a complete list, and what does each skill do?

Peter asked for this research on 2026-11-20, with `/deep-research`, in his reply to IDEA-005#17. His words: "this is another thing I'd like us to fan out and do some broad/deep research on - packages that provide mcps, what tools do their mcps provide to the agent/what do those tools do - what skills do they provide - for example figma has quite a few - I'd like to know the complete list of skills provided by each of these frameworks/packages and what they do."

Needed by: IDEA-005#06, the tools of the MCP server of 1.0; IDEA-005#07, the skills that ship for consumers; IDEA-005#12, tools that return user interface. Peter decided on the same day that the server of 1.0 is a documentation server with a search by intent (DEC-160), and he likes MCP Apps but is "not sure exactly what for".

Earlier records: RES-070 has the tools and the skills of fifteen design systems, joined into concepts; RES-082 has, for 112 projects, where the server and the skills live and a short detail of each; RES-066 and RES-080 have MCP Apps in Storybook and in three agent hosts.

## Answer
Answered on 2026-11-20. The survey has 106 projects: 100 from the sample of RES-082, and 6 that the critic of the run added (AWS, Redis, Auth0, Pulumi, Neon and Elastic). A second agent checked each record against the sources; 103 records got at least one correction.

Limits. The agents read source code, documentation and published packages. They started no server, so no live list of tools was compared with the code. The counts by kind are approximate, because each record applies the kinds in its own way. For hosted servers with closed code, several points are not confirmed.

The MCP servers:
- 85 projects have at least one official MCP server. 20 have none. For Bun a server exists, and its tools are not confirmed.
- The largest server of a project has 1 to 5 tools in 20 projects, 6 to 15 in 35, and more than 15 in 30. Neon has the most, 141. Then Sentry 74, Playwright 72, Trigger.dev 67, Qt 64, Terraform 61 and Sanity 60.
- Design systems and component libraries: MUI 3 tools; AG Grid 4; Mantine, Carbon and Salt 5 each; Ark UI 7; Ant Design 8; Chakra UI, React Spectrum and Storybook 9 each; HeroUI 10; daisyUI 11; Nuxt UI 12; NVIDIA Elements 16; Primer and Fluent UI Blazor 20 each; Atlassian 21; Vuetify 38.

The kinds of tools, by the count of projects:
- Search: about 64. The documentation or the API of one item: about 60. Tools that read or change the project, a running app or an account: about 45. A list of the components or items: about 38.
- A check of code or configuration that the agent wrote: about 25. Example code: about 20. Generate or scaffold: about 20. Tokens, theme or icons: about 17. Help with an upgrade: about 12.
- Concepts that many servers share: a search of the documentation, often named `search_docs`; a pair of search and fetch; for component libraries, a list of the components and then the documentation, the props or the examples of one; a lookup of tokens or icons; a tool that detects the project or its version; a tool that sends feedback to the maintainers.

How the search ranks:
- By words: 33 projects. By meaning: 12. Both: 7. No search tool: 19. Not confirmed: 15.
- 12 subjects have mcp_search_kind intent. The ranking runs on a project or vendor server: - Laravel and Nx: embeddings (Nx: OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 with Supabase). - Sentry: Cloudflare AutoRAG. - Shopify: OpenAI search as a backend option. - Telerik: vector embeddings at contextapi.telerik.com. - Sanity: semantic_search over an embeddings index. - DevExpress and Handsontable: semantic search. - Prisma: a cited answer. - AntV: Context7 or DeepWiki. - MongoDB: knowledge.mongodb.com.
- These 7 subjects combine ranking by meaning and by words: - Supabase: hybrid search with text-embedding-ada-002. - Untitled UI: multimodal embeddings with PRO sign-in, keyword search without. - Quarkus: BGE Small embeddings with pgvector for docs, plus keyword tool search. - .NET: Learn semantic search, plus Aspire lexical search. - Cloudflare: AI Search for docs, plus Orama BM25 for the Agents docs. - Neon: substring match for search, plus hybrid search for search_docs. - Elastic: lexical plus semantic_text hybrid.
- Where the ranking by meaning runs, for these 19 projects: on a server of the project or of a vendor in 13 records; not named in 5 (Cloudflare, Elastic, Handsontable, MongoDB and Untitled UI). Quarkus is the one record where it runs on the machine of the developer: its server starts a container that holds an embedding model, BGE Small, and a database for the vectors. For .NET, the search on the machine is the search by words of Aspire. No component library ranks by meaning on the machine of the developer.

Tools that return user interface:
- An MCP Apps view: 10 projects. An image: 9. Another way: 3. None: 59. Not confirmed: 5.
- 10 subjects have mcp_ui_kind mcp-apps. What each view is for: - Motion: transition editor, insert panel and performance report card. - Storybook: stories-preview, a live story in an iframe; it needs the running Storybook dev server. - Svelte: playground-link, an embedded svelte.dev playground. - Supabase: progress of create_project and create_branch (experimental, off by default). - Firebase: deploy and init views. - Clerk: get_user shown as a card. - Sanity: drafts widget with a carousel or table of created documents. - NVIDIA Elements: example preview, icon browser and token browser. - MongoDB: list-databases (preview flag mcpUI). - Redis: Cloud call_ui_tool, for example Agent Memory metrics.
- 9 subjects have mcp_ui_kind image. What each image is for: - daisyUI: Figma node render. - Expo: app screenshot from a simulator or device. - Figma: get_screenshot and get_figjam. - Highcharts: render_chart PNG. - Shopify: hosted theme_screenshot, an upload box and other in-chat views. - Flutter: flutter_driver screenshot of the running app. - Playwright: browser_take_screenshot, and the browser_annotate dashboard. - Sentry: snapshot and attachment images. - WebdriverIO: get_screenshot. Most of these need a running app, device or browser.

The skills:
- No skill for consumers: 13 projects. One skill: 11. 2 to 5: 34. 6 to 15: 27. More than 15: 21. Syncfusion has the most, 858. Then AWS 172, TanStack 169, .NET 108 and Telerik 78.
- The kinds, by the count of projects: how to use the library, as one umbrella skill or as a set by area, 86; an upgrade or a move from another tool, about 45; install and configure, about 40; a review of existing code, about 30; theme, tokens or visual design, about 19, and almost all of these are UI libraries.
- Each subject has one umbrella skill. Motion, Auth0 and NVIDIA Elements route to many reference files from inside that one skill. shadcn-vue and shadcn-svelte have 1 each.
- What the skills point at: the project's own MCP tools in 40 projects; files in the installed package in 23, among them Next.js, SolidJS, tRPC, Redux Toolkit, Web Awesome and Payload. In 31 projects that have a server, the skills do not use it and name a command line tool, scripts, files or web addresses. The `ag-update` skill of AG Grid forbids the server.

### Facts across the records
One agent of the run wrote these groups from the checked records. A project can be in several groups.

- **No official MCP server** (20): GSAP, React and React Native, Remotion, Tailwind CSS, Web Awesome, React Router, SolidJS, Vercel AI SDK, Hono, Bootstrap, tRPC, Redux Toolkit, React Navigation, Rspack and Rsbuild, Oxc, PixiJS, Meteor, Pydantic AI, Deno, Android. The record gives mcp_servers none or no-server. Remotion's former @remotion/mcp (1 tool) was shut down on 2026-10-26. React has only an unpublished react-mcp-server 0.0.0 (4 tools). Bootstrap closed its MCP issue as not planned. SolidJS lists an MCP bin as planned. shadcn-svelte, inside the shadcn-vue record, also has no server.
- **Server exists, tool count not confirmed** (1): Bun. https://bun.com/docs/mcp exists. No code or Bun documentation lists its tools. A third-party tracker reports 4.
- **1 to 5 tools (largest server)** (20): Astro, ESLint, TanStack, Syncfusion, Turborepo, Effect, Flowbite, DevExpress, Better Auth, Handsontable, MUI, AG Grid, Mantine, IBM Carbon, Salt Design System, Svelte, LangChain, Highcharts, Shopify, Cloudflare. ### The tools and the skills of each project
One part for each project, in the order of the alphabet. The lists are the lists of the checked records, word for word. A list is as complete as its source: the code that registers the tools where that code is public, else the documentation.

#### .NET (C#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI)
Checked: There is no single version. Checked on 2026-11-20: dotnet/skills main at commit c227688ed14de4467e3e45f95dc69a94e905e219 (2026-11-20), plugin versions dotnet 0.2.6, dotnet-test 1.0.1, dotnet-msbuild 0.1.12 and others. NuGet.Mcp.Server 1.4.23 (newest in the … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: Microsoft publishes four MCP servers that this record covers in full. A fifth .NET-specific server was found in review, and its tools are not confirmed. None of them ships in the .NET SDK or the runtime packages. (1) Microsoft Learn MCP Server: hosted at https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp over streamable HTTP. It searches and fetches Microsoft documentation, including the .NET docs, and searches code samples. It covers all Microsoft docs, not only .NET. GA on 2025-11-07; the newest release-notes entry is 2026-03-23. (2) NuGet MCP Server: the package NuGet.Mcp.Server 1.4.23 (registry name com.microsoft/nuget, stdio). It plans package version changes, fixes vulnerable packages, returns package docs and reviews NuGet supply-chain settings. (3) MSBuild Binlog MCP Server: the package Microsoft.AITools.BinlogMcp 3.0.5. It analyzes MSBuild .binlog files. The dotnet-msbuild plugin of dotnet/skills declares it in its plugin.json (`dotnet dnx Microsoft.AITools.BinlogMcp --yes --prerelease`). It controls and reads a running Aspire AppHost (resources, logs, traces) and searches the aspire.dev docs. Aspire is a separate Microsoft project (microsoft/aspire). Count it only if the survey treats Aspire as part of .NET. (5) Added in review: Microsoft.GitHubCopilot.Upgrade.DotNet.Mcp 1.1.816 (2026-11-13, author Microsoft, registry name com.microsoft/copilot-upgrade-dotnet-mcp). Its README calls it "The .NET extension MCP for the GitHub Copilot Upgrade Agent". It adds .NET upgrade and modernization tools. It is not meant to be installed alone: the `upgrade` orchestrator loads it. Its tool list is not documented.

- Tools:

  - microsoft_docs_search: semantic search of official Microsoft docs for a `query`; returns matching doc content with links.

  - binlog_overview: build status, duration, project count and error and warning counts.
  - binlog_errors: build errors with project, target, task, file and line context, deduplicated.
  - binlog_warnings: build warnings, filterable by warning code.
  - binlog_search: searches with the StructuredLog Viewer DSL; returns a tree with node [id]s.
  - binlog_projects: inventory of project executions and evaluations, with status and duration.
  - binlog_solution_membership: parses the embedded .sln/.slnx for the projects in each solution.
  - binlog_properties: MSBuild property values for each evaluation or execution context.
  - binlog_compare_property: compares recorded property values and their coverage across projects.
  - binlog_items: MSBuild items (PackageReference, Compile and others).
  - binlog_imports: the full import chain of .props and .targets files.
  - binlog_explain_property: shows where a property's value came from.
  - binlog_assembly_conflicts: MSB3277 and ResolveAssemblyReference conflict analysis for each target framework.
  - binlog_diagnose: automated diagnosis (failed targets, missing references, double writes, slow analyzers).
  - binlog_double_writes: finds duplicate file writes and their sources.
  - binlog_compiler: Csc/Vbc/Fsc command lines, response files and key switches.
  - binlog_nuget: NuGet restore information (packages, versions, sources, duration).
  - binlog_assets: reads the embedded project.assets.json.
  - binlog_reference_provenance: correlates a selected package asset with its RAR reference items and assembly versions; returns a paged JSON evidence envelope.
  - binlog_path_activity: traces a file or directory across Copy, compiler, signing, Exec and custom tasks.
  - binlog_files: lists or reads the source files embedded in the binlog.
  - binlog_search_files: text or regex search across the embedded source files.
  - binlog_preprocess: preprocessed view of a project file with its imports.

- Search, kind `both`: Learn microsoft_docs_search takes the input `query` (string) and ranks by meaning ("semantic search"). The ranking runs on Microsoft's servers, in the Learn knowledge service that also powers Ask Learn and Copilot for Azure, which Microsoft describes as RAG-based. The docs do not name the model or the index. A result holds doc content and links. The endpoint parameter `maxTokenBudget` caps the token count of search responses. Learn microsoft_code_sample_search takes `query` and an optional `language`, and runs on the same hosted service. Aspire search_docs takes `query` (required) and `topK`. It ranks by keywords ("keyword-based lexical search", with weighted matching across titles, headings, code identifiers and body text). It runs on the user's machine, in the Aspire CLI, over aspire.dev docs that it downloads from an llms.txt source and caches. Binlog binlog_search takes a StructuredLog Viewer DSL query and the paging parameters context (default 2), contextLines (default 20), maxResults (default 10) and offset (default 0). It returns tree matches with node [id]s and runs locally. binlog_search_files does a local text or regex search. NuGet MCP: no search tool.

The README documents no MCP resources. NuGet MCP: the README documents no prompts or resources. get_package_context returns its content inside a tool result. Aspire MCP: none. The server registers only ListToolsHandler and CallToolHandler. Learn MCP: none documented. Upgrade .NET MCP: not confirmed.

#### .NET Aspire
Checked: Aspire v17.0.0 (tag commit 2d325b1, dated 2026-11-17; https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/releases/latest redirects to it and the release page labels it 'Latest'). microsoft/aspire-skills v0.0.6 (commit e529b60, dated 2026-11-17). Checked on 2026-11-20. The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server, the 'aspire-mcp-server'. It is the `aspire agent mcp` subcommand of the Aspire CLI, version 17.0.0, and runs over stdio (StdioMcpTransportFactory.cs). It has no separate package. It serves runtime data of a running AppHost (resources, console and structured logs, traces, resource commands), environment checks, the hosting-integration catalog and the aspire.dev documentation. With --dashboard-url it runs in dashboard-only mode, which exposes only list_structured_logs, list_traces and list_trace_structured_logs.
- Number of tools: 15 fixed tools, counted from the code that registers them (KnownMcpTools.All and the registrations in AgentMcpCommand.cs). Dashboard-only mode exposes 3. With --apphost (pinned) mode, select_apphost and list_apphosts are not registered, which leaves 13. The server also forwards a variable number of extra MCP tools from running AppHost resources, which the AppHost proxies. The documentation page …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (src/Aspire.Cli/Mcp/Tools/*.cs at v17.0.0).
  - 1. list_resources: lists the resources of the selected AppHost, with type, state, source, endpoints, health, relationships and command metadata. It returns up to 64 per page (offset and limit).
  - 2. wait_for_resources: waits until the given resources (resourceNames, targetState healthy|up|down, timeoutSeconds 1-3600, default 120) reach the target state, then returns the result.
  - 3. list_console_logs: returns the console output of one resource (resourceName, optional full-text filter), including the output of resource commands.
  - 4. execute_resource_command: runs a named command (resourceName, commandName, optional arguments) on a resource, for example start, stop or restart, and returns a success or failure message.
  - 5. list_structured_logs: returns the OpenTelemetry structured logs of one or all resources, with an optional full-text filter.
  - 6. list_traces: returns distributed traces, with IDs, the resources in each trace, its duration and whether it had an error. It can be filtered by resource or by text.
  - 7. list_trace_structured_logs: returns the structured logs of one trace (traceId), each tied to a span_id.
  - 8. select_apphost: selects which running AppHost to use, by full or workspace-relative path.
  - 9. list_apphosts: lists the AppHost connections the server has detected, and says which are inside the working directory scope and which are outside.
  - 10. list_integrations: returns the available Aspire hosting integration NuGet packages, with short name, package ID and version, for use with `aspire add`.
  - 11. doctor: runs environment checks and returns each check's status (pass, warning or fail), its message and suggested fixes. It needs no running AppHost.
  - 12. refresh_tools: makes the server send a tools/list_changed notification so the client fetches the tool list again.
  - 13. list_docs: returns all aspire.dev documentation pages, with titles, slugs and short summaries.
  - 14. search_docs: runs a keyword search of the aspire.dev docs (query, topK default 5, max 10) and returns ranked results as markdown.
  - 15. get_doc: returns the full markdown of one docs page by slug, or only one section of it (optional section).
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool: search_docs. Inputs: query (string, required) and topK (integer, default 5, clamped to 1-10). One result holds a title, a slug, content (the page summary, or the title when there is no summary), the matched section and a score. The result is formatted as markdown with scores shown. Ranking: lexical weighted token matching in DocsIndexService and LexicalScoring. Weights are title 10, summary 8, H2/H3 headings 6, code identifiers 5 and body 1. There are bonuses for exact phrases and slug matches, and a 0.3x penalty for whats-new pages. No embedding model is used. The index is built from https://aspire.dev/llms-full.txt, which is fetched and cached by the CLI. Ranking runs on the user's machine, in the CLI process. The input schema's query description also says 'Use natural language to describe what you're looking for', but the matching is lexical.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. All 15 fixed tools return text content blocks. No ui:// resource and no image is returned (no ImageContent, EmbeddedResource or ui:// in src/Aspire.Cli/Mcp). The server declares only icons for itself in ServerInfo.
- Prompts and resources: none. The server sets only ListToolsHandler and CallToolHandler. No prompts or resources handlers are registered.
- Number of skills: 8, in the separate repository microsoft/aspire-skills under skills/ (v0.0.6). The same eight are mirrored in .github/plugins/aspire-skills/skills/, in opencode/v1/ (SKILL.md folders) and in opencode/v2/ (as <name>/<name>.md files with references/ and an index.json, not SKILL.md). The repo's .github/skills/pr-review is for contributors and is not counted. The CLI's `aspire agent init` fetches …
- Skills:
  - 1. aspire: the router skill. It detects AppHosts, enforces guardrails and sends any Aspire AppHost or CLI task to the right sub-skill.
  - 2. aspire-init: the first-run flow for adding Aspire to a repo. It picks `aspire new` or `aspire init`, drops the AppHost skeleton and hands off to aspireify. Used when no AppHost exists.
  - 3. aspireify: wires an AppHost (C#, file-based C#, TypeScript or Go) or repairs a TypeScript AppHost toolchain. It scans the repo, proposes a resource graph, edits the AppHost, wires ServiceDefaults and OTel, validates with `aspire start`, then stops.
  - 4. aspire-project-v2-migration: after a per-resource assessment and explicit approval, migrates eligible Aspire 13.6+ AppHosts from ProjectResource APIs to the experimental DotnetProjectResource APIs.
  - 5. aspire-orchestration: manages the app lifecycle (start, stop, wait, restart, isolated worktrees, update) in VS Code or the CLI, and handles file-lock and port-conflict errors.
  - 6. aspire-deployment: publishes and deploys Aspire apps from the AppHost model to Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Azure, AWS or preview Radius, and tears deployments down.
  - 7. aspire-monitoring: observes apps through logs, traces, metrics, resource state, telemetry export, browser telemetry and the standalone dashboard. It routes between the local CLI, AKS diagnostics and deployed Azure resource health.
  - 8. aspire-terminals: authors and automates Aspire terminals (WithTerminal, TerminalService, prompts, WithRepl, `aspire terminal ps/attach/tape play`, VHS tapes).
- What the skills point at: The skills send the agent to the Aspire CLI for facts, not to the MCP tools. CLI commands named: `aspire docs search`, `aspire docs get <slug>`, `aspire docs api search <query> --language csharp|typescript|go`, `aspire docs api get <id>` and `aspire docs api list <scope>`. They also name the runtime commands (aspire describe, ps, logs, otel logs/traces/spans, start, stop, wait, add, init, new, doctor). aspire-orchestration also names VS Code lifecycle tools (aspire_apphost_start, aspire_apphost_stop), which are not tools of the MCP server. Some web addresses appear, for example https://aspire.dev/install.sh and https://aspire.dev/reference/cli/commands/aspire-init/. The aspire skill …
- Not confirmed: The exact number of resource-provided MCP tools proxied at runtime. It depends on the user's AppHost and cannot be counted from the source.

Input: terms (a string or an array of strings). Result: a JSON array of icon or illustration names, sorted alphabetically, no scores. Ranking: none; terms are trimmed and lower-cased, a name matches when it contains a term as a substring, and an alias key matches when it contains the term or the term contains it, which adds the alias's target names. Data: bundled JSON files in the package (dist/data/icons.json, iconAliases.json, illustrations.json, illustrationAliases.json). Runs on the user's machine.

It returns one Markdown text that holds the query, the version, the framework, the result count and the `content` of each result, joined by `---`.

It finds the AG Grid version, the framework and whether Enterprise is used, then stores them as the default project. It returns a text with the project info, or a note that no AG Grid installation was found.
  - 3. list_versions — Fetches all available AG Grid versions from the API (`/versions`). It returns them as a Markdown list with the total and the version of the current project.
  - 4. set_versions — Sets the version and framework (both required; framework is one of vanilla, react, angular or vue) for later searches and resources. It first checks both against the list of available versions and the list of frameworks. It returns a confirmation text.

Ranking runs on a server of the project (search.ag-grid.com), not on the user's machine. The open-source client does not name a model, index or library for the ranking. Ranking: in-code BM25 (rankContent in src/content.js) over tokens from a light stemmer (plurals, -ing/-ed) and camel-case splitting, stop words dropped, weighted by query coverage and title coverage and a per-kind boost; no embedding model or library named. It is a programmatic interface to the Angular CLI: workspace discovery, version-specific best practices, documentation search, builds, tests, dev server and an OnPush/zoneless migration plan. Options in source: --root, --read-only, --local-only, --experimental-tool (alias -E); the docs page lists only --read-only and --local-only.
- Number of tools: 9 for @angular/cli mcp 22.3.0, counted from the code that registers the tools (STABLE_TOOLS in mcp-server.ts; EXPERIMENTAL_TOOLS is an empty array, so --experimental-tool adds none). The docs table also lists 9. --read-only drops devserver_start, devserver_stop and run_target (isReadOnly: false); --local-only drops search_documentation (isLocalOnly: false).
- Tools:
  - From the code that registers the tools (v22.3.0):
  - 1. ai_tutor: loads the instructions, curriculum and persona of the Angular AI Tutor (the 'Smart Recipe Box' tutorial) and returns that text as new instructions for the LLM, not for display.
  - 2. get_best_practices: returns the Angular Best Practices Guide as text; with workspacePath it loads the version-specific guide from the project's installed @angular/core, else the bundled generic guide.
  - 3. search_documentation: searches the angular.dev documentation index for a version (input query, includeTopContent, version) and returns searchedVersion and up to 10 results with title, breadcrumb, url, and for the top result optionally the page's main text.
  - 4. list_projects: returns all Angular workspaces (angular.json path, framework version), their projects (name, type, builder, root, source root, selector prefix, style language, unit test framework, targets) plus parsing and versioning errors.
  - 5. onpush_zoneless_migration: analyzes a file or directory (fileOrDirPath) and returns exactly one next actionable step to migrate to OnPush change detection / zoneless; read-only, does not modify code.
  - 6. run_target: executes a configured project target (build, test, lint, e2e, deploy, custom) with optional configuration and option overrides, and returns status (success/failure), logs and strategy extensions such as outputPath.
  - 7. devserver_start: starts `ng serve` for a project as a background process (optional port, else a random free port) and returns a message and the HTTP address.
  - 8. devserver_stop: sends SIGTERM to a dev server started by devserver_start and returns a message and the logs.
  - 9. devserver_wait_for_build: waits (default timeout 180000 ms) for the running dev server's build to finish and returns status (success/failure/unknown/timeout) and the latest build logs.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool search_documentation. Inputs: query (string, 'Concise search keywords or API names'), includeTopContent (boolean), version (number, major Angular version; clamped to min 17 (MIN_SUPPORTED_DOCS_VERSION), default 22 (LATEST_KNOWN_DOCS_VERSION), falls back to 22 when a newer index returns no results). One result: title, breadcrumb, url, and content (main-element text of the top hit fetched from angular.dev, only when includeTopContent). Ranking: Algolia hosted search, POST to https://L1XWT2UJ7F-dsn.algolia.net/1/indexes/angular_v{version}/query with hitsPerPage 10; Algolia text search, no embedding model named. Runs on a server (Algolia, the angular.dev search index), not on the user's machine; the tool is not local-only.

- Prompts and resources: Prompts: none (no registerPrompt in the mcp folder). Resources: one, 'instructions' at instructions://best-practices: the bundled Angular best-practices guide for an LLM to follow when generating code. The server also sends server instructions text (workflow: list_projects first, get_best_practices with the workspace path before coding, search_documentation for questions).

  - 2. antd_info: takes component (required) and detail (optional) and returns the component API: props, types and default values, plus whenToUse and FAQ with detail.
  - 3. antd_doc: takes component and returns the full markdown documentation of that component.
  - 4. antd_demo: takes component and optional name; without name it lists the demos of the component, with name it returns that demo's source code.
  - 5. antd_token: takes optional component and returns the global design tokens, or the component-level tokens when a component is given.
  - 6. antd_design_md: no input; returns the antd design-language document (design.md) with YAML front matter of color, typography, radius, spacing and component token values for the default light theme plus prose on design principles (published only for antd v6).
  - 7. antd_semantic: takes component and returns its semantic customization structure (the classNames/styles slots).
  - 8. antd_changelog: takes version (or range) for changelog-query mode, or v1+v2 (with optional component) for API-diff mode; returns changelog entries or the API diff between two versions.
  - Secondary, site WebMCP (from .dumi/scripts/webmcp.js): search-antd-docs: takes query and returns one fixed text line "Search Ant Design docs at: https://ant.design/components/overview. Query: <query>"; it does not search.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none in the official MCP server (antd mcp): every tool takes an exact component name or version, no query. Secondary: the browser WebMCP tool search-antd-docs takes `query` (string) but does no ranking; its handler returns the fixed text `Search Ant Design docs at: https://ant.design/components/overview. Query: ${input.query}`, run in the user's browser.

Resources: none (no resources capability declared). The site WebMCP server card says resources false, prompts false.

- Search, kind `intent`: Tool query_antv_document (mcp-server-antv). Inputs: library (enum), query (natural-language question), topic (keywords, usually from extract_antv_topic), intent, tokens, optional subTasks, channel (Context7 default | DeepWiki). One result: a Markdown text block with the documentation text and guidance. Ranking: the server ranks nothing itself. Context7 channel calls https://context7.com/api with topic and tokens (Context7's ranking method not named in the AntV source); DeepWiki channel calls the ask_question tool of https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp (hosted language-model answer). Runs on third-party hosted services, not on the user's machine and not on an AntV server.

The 24 non-map tools return a text content item with a remote image URL (rendered by POST to VIS_REQUEST_SERVER, default https://antv-studio.alipay.com/api/gpt-vis) plus _meta.spec. The user sees a static chart image only if the host renders the URL; no ui:// resource, no MCP image content, no interaction. No local dev server; needs the hosted AntV service or a self-hosted one. The three map tools pass through the hosted service's result object. mcp-server-antv returns no UI.

#### Apollo Client
Checked: @apollo/client 4.3.8 (npm dist-tag latest, published 2026-11-09T23:33:42Z; re-checked on 2026-11-20). The skill apollo-client has metadata version "1.0.0". apollographql/skills checked at commit 9dda139 (2026-10-30, still the head of main on 2026-11-20). … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: There is one official MCP server: GraphOS MCP Server at https://mcp.apollographql.com. Apollo hosts it, it uses Streamable HTTP and it has no version number. It was named 'GraphOS MCP Tools' until 2026-07-20. Without credentials it serves Apollo's documentation and the Apollo Connectors specification. After a GraphOS sign-in, or with an x-api-key header, it also reads and changes the user's GraphOS graphs. It covers the whole Apollo platform and is not specific to Apollo Client. Apollo Client itself has no MCP server: the 4.3.8 package holds no MCP code. Apollo MCP Server (apollographql/apollo-mcp-server) is a separate product that turns a user's own GraphQL operations into tools, so it is left out.
- Number of tools: GraphOS MCP Server: 48 tools. The count comes from the documentation's Tools reference page (48 tool headings), because the server code is not public. 3 tools need no credentials and 45 need GraphOS authentication.
- Tools:
  - Source: the documentation (Tools page), because the code is not public. The docs give display names. Only three wire names appear (ApolloDocsSearch, ApolloDocsRead, ApolloConnectorsSpec, in the Copilot config on the install page).
  - 1 Apollo Docs Search (ApolloDocsSearch): searches Apollo's documentation and returns the most relevant guides, examples and best practices.
  - 2 Apollo Docs Read (ApolloDocsRead): returns the full Markdown content of one Apollo docs page.
  - 3 Apollo Connectors Spec (ApolloConnectorsSpec): returns the official Apollo Connectors specification, so the agent can create and change Connectors in a schema.
  - 4 Get My Identity: returns the caller's identity and the organizations of its API key.
  - 5 Get Variant Details: returns a variant's identifier, federation version, endpoint URL and subgraphs.
  - 6 Get Latest Launch: returns the newest launch of a variant (status, subgraph changes, composition errors, schema diff summary) and the latest approved launch.
  - 7 Get Launch: returns one launch by ID in full detail.
  - 8 Get Launch History: returns recent launches of a variant with ID, status and timestamps.
  - 9 Get Top Operations: returns the most-used operations of a variant with request counts, types and signatures.
  - 10 Get Operation Metrics: returns, per operation, the request count, p50 and p99 latency and error count.
  - 11 Get Subgraph Metrics: returns, per subgraph or connector, the fetch count, p50 and p99 fetch latency and fetch errors.
  - 12 Get Client Metrics: returns traffic, latency and errors per client name, client version and operation.
  - 13 Get Persisted Query List Status: returns whether a variant has a PQL, with its ID, name, revision and operation count.
  - 14 Publish Persisted Queries: adds, replaces or removes operations in a PQL and returns the new revision and operation count.
  - 15 Get Lint Results: returns the lint diagnostics and counts of the latest schema checks.
  - 16 Lint Schema: lints a given schema against the graph's rules and returns the diagnostics without publishing.
  - 17 Get Schema Checks: returns a filtered list of past schema checks with ID, status, subgraph, variant, commit and task status.
  - 18 Get Check Results: returns one check's outcome: composition errors, lint, changes with affected operations, downstream and custom-check results.
  - 19 Run Schema Check: checks a proposed monograph or supergraph schema against a variant and returns a check ID and a link.
  - 20 Run Subgraph Check: checks a proposed subgraph schema against a variant and returns a check ID and a link.
  - 21 Validate Operations: validates client operations against a variant's schema and returns each problem's type, code, description and operation.
  - 22 Get Subgraph Schema: returns one subgraph's published schema with routing URL, revision and update time.
  - 23 Publish Subgraph: publishes a subgraph schema, which triggers composition, and returns created or updated status, composition errors and the launch.
  - 24 Delete Subgraph: removes a subgraph from a variant, or does a dry run of the removal, and returns the composition errors.
  - 25 Get Graph Schema: returns a variant's whole published API schema with hash and publication time.
  - 26 Get Supergraph Schema: returns a variant's composed supergraph schema with composition ID and errors.
  - 27 Publish Graph Schema: publishes a monograph schema and returns a result code, success, message and hash.
  - 28 Delete Graph: soft-deletes a graph and all its variants.
  - 29 Get Contract Config: returns a contract variant's include and exclude tags, source variant and description.
  - 30 Publish Contract: creates or updates a contract variant, starts a launch and returns the variant and a launch link or the errors.
  - 31 Get Readme: returns a variant's README with its last update time and author.
  - 32 Publish Readme: replaces a variant's README.
  - 33 Get Proposals: returns a filtered list of schema proposals with IDs, titles, statuses and authors, and a total count.
  - 34 Get Proposal: returns one proposal with its latest revision, check, launch and reviews.
  - 35 Create Proposal: creates a draft schema proposal against a source variant.
  - 36 Publish Proposal Revision: saves a revision of a proposal by publishing changed subgraph schemas to its proposal variant.
  - 37 Update Proposal Status: changes a proposal's status, for example from draft to open.
  - 38 Review Proposal: approves or rejects a proposal's latest revision, with an optional comment.
  - 39 Add Proposal Comment: adds a general comment, a reply or a comment on one schema change.
  - 40 Get Graph Artifact: returns a graph artifact by digest (ID, status, build errors, launch, registry location, tags).
  - 41 Get Graph Artifact Tags: returns the artifact tags of a graph and the artifact each tag points to.
  - 42 Tag Graph Artifact: assigns or moves a tag to an artifact.
  - 43 Untag Graph Artifact: deletes a tag and its history.
  - 44 Get API Keys: returns the organization's API keys and client-credential pairs, without their values.
  - 45 Create API Key: creates an API key and returns its value.
  - 46 Rename API Key: renames an API key.
  - 47 Delete API Key: deletes an API key.
  - 48 Get Offline License: returns the organization's offline Enterprise license for GraphOS Router.

- MCP servers: Ark UI has one official server: the npm package @ark-ui/mcp (bin ark-ui-mcp, stdio). Its newest version is 1.3.0, published 2026-08-03. It gives an agent the Ark UI components, examples, props, the data attributes and CSS variables for styling, and the doc pages, for React, Vue, Solid and Svelte. The source also has an HTTP entry, src/http.ts (dist/http.js ships in the package), but the docs say the server supports only stdio. Zag.js has no official MCP server. I looked in the zag repository: it has no MCP package, and its website has only the llms.txt routes. npm returns 404 for @zag-js/mcp.
- Number of tools: @ark-ui/mcp 1.3.0 has 7 tools. The count comes from the code that registers the tools: the tools array in packages/mcp/src/tools/index.ts. The same 7 names appear in the published dist/stdio.js, and the README lists 7. The docs page ark-ui.com/docs/ai/mcp-server lists only 4: it omits get_component_props, search_docs and get_docs. Zag.js: no-server.
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (packages/mcp/src/tools/*.ts). Each tool fetches JSON from https://ark-ui.com/api.
  - 1. list_components: takes a framework (react|vue|svelte|solid) and returns a JSON array with the names of all Ark UI components, from /api/types/{framework}.
  - 2. list_examples: takes a framework and a component and returns a JSON array of the example ids for that component, from /api/examples/{framework}/{component}.
  - 3. get_example: takes a framework, a component and an exampleId and returns that example as JSON: its id, framework, component and files, where each file has a name, its content and its npmDependencies.
  - 4. get_component_props: takes a framework and a component and returns JSON with the framework, the component and its props, from /api/types/{framework}/{component}.
  - 5. styling_guide: takes a component and returns its data attributes and CSS variables as JSON (dataAttr, cssVar), from /api/style-guide/{component}. For some components it adds hand-written styling notes, such as keyframes and the required toast root styles.
  - 6. search_docs: takes a query and returns the matching doc pages as JSON (query, results). Each result has a slug, title, description, category and url.
  - 7. get_docs: takes a page slug (for example "components/dialog") and returns the full markdown of that page.
- Search, kind `keyword`: The tool is search_docs. It has one input field: query (string, min 1, for example "composition", "initial focus" or "styling"). The response is JSON { query, results[] }. Each result has a slug, title, description, category and url, but no page content; get_docs fetches the content. The ranking runs on a server of the project. The tool calls https://ark-ui.com/api/docs?q={query}. That route (website/src/app/api/docs/route.ts) ranks with the library match-sorter (fuzzy word matching) over the keys title, description, slug and category, and returns at most 10 results (limit = 10 by default).
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Every tool returns only text content (JSON or markdown). No tool names a ui:// resource or returns an image. Zag.js has no server.
- Prompts and resources: none. src/server.ts declares the empty capabilities prompts: {} and resources: {}, but the source registers no prompt and no resource. It has no registerPrompt or registerResource call, and the published dist/stdio.js has none either. Zag.js has no server.

Both repositories have a .claude/ folder, but it holds only agents, commands and docs for contributors. The AI doc pages of both projects (Ark: pages/ai/llms.txt.mdx and pages/ai/mcp-server.mdx; Zag: the llms.txt routes) do not mention skills. A web search found official skills …

  - none (0 skills).

Checked: @atlaskit/ads-mcp 2.0.3 (npm latest, published 2026-11-20T03:29:14Z, README 'Current state: Early Access'); @atlaskit/ads-cli 1.0.3 (npm latest, published 2026-11-20T03:29:13Z). Both re-read from fresh npm tarballs on 2026-11-20. The second agent's verdict: corrected.

(2) The hosted remote server https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/ads/public/mcp (HTTP transport), which the README calls a hosted version of the ADS MCP server. Purpose: ADS tokens, icons, components and primitives, foundations guidelines, lint-rule docs, migrations, i18n and accessibility tooling for agents building Atlassian-style UI.
- Number of tools: Local @atlaskit/ads-mcp 2.0.3: 21 tools, counted from the code that registers them (getToolRegistry in dist/es2019/index.js, an unconditional registry of 21 entries). Remote https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/ads/public/mcp: 20 according to the documentation in a tool description, which says that ads_analyze_localhost_a11y is not in the remote deployment. The remote count was not checked against a live …
- Tools:
  - Taken from the code that registers the tools (the name and description in each tools/*/list-*-tool.js of the 2.0.3 tarball). All tools return JSON or Markdown as text content.
  - 1. ads_analyze_a11y: analyzes a string of React/JSX code (input: code, componentName, context, includePatternAnalysis) with axe-core and regex heuristics, and returns accessibility violations with hints, often pointing to ads_suggest_a11y_fixes.
  - 2. ads_analyze_localhost_a11y: loads a live URL in headless Puppeteer, runs axe-core (optionally scoped by a CSS selector), and returns violations with follow-up hints. Local only.
  - 3. ads_get_a11y_guidelines: returns ADS accessibility guidance (best practices and patterns) for one topic key, or all topics when no topic is given.
  - 4. ads_get_all_components: returns every canonical ADS component record as JSON text chunks (the full catalog).
  - 5. ads_plan: runs ads_search_tokens, ads_search_icons, ads_search_components and optionally atlaskit_search_components in one call, and returns one JSON payload with each non-empty section.
  - 6. ads_search_components: fuzzy-searches the ADS component catalog and returns name, package, examples, props and an optional references.figmaUrl for each match.
  - 7. ads_search_icons: fuzzy-searches the ADS icon catalog and returns componentName, package and usage for each match.
  - 8. ads_search_tokens: fuzzy-searches design tokens and returns name and exampleValue for each match, plus the description and usage guidelines when includeMetadata is true.
  - 9. ads_suggest_a11y_fixes: matches a natural-language violation description and a code snippet against a curated recipe map, and returns ADS-biased fix examples or generic guidance.
  - 10. ads_migration_guides: returns a structured migration guide (before/after examples, best practices, links) for one known migration id: avatar-xsmall-to-xxsmall, interaction-to-entry-point, jira-spotlight, single-step, multi-step or motion.
  - 11. ads_i18n_conversion_guide: returns a bundled step-by-step guide for replacing hardcoded UI strings with formatMessage (guide: hardcoded-string-to-formatmessage).
  - 12. ads_get_guidelines: returns ADS foundations guidelines as Markdown (content, color, spacing, tokens, typography and so on), either fuzzy-matched by terms or the full set.
  - 13. ads_get_all_tokens: returns every ADS design token (name, description, example value, usage guidelines) as one JSON object per token.
  - 14. ads_get_all_icons: returns every ADS icon record as JSON text chunks.
  - 15. ads_get_lint_rules: returns the bundled docs of the ADS ESLint rules (purpose, examples, fixes), all rules or those fuzzy- or exact-matched by terms. It does not run ESLint.
  - 16. atlaskit_get_components: returns a compact inventory (names and packages) of public @atlaskit/* and internal @atlassian/* Platform component packages not covered by the ADS catalog.
  - 17. atlaskit_search_components: fuzzy-searches the non-ADS component catalog and returns name, package, description, examples and props for each match.
  - 18. atlaskit_get_utilities: returns a compact inventory (names and packages) of the non-ADS @atlaskit/* utilities (functions, constants, types).
  - 19. atlaskit_search_utilities: searches the non-ADS @atlaskit/* utilities by name, package, category, description or keywords, and returns usage details.
  - 20. atlaskit_get_hooks: returns a compact inventory (names and packages) of the non-ADS @atlaskit/* hooks.
  - 21. atlaskit_search_hooks: searches the non-ADS @atlaskit/* hooks by name, package, category, description or keywords, and returns usage details.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Search tools: ads_search_components, ads_search_tokens, ads_search_icons, ads_plan, atlaskit_search_components, atlaskit_search_hooks and atlaskit_search_utilities; ads_get_guidelines and ads_get_lint_rules also search when given terms. Inputs: `terms` (a string or an array of strings) and `limit` (matches per term, default 2; default 1 for ads_get_lint_rules). ads_search_tokens also takes `includeMetadata`. ads_plan takes the arrays `tokens`, `icons`, `components` and `atlaskitComponents`, plus `limit`. ads_get_lint_rules also takes `exactName`. Result of a component search: a JSON object with name, package, examples, props and an optional references.figmaUrl. A token result holds name and exampleValue; an icon result holds componentName, package and usage. Ranking: Fuse.js 6 fuzzy matching over weighted fields. For components the weights are name 5, package 3, category, description, keywords and usageGuidelines 2, content, accessibility guidelines and examples 1, with threshold 0.4. Each term is searched alone and all terms are also searched joined; the hits are merged by Fuse score and de-duplicated (mergeMultiTermFuseResults). ads_suggest_a11y_fixes ranks curated recipes by keyword matches. No embedding model or language model. Where it runs: inside the MCP process, over data bundled in the package. With the stdio package that is the user's machine; with the hosted endpoint it is Atlassian's server.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool returns a ui:// resource or an image. ads_analyze_localhost_a11y loads a page in headless Puppeteer but returns only text (axe violations).
- Prompts and resources: none. The server declares only the `tools` capability and the server `instructions` string. It sets no handler for prompts or resources. The instructions point the agent to https://atlassian.design/llms.txt, llms-a11y.txt and the Context Engine tools.

(6) afm-platform-offerings: finding reusable Platform components, hooks, and utilities. (7) a11y-foundation: accessibility decisions with WCAG and Atlassian guidance. #### AWS (AWS CDK and SDKs, Agent Toolkit for AWS)
Checked: Agent Toolkit for AWS repository github.com/aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws, re-read at HEAD commit 720addd (2026-11-20 16:17 UTC). The first reader used faab230 from the same day, and the skill counts and names are identical at both commits. Plugin versions: … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: Scope: the servers that cover the CDK and the SDKs. (1) The AWS MCP Server at https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp (other regions also exist, for example https://aws-mcp.eu-central-1.api.aws/mcp). It is the server of the Agent Toolkit: a managed, closed-source, hosted server. The aws-core, aws-data-analytics and aws-startup-advisor plugins reach it through the local proxy mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli==1.8.0. It searches AWS documentation and skills and runs AWS API calls under the user's IAM credentials. It has no public version; the newest user-guide history entry is 2026-09-30. (2) The AWS Knowledge MCP Server at https://knowledge-mcp.global.api.aws. It is hosted and closed source, bundled in the aws-agents plugin, and serves AWS, CDK, CloudFormation and Strands documentation, regional availability and skills. It is GA, with no version given. (3) Legacy: AWS Labs' awslabs.aws-iac-mcp-server 1.0.27 (PyPI, 2026-11-17) is open source and runs locally. It offers CDK and CloudFormation documentation search, samples, best practices and template validation. The 'CDK MCP Server' named in the awslabs README text no longer has a folder under awslabs/mcp/src, so the IaC server is the CDK-covering server there. The awslabs README calls the Agent Toolkit 'the successor to the MCP servers, plugins, and skills available on AWS Labs'. Not surveyed: product servers that some plugins also configure, namely the AWS DevOps Agent MCP (devsecops plugin), the SageMaker Unified Studio spark-troubleshooting and spark-code-recommendation servers (data-analytics plugin, through mcp-proxy-for-aws==1.7.0), and the about 60 other awslabs/mcp servers.
- Number of tools: The AWS MCP Server has 8 tools, counted from the documentation because the server is not open source. The AWS Knowledge MCP Server has 5 tools, counted from the documentation in the awslabs aws-knowledge-mcp-server README because it is hosted and not open source. The legacy aws-iac-mcp-server 1.0.27 has 9 tools, counted from the code: 8 @mcp.tool() functions in server.py, plus 1 tool proxied from …
- Tools:
  - AWS MCP Server, from the documentation (8 tools): aws___retrieve_skill - retrieves an AWS agent skill by name and returns the full skill content, including its reference materials. | aws___search_documentation - searches all AWS documentation, API references, best practices, service guides and skills, with an optional topic filter, and returns ranked results. | aws___read_documentation - retrieves an AWS documentation page and returns it as markdown. | aws___list_regions - returns all AWS regions with their identifiers and names. | aws___get_regional_availability - returns regional availability for services, features, SDK APIs and CloudFormation resources. | aws___run_script - runs Python code in a sandbox with AWS API access under the user's credentials, for listing resources, parallel calls and multi-step workflows. | aws___get_presigned_url - returns pre-signed Amazon S3 URLs for upload or download. | aws___get_tasks - returns the status of long-running tasks that aws___run_script started. The docs also describe a 'serverless capability' with the helper functions diagnose, search_logs, get_live_config, get_recent_changes and get_trace_summary, which the agent 'invokes ... automatically through AWS MCP Server'. The tool page does not list them as tools. Skills in the repository also name aws___call_aws and aws___recommend, which the current tool page does not list. A search-engine excerpt of the official tool page says: 'We deprecated aws___call_aws as of July 15, 2026 and will remove it on August 31, 2026'. The live page no longer carries that sentence.
  - AWS Knowledge MCP Server, from the documentation (5 tools). The README gives the names without a prefix; the IaC server code calls them as aws___search_documentation and aws___read_documentation. search_documentation - searches AWS documentation, agent skills and Strands Agents SDK docs with optional topic filtering, and returns ranked results. | read_documentation - returns AWS and strandsagents.com pages as markdown. | list_regions - returns all AWS regions with their identifiers and names. | get_regional_availability - returns regional availability for services, features, SDK service APIs and CloudFormation resources. | retrieve_skill - returns an AWS agent skill by skill_name, with an optional file parameter for its reference files.
  - Legacy aws-iac-mcp-server 1.0.27, from the code (9 tools): validate_cloudformation_template - validates template syntax, schema and properties with cfn-lint, and returns valid, error, warning and info counts and issues with line numbers. | check_cloudformation_template_compliance - validates a template against security and compliance rules with cfn-guard, and returns violations with remediation guidance. | troubleshoot_cloudformation_deployment - analyzes a failed stack in a region by correlating stack events with CloudTrail, and returns root-cause analysis. | get_cloudformation_pre_deploy_validation_instructions - returns instructions for pre-deploy validation with change sets. | search_cdk_documentation - searches the CDK API reference, best practices, samples and cdk-nag rules, and returns JSON results with rank, title, url and context. | search_cloudformation_documentation - searches the CloudFormation docs and returns the same result shape. | search_cdk_samples_and_constructs - searches CDK samples and community constructs for a query and a language (typescript by default, python, java, csharp or go), and returns the same result shape. | cdk_best_practices - returns the CDK best-practices and security guidelines bundled in the package. | read_iac_documentation_page - a proxy of the Knowledge server's aws___read_documentation that returns a full documentation page with pagination.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: The search tool is aws___search_documentation, on both the AWS MCP Server and the Knowledge server. Its input fields, as the IaC server's client code calls it: search_phrase (string), topics (a list, for example 'cdk_docs', 'cloudformation', 'cdk_constructs', 'agent_skills' or 'strands_docs') and limit (int, 10 by default in the IaC client). One result holds rank_order, title, url and context, which is an excerpt or the page content. The ranking runs on AWS's hosted server, not on the user's machine. No source names the ranking method, model or index. The Knowledge README says users can 'just ask questions naturally', and the IaC tool docstrings advise boolean operators and wildcards ('Lambda AND API Gateway', 'example*'), so the evidence points both ways. The legacy IaC server's search_cdk_documentation, search_cloudformation_documentation and search_cdk_samples_and_constructs take a query (and a language) and forward it to the Knowledge server's aws___search_documentation with a fixed topic. They do no ranking of their own.

- Prompts and resources: AWS MCP Server and AWS Knowledge MCP Server: not confirmed, because the documentation names no prompts or resources and the servers are not open source. Legacy aws-iac-mcp-server: none, because server.py has no @mcp.prompt or @mcp.resource. It declares server instructions with a tool-selection guide.

#### Better Auth
Checked: better-auth 1.7.27 and CLI package `auth` 1.7.27, published to npm 2026-11-20 (registry times 10:53:10Z and 10:52:39Z). Skills repo github.com/better-auth/skills at 20c9e88 (2026-09-01 +0900). Cursor plugin repo at d2a7722 (2026-07-28). The remote … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: One official MCP server for coding agents: the remote documentation MCP server at https://mcp.better-auth.com/mcp, which is hosted by the project and has no npm package and no version number. It is for searching and retrieving Better Auth documentation. It is the current endpoint as of 2026-11-20, and CLI `auth` 1.7.27 points to it (REMOTE_MCP_URL in packages/cli/src/commands/mcp.ts). The server's source is not public: no repository in the better-auth GitHub organization holds it, and the main repository holds only the CLI that adds it to a client. Two other things are left out because they are not documentation servers for coding agents: (a) the `@better-auth/mcp` package / MCP plugin, which is an auth plugin that adds MCP provider authentication to a user's app; (b) the Agent Auth MCP server that the `auth ai` command installs (better-auth/agent-auth), which is a client for the Agent Auth protocol and lets agents authenticate to services.
- Number of tools: 2 for mcp.better-auth.com/mcp. The count is not from code that registers the tools, because that code is not public, and the docs page lists no tools. The two names come from the maintainers' own best-practices SKILL.md, which tells the agent to call `get_doc` and `search_docs`. The count therefore rests on documentation from the maintainers, not on code or tools/list. A third-party directory …

Checked: MCP server @chakra-ui/react-mcp 2.1.1 (published 2025-11-03T11:58:46Z, newest of 9 versions on npm, rechecked 2026-11-20; source apps/mcp at main commit 4fca088 of 2026-11-19 holds an unreleased search_docs tool). Skills: skills/ folder of … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: npm package @chakra-ui/react-mcp, newest release 2.1.1 (2025-11-03), run with `npx -y @chakra-ui/react-mcp` over stdio. It gives agents Chakra UI component lists, props, examples, theme tokens, theme customization templates, installation steps, v2-to-v3 migration snippets and (with CHAKRA_PRO_API_KEY) Chakra UI Pro templates. Source: apps/mcp of the monorepo (stdio.ts, plus an HTTP entry http.ts and vercel.json). Every tool fetches its data from chakra-ui.com or pro.chakra-ui.com APIs, or returns data built into the package.
- Number of tools: 9 in release 2.1.1. Of these, 7 are always registered and 2 (list_component_templates, get_component_templates) only when an API key (CHAKRA_PRO_API_KEY) is set. Counted from the code that registers the tools (apps/mcp/src/tools/index.ts) and checked against the published dist/stdio.js of 2.1.1. The source on main has 10: it adds search_docs, which CHANGELOG lists under [Unreleased].
- Tools:
  - From the code that registers the tools (apps/mcp/src/tools/*.ts), with names checked against the published 2.1.1 dist.
  - 1. list_components: returns a JSON list of the names of all Chakra UI components and charts, fetched from chakra-ui.com/api/types.
  - 2. get_component_props: takes a component name (an enum) and returns JSON of its props and configuration options, from chakra-ui.com/api/types/{component}.
  - 3. get_component_example: takes a component name (an enum) and returns JSON with example code and usage patterns, from chakra-ui.com/r/examples/{component}.json.
  - 4. get_theme: takes no input and returns a text guide to tokens, semanticTokens, layerStyles, textStyles and animationStyles, plus the theme specification as JSON from chakra-ui.com/api/theme.
  - 5. customize_theme: takes a token category (an enum built from chakra-ui.com/api/theme/tokens plus built-in scenarios such as animations, breakpoints, colors, conditions, cursor, sizes, spacing and globalCss) and returns JSON with a defineConfig/createSystem usage template for adding or changing tokens of that category.
  - 6. v2_to_v3_code_review: takes a migration scenario (an enum of 45 snake_case keys, such as boolean_prop_naming, named 'Boolean Prop Naming') and returns JSON with that scenario's v2-to-v3 before/after code snippets. Its description tells the agent to use it to review any generated code.
  - 7. installation: takes a framework (vite, next-app, next-pages or general) and returns JSON installation steps (packages, snippet commands, Provider setup).
  - 8. list_component_templates (only with CHAKRA_PRO_API_KEY): returns JSON of the Chakra UI Pro blocks (template categories and variants), from pro.chakra-ui.com/api/blocks.
  - 9. get_component_templates (only with CHAKRA_PRO_API_KEY): takes a block category and a variant id and returns the JSON code of that Chakra UI Pro template, from pro.chakra-ui.com/api/blocks/{category}/{id}.
  - Unreleased on main, not in 2.1.1: search_docs takes a query string and returns a text list of matching documentation pages with label, category, description and URL. Its description says to use it as a last resort.
  - Note: the docs page (mdx source and live page) names the theme tool `theme_customization` and leaves out `installation`. The apps/mcp README names `get_components` and `list_blocks`. The code names are the ones above.
- Search, kind `no-search`: None in release 2.1.1. On main, unreleased: tool search_docs, input `query` (string). It calls https://chakra-ui.com/api/search?query=..., so the ranking runs on a project server (the docs site). Each result holds label, slug, url, description and category; the tool prints label, category, description and URL. The ranking is keyword/fuzzy: Fuse.js over label (weight 0.5), description (0.3) and category (0.2) of the docs search index, threshold 0.3, extended search, sorted by Fuse score.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Every tool returns only text content: JSON or text. No tool names a ui:// resource and none returns an image (source and 2.1.1 dist checked).
- Prompts and resources: none. server.ts declares empty prompts and resources capabilities, but no prompt or resource is registered: the source and the 2.1.1 dist hold no prompt or resource registration.
- Number of skills: 3, in the folder skills/ of github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui (main), installed with `npx skills add https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/tree/main/skills`. They are not in an npm package. The repository has no other SKILL.md: .claude/ holds only agents and commands.
- Skills:
  - 1. chakra-ui-builder: builds responsive, accessible UI components and layouts with Chakra UI v3, installs or configures Chakra UI, and designs themes with tokens, semantic tokens, recipes and slot recipes (with reference files theming.md, charts.md and component-decision-tree.md). An agent uses it for any Chakra UI building, setup, theming or charts request.
  - 2. chakra-ui-migrate: migrates Chakra UI projects from v2 to v3, covering package changes, codemods, provider setup, color mode, prop renaming, compound components, theming, recipes and Next.js updates. An agent uses it when a user upgrades, hits breaking changes or converts v2 patterns.
  - 3. chakra-ui-refactor: reviews, converts and improves UI code with Chakra UI v3. An agent uses it to review Chakra code for issues, to convert HTML/CSS, Tailwind, CSS Modules or styled-components to Chakra, or to clean up components and token usage.
- What the skills point at: No skill names the MCP server or a web address. Pointers: the CLI `npx @chakra-ui/cli snippet add` (builder SKILL.md, also `--all` and `snippet list`; migrate); `npx @chakra-ui/cli typegen ./theme.ts` (migrate SKILL.md; for builder in references/theming.md, with `npx @chakra-ui/cli eject`); `npx @chakra-ui/codemod upgrade --dry` and `upgrade` (migrate); and builder's own reference files references/theming.md, references/charts.md and references/component-decision-tree.md. chakra-ui-refactor holds all its content itself.
- Not confirmed: Whether a hosted HTTP deployment of the server (src/http.ts, vercel.json) is public; the docs name only stdio.

- Tools:
  - Source: the documentation (the 'Available tools' tables). The server code is not public.
  - 1. whoami: shows the connected user, the workspace and the granted permissions.
  - 2. list_applications: lists the applications in the workspace; the results include each instance's Publishable Key.
  - 3. get_application: inspects one application and its instances, with the Publishable Keys.
  - 4. create_application: creates an application and returns its keys; it returns the encrypted Secret Key when given recipient_public_key.
  - 5. update_application: renames an application.
  - 6. get_instance_config: reads an instance's configuration, with sensitive values redacted.
  - 7. get_instance_config_schema: reads the schema of the instance configuration.
  - 8. patch_instance_config: updates part of an instance's configuration, with an optional dry-run preview.
  - 9. put_instance_config: replaces an instance's configuration, with an optional dry-run preview.
  - 10. list_native_applications: lists the iOS and Android apps registered with an instance.
  - 11. create_ios_application: registers an iOS app with an instance.
  - 12. create_android_application: registers an Android app with an instance.
  - 13. enable_native_api: turns on the instance's Native API.
  - 14. list_redirect_urls: lists an instance's allowlisted redirect URLs for SSO in mobile and desktop apps.
  - 15. create_redirect_url: adds an allowlisted redirect URL.
  - 16. list_users: finds the users of an instance with filters.
  - 17. get_user: gets a user by ID; clients that support MCP Apps show the user as a card.
  - 18. create_user: creates a user in an instance.
  - 19. update_user: updates a user's first or last name, username, external ID, locale or timezone.
  - 20. update_user_metadata: changes a user's public, private or unsafe metadata and sets bypass_client_trust (Device Trust bypass).
  - 21. list_organizations: lists or searches Organizations.
  - 22. list_organization_memberships: lists an Organization's members.
  - 23. list_user_organization_memberships: lists a user's Organizations.
  - 24. list_domains: lists domains and the DNS records they need.
  - 25. get_domain_status: checks a domain's verification status.
  - 26. check_domain_dns: requests a new DNS check for a domain.
  - 27. get_deploy_oauth_providers: lists the OAuth providers that need production credentials.
  - 28. create_production_instance: creates a production instance from development; it requires confirm: true and can return the encrypted Secret Key.
  - 29. create_browser_session: returns a one-time link, valid for about an hour, that opens the Clerk Dashboard signed in as the user, read-only.
  - 30. configure_mcp_server: registers the URL of the user's own MCP server as an OAuth resource on an instance, with a dry run.
  - 31. check_mcp_server: reads saved discovery results for that MCP server, or requests a fresh check with force_recheck: true.
  - 32. list_application_feedback: reads the feedback that AI agents reported through the user's own MCP server, filtered by kind, impact or user.
  - 33. submit_feedback: reports problems and missing documentation to the Clerk team.
  - 34. clerk_sdk_snippet: returns a code snippet for a Clerk feature, or a bundle of snippets for a common setup such as b2b-saas or organizations.
  - 35. list_clerk_sdk_snippets: lists the available snippets and bundles, optionally filtered by tag.

(2) Cloudflare Documentation MCP server at https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Source apps/docs-ai-search in github.com/cloudflare/mcp-server-cloudflare, release docs-ai-search@0.5.0 of 2026-10-22. It is for up-to-date Cloudflare reference documentation. (3) Agents SDK Documentation MCP server at https://agents.cloudflare.com/mcp. Source site/agents/src/server/index.ts in github.com/cloudflare/agents (HEAD 8d8acd0, 2026-11-20), server info agents-mcp 0.0.1. It is for token-efficient search of the Agents SDK documentation. The mcp-server-cloudflare repository holds more official servers that are not about Workers development; their tools were not listed here. Current: Container, Browser Run, DEX, Cloudflare One CASB, Blog and Demo Day. Deprecated: AI Gateway, Audit Logs, AutoRAG, DNS Analytics, GraphQL, Logpush, Observability, Radar, Workers Bindings and Workers Builds.
- Number of tools: Cloudflare API MCP server in its default Code Mode: 5 by the registering code (src/server.ts registers docs, search, execute, whoami and submit_feedback); submit_feedback registers only when the FEEDBACK_URL environment value is set, so 4 without it. submit_feedback was added in the HEAD commit of 2026-11-19, and the README table still lists 4 tools. With ?codemode=false, the server lists docs, …
- Tools:
  - Taken from the registering code. Cloudflare API MCP server (Code Mode): docs: searches the Cloudflare developer documentation for a query and returns semantically similar chunks, each with similarity, id, url, title and text. search: runs JavaScript that the agent writes against the pre-resolved Cloudflare OpenAPI spec (spec.paths) in a sandbox and returns what the code returns, such as matching endpoints and their schemas; the result is capped at about 6,000 tokens unless truncate is false. execute: runs JavaScript that the agent writes, calling cloudflare.request() against the live Cloudflare API with an optional account_id, and returns the result; it can read, create, update or delete resources. whoami: takes no arguments and returns the authenticated user or account as {id, email} or {id, name}. submit_feedback: sends a problem report or feedback (message, type, impact, plus optional product, tool, task, expected and actual) to Cloudflare and returns a submission_id. Documentation MCP server: search_cloudflare_documentation: searches the Cloudflare documentation for a query and returns semantically similar chunks, each with similarity, url, title and text. migrate_pages_to_workers_guide: takes no input and returns the Pages-to-Workers migration guide text from developers.cloudflare.com/workers/prompts/pages-to-workers.txt. Agents SDK Documentation MCP server: search-agent-docs: takes query and optional k (default 5), searches the Agents SDK docs/*.md files of the cloudflare/agents repository and returns up to k Markdown results, each with the file name, a link to the full content and the matching chunk text.
- Search, kind `both`: (a) docs on the API server and search_cloudflare_documentation on the docs server. Input: query (string). One result holds similarity, url, title and text; docs also returns id. Ranking is semantic, through Cloudflare AI Search on Cloudflare's servers: the API server calls ai.autorag('docs-mcp-rag').search({query}), and the docs server calls the DOCS_AI_SEARCH AI Search binding's search({query}). The source does not name the embedding model. (b) search on the API server. Inputs: code (a JavaScript async arrow function) and truncate (optional). There is no ranking; the agent's code filters the pre-resolved OpenAPI spec by names, tags or paths, which is word or name matching that the agent writes. The code runs on Cloudflare's servers in a sandboxed Worker. (c) search-agent-docs on the Agents SDK Documentation server. Inputs: query (string) and k (number, default 5). One result holds the file name, a link to the full content and the chunk text. Ranking is keyword: an Orama index with BM25 and stemming over the recursively chunked docs/*.md files fetched from GitHub, cached in KV for one day, running in a Cloudflare Worker on Cloudflare's servers.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool of the three servers names a ui:// resource. In direct mode (?codemode=false) of the API server, a forge API tool passes a binary API response body on as an image or audio content block (src/tools/response-body.ts); that is raw API data, not a view. whoami carries OpenAI Apps metadata 'openai/profile': true, which marks a profile tool and is not a widget.
- Prompts and resources: Cloudflare API MCP server: no prompts. Resources: through the MCP Skills extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/skills), the server answers skills/list and skills/get, and resources/read serves every skill file at skill://<name>/<path>; resources/list lists each skill's SKILL.md. The catalog is the cloudflare/skills set, synced by a six-hourly cron. Documentation MCP server: one prompt, workers-prompt-full, a detailed prompt for generating Workers code fetched from https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/prompt.txt; no resources. Agents SDK Documentation MCP server: none (it registers only its one tool).
- Number of skills: 22. They are in github.com/cloudflare/skills under skills/<name>/SKILL.md. The repository is also a plugin marketplace with manifests for Claude Code (.claude-plugin), Codex (.codex-plugin), Cursor (.cursor-plugin) and Antigravity (.antigravity-plugin); plugin version 1.0.4. The same skills are served by the Cloudflare API MCP server. No contributor-only skills in that repository: .agents holds …

  - agents-sdk: Build, debug or review Cloudflare Agents SDK applications that use the agents package. basin: Build and troubleshoot Basin analytics workflows (Pipelines, Catalog, SQL) for streaming - Tools:
  - Taken from the code that registers the tools (package/src/cli/lib/mcp/tools/*.ts, convex 1.51.0):
  - 1. status: lists all deployments of a Convex project directory and returns each one's deployment selector, URL and dashboard URL, which the other tools take as input.
  - 2. data: reads one page of documents from a table in a deployment and returns page, isDone and continueCursor.
  - 3. tables: lists all tables in a deployment and returns the inferred and the declared schema of each.
  - 4. functionSpec: returns the metadata of each function in the deployment: its identifier, argument and return validators, its type (query, mutation or action) and its visibility (public or internal).
  - 5. run: runs a Convex function (query, mutation or action) on the deployment and returns its result and the log lines it produced.
  - 6. envList: lists the names of the deployment's environment variables, with their values only when includeValues is true.
  - 7. envGet: returns one environment variable of the deployment.
  - 8. envSet: sets an environment variable in the deployment.
  - 9. envRemove: removes an environment variable from the deployment.
  - 10. runOneoffQuery: runs a JavaScript string as a one-off read-only query on the deployment and returns its result.
  - 11. logs: fetches one batch of recent function execution log entries (it does not tail), with an optional failure-only filter, and returns the entries with a cursor for the next batch.
  - 12. insights: returns health insights for the last 72 hours: OCC conflicts (occRetried, occFailedPermanently) and resource-limit issues.

- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool returns a ui:// resource or an image (no match for ui:// or image content in the MCP source). Tools return JSON data, and the status tool returns dashboard URLs as text.

The repository has no SKILL.md outside skills/, so it has no contributor skills. Note: the README's 'Available Skills' section lists six names, three of which have no folder (convex-setup-auth, convex-migration-helper, convex-performance-audit). The count here …
- Skills:
  - From the description in each SKILL.md:
  - 1. convex: the umbrella entry point for any project that uses Convex or needs a backend; it routes to the bundled convex-* skills and the served capability catalog.
  - 2. convex-add: adds a capability (billing, crons, auth, agent, search, hosting) to the current Convex app from the served capability catalog; used on /add.
  - 3. convex-advisor: reads the deployment's 72-hour insights (read limits, OCC contention), finds the cause in code and reports performance and cost findings with fixes.
  - 4. convex-agent: adds an AI agent or RAG backend (@convex-dev/agent) to the app.
  - 5. convex-auth: adds Convex Auth sign-in (passkeys by default) to a new or existing app, including auth.config.ts.
  - 6. convex-authz: audits and hardens authorization for four failure patterns, applies requireIdentity/requireOwner and verifies with tsc; used on 'secure my app'.
  - 7. convex-backup: sets up backups and runs a restore drill into a preview deployment, with a schedule and a recovery runbook.
  - 8. convex-billing: adds Stripe billing through @convex-dev/stripe (checkout, webhook, gating).
  - 9. convex-cost: previews Convex spend by ranking functions from insights and projecting cost growth, and names the cheapest fix.
  - 10. convex-create-component: builds reusable Convex components with isolated tables and app-facing APIs.
  - 11. convex-crons: adds recurring scheduled jobs (crons).
  - 12. convex-deploy-guard: names the target deployment before any command that affects it, asks for fresh consent for production and supports a read-only session mode.
  - 13. convex-design: designs and builds Convex backends (schema, functions, indexes, auth, storage, scheduling, realtime, agent workflows).
  - 14. convex-docs: fetches the Convex docs for the installed version (page as markdown or node_modules types) instead of writing an API from memory.
  - 15. convex-domains: points a domain the user owns at the Convex app (DNS, custom-domain attach, auth-origin rebind).
  - 16. convex-env: sets and wires deployment environment variables and secrets.
  - 17. convex-expert: a Convex backend specialist for any code in a convex/ directory.
  - 18. convex-explain-app: explains an existing app (data model, public and internal functions, auth model, components, a request flow); read-only.
  - 19. convex-improve-convex-plugin: sends the session transcript to the Convex team for an AI post-mortem; only when the user asks.
  - 20. convex-insights: answers questions about a running app's logs and health through the official MCP server, with a dashboard deep link.
  - 21. convex-launch-readiness: runs the authz, reviewer, advisor and insights audits into one scored readiness report with a fix plan.
  - 22. convex-migrate-rehearse: rehearses a schema change and backfill on a snapshot-seeded preview deployment, then promotes it to production with the snapshot as rollback.
  - 23. convex-migrate: migrates the schema and backfills data on a deployed app with @convex-dev/migrations.
  - 24. convex-monitor: watches for the next dev or production error or request and reacts to it.
  - 25. convex-optimize: audits and optimizes an existing app for security, scale, upgrades and observability.
  - 26. convex-quickstart: gets a barebones Convex and web template running from a one-sentence idea.
  - 27. convex-reviewer: reviews Convex code for security, auth, validators, performance and patterns before shipping.
  - 28. convex-seed: seeds or imports data into the Convex database.
  - 29. convex-self-heal: triages and root-causes a production error, repairs it and certifies the fix, then opens a fix PR for a human to merge (never merges it).
  - 30. convex-sentinel: sets up Sentinel production error capture in the user's deployment.
  - 31. convex-suggest: passively suggests a matching Convex component when the user hand-rolls a pattern it already solves; never installs without consent.
  - 32. convex-test: generates convex-test tests for the app's functions.
  - 33. convex-verify: proves a feature works with seeds and several mocked users in convex-test, including negative authz cases.
- What the skills point at: Several sources. (1) The project's MCP server: convex-insights wraps the tools logs, insights, functionSpec and status, and convex-advisor uses insights.
