#### Cypress
Checked: cypress-io/ai-toolkit at commit e40f7be90bf1c09de6064ddaa36f0cefc3a59df0 (2026-11-16), plugin `cypress` 1.5.1 (.claude-plugin/plugin.json and .cursor-plugin/plugin.json); Cloud MCP registry entry io.cypress.mcp/cypress-cloud version 1.0.0 (mcp/server.json); … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: One official server: Cypress Cloud MCP, a remote server hosted by Cypress at https://mcp.cypress.io/mcp (streamable HTTP; OAuth or a personal access token as Bearer header). Registry name io.cypress.mcp/cypress-cloud, version 1.0.0 in mcp/server.json. It is generally available since 2026-05-20. Purpose: read-only access for an agent to the user's Cypress Cloud data, such as runs, specs, tests, failures, flaky tests, screenshots, and Accessibility and UI Coverage reports. The server code is not public. The repository holds only the config files and a VS Code extension (Cypress-io.vscode-cypress-cloud-mcp) that registers the remote URL. GitHub issues #33371 and #33412 in cypress-io/cypress propose a local @cypress/mcp server; they are proposals, not a published server.
- Number of tools: Cypress Cloud MCP: 14 tools. The count comes from the documentation (the Available tools table), because the server source is not public. The docs say that new tools appear on reconnect, and that plan- or product-specific tools appear only when the organization has the matching subscription.
- Tools:
  - Source: the documentation (the server code is not public).
  - 1. cypress_get_projects: lists all projects in the user's organization, so that the agent can find the projectId for later queries.
  - 2. cypress_get_runs: returns run summaries for a project, run URL or git branch, with an optional filter by status. A summary holds the run number, status, URL, tags, test status counts, commit author, duration in ms and CI build ID.
  - 3. cypress_get_specs: returns per-spec results for a run, filterable by status, with each spec's duration in ms, group and test counts, 25 specs per page.
  - 4. cypress_get_tests: returns per-test results for a run at any status, including skipped and pending, with test and per-attempt durations and a Test Replay link. It filters by test or spec status.
  - 5. cypress_get_failed_tests: returns attempt details of failed tests (error, stack trace, durations, Test Replay link), without test artifacts.
  - 6. cypress_get_flaky_tests: returns the flaky tests in a run, with test and per-attempt durations.
  - 7. cypress_get_test_screenshots: returns a test's screenshots, including failure screenshots and screenshots from cy.screenshot(), from the last attempt by default.
  - 8. cypress_get_accessibility_report: returns a high-level accessibility report for a run: violation counts by severity, failing rules with element counts, and the top 5 views by failure count.
  - 9. cypress_get_accessibility_views: returns paginated views from an accessibility report, sorted by number of failing rules.
  - 10. cypress_get_accessibility_rule_failures: returns paginated failing DOM elements for one accessibility rule, with CSS selector, view and failure message, optionally scoped to one view.
  - 11. cypress_get_ui_coverage_report: returns a high-level UI Coverage report for a run: coverage score, tested and untested element and link counts, and the top 5 riskiest views.
  - 12. cypress_get_ui_coverage_views: returns paginated views from a UI Coverage report, sorted by most untested elements and links.
  - 13. cypress_get_ui_coverage_elements: returns paginated interactive elements for a run, filterable by tested or untested and optionally scoped to one view by name.
  - 14. submit_mcp_feedback: sends the user's feedback to Cypress from the agent.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none. The 14 documented tools fetch and filter Cloud data by project, run, branch, status or view. No tool takes a free-text query or searches documentation.
- User interface from a tool, kind `not confirmed`: cypress_get_test_screenshots returns a test's screenshots: failure screenshots and screenshots from cy.screenshot(), from the last attempt by default. A docs example prompt asks the agent to compare screenshots of failed and passing attempts. The docs do not say whether the tool returns MCP image content or image URLs. No tool names a ui:// resource (MCP Apps), and none is documented. The tool reads recorded Cloud data and needs no local dev server or other local process.
- Prompts and resources: not confirmed. The docs name tools only and list no MCP prompts or resources. The server source is not public, so the absence cannot be checked in code.
- Number of skills: 5. They live in github.com/cypress-io/ai-toolkit under skills/ (skills/<name>/SKILL.md). They ship in the plugin `cypress` 1.5.1 for Claude Code and Cursor ("skills": "./skills/") and install with `npx skills add cypress-io/ai-toolkit`. All five are for consumers; the repository has no contributor-only skills.

  - 2. cypress-explain (1.0.2): explains Cypress tests and answers questions about Cypress use and behavior. Use it when the user asks how a test or Cypress works, or asks to review or critique a test without writing code.

- MCP servers: One official MCP server: daisyUI Blueprint, npm package daisyui-blueprint 1.8.2 (2026-10-04). It is a local stdio server that needs a paid license (bin daisyui-blueprint -> server.js, started with npx -y daisyui-blueprint@latest, env LICENSE and EMAIL, optional FIGMA). It runs a guided workflow that supplies daisyUI setup, rules, design direction, page plans, component syntax and a quality audit, plus conversion workflows. Its reference data ships in the package as 8 encrypted chunks (chunks/1-8.json). The server checks the license at startup (startLicensedServer). The repository named in package.json (github.com/saadeghi/daisyui-blueprint) is not public. The main daisyUI repo holds only the plugin wrapper (packages/blueprint: mcp.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json version 1.5.0, .cursor-plugin/plugin.json).
- Number of tools: 11 for daisyui-blueprint 1.8.2. Sources: the code in server.js plus the documentation. server.js registers tools in four groups: registerBlueprintResources(ctx) registers one tool for each definition in the encrypted data. These are 5 tools, and their names are confirmed by the readable SKIPPABLE_TOOL_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES map and by the README. registerQualityCheck registers …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code (server.js) gives the names and schemas of the two hard-coded tools and the names of the five data-driven tools (SKIPPABLE_TOOL_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES). The README and the documentation describe the five data-driven tools. The four conversion tools come from the documentation only. In the order of the workflow:
  - 1. daisyui_setup_expert (Setup Expert): returns project-specific setup resources: framework and dependency facts, Tailwind CSS and daisyUI install guidance, configuration, themes, colors, fonts, icons and file structure. It starts a workflow (workflowId, projectRoot).
  - 2. daisyui_rules_enforcer (Rules Enforcer): returns the daisyUI rules for component syntax, accessibility, responsive behavior, themes, media and code quality.
  - 3. daisyui_creative_director (Creative Director): returns design guidance: content, audience, UX, taste, composition, color, typography, a design-trend catalog and motion.
  - 4. daisyui_page_architect (Page Architect): with only `context`, returns matching page options from 211 page architectures; with chosen `PageIDs`, returns the page plans and the suggested component IDs for each page.
  - 5. daisyui_component_syntax_expert (Component Syntax Expert): returns the exact daisyUI syntax for the requested component and block IDs (structure, class names, variants, rules, snippets, examples), in batches within MAX_COMPONENT_RESPONSE_CHARS (default 24000), with the remaining SnippetIDs in its next step.

It returns status, action, edit policy, findings, manual checks and a summary.

#### Drizzle ORM
Checked: drizzle-kit 1.0.0-rc.5 (npm dist-tag "rc", published 2026-10-21T18:01:51Z), the newest release that holds the MCP server and the skill. The npm "latest" tag is drizzle-kit 0.31.11 (2026-09-21), which has no MCP server and no skill. drizzle-orm: latest 0.45.4, … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: the `mcp` subcommand of the drizzle-kit npm package (`drizzle-kit mcp`). It is a stdio server with the McpServer name "drizzle", version 1.0.0-rc.5, released 2026-10-21. It exposes the drizzle-kit migration lifecycle (generate, fix_conflicts, push, pull, check, export, up) as tools. drizzle-orm itself has no server. The docs site documents the same server at orm.drizzle.team/docs/drizzle-kit-mcp.
- Number of tools: drizzle-kit mcp: 7, counted from the code that registers the tools (server.registerTool calls in createDrizzleMcpServer in bin.cjs of rc.5). The beta-branch src/mcp/server.ts and the tools table of MCP.md have the same 7.
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (rc.5 bin.cjs). Each tool returns the drizzle-kit JSON envelope as text and as structuredContent, with status ok / no_changes / missing_hints / error. isError is true for error and missing_hints.
  - generate: diffs the current schema against the latest snapshot and writes a new migration file. Inputs are config, hints, name, custom and ignoreConflicts. A missing_hints result asks the agent to call it again with hints (destructiveHint false).
  - fix_conflicts: postgresql only. Deletes the conflicting migrations that check reports, with all their children, then generates one new migration from the schema. It is destructive (destructiveHint true). Inputs are config, hints, name and custom.
  - push: applies the current schema directly to a live database without writing a migration file. It is destructive. Inputs are config and hints.
  - check: checks the snapshot history for migration conflicts and is read-only and idempotent. For postgresql it also compares the schema with the migrations and returns warnings (schema_changed, merge_needed, not_compared). Inputs are config and ignoreConflicts.
  - export: exports the full schema as a SQL dump by diffing it against an empty state. It is read-only and idempotent, with no database connection and no files written. Input is config.
  - up: upgrades the migrations folder to the current layout and snapshot format. It moves meta/_journal.json into per-migration folders and converts postgresql snapshots to format 9. It is idempotent. Input is config.
  - pull: introspects a live database and writes schema.ts, relations.ts and a snapshot to the out directory. With init true, it also records the pulled migration as applied in the live migrations table and sets _meta "com.drizzle.team/pull.destructiveHint". Inputs are config and init.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: none. createDrizzleMcpServer calls only registerTool. The only registerPrompt and registerResource matches in bin.cjs are the method definitions of the bundled MCP SDK class (lines 178243 and 178426).
- Number of skills: 1. The skill lives in the drizzle-kit npm package at skills/drizzle/SKILL.md, with the topic files migrations.md, generate.md, push.md, pull.md, hints.md, output-modes.md and responses-and-errors.md. In the repository it is drizzle-kit/skills/drizzle on the beta branch. `drizzle-kit skills` installs it. The drizzle-orm package ships no skill. The docs page says rc5 replaced the separate skills of …
- Skills:
  - drizzle: the entry point for all Drizzle work, covering drizzle-orm schema and query code and drizzle-kit migrations. An agent loads it before it reads or edits any file that imports drizzle-orm/*, before it edits drizzle.config.ts, and for generate, push, pull, missing_hints, output modes, JSON responses and errors, migration conflicts from several git branches, or `drizzle-kit up`. Each session it also runs a check that the installed skill is not out of date (metadata.revision 15).

It gives an MCP host the Agent Builder tools, which query and change the user's Elasticsearch and Kibana data. It is GA in Stack 9.3+ and on Serverless, and was a preview in 9.2. Its source is Kibana x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/agent_builder/server/routes/mcp.ts, at main 527d118 (2026-11-20). (3) The standalone Elasticsearch MCP server mcp-server-elasticsearch, a Docker image (docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch), version 0.4.6. It reads Elasticsearch directly. It is deprecated: 'This MCP server is deprecated and will only receive critical security updates going forward. It has been superseded by the Elastic Agent Builder MCP endpoint'.

- Tools:
  - A) Docs MCP server, 9 tools, from the code (Tools/*.cs; the names come from templates resolved for the public profile, {resource}=docs, {scope}=empty):
  - search_docs: Searches all published Elastic documentation by meaning, with query, pageNumber, pageSize, productFilter and sectionFilter. Returns documents with AI summaries, relevance scores and navigation context.
  - find_related_docs: Finds documentation pages related to a topic. Returns a list of related pages, with a limit and a product filter.
  - get_document_by_url: Retrieves one page by URL or path. Returns the title, AI summaries, headings, navigation context, and the body only when includeBody is true.
  - analyze_document_structure: Analyzes the structure of one page. Returns the heading count, link count, parent pages and whether AI summaries are present.
  - search_api_operations: Searches the Elastic REST API reference by words, an endpoint or a field path. Returns operations with method, path, operation id and the matched fields.
  - get_api_operation: Retrieves one REST API operation by operationId or endpoint. Returns its routes, versions, every documented field, and the page body when asked.
  - list_api_operations: Lists the REST APIs with their keys and versions, or the operations of one API by group.
  - check_docs_coherence: Checks how coherently a topic is covered across the docs. Returns a coverage analysis across products and sections.
  - find_docs_inconsistencies: Finds possible inconsistencies between pages on the same topic, with an optional focus area.

  - C) mcp-server-elasticsearch 0.4.6, 5 tools, from the code:
  - list_indices: Lists Elasticsearch indices matching index_pattern.
  - get_mappings: Returns the field mappings of one index.
  - search: Runs a Query DSL search on an index; returns hits and aggregations.
  - esql: Runs an ES|QL query; returns the results.
  - get_shards: Returns shard information for all or some indices.
- Search, kind `both`: Docs MCP search_docs takes query (a question or keywords), pageNumber, pageSize (default 10, max 50), productFilter and sectionFilter. Each result holds url, title, contentType, description, score, aiShortSummary, navigationSection, product and lastUpdated, and the response has isSemanticQuery and totalHits. Ranking is a hybrid in Elasticsearch: a lexical query (multi_match, keyword and phrase clauses, with synonyms) plus semantic queries on semantic_text fields (title, abstract, ai_rag_optimized_summary, ai_questions). The semantic branch is added only when semantic search is enabled and the query looks like a question: it ends with '?', has more than 3 words, or starts with a question word (regex ^(how|why|what|when|where|can|should|is it|do i|does|will|would|could)). The inference model behind semantic_text is not named in the code read. Ranking runs on Elastic's server. find_related_docs takes topic, limit and productFilter. Docs MCP search_api_operations is keyword matching on the API reference (term, regexp and synonym matching, minimum_should_match '2<75%'), with no semantic clause. Agent Builder platform.core.search takes natural language, and the server picks Query DSL or ES|QL for the user's data in Kibana and Elasticsearch, using the configured LLM. platform.core.product_documentation searches the Elastic docs installed in Kibana. mcp-server-elasticsearch search takes index, a Query DSL query_body and fields; it does not search documentation.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No ui:// resource or image content exists in any of the three servers. The Agent Builder MCP route wraps every tool result as one JSON text item. The docs say some built-in tools, such as platform.core.create_visualization, return results 'that only Elastic Agent Builder chat can use' and exclude them from MCP. security.get_entity_graph and security.get_entity_risk_score_history render a preview or chart in Agent Builder chat, but over MCP they also return text.
- Prompts and resources: Agent Builder MCP: none. The route calls only server.registerTool, with no prompts or resources. mcp-server-elasticsearch: none. ServerCapabilities enables tools only, and a 'prompts' config field exists but nothing registers prompts. Docs MCP: none found in the source. No McpServerPrompt or McpServerResource matches in src. It sends server instructions (ComposeServerInstructions) with triggers and tool guidance.

The areas are cloud (2), elasticsearch (10), kibana (7), observability (6) and security (6). The README's 'Available Skills' tables list the same 31. plugins/<area>/skills/ holds the same 31 skills again (31 SKILL.md files) for the Claude and Cursor plugins. All 31 are for users of Elastic.

  - elasticsearch-cluster-health: Diagnoses a yellow or red cluster and gives the most likely cause with remediation; used for unassigned shards and allocation failures.
  - elasticsearch-esql: Executes ES|QL queries; used to query data, analyze logs, aggregate metrics or build charts from ES|QL.
  - elasticsearch-index-design: Designs and reviews index mappings and shard settings for access patterns; used when creating an index or fixing field types.
  - elasticsearch-ingest: Loads CSV, JSON and NDJSON files with the bulk API and explicit mappings; used for batch imports of local files.
  - elasticsearch-onboarding: Takes a developer new to Elasticsearch from zero to a working search experience; used when a user shows intent to build search.
  - elasticsearch-query-optimization: Diagnoses slow Query DSL searches with profiling and proposes measured fixes; used when a search is slow.
  - elasticsearch-reindex: Guides reindex (local, remote, slicing, throttling, task API); used when copying or migrating indices or changing mappings.
  - elasticsearch-search-relevance: Tunes relevance with query rules, multi_match and boosts; used when results rank poorly.
  - kibana-agent-builder: Creates and manages Agent Builder agents and custom tools; used to create, update, test or inspect them.

  - security-ml-integrations: Installs and manages the security ML integration packages (beaconing, ded, dga, lmd, pad, problemchild); used to set up or troubleshoot them.

- Tools:
  - HOSTED SERVER (from the documentation table, 56):
  - read_documentation - fetches one Expo documentation page and returns its content as markdown, up to ~5000 tokens per call, with offset for paging.
  - search_documentation - searches the official Expo documentation and returns page URLs ranked by relevance for a user query (requires an Expo Services paid plan).
  - usage_budget_get - returns usage limits and available usage (minutes exclude active reservations).
  - usage_budget_create - creates a usage budget with user-approved limits and returns a usageBudgetId for metered operations.
  - workflow_info - returns status, job results, errors and artifacts of one workflow run by ID.
  - workflow_list - lists recent workflow runs for a project (appId or appFullName).
  - workflow_logs - returns a summary of log sections of a workflow job, or one section by sectionIndex or phase.
  - workflow_run - triggers a workflow run from a git reference.
  - workflow_cancel - cancels a running workflow.
  - workflow_validate - validates workflow YAML syntax and configuration.
  - build_list - lists builds for a project, newest first, with status and artifacts.
  - build_info - returns status and details (errors, artifacts) of one build by ID.
  - build_logs - returns the logs of a finished or errored build.
  - build_submit - submits a finished build to the App Store or Google Play Store.
  - build_run - triggers a new build from an eas.json build profile (needs a connected GitHub repository).
  - build_cancel - cancels a queued or in-progress build.
  - sandbox_stop - requests cancellation of a sandbox's backing job and returns its status.
  - sandbox_list - lists sandboxes for a project, newest first, with status filter and cursor.
  - sandbox_create - creates a billable sandbox environment for a project.
  - sandbox_wait - waits until a sandbox is RUNNING, STOPPED or ERRORED and returns the last status.
  - sandbox_exec - executes a shell command in a running sandbox.
  - sandbox_write_stdin - reads output from, or sends input to, a sandbox command session.
  - sandbox_artifact_create - uploads one file from a running sandbox as an artifact and returns its upload status.
  - sandbox_artifact_get - reads a sandbox artifact and returns a new download URL.
  - sandbox_artifact_list - lists the artifacts of a sandbox, newest first.
  - sandbox_read_file - reads a UTF-8 text file (up to 40000 bytes) or a PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP image (as image content, up to 3000000 bytes) from a running sandbox.
  - observe_versions - lists app versions seen by Expo Observe with build numbers, build/update IDs, event and unique-user counts.
  - observe_metrics_summary - compares Observe performance metrics by app version and platform (counts, min, max, median, average, p80, p90, p99).
  - observe_metrics - finds individual Observe performance samples such as the slowest startup/navigation events, paginated.
  - observe_routes - compares navigation routes by cold TTR, warm TTR and TTI per platform.
  - observe_event_names - lists custom events emitted with Observe.logEvent with counts and first/last seen times.
  - observe_events - reads custom events with properties, severity and session IDs.
  - observe_session - reads one session's metric samples, logs and request trace spans.
  - observe_span_names - lists request trace span names with kinds and counts.
  - observe_spans - finds request trace spans (slow or failed requests) by name, host, status, duration or session.
  - observe_trace - reads every span of one request trace by trace ID.
  - observe_errors - lists error groups (JS errors and native crashes) with occurrence, user and session counts.
  - observe_error_occurrences - reads individual errors and crashes with stack traces, newest first.
  - observe_error_breakdown - splits one error group by app version, OS, device model or country.
  - simulator_start - starts a billed cloud simulator session and returns simulatorSessionId.
  - simulator_get - returns status and dashboardUrl of a cloud simulator session, optionally polling.
  - simulator_list - lists cloud simulator sessions for a project, newest first.
  - simulator_stop - stops a cloud simulator session.
  - automation_tap - taps the connected device (cloud simulator by simulatorSessionId, or local device through the expo-mcp tunnel by projectRoot) by testID or x/y.
  - automation_take_screenshot - takes a screenshot of the connected device at 0.3 scale and returns the image with imageScale and tapUnit text.
  - automation_find_view - finds a view by testID or accessibility label and returns frame, is_visible, is_hittable and is_enabled.
  - automation_type - types text on the connected device, into a testID field or the focused field.
  - automation_scroll - scrolls the connected device screen in a direction by a fraction or a fixed distance.
  - testflight_crashes - lists recent TestFlight crashes, or returns one full crash log with stack trace.
  - testflight_feedback - returns TestFlight screenshot feedback with device info, comments and screenshot URLs.
  - appstore_reviews - returns public App Store customer reviews (rating, title, body, reviewer, territory).
  - appstore_reply_review - posts or edits the public developer response to an App Store review (a write action).
  - appstore_delete_review_response - deletes the public developer response on an App Store review (a write action).
  - playstore_crashes - lists Google Play crash/ANR issues, or returns one full error report with stack trace.
  - playstore_reviews - returns Google Play user reviews with author, rating, device info and text.
  - playstore_reply_review - posts or edits a public developer reply to a Google Play review (a write action).
  - EXPO-MCP LOCAL CAPABILITIES (from the registering code, 6):
  - expo_router_sitemap - runs npx -y expo-router-sitemap@latest in the project and returns the list of all routes as text (registered only in an Expo Router project).
  - open_devtools - opens React Native DevTools for the running app and returns text on the dev server URL found (needs a running Metro dev server).
  - collect_app_logs - collects logs for up to 10000 ms (default 2000) from Android logcat, iOS syslog and/or the JS console, with optional regex filter and log level, and returns them as text.
  - automation_tap - taps the running app at x/y or on a React Native testID and returns the result as JSON text.
  - automation_take_screenshot - takes a screenshot of the full screen or of one testID view and returns it as a JPEG image.
  - automation_find_view - finds a view by testID and returns its properties (position, size, visibility) as JSON text.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: Tool search_documentation on the hosted server (Server; requires an Expo Services paid plan). Input: a user query (exact input field names not documented). One result: a documentation page URL; the agent then calls read_documentation for content. Ranking: 'ranked by relevance'; the model, index or library is not named. It runs on Expo's hosted server (https://mcp.expo.dev/mcp), not on the user's machine. The docs state the server does not run an AI model itself.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: automation_take_screenshot (local expo-mcp): returns a JPEG image of the running app's full screen or one testID view; the user sees a static image, no interaction in the view; needs a booted simulator/device running the app and the local dev server (EXPO_UNSTABLE_MCP_SERVER=1 npx expo start, or the expo-mcp CLI with --dev-server-url). automation_take_screenshot (hosted): returns a screenshot at 0.3 scale plus imageScale/tapUnit text, either from a cloud simulator session (simulatorSessionId; no local process) or from the local device through the expo-mcp tunnel (projectRoot; needs the local dev server with expo-mcp). sandbox_read_file (hosted): returns a PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP image file from a running cloud sandbox; no local process. No tool names a ui:// resource in the expo-mcp code; the docs name no MCP Apps view for the hosted server. simulator_get returns a dashboardUrl to view the device in a browser after login (a link, not a returned view).
- Prompts and resources: Prompts: expo_router_sitemap (local expo-mcp, only in an Expo Router project) - returns the routes of the project from expo-router-sitemap as an assistant message. The hosted server documents no prompts of its own (the docs Prompts table has only this Local row). Resources: none in expo-mcp (src/ calls no registerResource; only the mcp-tunnel proxy classes define the method); the docs list no resources for the hosted server.
- Number of skills: 24: 23 in plugins/expo/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (plugin expo 1.15.5) and 1 in plugins/expo-experiments/skills/expo-migrate-module/SKILL.md (plugin expo-experiments 0.2.2), in github.com/expo/skills (marketplace expo-plugins). Left out: .claude/skills/expo-skill-eval (contributor skill for the repository's evaluation).

#### Figma (MCP server and its skills)
Checked: Remote MCP server com.figma.mcp/mcp version 2.2.211 (server.json and plugin.json in github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide, commit 43a06ff, 2026-11-18, re-cloned 2026-11-20). Tools page, desktop-server page and Help Center skills article read on 2026-11-20. The … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: Two official servers, both closed source. (1) The remote server at https://mcp.figma.com/mcp uses Streamable HTTP. Its registry name is "com.figma.mcp/mcp", version 2.2.211. It reads designs from Figma, writes designs into Figma, does Code Connect, works with generative plugins and shaders, and runs Figma Weave. (2) The desktop server runs inside the Figma desktop app at http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp. It cannot write to the canvas or send UI to Figma. It has no separate version number; it ships with the app.
- Number of tools: Remote server: 44 tools. That is 20 read tools, 15 write tools and 9 Figma Weave tools. Desktop server: 12 tools, the ones in the read and write tables without the 'Remote only' mark. It is not confirmed whether the desktop server has the Weave tools, because the Weave tools are listed separately and have no such mark. (The desktop page's own list of 7 tools plus the prompt applies only to Figma …
- Tools:
  - Source: the documentation (tools-and-prompts page). The server code is not public.
  - Read tools (20):
  - download_assets: downloads assets for up to 20 nodes per call and returns temporary URLs. It gives export renders (PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF) and the raw source images.
  - export_video: exports the keyframe animation of a frame as an MP4. It returns a jobId to poll, then a downloadUrl and availableUntil.
  - get_code_connect_map: returns the Code Connect mappings for the instances in a selection: componentName, source, snippet, snippetImports, snippetNestedFunctions, version and label.
  - get_code_connect_suggestions: detects Figma components and suggests code components to map them to. Figma or the figma-code-connect skill calls it.
  - get_comments: reads comment threads and replies. It returns links, reactions, image attachment URLs, read/unread status, and canvas locations or Make preview locations. It can filter by page, author, mention, unread, resolved or thread.
  - get_context_for_code_connect: returns component details for Code Connect templates: properties, variant options, nested instances and text layers.
  - get_design_context: returns the design context and code for a layer or selection. The code is React and Tailwind by default; a prompt can ask for another framework. It includes a shader runtime when the design uses shaders.
  - get_figjam: returns an XML outline of FigJam diagrams, with screenshots of the nodes.
  - get_generative_plugin: reads one generative plugin. It returns the name, description, owner, version, and the source files as {filename, bytes, uri} resources, or inline with includeSource.
  - get_libraries: lists the libraries already added to a file and the libraries that can be added. Each result has a name, key, description and source.
  - get_metadata: returns a lightweight XML outline of a selection: layer IDs, names, types, positions and sizes. Without a node ID it returns the list of pages.
  - get_motion_context: returns the animated nodes, keyframe tracks with easing, CSS @keyframes and Motion snippets, and hints about nodes that animate together.
  - get_screenshot: takes a PNG screenshot of one node. It returns a URL, or inline base64 with enableBase64Response.
  - get_shader: reads one shader effect or fill. It returns the name, description, owner, type, version, and the source files as URIs.
  - get_variable_defs: returns the variables and styles that a selection uses (colors, spacing, typography).
  - list_file_shaders: lists up to 100 shaders that a file uses, with the source at the exact version the file uses.
  - list_generative_plugins: lists the generative plugins in the account library (id, name, description, owner, nextCursor).
  - list_shaders: lists the shader effects and fills in the account library (id, name, description, owner, type, nextCursor).
  - search_design_system: searches the connected libraries for components, variables and styles that match a text query. Several queries can go in one call.
  - whoami: returns the email, the plans and the seat type on each plan.
  - Write tools (15):
  - add_code_connect_map: maps a Figma component to its code component.
  - create_generative_plugin: creates a starter generative plugin that draws a square, and returns its ID.
  - create_new_file: creates a blank Figma Design, FigJam or Slides file in the drafts.
  - create_shader: creates a starter shader effect or fill, and returns its ID.
  - generate_diagram: generates a FigJam diagram from a description or from Mermaid syntax: flowchart, Gantt, state, sequence, architecture or ERD.
  - generate_figma_design: sends the live UI of a web app or site to Figma as design layers, in a new file, an existing file or the clipboard.
  - generate_image: generates an image from text, places it in a file, and returns the node ID, model, width and height. It uses AI credits.
  - generate_vector_illustration: generates editable vector graphics (an icon or an illustration) from text, places them, and returns the node ID. It uses AI credits.
  - html_to_figma: converts a self-contained HTML document into plain design layers, up to 20 frames per call.
  - send_code_to_figma: imports a local project, packed as an archive, into a Figma Make file or into a code layer in a Design file.
  - send_code_connect_mappings: confirms the mappings that get_code_connect_suggestions suggested.
  - update_generative_plugin: replaces code.ts and ui.html of a plugin with a commit message. Figma builds, versions and deploys it, and the tool returns the version or compiler output.
  - update_shader: replaces main.ts of a shader with a commit message, and returns the version or compiler output.
  - upload_assets: uploads images and SVGs into a file, up to 60 files of 10 MB each. Images become fills; SVGs become vector layers.
  - use_figma: the general-purpose tool that creates, edits, deletes or inspects content in Design, FigJam, Slides and Specs files by running Plugin API JavaScript.
  - Figma Weave tools (9):
  - weave_list_tools: lists the runnable Weave tools, with an optional name search.
  - weave_get_tool_inputs: returns the version, outputs and inputs of a Weave tool.
  - weave_upload_asset: returns a single-use submitUrl that uploads a file to use as a Weave input.
  - weave_run_tool: runs a Weave tool. It returns runIds, or inputs_required, or cost_confirmation_required.
  - weave_get_tool_run_output: returns the status, progress, errors and output of tool runs.
  - weave_cancel_tool_run: cancels runs that are in progress.
  - weave_find_model: finds a Weave model by name, and returns its cost and inputs.
  - weave_run_model: runs a Weave model directly, and returns a prediction ID or a cost to approve.
  - weave_get_model_run_output: returns the status and output links of model runs.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: search_design_system. Input: `queries`, an array of {entity: "component"|"variable"|"style", query}; `fileKey` (required); optional `includeLibraryKeys`, which take keys from get_libraries. A result is one entry for each query. For components: name, libraryName, assetType, componentSetKey, description. For variables: name, variableType, variableSetKey, key, scopes, variableCollectionName. Styles are returned too. How it ranks: per the skill text, components are matched by name and description 'via a recommendation engine (relevance-ranked, not exact match)', and variables are matched against variable names. Queries do not apply OR semantics. No source names a model or an index. The ranking runs on Figma's servers, because the server is hosted. weave_list_tools takes a `search` field that matches tool names without regard to case. weave_find_model takes a `query` with the model name.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: get_screenshot: the agent sees a PNG render of one Figma node. It comes as a URL, or inline base64 with enableBase64Response. Nobody can interact with it. get_figjam: an XML outline plus screenshots of the FigJam nodes. Nobody can interact with them. Neither tool needs a local dev server. The remote server renders on Figma's servers; the desktop server needs the Figma desktop app to run. No documented tool returns a ui:// MCP Apps resource.
- Prompts and resources: Prompts: 1. create_design_system_rules creates a rules file that gives the agent the context to turn designs into code that fits the codebase. Resources: (a) Figma Make files: the server shares the files of a Make project as MCP resources. (b) The source files of generative plugins and shaders: get_generative_plugin, get_shader and list_file_shaders return them as resource URIs. (c) The skills are served as MCP resources. The figma-use SKILL.md refers to a skill 'loaded via an MCP resource'. The URI scheme skill://figma/<name>/SKILL.md is not stated on a public documentation page or in the guide repository.
- Number of skills: 19 skills for users, all in github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide. 17 are bundled with the Figma plugin in skills/<name>/SKILL.md. 2 are standalone workflow skills in workflow-skills/<name>/SKILL.md, which the plugin does not bundle. The folder skills-figquery/ holds a variant of the same 17 skills, generated for Cursor only, so they are not counted twice. figma-power/ holds a Kiro 'Power' (POWER.md …
- Skills:
  - figma-3d-transforms: adds or edits 3D transforms (depth, perspective, z-axis rotation, tilt, isometric, parallax). Use it when a request reaches into the third dimension.
  - figma-code-connect: creates and maintains Code Connect template files (.figma.ts or .figma.js) that map Figma components to code snippets. Use it when the user mentions Code Connect or component mapping.
  - figma-code-workflows: imports local HTML or project files into Figma as editable Design frames, runnable Code Layers or standalone Code (Make), and repairs imported previews. Use it only when the user names that kind of output or gives a Figma file as the destination.
  - figma-create-new-file: creates a new Figma Design, FigJam or Slides file. The agent must invoke it before every create_new_file call.
  - figma-design-to-code: a mandatory prerequisite before get_design_context. It is the workflow to implement a Figma design as code.
  - figma-generate-design: translates a page, view or multi-section layout into Figma by finding the design-system components, variables and styles and assembling them section by section. Use it with figma-use.
  - figma-generate-diagram: a mandatory prerequisite before generate_diagram. It routes to guidance for each diagram type and sets the Mermaid constraints for flowcharts, sequence diagrams, ERDs, state diagrams, Gantt charts and timelines.
  - figma-generate-library: builds or updates a design system in Figma from a codebase: variables and tokens, components with variants, theming and documentation. Use it with figma-use, and also to create any single component.
  - figma-generative-plugins: a mandatory prerequisite before create_generative_plugin or update_generative_plugin. Use it to author or fix a reusable generative plugin.
  - figma-implement-motion: translates Figma motion and animations into production code. Use it when a design node is animated or get_design_context points to get_motion_context.
  - figma-shaders: a mandatory prerequisite before create_shader or update_shader. Use it to author or iterate on shader effects and fills.
  - figma-spec: required to create, read, edit, review or comment on Figma specs (a PRD, brief or RFC), standalone or embedded in a file.
  - figma-swiftui: SwiftUI to Figma translation in both directions. Use it whenever the request involves Swift, SwiftUI or iOS.
  - figma-use: a mandatory prerequisite before every use_figma call. It holds the Plugin API rules for write actions and for script-based reads.
  - figma-use-figjam: helps the agent use use_figma in a FigJam file. Use it alongside figma-use.
  - figma-use-motion: animation context for use_figma (keyframes, animation styles, easing, timeline duration). Load it alongside figma-use.
  - figma-use-slides: helps the agent use use_figma in a Figma Slides file. Use it alongside figma-use.
  - generate-project-plan (standalone): makes a FigJam project plan board from a PRD and the codebase in an interactive flow, section by section.
  - video-interaction-mapper (standalone): takes the key moments from a UI screen recording, infers the interaction triggers, and builds an annotated Figma storyboard.
- What the skills point at: The skills point mainly to the MCP tools of the server. Word occurrences in the Markdown files under skills/ at commit 43a06ff: use_figma (230), generate_diagram (70), get_design_context (54), get_motion_context (45), get_metadata (37), get_screenshot (34), search_design_system (34); also create_new_file, upload_assets, generate_figma_design, get_libraries, update_shader, update_generative_plugin, whoami, get_figjam, Code Connect tools, html_to_figma, send_code_to_figma, export_video, download_assets, and create_session. They also point to reference files inside each skill folder, such as skills/figma-use/references/plugin-api-standalone.d.ts and gotchas.md, and to other skills. There is no …

#### Firebase
Checked: firebase-tools 15.37.0 (npm dist-tag latest, published 2026-11-18T23:22:23Z; a preview tag 15.37.1-feat-crashlytics-mcp-phase2a.0 also exists). Checked by a shallow clone of tag v15.37.0. firebase/agent-skills at 99954a3 (2026-11-09, 'Add skill for … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: the Firebase MCP server, the `mcp` subcommand of the npm package `firebase-tools` (newest 15.37.0, 2026-11-18). Registry name io.github.firebase/firebase-mcp. It is a local stdio server that gives agents tools for Firebase projects, services and data, using the Firebase CLI credentials. In the same process it also proxies tools from remote Google MCP endpoints: firestore.googleapis.com, firebasedataconnect.googleapis.com and developerknowledge.googleapis.com. Its code calls these endpoints `ONEMCP_SERVERS`, and their tools appear as tools of the Firebase server, renamed `${feature}_${name}`.
- Number of tools: There are two counts. (a) The code registers 43 local tools in src/mcp/tools/*/index.ts (apphosting 2, auth 3, core 17, crashlytics 9, dataconnect 3, firestore 1, functions 2, messaging 1, realtimedatabase 2, remoteconfig 2, storage 1). Two more, apptesting_run_test and apptesting_check_status, are added only when the experiment flag `mcpalpha` is on. (b) The code also fetches remote tools at run …
- Tools:
  - Sources: the local tools (1-43) come from the code at v15.37.0, with the humanReadableDescription of each. The Firestore and Developer Knowledge remote tools (44-70) come from the documentation table. The Data Connect remote tools (71-76) come from the allowlist in the code, which gives names only. Each local tool name is the feature prefix plus the name in the code (the code name of dataconnect_build is `build`, in compile.ts).
  - 1 apphosting_fetch_logs: Fetches recent service or build logs for an App Hosting backend.
  - 2 apphosting_list_backends: Lists App Hosting backends, their traffic configurations and custom domains.
  - 3 auth_get_users: Returns Firebase Auth users by UID, email or phone number, or lists all users.
  - 4 auth_update_user: Enables or disables a user account, or sets custom claims on it.
  - 5 auth_set_sms_region_policy: Sets an SMS region policy that allows or denies country codes for Firebase Authentication.
  - 6 firebase_login: Signs the user in to the Firebase CLI and the MCP server, or checks the current sign-in status.
  - 7 firebase_logout: Signs the user out of the Firebase CLI and the MCP server.
  - 8 firebase_validate_security_rules: Checks the syntax of Firestore, Storage or Realtime Database security rules and returns the errors.
  - 9 firebase_get_project: Returns the metadata and configuration of the active Firebase project.
  - 10 firebase_list_apps: Lists the Firebase apps in the active project.
  - 11 firebase_list_projects: Lists the Firebase projects that the signed-in user can access.
  - 12 firebase_get_sdk_config: Returns the SDK configuration, or the content of the config file, for a registered app.
  - 13 firebase_create_project: Creates a Firebase project, or adds Firebase to an existing Google Cloud project.
  - 14 firebase_create_app: Creates an iOS, Android or Web app in the active project.
  - 15 firebase_create_android_sha: Adds a SHA-1 or SHA-256 certificate hash to an Android app.
  - 16 firebase_get_environment: Returns the CLI and MCP environment, with the active project and the signed-in user.
  - 17 firebase_update_environment: Changes the project directory, the active project or the active user account, and has an MCP App view.
  - 18 firebase_init: Sets up Firebase services in the local project and writes firebase.json and rules files, and has an MCP App view.
  - 19 firebase_get_security_rules: Returns the active security rules for Firestore, Storage or Realtime Database.
  - 20 firebase_read_resources: Returns the content of firebase:// guide and docs resources, or lists all of them.
  - 21 firebase_deploy: Starts a background deploy of the services in firebase.json and returns a job ID, and has an MCP App view.
  - 22 firebase_deploy_status: Returns the status and progress of a background deploy job.
  - 23 crashlytics_create_note: Adds a note to a Crashlytics issue.
  - 24 crashlytics_delete_note: Deletes a note from a Crashlytics issue.
  - 25 crashlytics_get_issue: Returns the details and metadata of a Crashlytics issue.
  - 26 crashlytics_list_events: Lists recent crash events that match filters.
  - 27 crashlytics_batch_get_events: Returns crash events by their resource names.
  - 28 crashlytics_list_notes: Lists the notes of a Crashlytics issue.
  - 29 crashlytics_get_report: Returns aggregated numerical reports for Crashlytics issues and events.
  - 30 crashlytics_update_issue: Sets a Crashlytics issue to OPEN or CLOSED.
  - 31 crashlytics_setup: Returns setup instructions for Crashlytics in web apps.
  - 32 realtimedatabase_get_data: Reads the data at a path in the Realtime Database.
  - 33 realtimedatabase_set_data: Writes JSON data to a path in the Realtime Database.
  - 34 dataconnect_build: Compiles the SQL Connect schema, operations and connectors and returns the build errors.
  - 35 dataconnect_list_services: Lists the local and deployed SQL Connect services.
  - 36 dataconnect_execute_in_emulator: Runs a GraphQL operation against a local SQL Connect emulator and returns the result.
  - 37 firestore_query_collection: Queries the documents of a collection, with optional filters and ordering.
  - 38 functions_get_logs: Returns Cloud Functions log entries from Cloud Logging, with filters.
  - 39 functions_list_functions: Lists the deployed Cloud Functions.

  - 46 firestore_update_document: Updates a document.

The main branch is at 1.2.3-wip (dart-lang/ai commit 7162376, 2026-11-19); its generated tools table is identical to 1.2.2, and … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: the pub package dart_mcp_server (the Dart and Flutter MCP server). Newest release 1.2.2, 2026-10-27. It exposes Dart and Flutter development tools to an agent: analysis, pub, tests, and live connections to running apps through the Dart Tooling Daemon (DTD). It runs over stdio, started as `dart mcp-server`. The dart-flutter plugin in flutter/agent-plugins starts the same server (entry "dart-mcp-server", command dart, args ["mcp-server"]) in its Claude, Cursor and Codex manifests. The Flutter docs name only this server as part of the official tooling; they also point to Google's Developer Knowledge MCP server for documentation search, which is published by Google Developers, not by the Flutter or Dart project.
- Number of tools: dart_mcp_server 1.2.2: 24 tools. Count of the registerTool calls in lib/src/mixins: analyzer 2, dtd 8, flutter_launcher 5, dash_cli 4, pub 1, pub_dev_search 1, grep_packages 1, package_uri_reader 1, roots_fallback_support 1 (the registerTool definitions in analytics.dart and server.dart are overrides, not tools). The generated README tools table also has 24 rows. Disabled by default (README …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (dart_mcp_server 1.2.2), with the descriptions from the generated README table.
  - 1. analyze_files: analyzes the given paths, or the whole project, with the analysis server, including custom_lint plugins, and returns the errors.
  - 2. lsp: runs Language Server Protocol commands (hover, signatureHelp, resolveWorkspaceSymbol) and returns docs and types at a position, signature help, or symbols that match a fuzzy name query.
  - 3. dtd: manages Dart Tooling Daemon connections with the commands listDtdUris, connect, listConnectedApps and disconnect, and returns DTD URIs and the connected apps with their VM Service URIs.
  - 4. get_runtime_errors: returns the most recent runtime errors of the connected running app.
  - 5. get_active_location: returns the current active location, such as the cursor position, in the connected editor (off by default).
  - 6. hot_reload: hot-reloads the connected Flutter app and returns the result.
  - 7. hot_restart: hot-restarts the connected Flutter app, which resets app state, and returns the result.
  - 8. widget_inspector: runs widget inspector commands (get_widget_tree, get_selected_widget, set_widget_selection_mode) and returns the widget tree or the selected widget.
  - 9. flutter_driver_command: runs a Flutter Driver command on the running app (tap, enter_text, scroll, waitFor, get_text, get_diagnostics_tree, screenshot and others) and returns the driver's response, or a PNG image for screenshot.
  - 10. vm_service: connects to or disconnects from an app by its VM service URI, calls VM service methods, or lists the services that clients registered, and returns the result.
  - 11. launch_app: launches a Flutter app and returns its DTD URI (off by default).
  - 12. stop_app: kills a Flutter process that launch_app started (off by default).
  - 13. list_devices: returns the available Flutter devices (off by default).
  - 14. get_app_logs: returns the collected logs of a flutter run process that launch_app started (off by default).
  - 15. list_running_apps: returns the process IDs and DTD URIs of the apps that launch_app started (off by default).
  - 16. dart_fix: runs `dart fix --apply` in the given project roots and returns the output (off by default).
  - 17. dart_format: runs `dart format .` in the given project roots and returns the output (off by default).
  - 18. run_tests: runs Dart or Flutter tests with output made for agents and returns the results (off by default).
  - 19. create_project: creates a new Dart or Flutter project (off by default).
  - 20. pub: runs a pub command, such as `dart pub get` or `flutter pub add`, in the given project roots and returns its output.
  - 21. pub_dev_search: searches pub.dev for a query and returns up to 10 packages, each with its latest version, description, links, library doc URLs, scores, topics, licenses and publisher.
  - 22. rip_grep_packages: finds patterns in the package dependencies with ripgrep, which must already be installed, and returns the matches.
  - 23. read_package_uris: reads files or lists directories at package: and package-root: URIs in the dependencies and returns their contents (text, or image content for image files).
  - 24. roots: adds or removes project roots (commands add and remove).
- Search, kind `keyword`: (1) pub_dev_search. Input: `query` (string), which accepts pub.dev search expressions such as "exact phrase", dependency:, topic:, publisher:, sdk:, runtime:, updated: and has:executable. The tool calls https://pub.dev/api/search?q=<query> and keeps the first 10 package names (`.take(_resultsLimit)`). For each package it then fetches api/packages/<name>, api/packages/<name>/score and documentation/<name>/latest/index.json. One result is a JSON object with packageName, latestVersion, description, homepage, repository, documentation, libraries (doc URLs), scores (pubPoints, maxPubPoints, likes, downloadCount), topics, licenses and publisher. The order is pub.dev's search order, so the ranking runs on pub.dev, a server of the project. The source does not name the ranking method beyond "freeform keyword search". (2) lsp with command resolveWorkspaceSymbol. Input: `query`. A fuzzy search of symbols by name, run by the local Dart analysis server on the user's machine. (3) rip_grep_packages runs ripgrep pattern matching over the dependencies on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: flutter_driver_command, command screenshot: returns a PNG image of the running app's screen as MCP image content (the format defaults to '4' /*png*/). The user can only view the image; there is no interactive view. It needs a running Flutter app that imports flutter_driver's driver_extension and calls enableFlutterDriverExtension() before runApp, a DTD or VM Service connection, and so a local `flutter run` process. read_package_uris also returns image content when the URI points to an image file in a dependency; that is a file read, not a rendered view. No tool names a ui:// resource.
- Prompts and resources: Prompts: one, flutter_driver_user_journey_test. It prompts the model to carry out a user journey in the running app with Flutter Driver and then write those steps as a Flutter Driver test (argument user_journey). Resources: one dynamic resource for each connected app, with URI runtime-errors://<vmServiceId> and name 'Errors for app <name>', which returns the recent runtime errors of that app. There are no resource templates. The server also sends instructions: hot reload after changes, connect to DTD first, and use read_package_uris and rip_grep_packages for dependencies. The README does not list the prompt; it is declared in code.
- Number of skills: 25 skills in github.com/flutter/agent-plugins/skills/<name>/SKILL.md: 10 flutter-* and 15 dart-*. The plugin dart-flutter ships them for Claude, Codex and Cursor; the Flutter docs also install them with `npx skills add flutter/agent-plugins` and `npx skills add dart-lang/skills`. The 15 dart-* skills also live in github.com/dart-lang/skills/skills (same 15 folders). Four of them …

CLI commands: dart analyze, dart fix --dry-run and --apply, dart format, dart test, and dart pub / flutter pub commands (dart-resolve-package-conflicts, …

I unpacked the published tarball and read dist/mcp/*.js; the server calls itself 'Genkit MCP', title 'Genkit MCP Server', version '0.0.2'. For comparison I also read … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server, 'Genkit MCP' (title 'Genkit MCP Server', server version 0.0.2). It is the `genkit mcp` subcommand of the npm package genkit-cli (newest 1.45.0, 2026-11-02), runs over stdio and is marked experimental. It is for looking up the Genkit docs and usage guide, managing the local Genkit runtime, finding and running flows, and reading traces.
- Number of tools: 10 (genkit mcp in genkit-cli 1.45.0), counted from the registration code in the published package: registerTool calls in dist/mcp/docs.js (3), flows.js (2), trace.js (1) and usage.js (1), plus runtime.js (start_runtime directly, and the registerControlTool helper called twice, for kill_runtime and restart_runtime). The unreleased main branch (commit 9a7d0b6) has 9: it no longer has usage.ts …
- Tools:
  - From the registration code in the published genkit-cli 1.45.0 (dist/mcp):
  - 1. get_usage_guide: returns the bundled Genkit usage guide (project setup and API best practices) for js or go; language is optional and auto-detected. For other languages it returns text telling the agent to use the docs tools instead.
  - 2. list_genkit_docs: lists the Genkit documentation files for one language (js, go, python, dart; auto-detected by default) and returns text with each FilePath, Title and Description.
  - 3. search_genkit_docs: searches one language's docs by keywords (query, optional language) and returns up to 10 ranked results, each with title, FilePath and description.
  - 4. read_genkit_docs: takes an array of filePaths from the list or search tools and returns the full markdown text of each document.
  - 5. list_flows: lists the flows of the running Genkit runtime and returns each flow's name, description and JSON input schema.
  - 6. run_flow: runs a named flow with a JSON-string input against the running runtime and returns the response as JSON.
  - 7. get_trace: returns the full execution trace (spans, inputs, outputs, errors) for a traceId, as JSON text.
  - 8. start_runtime: starts the user's app as a Genkit runtime process from a command and args (e.g. npm run dev) and returns 'Done.' or an error.
  - 9. kill_runtime: kills the runtime that start_runtime started and returns 'Done.'.
  - 10. restart_runtime: restarts the runtime that start_runtime started and returns 'Done.'.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool: search_genkit_docs. Inputs: query (string of keywords) and language (optional: js, go, python or dart; auto-detected from the project by default). One result: the doc's title, FilePath and description (top 10 results). Ranking: searchDocs lowercases the query and splits it on whitespace, drops terms of 2 characters or fewer and the stop words and/the/for, then adds substring-match scores per term: title +10, description +5, headers +3, file path +5. It drops results that score 0 and sorts the rest by score, highest first. No embedding model or language model is used. The ranking runs on the user's machine, over a docs bundle downloaded from https://genkit.dev/docs-bundle-experimental.json (overridable with GENKIT_DOCS_BUNDLE_URL) and cached in ~/.genkit/docs/<version>/bundle.json for one week.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Every tool returns text content only: no ui:// resource and no image. (start_runtime says the runtime 'will be picked up by the `genkit start` command to power the Dev UI', but no tool returns that UI.)

  - 1. init: fetches primer.style/product/getting-started/react and returns it as Markdown with a checklist for setting up a project with @primer/react, ThemeProvider/BaseStyles, a @primer/primitives theme, octicons and agent instructions.
  - 2. list_components: returns the names of all @primer/react components (from @primer/react/generated/components.json).
  - 3. get_component: returns the llms.txt documentation of exactly one component from primer.style/product/components/<slug>/llms.txt.
  - 4. get_component_batch: returns the llms.txt documentation of 2 to 10 components in one call, with an in-band not-found or fetch-error entry per failed name.
  - 5. get_component_examples: returns the component's primer.style docs page converted to Markdown as usage examples.
  - 6. get_component_usage_guidelines: returns the component's /guidelines page from primer.style as Markdown.
  - 7. get_component_accessibility_guidelines: returns the component's /accessibility page from primer.style as Markdown.
  - 8. list_patterns: returns the names of Primer patterns, split into scenario patterns and UI patterns.
  - 9. get_pattern: returns the primer.style page of one scenario or UI pattern as Markdown.
  - 10. find_tokens: searches the design tokens of @primer/primitives by keywords and/or group and returns matching tokens with value, use case and rules (default limit 15).
  - 11. get_token_group_bundle: returns all tokens of an array of token groups (e.g. overlay, shadow) with usage hints.
  - 12. get_design_token_specs: returns the token logic matrix, the list of valid token groups and the DESIGN_TOKENS_GUIDE.md of @primer/primitives.
  - 13. get_token_usage_patterns: returns 'Golden Example' CSS for Button (interactions) and Stack (layout) showing token, motion and spacing use.
  - 14. lint_css: runs `npx stylelint --stdin --fix` on the given CSS and returns the Stylelint output or remaining errors.
  - 15. get_color_usage: returns primer.style color-usage foundation guidelines as Markdown.
  - 16. get_typography_usage: returns primer.style typography foundation guidelines as Markdown.
  - 17. list_icons: returns all Octicons with their keywords and available sizes.
  - 18. get_icon: returns the primer.style docs page of one Octicon at a given size (default 16).
  - 19. primer_coding_guidelines: returns fixed text with Primer coding rules (prefer tokens, Primer components, icons and patterns; no sx prop, no Box for styling; use CSS Modules).
  - 20. review_alt_text: evaluates image alt text against accessibility practice and the surrounding text by asking the client's model through an MCP sampling request (inputRequired.createMessage), and returns the evaluation with next steps (marked experimental in source).
  - @primer/brand-mcp 0.81.0 (8):
  - 1. primer_brand_setup: detects or takes the framework (next-app, next-pages, vite, astro, remix) and returns install, root ThemeProvider, fonts and styles setup steps, and adds or updates a Primer Brand pointer in AGENTS.md of the package that declares @primer/react-brand.
  - 2. primer_brand_page_design: returns page-composition guidance (header/footer, hero media, gridlines, card grids) and current-brand reference templates from bundled content/page-design.md.
  - 3. primer_brand_component: without a name lists all Primer Brand components; with a name returns its import, sub-components, props with allowed values and a canonical Storybook example (on an unknown name, suggests up to 5 close names).
  - 4. primer_brand_examples: returns ranked, tested component examples (JSX and CSS) for a goal, plus a full-page recipe source for page goals (default set Hero, SectionIntro, River, Pillar, CTABanner).
  - 5. primer_brand_tokens: searches Primer Brand design tokens by intent words and optional group and returns CSS variables with values.
  - 6. primer_brand_asset: searches Octicons and Octovisuals by name and returns import statements.
  - 7. primer_brand_docs: searches the Primer Brand docs index (bundled with the installed @primer/react-brand, else primer.style/brand llms.txt) or reads one doc by path.

One result: token name, value, use case (U) and rules (R), grouped by token group. Ranking: no ranking; a filter where every query keyword must be a substring of name + useCase + rules + group (logical AND), over tokens loaded from the installed @primer/primitives; runs on the user's machine. (The docs page says 'Finds Primer design tokens by intent or value', but the code matches words.) @primer/brand-mcp: primer_brand_docs (query or path; result: label, path, description, up to 25), primer_brand_tokens (query, group, limit 1-50 default 15; result: var(name) = value (group); query words expanded by a fixed synonym map, e.g. red->danger), primer_brand_asset (query, kind icon|illustration, limit 1-50 default 12; result: name, kind, import line), and primer_brand_examples (goal); primer_brand_component also uses rank() for 'Did you mean' suggestions on an unknown name.   - search_docs: searches the Handsontable and HyperFormula knowledge base (guides, API reference, HyperFormula guides, code recipes from the skills, release notes, GitHub issues, blog posts) for a query. It returns ranked page-level snippets, each with a url when a public page exists, and reports which product versions the knowledge base covers.
  - hyperformula-calc (from the registering code):
  - calc_formulas: evaluates an array of Excel-compatible formulas against a dataset given as CSV, a 2D JSON array or, in the local stdio server, a local .xlsx/.xls/.csv file. It returns one result for each formula in order and can write an .xlsx with output_file in the local server.
  - calc_groupby: groups rows of a dataset with a header row by one column and computes SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MIN, MAX or MEDIAN for each group. It returns one row for each group.

#### Highcharts
Checked: highcharts 13.1.1 (npm, newest; registry modified 2026-10-20); @highcharts/react 5.4.0 (published 2026-10-12); highcharts/highcharts-skills at commit 10af685a89a9 (2026-10-29); highcharts/highcharts master at aebdd38 (2026-11-20) for the contributor skills; … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: Three official hosted remote HTTP servers from Highsoft. None of them is an npm package, and none has public source code: the highcharts GitHub organisation has no MCP repository. (1) Highcharts Dev Assist, https://mcp.highcharts.ai/developers/mcp. It searches the docs and runnable examples, recommends a chart type and validates a config. (2) Highcharts Chart Chooser (also written Chartchooser), https://chartchooser-mcp.highcharts.ai/mcp. It takes a pasted dataset and returns a chart type or dashboard, a data story, accessibility and production-ready HTML; a 2026-11 post documents it in Claude and ChatGPT. (3) Highcharts Render, https://mcp.highcharts.ai/export/mcp. It renders a Highcharts config to a PNG. None of the three publishes a version number. The Dev Assist serverInfo value 'highsoft-docs 3.4.7' from the lead was not checked, because connecting to a server was not allowed. The intro of the MCP page says 'Two', but the page lists three endpoints. Third-party servers that a web search finds (hasnaintypes/highchart-mcp-server, austenstone/mcp-highcharts) are not official.
- Number of tools: Dev Assist: 5. Render: 1. Chart Chooser: not confirmed. All counts come from the documentation, in a Highcharts blog post (a guest post by a Highcharts support engineer), because no registering code is public.
- Tools:
  - Source: documentation only (no public code). The Chart Chooser tools are not listed, so the list is complete only for Dev Assist and Render.
  - Dev Assist:
  - search_docs: searches the official Highcharts documentation, including the Morningstar connector docs, and returns passages that each carry their source URL, e.g. '--- Result 1 (source: https://www.highcharts.com/docs/morningstar/dws/asset-allocation-breakdown) ---'.
  - search_snippets: searches runnable Highcharts code examples that match a use case.
  - recommend_chart: takes a description of the data and an objective (for example 'comparison') and recommends a chart type.
  - get_chart_type_info: returns details and use-case guidance for one chart type, including the data format it expects.
  - validate_config: takes a Highcharts configuration as a JSON string and checks it against the official schema (tree.json). It returns a status and one warning line for each unknown option, and the status can still read as valid when there are warnings.
  - Render:
  - render_chart: takes a Highcharts configuration as an object, with optional width, height and scale, and returns an export-quality PNG image.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: Tools: search_docs and search_snippets on Dev Assist. They take a query; the exact input field names are not documented. A search_docs result is a documentation passage with its source URL. The ranking method, model or index is not documented. The search runs on a Highsoft server, because Dev Assist is a hosted endpoint at mcp.highcharts.ai.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: render_chart (Highcharts Render): the user sees a static PNG of the chart in the conversation and cannot interact with it. It needs no local process, because rendering runs on the hosted server. Chart Chooser asks five discovery questions through an 'elicitation UI', which shows clickable options in the host, and returns an HTML file. Whether it uses MCP Apps (ui:// resources) or the OpenAI Apps SDK is not confirmed.
- Prompts and resources: Chart Chooser declares at least one prompt: in Claude, the user adds 'the Chartchooser prompt' to the chat. Its name is not documented. No prompts or resources are documented for Dev Assist or Render. Full declarations are not confirmed, because no code is public and connecting was not allowed.

#### IBM Carbon Design System
Checked: Carbon MCP v1.14.0 (newest GitHub release of carbon-design-system/carbon-mcp, released 2026-09-30, marked Latest, "Carbon MCP has officially launched!"); carbon-builder skill version 1.3.1 (SKILL.md frontmatter at repo HEAD c8af755, 2026-10-30). Checked … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: Carbon MCP, a hosted remote server at https://mcp.carbondesignsystem.com/mcp (streamable HTTP, IBMid OAuth sign-in, or token and session ID for clients without OAuth), newest release v1.14.0 of 2026-09-30. Purpose: gives AI agents Carbon components, icons, charts and documentation, and checks code against Carbon guidelines. The server source is not public; the repository carbon-design-system/carbon-mcp holds README, terms, support, workflows and public/ assets (carbon-builder skill and zip, Figma Make kit, llms.txt, hero images) only.
- Number of tools: 5 (Carbon MCP). Source: documentation (README Tools table and the Concepts page on carbondesignsystem.com); the code that registers the tools is not public. The carbon-builder SKILL.md lists the same five tools in allowed-tools.
- Tools:
  - From the documentation (README Tools table, Concepts page) and the skill's capability matrix and references; registration code is not public.
  - 1. code_audit: validates code (one file via `code`, or `files[]` up to 50) against Carbon guidelines for design tokens, component usage, accessibility, layout and best practices; returns compact JSON with valid, total, sev (severity counts), cat (category counts) and issues[] (with msg, fix, line and an optional autoFix {orig, repl, scssImports}).
  - 2. code_search: searches Carbon React and Web Components code examples (incl. Carbon for IBM Products and AI Chat examples), icons and pictograms; returns component_id, component_type, imports[], variants[] (with props and Storybook links), or for icons import, import_stmt, usage[] and available_sizes[], or AI Chat example files (doc_id, example_root, example_files[], code).
  - 3. docs_search: searches Carbon Design System and IBM Products documentation (usage, accessibility, reference; AI Chat docs); returns documentation chunks with page_url, anchor_url, component_id, page_type, section_heading, chunk_text, last_crawled_at.
  - 4. get_charts: returns Carbon Charts code for React, Angular, Vue, Svelte, Vanilla JS and HTML for a framework and chart_type, by mode; returns tool_policy, chosen_variant, available_variants[], source_files[] and assembly hints (install_command, styles_import).
  - 5. labs_search: searches Carbon Labs experimental components (@carbon-labs/*); returns component_name, package_name, framework, variants[], props[], install_command, import_hint, usage_hint.
- Search, kind `keyword`: code_search: inputs query, size, filters {component_type, component_id, ibm_products, asset_type, variant_id}; one result is a component (component_id, component_type, imports[], variants[]) or an icon (import, import_stmt, usage[], available_sizes[]) or an AI Chat example file. docs_search: inputs query, size, filters {component_id, page_type}; one result is a documentation chunk (page_url, anchor_url, section_heading, chunk_text, page_type, last_crawled_at). labs_search: inputs query, framework, limit; one result is a Labs component (component_name, package_name, variants[], props[], install_command). Ranking: Elasticsearch text matching with field boosts (description boost 7 for AI Chat examples; icon index scores on name, kebab, aliases, displayName fields). No embedding model is named in the sources read. Ranking runs on the project's hosted server on IBM Cloud, not on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none: all five documented tools return JSON text; no ui:// resource or image result is documented in the README, the Concepts page or the skill.
- Prompts and resources: not confirmed: the README, Concepts page and skill do not mention MCP prompts or resources, and the server source is not public; the server was not connected to (read-only rule).
- Number of skills: 1: carbon-builder, at public/skills/carbon-builder/ in carbon-design-system/carbon-mcp (also carbon-builder.zip in public/skills and as a release asset on v1.14.0; install via `npx skills add https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-mcp/tree/main/public/skills/carbon-builder -g -a <agent>`). Left out: the Figma Make kit file public/figma-make-kit/skill/carbon-builder-figma-make-react.md …

  - carbon-builder: Carbon Design System expert for React and Web Components; an agent uses it for Carbon components, IBM Products UI, Carbon Charts, icons and pictograms, design tokens and IBM Plex, usage and accessibility docs, AI Chat / watsonx integration, or any Carbon code generation.
- What the skills point at: The skill points the agent to the Carbon MCP server tools code_search, docs_search, get_charts, labs_search and code_audit (MCP-First Rule), and to its own bundled reference files (references/*.md). It tells the agent to run get_charts' assembly.install_command (only when it installs @carbon/* packages) and limits CDN use to the IBM CDN 1.www.s81c.com. No CLI of the project and no installed-package path is used as a fact source.

#### Ignite UI (Infragistics)
