- MCP servers: Two official stdio MCP servers. (1) @igniteui/mcp-server 16.0.0 (bin igniteui-mcp; mcpName io.github.IgniteUI/mcp-server; server name "igniteui-mcp-server"): documentation, API reference, import paths and project setup guidance for Angular, React, Web Components and Blazor, from a bundled SQLite docs database. It also starts through the CLI with `npx -y igniteui-cli mcp` or `ig mcp`, which spawns the same package (a dependency of igniteui-cli). The CLI's ai-config writes it under the key "igniteui-cli". Source: igniteui-cli monorepo, packages/igniteui-mcp/igniteui-doc-mcp. (2) igniteui-theming 30.2.0 (bins igniteui-theming and igniteui-theming-mcp, both dist/mcp/index.js; server name "igniteui-theming"): generates Sass or CSS theming code (palettes, typography, elevations, themes, component themes, layout scales). The CLI's `ai-config` writes both servers into the MCP configuration.
- Number of tools: @igniteui/mcp-server 16.0.0: 7 tools (counted from the server.registerTool calls in src/index.ts; the published dist/index.js registers the same 7). igniteui-theming 30.2.0 MCP: 15 tools (counted from the server.registerTool calls in registerTools() of the published dist/mcp/server.js). The package description of @igniteui/mcp-server names "GitHub API, and CLI scaffolding", but the source …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (doc server: src/index.ts and src/tools/constants.ts; theming server: dist/mcp/server.js and dist/mcp/tools/descriptions.js).
  - @igniteui/mcp-server (7):
  - list_components: browses the component documentation index for one framework, grouped by the documentation table of contents, with filter, group and detail options; returns doc names (to pass to get_doc) with group or doc summaries.
  - get_doc: returns the full markdown of one doc by its kebab-case name (with alias and fuzzy resolution), as YAML frontmatter (component, package@version, keywords, summary) and the body with code samples.
  - search_docs: full-text search over one framework's docs; returns up to 20 results, each with doc name, display name, summary and a highlighted excerpt.
  - get_project_setup_guide: returns project setup guide text for a framework (Ignite UI CLI setup and templates for Angular, React, Web Components; dotnet new and NuGet steps for Blazor); read-only, it does not create files or run commands.
  - get_api_reference: returns the API reference of one component or class by exact name (Package line, summary, properties, methods, events), optionally one section or one member.
  - search_api: keyword search over API entries of all four frameworks; returns up to 10 results with component name, framework, API type, package@version, match count, keywords and an excerpt.
  - resolve_import: returns ready-to-paste import statements (package and entry point; for Blazor the NuGet package, @using namespace and module registration) for up to 50 symbols, with "Did you mean" suggestions.
  - igniteui-theming MCP (15):
  - detect_platform: reads the project's package.json and config files and returns the detected platform (angular, webcomponents, react, blazor, generic) with confidence scoring.
  - create_palette: generates a full color palette (shades 50-900, A100-A700) from base colors with the palette() Sass function, as Sass or compiled CSS custom properties.
  - create_custom_palette: generates a palette from hand-given shade values for each color, as Sass or CSS.
  - create_typography: generates typography setup (typography() mixin) for a font family and design-system type scale.
  - create_elevations: generates the elevation shadow setup (elevations() mixin, levels 0-24) for the Material or Indigo preset.
  - create_theme: generates a complete theme (palette, typography, elevations, optional spacing, theme mixin) in one operation.
  - set_size: returns CSS/Sass that sets --ig-size globally or for one component or scope.
  - set_spacing: returns CSS/Sass that sets --ig-spacing (and optional inline/block overrides) globally or for one component or scope.
  - set_roundness: returns CSS/Sass that sets --ig-radius-factor globally or for one component or scope.
  - get_component_design_tokens: returns the list of themeable design tokens of one component with types and descriptions.
  - create_component_theme: generates Sass or CSS that customizes one component with given token values and an optional selector.
  - get_color: returns a CSS variable reference to a palette color (shade, contrast, opacity).
  - get_chart_series_colors: returns the shared chart series brush palette and per-chart-type token guidance, and validates custom brush lists.
  - fit_color_scale: derives a shade-scale spec from an existing color ladder, to pass to create_palette or create_theme.
  - read_resource: returns one theming resource by URI (platform configs, palette, typography and elevation presets, color guidance, layout docs).
- Search, kind `keyword`: search_docs: inputs query (string; trailing * prefix match, hyphenated terms as phrases) and framework (angular|react|blazor|webcomponents). One result: doc name, display name, summary, and an excerpt with hits between >>> and <<<; up to 20 results (from up to 200 FTS rows). Ranking: SQLite FTS4 MATCH (sql.js, WebAssembly) on the docs_fts table of the bundled docs database, then a field-weighted re-rank (title +10, keywords +5, filename +4, summary +3 per term). Runs on the user's machine by default; with `--remote <url>` the server instead calls a docs backend at /api/docs/search. search_api: inputs query (max 256 chars) and optional platform. One result: component name, framework, API type, package@version, match count, keywords, excerpt; up to 10. Ranking: in-process word-boundary regex matching of each term against content, keywords, component name and type, sorted by the number of matched terms; runs on the user's machine. No embedding or language model.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. All tools of both servers return text content; no tool names a ui:// resource or returns an image (no ui:// or image content type in either published dist).
- Prompts and resources: @igniteui/mcp-server: 1 prompt, igniteui-usage-guide (instructions on framework detection and which doc, API and setup tool to use); no resources. igniteui-theming MCP: no prompts; 28 resources (scheme theming://), registered from RESOURCE_DEFINITIONS: theming://platforms (supported platforms), platforms/angular, platforms/webcomponents, platforms/react, platforms/blazor, platforms/generic (platform configs); presets/palettes, presets/palettes/light, presets/palettes/dark (palette presets); presets/typography (typography presets); presets/elevations (elevation presets); guidance/platform-setup (platform setup guide); guidance/colors, guidance/colors/rules, /usage, /roles, /states, /themes, /charts, /scales (color guidance); presets/chart-brushes (chart series brush palettes); docs/spacing-and-sizing, docs/functions/pad, docs/functions/sizable, docs/functions/border-radius, docs/mixins/spacing, docs/mixins/sizing, docs/mixins/sizable (layout docs). The same resources are readable through the read_resource tool.
- Number of skills: 22 distinct consumer skills: 5 in the igniteui-angular 22.3.0 npm package (package/skills/), 5 in igniteui-react 19.11.0 (package/skills/), 8 in igniteui-webcomponents 7.5.0 (package/skills/), and 4 Blazor skills bundled in igniteui-cli 16.0.0 under templates/blazor/igb/projects/ai-config/files/skills/. igniteui-cli 16.0.0 also bundles copies of the 5 React and 8 Web Components skills …

#### Laravel
Checked: laravel/boost v2.10.4 (tag commit 9cd5e7d, 2026-10-30), the newest tag on github.com/laravel/boost on 2026-11-20; main at 6004f09 (2026-11-14) registers the same ten tool classes, one resource and five prompts The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: laravel/boost (Composer dev dependency, https://github.com/laravel/boost), newest release v2.10.4 of 2026-10-30. It is a local stdio server that runs inside the user's Laravel app through Artisan (server class Laravel\Boost\Mcp\Boost, name 'Laravel Boost'). It gives the agent live access to the app (database, logs, errors, URLs, optionally Tinker) and a hosted documentation search.
- Number of tools: laravel-boost: 10 tool classes in the code that registers the tools (discoverTools() of src/Mcp/Boost.php). With the default config the server exposes 9: Tinker registers only when boost.tinker_tool_enabled is true, and that defaults to false; record-rule registers only while boost.rules.enabled is true, which is the default. Users can also drop or add tools with boost.mcp.tools.exclude and …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (src/Mcp/Tools/*.php at v2.10.4). Each tool name is the kebab-case of its class name: laravel/mcp Primitive::name() falls back to Str::kebab(class_basename($this)), and no tool class sets a #[Name] or $name.
  - 1. browser-logs: reads the last N entries of the browser log (input: entries), for debugging the frontend and JavaScript, and returns the log lines.
  - 2. database-connections: lists the database connection names that the app configures, and returns those names.
  - 3. database-query: runs a read-only SQL query (SELECT, SHOW, EXPLAIN or DESCRIBE) on a database connection, which defaults to the app's default connection, and returns the rows.
  - 4. database-schema: reads the database schema, with options summary, database, filter, include_column_details, include_views and include_routines, and returns table names, columns, indexes and foreign keys.
  - 5. get-absolute-url: turns a relative path or a named route into an absolute URL, or returns the URL of '/' when it gets no argument.
  - 6. last-error: returns the details of the last error or exception that the app's backend logged.
  - 7. read-log-entries: reads the last N entries of the application log, handles multi-line PSR-3 and JSON logs, and returns those entries.
  - 8. record-rule: writes a durable project rule into the committed markdown notes in .ai/rules, grouped by a file glob (inputs: a glob, a heading and the rule text); agents call it only when the user explicitly asks for a rule. Registered while boost.rules.enabled is true (default).
  - 9. search-docs: sends queries (with optional packages and token_limit) and the installed package versions to the hosted Laravel documentation API, and returns version-specific documentation as markdown.
  - 10. tinker: runs PHP code in the app's context, like artisan tinker, and returns the output. Registered only when boost.tinker_tool_enabled is true (default false).
- Search, kind `intent`: Tool search-docs. Inputs: queries (an array of strings; you can pass several wordings), packages (optional Composer or npm package names), token_limit (3,000 by default, at most 1,000,000). The tool adds each installed PHP and JS package with its major version ('<major>.x') and POSTs {queries, packages, token_limit, format: 'markdown'} to https://boost.laravel.com/api/docs (the config key is boost.hosted.api_url). It returns the response body as text: markdown documentation for the installed versions, cut to the token limit. The ranking runs on a Laravel-hosted server, not on the user's machine. The docs call it semantic search with embeddings over 'over 17,000 pieces of Laravel-specific information'. The sources do not name the embedding model or the index.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Every tool returns text or data. None names a ui:// resource and none returns an image.
- Prompts and resources: Resources (1): application-info at URI file://instructions/application-info.md, which gives the PHP version, the Laravel version, the database engine and all installed packages with their versions (name from the kebab-case class-name rule of laravel/mcp). Prompts (5, declared in discoverPrompts()): laravel-code-simplifier, which simplifies and refines PHP/Laravel code without changing what it does and focuses on recently changed code; upgrade-ai-sdk-v1, step-by-step guidance to upgrade the Laravel AI SDK from 0.11 to 1.0; upgrade-inertia-v3, from Inertia v2 to v3; upgrade-laravel-v13, from Laravel 12.x to 13.0; upgrade-livewire-v4, from Livewire v3 to v4. The upgrade prompts register only when the project matches (for example upgrade-laravel-v13 only for Laravel >=12.0.0 <13.0.0; upgrade-livewire-v4 only when Livewire is installed).
- Number of skills: 15 distinct skills in 22 SKILL files, all inside the laravel/boost package under .ai/<package>/[<major>/]skill/<name>/ (SKILL.md or SKILL.blade.php). Several have one variant for each major version or edition: fluxui-development (free, pro), inertia-react/svelte/vue-development (v1, v2), livewire-development (v2, v3, v4) and tailwindcss-development (v3, v4). The Boost CLI copies into the user's …

  - 1. infer-conventions: analyzes how a Laravel app is written and records its conventions as shared rules in .ai/rules through the record-rule tool; the agent uses it only when the user explicitly asks.
  - 2. deploying-to-cloud: deploys and manages Laravel apps on Laravel Cloud with the `cloud` CLI; the agent uses it for deploys, environments, databases, domains, billing and Cloud infrastructure.

  - 7. inertia-vue-development: the same for Vue pages, forms and navigation with Inertia.
  - 8. laravel-best-practices: best practices for writing, reviewing or refactoring Laravel PHP code (controllers, models, queries, N+1, caching, security, queues).

#### Mantine
Checked: @mantine/mcp-server 9.8.2 (npm dist-tag latest; registry time.modified 2026-11-20T12:07:36.544Z), read from the published tarball. Skills: mantinedev/skills at commit 607846dbc328b6ddc85106d8aad3c080f9f57a1d, 2026-10-04, "Update skills for Mantine 9.7 (#2)" … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: One official server: npm @mantine/mcp-server, version 9.8.2 (2026-11-20). It is a stdio MCP server for the Mantine documentation. It fetches static JSON data (index.json, sections.json, docs/<id>.json) from https://mantine.dev/mcp, which MANTINE_MCP_DATA_URL can override, with a timeout set by MANTINE_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS (default 10000). Its source is in mantinedev/mantine at packages/@mantine/mcp-server. The docs page https://mantine.dev/guides/llms/ documents it.
- Number of tools: @mantine/mcp-server 9.8.2: 5. Counted from the code that registers the tools (esm/tools.mjs, five server.registerTool calls, built from packages/@mantine/mcp-server/src/tools.ts). The README and the docs page https://mantine.dev/guides/llms/ list the same five.
- Tools:
  - From the code that registers the tools (esm/tools.mjs):
  - 1. search_docs: searches all the Mantine documentation (components, hooks, @mantine/form, styling, theming, guides, FAQ) for a free-text query, with optional kind, package and limit filters. It returns ranked JSON matches, and a match can point to one section of a page.
  - 2. get_item_doc: returns the documentation of one component, hook, guide or FAQ page by name or id. By default it returns an outline (the description and a list of sections); with section it returns that part, and with full:true the whole page. When nothing matches, it returns an error with name suggestions.
  - 3. get_item_props: returns the props of a component or the TypeScript signature of a hook. Pages that document an API in prose point to the relevant section instead.
  - 4. list_items: lists documentation items, filtered by kind, nav group, category, package or a text query (default 30, max 500).
  - 5. get_api: resolves a symbol such as useForm, useDisclosure or UseFormReturnType to its TypeScript signature and exported types, without knowing which page documents it.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool search_docs. Inputs: query (string, free text, e.g. "validate a form with zod"), kind (optional enum component | hook | guide | faq), package (optional, e.g. "@mantine/form"), limit (optional, default 20, max 100). One result holds id, name, kind, package, route, docsUrl, description, and, for a section hit, section (slug), heading and snippet, plus score. Ranking: the query is tokenized; tokens of two characters or fewer and stopwords are removed. Each page (searchText) and each section (heading + snippet) gets an IDF-weighted token-coverage score (substring match), plus bonuses for an exact, prefix or contained match of the name or heading. Page and section hits are merged and sorted by score. There is no embedding or language model. Failed lookups in the other tools suggest names by edit distance (suggestNames). Where it runs: on the user's machine, in the local server process, over index.json and sections.json fetched from https://mantine.dev/mcp and cached (index revalidated every 300000 ms).
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: none. The server code calls only registerTool. No registerPrompt or registerResource appears in esm/ or cjs/ (grep found none).
- Number of skills: 3, in the separate GitHub repository mantinedev/skills under skills/ (each skill also has references/api.md and references/patterns.md). All three are for consumers; the repository has no contributor skills. Install: npx skills add https://github.com/mantinedev/skills --skill <name>. The docs page https://mantine.dev/guides/llms/ lists the same three.
- Skills:
  - 1. mantine-combobox: builds custom dropdown, select, autocomplete or multiselect components with the Combobox primitives. Use it for a searchable dropdown, a multi-select or tags input, custom option rendering or filtering, or any task with useCombobox, Combobox.Target, Combobox.Option or Combobox.Dropdown.
  - 2. mantine-form: builds forms with @mantine/form. Use it for useForm setup, validation rules, schema validation (zod, valibot, arktype) or async validation, nested object or array fields, createFormContext, controlled or uncontrolled mode, form.useWatchValue, the standalone useField hook, getInputProps, onSubmit or insertListItem.
  - 3. mantine-custom-components: builds custom components that integrate with Mantine theming, the Styles API and core features. Use it for factory(), polymorphicFactory() or genericFactory(); Styles API support (classNames, styles, vars, unstyled); CSS variables through createVarsResolver; compound components; registration through Component.extend(); or Factory, useProps, useStyles, BoxProps, StylesApiProps or ElementProps.
- What the skills point at: Each skill first points to its own reference files (references/patterns.md, references/api.md). For facts beyond those files, each points to the MCP server @mantine/mcp-server: search_docs and get_item_doc (combobox, form), and also get_api (custom-components). The fallback is the web address https://mantine.dev/llms.txt, and the combobox skill adds https://mantine.dev/combobox/. No skill names a CLI command or a path in an installed package.
- Not confirmed: Whether the mantinedev/mantine monorepo source at master differs from the 9.8.2 tarball was not checked; the record rests on the published build.

  - 3. startMastraCourse - registers the user by email with https://mastra.ai/api/course/register if needed (storing device credentials locally) and starts or resumes the interactive Mastra course, returning the lesson step text.
  - 4. getMastraCourseStatus - returns the user's course progress (lessons and steps completed) and a status URL https://mastra.ai/course/<deviceId>.
  - 5. startMastraCourseLesson - starts or resumes a named lesson at its first incomplete step and returns that step's content.
  - 6. nextMastraCourseStep - marks the current step complete and returns the next step (or next lesson) content.
  - 7. clearMastraCourseHistory - with confirm=true deletes the local course progress file and returns a confirmation.
  - 8. getMastraHelp - takes projectPath, lists installed @mastra packages that have embedded docs, and returns a guide to the server's local, remote and course tools.
  - 9. listMastraPackages - takes projectPath and returns the @mastra/* packages (from a fixed list of 14) installed under node_modules that ship dist/docs.
  - 10. getMastraExports - reads a package's dist/docs/assets/SOURCE_MAP.json and returns its exports (optionally filtered by name) with source file locations.
  - 11. getMastraExportDetails - returns the TypeScript type definition (about 50 lines) of one export and optionally lines of its implementation source from node_modules.
  - 12. readMastraDocs - lists the topics of a package's embedded dist/docs, or returns all Markdown files of a topic, or one file.
  - 13. searchMastraDocs - case-insensitive substring search of a query across the embedded dist/docs Markdown of installed packages; returns up to maxResults (default 10) excerpts with file paths, sorted by occurrence count.
  - Note: getMastraHelp's text also names mastraBlog, mastraExamples and mastraChanges, which are not registered in 1.3.15.
- Search, kind `keyword`: searchMastraDocs: inputs query (string, case-insensitive), package (optional), maxResults (optional, default 10), projectPath (absolute, required). It walks every .md file under node_modules/@mastra/<pkg>/dist/docs of the installed packages, keeps files that contain the whole query as a lowercase substring, and takes as excerpt the first matching line with 1 line before and 2 after (max 300 chars). One result holds package name, file path relative to dist/docs, excerpt; score = number of occurrences of the query in the file; results sorted by score. No embedding model, index or library; runs on the user's machine. Secondary keyword ranking in mastraDocs and mastraMigration (queryKeywords, array of words): getMatchingPaths/searchDocumentContent scans bundled .docs Markdown line by line, score = totalMatches + 3*titleMatches + 2*pathRelevance + 5*distinct keywords + 10 if all keywords match; returns the top 10 paths; runs locally. The hosted kapa endpoint (https://mastra.mcp.kapa.ai) has, per kapa.ai docs, a retrieval tool search_<PRODUCT_NAME>_knowledge_sources running on kapa's servers; its exact name and ranking for Mastra were not confirmed.

Resources: none declared (serverConfig has only name, version, tools and prompts).

- Skills:
  - meteor-accounts: Use it to set up authentication in a Meteor 3 app: accounts-password, OAuth providers, 2FA, passwordless login, email verification, and token storage compared with HttpOnly cookies.
  - meteor-blaze: Use it to build or debug Meteor 3 Blaze interfaces: Spacebars, helpers and events, Tracker and ReactiveVar, Promise helpers, Blaze.render, blaze-hot HMR, reactivity lost after await, and template errors.
  - meteor-cli-installation: Use it to install, locate, repair, reset or uninstall the Meteor CLI: 'meteor: command not found', npx meteor, PATH problems, specific versions, and meteor reset.
  - meteor-community-packages: Use it to choose, evaluate, adopt, configure or debug a package from Meteor's documented community catalog, or to move to a promoted core package such as roles.
  - meteor-debugging: Use it to diagnose an unexplained failure in a Meteor 3 app before the failing layer is known: server crashes, client errors, stuck subscriptions, DDP disconnects, flaky tests, and slow builds.
  - meteor-deployment: Use it to deploy a Meteor 3 app: meteor build, meteor deploy and Galaxy, Docker or Kubernetes, settings.json, environment variables (MONGO_URL, ROOT_URL), and Node version matching.
  - meteor-methods: Use it to write or debug Meteor methods: Meteor.methods and callAsync, argument checks with check(), optimistic UI stubs, Meteor.Error, and DDPRateLimiter.
  - meteor-modern-build-stack: Use it to configure or tune the Meteor 3 modern build stack: the SWC transpiler and minifier, @parcel/watcher, .meteorignore, and the Rspack integration (rspack.config.js, Meteor.* config helpers).
  - meteor-mongo-minimongo: Use it to write or debug Mongo queries in Meteor 3: async queries on the server compared with synchronous Minimongo on the client, oplog compared with change streams, indexes, selectors, and modifiers.
  - meteor-native: Use it to build or maintain Meteor 3 Android and iOS apps through Cordova: add-platform, mobile-config.js, plugins, signing and store artifacts, and mobile hot code push.
  - meteor-pubsub: Use it to write or debug publications and subscriptions: publication strategies, the low-level added/changed/removed API, cursor authorization, reactive joins, and leaked documents.
  - meteor-react: Use it to build or debug React interfaces in Meteor 3: the scaffold, Rspack and Fast Refresh, react-meteor-data hooks (useTracker, useSubscribe, useFind), and Suspense.
  - meteor-security: Use it to audit or harden a Meteor 3 app: check() coverage, this.userId guards, browser-policy CSP, DDPRateLimiter rules, oauth-encryption, and allow/deny patterns.
  - meteor-testing: Use it to set up, write or repair tests and test harnesses: meteortesting:mocha, testing methods and publications, --full-app mode, and Playwright or Cypress E2E tests.
  - meteor-typescript: Use it to set up or repair the app's type declarations, TypeScript or jsconfig settings, IntelliSense, and type-checks with tsc --noEmit, for example with meteor types, zodern:types or @types/meteor.
  - migrate-to-meteor-3: Use it to migrate a Meteor 2.x app to 3.x: callAsync, async Mongo, the removal of Fibers, lost Blaze reactivity, Express 5 WebApp handlers, and Atmosphere package resolution.
  - migrate-to-rspack: Use it to migrate an existing Meteor app to Rspack (Meteor 3.4+), or to move from Rspack 1 to 2 on Meteor 3.6: nested imports, replacements for build plugins, CommonJS interop, and CI or Docker builds.

- MCP servers: One official, public MCP server: Fluent UI Blazor MCP Server, NuGet package Microsoft.FluentUI.AspNetCore.McpServer (MCP registry name io.github.microsoft/fluentui-blazor-mcp, stdio, runtimeHint dnx, command fluentui-mcp), newest version 5.1.0 (published 2026-11-16). The React repository microsoft/fluentui (master 254b9070, 2026-11-20), microsoft/fluentui-system-icons and microsoft/fluentui-contrib hold no MCP server: a list of all files in each repository has no MCP server source; fluentui-contrib has only a .vscode/mcp.json for contributors. - Number of tools: Fluent UI Blazor MCP Server 5.1.0: 20 tools. Counted from the code that registers them: 20 methods with [McpServerTool] in 7 classes ([McpServerToolType]) under src/Tools/McpServer/Tools, all registered by WithToolsFromAssembly(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly()). The server README tool table lists only 13 tools; it leaves out the 4 icon tools and 3 of the 4 tools in MigrationTools.cs …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (v5.1.0). The attributes give no names, so the C# MCP SDK 2.4.0 makes each name from the method name in snake_case (AIFunctionMcpServerTool.DeriveName, JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower). The README and the docs site use the PascalCase method names (for example ListComponents). Every tool returns Markdown text.
  - 1. list_components: lists all components with names and short descriptions, grouped by category, with an optional category filter.
  - 2. search_components: finds components whose name, summary or documentation text contains the search term, and returns name, category and summary for each.
  - 3. list_categories: lists the component categories, for use as the filter of list_components.
  - 4. get_component_details: returns the full documentation of one component: usage guide, code examples, parameters, events and methods (input componentName; the 'Fluent' prefix is optional).
  - 5. get_enum_values: returns one enum type with all its values, with an optional filter on the values.
  - 6. get_component_enums: lists the enum types that one component uses and the property or parameter that uses each.
  - 7. list_enums: lists all enum types of the library.
  - 8. list_documentation: lists the documentation topics (installation, migration, localization, styles and others).
  - 9. get_documentation_topic: returns the full documentation of one topic by name or route.
  - 10. search_documentation: finds documentation topics whose title, content or summary contains the keyword.
  - 11. get_migration_guide: returns the migration documentation for the upgrade to v5.
  - 12. search_icons: finds Fluent UI icons by name or keyword, with synonyms (for example 'trash' to Delete), and optional variant and size filters.
  - 13. get_icon_details: returns all variants (Filled, Regular, Light, Color) and sizes of one icon.
  - 14. get_icon_usage: returns ready-to-use Blazor code snippets for one icon (basic render, color, button slots, click handler, accessibility attributes) for a given variant and size.
  - 15. list_all_icon_names: lists all icon names, optionally filtered by a prefix, grouped by first letter.
  - 16. get_migration_overview: returns the general v4-to-v5 migration overview (CSS bundling, JavaScript interop, ToAttributeValue() changes); the description says to call it first.
  - 17. list_component_migrations: lists the components that have a v4-to-v5 migration guide, each with a short summary.
  - 18. get_component_migration: returns the v4-to-v5 migration guide of one component: renamed, removed and new properties, appearance changes and code examples.
  - 19. get_version_info: returns the MCP server version and the recommended Microsoft.FluentUI.AspNetCore.Components package version and PackageReference.
  - 20. check_project_version: compares the version in the user's .csproj (input projectVersion) with the server version and reports COMPATIBLE or INCOMPATIBLE, with the risks and the upgrade command.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Three search tools. All run on the user's machine in the local server process, against data embedded in the package; the README says 'No network access - Runs entirely offline'. (1) search_components, input searchTerm. It matches the term as a case-insensitive substring of the component name or summary in the generated API JSON (FluentUIDocumentationService.SearchComponents), and of the raw Markdown or title of the component documentation (ComponentDocumentationService.SearchDocumentation). It merges the two sets and sorts them alphabetically by name; there is no relevance ranking. Each result holds the component name (with <T> if generic), its category and its summary. (2) search_documentation, input searchTerm. Case-insensitive substring match on the title, content or summary of the documentation topics that are not hidden, sorted by the topic's Order field. (3) search_icons, inputs searchTerm, optional variant and optional size. Substring match on the icon names, plus a hand-made synonym table (IconSynonymService) with exact and partial key matches, then filters by variant and size; results are capped at MaxResults. Its description tells the agent: 'If no results are found, call ListAllIconNames to retrieve the full icon catalog and perform your own fuzzy/semantic term matching'. No embedding model, language model or search index is used.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: Fluent UI Blazor MCP Server 5.1.0 declares 15 prompts and 14 resources, taken from the code (registered by WithPromptsFromAssembly and WithResourcesFromAssembly). All resources are text/markdown. Prompts: implement_accessibility (accessibility guidance); compare_components (compares two or more components to choose one); configure_localization (translating component strings); configure_theming (themes, colors and design tokens); create_datagrid (code for a FluentDataGrid with sorting and pagination); create_dialog (a modal dialog with DialogService); create_drawer (a side drawer with DialogService); create_form (a form with validation and data binding); explain_component (explains one component); find_icon (finds the best icon for a purpose); use_icon (Blazor code that uses one icon in several contexts); migrate_to_v5 (v4-to-v5 migration guidance); setup_project (setting up a new project step by step); suggest_components (components for a use case); troubleshoot_issue (rendering, styling and behavior problems). Resources (name, URI): components (fluentui://components, all components by category); enums (fluentui://enums, all enum types); component (fluentui://component/{name}, documentation of one component); category (fluentui://category/{name}, the components of one category); enum (fluentui://enum/{name}, one enum type with its values); documentation (fluentui://documentation, the list of documentation topics); documentation-topic (fluentui://documentation/{topic}, one topic); migration (fluentui://documentation/migration, the complete v5 migration guide); icons (fluentui://icons, an overview of the icon catalog); icon_variants (fluentui://icons/variants, a guide to icon variants and sizes); icon_details (fluentui://icon/{name}, one icon with its variants, sizes and snippets); migration-overview (fluentui://migration/overview, the v4-to-v5 overview); migration-components (fluentui://migration/components, the list of component migration guides); migration-component (fluentui://migration/components/{component}, the migration guide of one component). The README also lists fluentui://categories, but no [McpServerResource] in the v5.1.0 source declares it.

- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools at tag v3.3.0 (packages/tools-*/src/index.ts arrays, names from `static toolName`), checked against the README and the docs page.
  - Database tools (25):
  - aggregate - runs an aggregation pipeline against a collection and returns the result documents.
  - aggregate-db - runs an aggregation pipeline against a database and returns the results.
  - collection-indexes - returns the indexes of a collection, including vector and lexical search indexes.
  - collection-schema - returns a schema of a collection inferred from sampled documents.
  - collection-storage-size - returns the storage size of a collection.
  - connect - connects to a MongoDB instance and returns a connectionId for the other tools.
  - count - returns the number of documents in a collection that match an optional filter.
  - create-collection - creates a collection, and the database if it does not exist.
  - create-index - creates an index on a collection, including vector and lexical search indexes.
  - db-stats - returns usage statistics for one database.
  - delete-many - deletes all documents that match a filter and returns the deleted count.
  - disconnect - closes a connection and revokes its connectionId.
  - drop-collection - drops a collection or view and its indexes.
  - drop-database - drops a database and deletes its data files.
  - drop-index - drops an index from a collection.
  - explain - returns the winning query plan and execution statistics for a find, aggregate or count.
  - export - exports query or aggregation results as EJSON to a file, which the exported-data resource then serves.
  - find - runs a find query against a collection and returns the documents.
  - insert-many - inserts an array of documents into a collection.
  - list-collections - lists the collections of a database.
  - list-connections - lists the active connections and their connectionIds.
  - list-databases - lists the databases of a connection.
  - mongodb-logs - returns the most recent logged mongod events.
  - rename-collection - renames a collection.
  - update-many - updates all documents that match a filter and returns the counts.
  - Atlas tools (22):
  - atlas-list-clusters - lists the Atlas clusters.
  - atlas-list-projects - lists the Atlas projects.
  - atlas-inspect-cluster - returns the metadata of one Atlas cluster.
  - atlas-create-free-cluster - creates a free Atlas cluster.
  - atlas-create-access-list - adds IP or CIDR ranges to the project access list.
  - atlas-inspect-access-list - returns the IP and CIDR ranges that have access.
  - atlas-list-db-users - lists the Atlas database users.
  - atlas-create-db-user - creates an Atlas database user.
  - atlas-create-project - creates an Atlas project.
  - atlas-list-orgs - lists the Atlas organizations.
  - atlas-connect-cluster - connects to an Atlas cluster and returns a connectionId, creating a temporary database user when needed.
  - atlas-list-alerts - lists the triggered alerts of a project, OPEN by default.
  - atlas-get-performance-advisor - returns Performance Advisor suggested indexes, drop-index suggestions, schema suggestions and up to 50 slow query logs.
  - atlas-get-regions - returns the supported Atlas regions of a cloud provider.
  - atlas-load-sample-dataset - starts loading a sample dataset into a cluster, or returns the status of a load by jobId.
  - atlas-create-cluster - creates a dedicated M10-M80 cluster with autoscaling and returns at once.
  - atlas-pause-resume-cluster - pauses or resumes a dedicated M10+ cluster.
  - atlas-streams-discover - lists and inspects Stream Processing workspaces, connections and processors and diagnoses them.
  - atlas-streams-build - creates Stream Processing workspaces, connections, processors or PrivateLink.
  - atlas-streams-manage - starts, stops and modifies processors and updates workspaces and connections.
  - atlas-streams-teardown - deletes Stream Processing resources after safety checks.
  - atlas-upgrade-cluster - upgrades Free or Flex clusters, or scales a dedicated cluster and its autoscaling.
  - Atlas Local tools (4):
  - atlas-local-create-deployment - creates a local Atlas deployment in Docker (preview image by default).
  - atlas-local-list-deployments - lists the local Atlas deployments.
  - atlas-local-delete-deployment - deletes a local Atlas deployment.
  - atlas-local-connect-deployment - connects to a local deployment and returns a connectionId.
  - Assistant tools (2):
  - list-knowledge-sources - lists the data sources and versions of the MongoDB Assistant knowledge base, for use as search filters.
  - search-knowledge - searches the MongoDB Assistant knowledge base (official docs and curated expert guidance) and returns results as YAML, each with url, title, text chunk and metadata tags.
  - Total: 53. (Remote-only, not in the local code: remote-atlas-connect - connects to an Atlas cluster on the Remote MCP Server and returns a connection handle; from the docs.)
- Search, kind `intent`: Tool: search-knowledge. Inputs: `query` (a string, a natural-language question or topic); `limit` (1-100, default 5); `dataSources` (optional array of {name, versionLabel}, whose values come from list-knowledge-sources). One result holds url, title, text ("The text of the page chunk returned from the search") and metadata {tags, ...}. The tool returns the results as YAML, wrapped as untrusted data. Where the ranking runs: on a server of MongoDB. The user sees the list of databases. The code does not show which actions the view offers beyond display. It works only with the preview feature `mcpUI` (--previewFeatures mcpUI). It uses MCP-UI (@mcp-ui/server createUIResource): the tool result carries an embedded `ui://list-databases` rawHtml resource, with the data as initial-render-data. The tool does not name the view in its `_meta` (its toolMeta holds only transport and payload-size keys), as the MCP Apps format does. The HTML is bundled into the server package, so the view needs no dev server or other local process.

#### Motion (motion.dev)

- MCP servers: Two official hosted HTTP servers, both closed source. (1) 'motion' (named 'Motion' in the Cursor plugin mcp.json) at https://mcp.motion.dev: free, needs no account, searches docs and example metadata, opens the insert panel and generates CSS easing. (2) 'motion-plus' (named 'Motion+' in the Cursor plugin mcp.json) at https://mcp.motion.dev/plus: the editor signs in to it separately. A free Motion account is enough for saving a transition; a Motion+ account unlocks premium example and Motion UI source, the fully open insert panel, the transition editor (MCP App) and the MotionScore/Performance Doctor audit methodology and report card. Neither server has its own version number. The newest kit release is CHANGELOG 7.0.1 (2026-10-15) and the newest installer is npm motion-ai 14.2.0 (2026-10-15). The installer configures the free server, and `--plus` also adds the Motion+ server.
- Number of tools: From the documentation, because the server code is not public. The skill file codex/index.md names 3 tools on 'motion' and 4 on 'motion-plus'; performance-audit/index.md names 2 more on the Motion+ server. Count: motion = 3; motion-plus = 6. transition-preview/index.md also names 2 tools, visualise-spring and visualise-cubic-bezier, that the 'Motion AI Kit additionally ships' and that 'are not …
- Tools:
  - Source: documentation (the SKILL.md sub-files in motiondivision/ai-kit), because the server code is not public.
  - Server 'motion' (3):
  - search-motion-docs: takes { platform: js|react|vue, searchTerm } and returns adaptation rules plus resource links: up to 3 docs (motion://docs/{platform}/{id}), up to 5 examples (motion://examples/{platform}/{id}), Motion UI items (motion://ui/react/{id}) and the signed-in user's saved transitions as JSON. Gated items come as metadata only: title, description, APIs, MotionScore grade and a demo link.
  - insert-motion-component: takes { platform, query } and opens Motion's insert panel (MCP App) of Motion UI components, sections and examples, with live previews and MotionScore grades. Free examples are open and Motion+ items show as locked. In hosts without MCP Apps it returns the matches as resource_links.
  - generate-css-easing: takes { kind: spring|bounce, duration, bounce } and returns the `<duration> <easing>` half of a CSS transition, with a linear() easing that samples a spring or bounce.
  - Server 'motion-plus' (6):
  - search-motion-source: takes { platform, searchTerm } and returns resource_links that resolve to complete paste-ready source of Motion+ examples and Motion UI. For Motion UI that is every file, with its transitive dependencies and the theme.
  - insert-motion-plus-component: takes { platform, query } and opens the same insert panel with every item open; each pick reads paste-ready source.
  - save-transition: saves a transition to the user's Motion account (the skill names the tool but gives no input or return).
  - open-transition-editor: takes { name, property, transition } and opens the transition editor inline (live preview, curve, sliders). On Apply, the tuned transition comes back as a new message. Hosts without MCP Apps get the transition as text.
  - open-performance-report: takes the audit findings and opens the Performance Doctor report card, with a Fix button on each finding. Hosts that cannot show it get a numbered list.
  - update-performance-report: reports the progress of each fix, so the card shows Fixing, Fixed or Rolled back.
  - Not attributed to a server: visualise-spring and visualise-cubic-bezier, which 'render a curve as a PNG for hosts that display images inline'.
- Search, kind `keyword`: search-motion-docs (on 'motion') and search-motion-source (on 'motion-plus'). Inputs: platform (required, exactly one of "js", "react", "vue") and searchTerm (required, at least 2 characters). The tool strips the words animate, animation, animations and animated, and a query of only those words returns "too generic". A result of search-motion-docs holds adaptation rules, then MCP resource links: up to 3 docs, then up to 5 examples, then Motion UI items (react only), then the signed-in user's saved transitions as JSON. Gated items come as a metadata block: title, description, APIs, MotionScore grade and a public demo link. search-motion-source returns resource_links to complete source. Ranking is fuzzy and typo-tolerant; the source names no model, index or library. It runs on Motion's hosted server (mcp.motion.dev).
- User interface from a tool, kind `mcp-apps`: - open-transition-editor (Motion+): an inline editor with a live preview, the easing or spring curve and sliders for the values (delay control added in 7.0.0). The user tunes the transition and presses Apply, and the transition comes back to the agent as a new message. Saving to the profile is a separate feature (save-transition). It needs only a host that renders MCP Apps (skill: 'Cursor 2.6 and later'), with no local process. - open-performance-report (Motion+): the Performance Doctor report card, with findings and a Fix button on each; per the performance-doctor docs the user can also Fix all, Undo, Try again and Copy prompt, and each request goes back to the agent as a message. update-performance-report updates each finding's state. The card needs no dev server, but a runtime audit that feeds it runs `npx motionscore <url> --agent` locally against a running page. - insert-motion-component / insert-motion-plus-component: the insert panel of Motion UI components, sections and examples, with live previews and MotionScore grades. The user picks one, and the pick arrives as a new message. On the free server, Motion+ items are locked. Hosts named: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor 2.6 and later, VS Code. It needs no local process. The ui:// resource URIs are not named in the sources. visualise-spring and visualise-cubic-bezier return PNG images; the server that carries them is not confirmed.
- Prompts and resources: Resources, from the skill files: - motion://docs/{platform}/{id}: one Motion docs page. Every docs page is a resource and free to all. - motion://examples/{platform}/{id}: an example. Source is gated to Motion+. - motion://ui/react/{id}: a multi-file Motion UI component or section, with its dependencies and motion.theme.ts. - motion://skills/performance-audit (Motion+ server): the MotionScore audit methodology, which the agent must read before an audit. - motion://motionscore/grades: added to the skill in commit b36715b (2026-07-28) and removed in the next commit 7e7207f ('the grade system lives in the authenticated methodology only'); its current status on the server is not confirmed. The docs tools call the hosted backend https://chat-backend.mui.com (MUI_DOCS_BASE_URL). Code generation calls https://chat-backend.mui.com (MUI_RECIPES_BACKEND_BASE_URL) and needs MUI_RECIPES_API_KEY, which is exchanged for a JWT at https://api.mui.com (MUI_BACKEND_BASE_URL).

The published tarball has the same 3 registerTool calls (codegen/register.js 1, docs/register.js 2). useMuiDocs is registered only after the docs catalog loads, announced through …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (packages/x-agent-tools/src/docs/tools.ts, src/codegen/tools.ts and src/codegen/schemas.ts).
  - 1. useMuiDocs: takes `sources` (llms.txt URLs, or package names such as "@mui/x-data-grid", or name@version). It fetches the llms.txt file of each package and returns its content as a string, the docs catalog of page URLs (resolved to absolute URLs) with their summaries. The tool description lists the available packages and versions, read from the backend catalog /v1/public/packages/list.
  - 2. fetchDocs: takes `urls` (an array). It fetches those documentation pages and returns their content joined and converted to markdown, or an error message. Only MUI documentation origins are allowed.
  - 3. generateReactCode: takes `prompt`, plus optional `threadId`, `designContext` (a Figma frame or an opaque payload), `muiPairing` (the Material UI and MUI X major versions) and `model`. It generates React + Material UI code on MUI's hosted recipes backend and returns { threadId, files[{filename, contents}], explanation, muiPairing? } as structuredContent, also rendered as markdown text. It needs MUI_RECIPES_API_KEY.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none. The server has no search tool. The agent picks a package from the list in the useMuiDocs description, reads that package's llms.txt index, and then passes page URLs to fetchDocs. No tool takes a query. The only matching in the code is a name-similarity hint for an unknown package (suggestPackageNames: a substring check after normalization, at most 5 names), which runs on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool names a ui:// resource or returns an image. The docs tools return one text block; generateReactCode returns text plus structuredContent. Its input can carry an optional Figma thumbnailDataUrl, but that is input only.
- Prompts and resources: none. The source (packages/mcp/src) and the published tarball of @mui/mcp 0.1.10 have no registerPrompt or registerResource call. There are only 3 registerTool calls.

Each folder has SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, README.md, metadata.json (version 1.0.0, muiVersion ">=9.0.0 <10.0.0") and reference.md. Not counted, because they serve contributors: .agents/skills/material-ui-review and mui-release in …

  - 2. material-ui-theming: guides Material UI theming and design tokens (createTheme, ThemeProvider, palette, colorSchemes, cssVariables, theme.vars, dark mode, TypeScript augmentation); the agent uses it when it builds or extends a theme, toggles light/dark or aligns tokens.
  - 3. material-ui-nextjs: integrates Material UI with the Next.js App and Pages routers (@mui/material-nextjs, Emotion cache providers, next/font, CSS layers, Link, App Router useSearchParams + Suspense); the agent uses it when it sets up or debugs MUI in a Next.js app.

#### Neon (serverless Postgres and its drivers)
Checked: MCP server: hosted remote server com.neon/mcp version 2.0.0 (package.json of neondatabase/mcp-server-neon, main at commit a7c1158, 2026-11-19), with its tools from @neon/tools 2.17.1 (pinned; npm latest is @neon/tools 2.18.0, modified 2026-11-20T03:53Z, not … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: the Neon MCP Server, a remote, hosted Streamable HTTP server at https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp (registry name com.neon/mcp), version 2.0.0 (repo main a7c1158, 2026-11-19), source at github.com/neondatabase/mcp-server-neon. It is for managing Neon projects, branches, computes, Postgres databases and roles, SQL, migrations, Neon Auth, Data API, Functions, Object Storage, Realtime and logs, and for searching the Neon docs. The old local npm package @neondatabase/mcp-server-neon (last 0.6.5) is deprecated in favour of the remote server.
- Number of tools: 141 tools (Neon MCP Server 2.0.0). Source: the code that registers the tools: mcp/tools/operations.ts builds TOOL_IDS from CUSTOM_TOOL_GRANTS and GENERATED_TOOL_SCOPES; mcp/tools/mcp-tool-names.json maps 141 operation ids to 141 distinct published names; app/api/[transport]/route.ts registers each with server.registerTool. One connection sees fewer when filtered by grant category, project scope, …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (names from mcp/tools/mcp-tool-names.json in mcp-server-neon; descriptions from the published @neon/tools 2.17.1 package, dist/descriptions.gen.js, dist/lib/custom/*.js and dist/lib/ergonomic/*.js, which the server passes through in mcp/tools/definitions.ts). 141 tools:
  - add_auth_oauth_provider: Adds a social login provider (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Vercel, Apple, Discord) to a branch's Neon Auth.
  - add_auth_trusted_domain: Adds a domain a branch's Neon Auth may redirect to after sign-in.
  - compare_database_schema: Diffs one database's SQL schema on a branch against another branch, by default its parent, and returns the diff.
  - complete_database_migration: Applies or discards a prepared migration and deletes the temporary branch.
  - complete_query_tuning: Applies or discards query-tuning changes and deletes the temporary branch.
  - count_projects: Counts an organization's active projects without listing them.
  - create_auth_oauth_client: Registers an OAuth client with a branch's Neon Auth OAuth server and returns a confidential client's secret once.
  - create_auth_user: Creates a Neon Auth user on a branch who can sign in right away.
  - create_branch: Creates a branch from its parent's current data, with a read-write compute unless no_compute, and waits until it is ready (no connection string).
  - create_credential: Issues a scoped credential on a branch, returning api_token and s3_secret_access_key once.
  - create_postgres_database: Creates a database on a branch, owned by owner_name.
  - create_postgres_endpoint: Creates a compute endpoint on a branch (one read-write, any number read-only).
  - create_postgres_role: Creates a Postgres role on a branch and returns its password.
  - create_project: Creates a project with a default branch and read-write compute and waits until it is ready.
  - create_snapshot: Creates a snapshot of a branch.
  - create_storage_bucket: Creates an object storage bucket on a branch.
  - create_trigger: Creates a trigger that calls a function on a five-field UTC cron schedule, or after an upload to one bucket.
  - delete_auth_oauth_client: Deletes an OAuth client from Neon Auth's OAuth server, irreversibly.
  - delete_auth_oauth_provider: Removes a social login provider from a branch's Neon Auth.
  - delete_auth_trusted_domain: Removes a domain from the ones a branch's Neon Auth may redirect to.
  - delete_auth_user: Deletes a Neon Auth user from a branch.
  - delete_branch: Deletes a branch with all its data and disconnects its clients.
  - delete_data_api: Deletes the Neon Data API for a database.
  - delete_function: Deletes a function from a branch.
  - delete_functions_custom_domain: Removes a custom domain from a branch and stops routing it.
  - delete_postgres_database: Deletes a database and its data from a branch.
  - delete_postgres_endpoint: Deletes a compute endpoint and drops its connections.
  - delete_postgres_role: Deletes a Postgres role from a branch.
  - delete_project: Deletes a project with all its branches, computes, databases, and roles.
  - delete_snapshot: Deletes a snapshot.
  - delete_storage_bucket: Deletes a bucket from a branch.
  - delete_storage_object: Deletes one object from a bucket on a branch.
  - delete_storage_objects_by_prefix: Soft-deletes every object on the branch whose key starts with a prefix and returns the count.
  - delete_trigger: Deletes a function trigger, or hides an inherited one on this branch.
  - deploy_function: Deploys a function version from any of zip, environment, and runtime.
  - describe_branch: Returns a branch summary, its database names, and a tree of one database's schemas, tables, views, indexes, sequences, and functions.
  - describe_project: Gets a project's settings, owner, and usage.
  - describe_table_schema: Returns a table's columns, indexes, constraints, and sizes.
  - disable_auth: Disables Neon Auth on a branch.
  - disable_realtime: Disables Realtime on a branch, discarding its secret, and waits until it is applied.
  - enable_realtime: Enables Realtime on a branch, or changes its allowed origins, and waits until it is applied.
  - explain_sql_statement: Returns a statement's execution plan as JSON.
  - fetch: Returns an organization, project, branch, compute, or snapshot by an id from search: markdown text, console URL, and records in metadata.
  - finalize_branch_restore: Finalizes a restored branch by moving the original branch's computes onto it and taking over its name.
  - get_ai_gateway: Gets a branch's AI Gateway host.
  - get_auth: Gets a branch's Neon Auth integration record: provider, base URL, JWKS URL, and database.
  - get_auth_oauth_client: Gets an OAuth client of a branch's Neon Auth OAuth server, without its secret.
  - get_auth_oauth_server: Gets a branch's Neon Auth OAuth 2.1 server settings (oauth_provider plugin).
  - get_branch: Gets a branch record: name, parent, state, protection, size, and timestamps.
  - get_branch_consumption: Returns per-branch consumption metrics for project_ids.
  - get_connection_string: Returns a Postgres connection string with a role password.
  - get_data_api: Gets the Neon Data API configuration for one database on a branch.
  - get_database_tables: Lists a database's tables and views outside the system schemas.
  - get_default_branch: Gets the project's default branch by its default flag.
  - get_doc: Returns one neon.com page as markdown, by the slug of a search_docs hit.
  - get_function: Gets a function on a branch by slug.
  - get_neon_auth_config: Returns a branch's Neon Auth integration and settings: trusted origins, localhost, email and password, OAuth and email providers, plugins, webhook, and logs export.
  - get_operation: Gets one operation and its status.
  - get_postgres_database: Gets a database on a branch and its owner.
  - get_postgres_endpoint: Gets a compute endpoint (ep-...), including its host and state.
  - get_postgres_role: Gets a Postgres role on a branch.
  - get_project_consumption: Returns per-project consumption in an organization.
  - get_realtime: Gets a branch's Realtime state, URL, and allowed origins.
  - get_realtime_secret: Gets the secret the application backend issues Realtime tokens with.
  - get_snapshot_schedule: Gets a branch's automatic snapshot schedule.
  - get_storage: Checks whether object storage is available on a branch.
  - get_trigger: Gets a function trigger on a branch.
  - inspect_database: Runs one read-only neon inspect db check (for example outliers, lfc-hit-rate, working-set) and returns its result.
  - list_auth_oauth_clients: Lists the OAuth clients (apps, MCP clients) of a branch's Neon Auth OAuth server, without secrets.
  - list_auth_oauth_providers: Lists the social login providers of a branch's Neon Auth.
  - list_auth_trusted_domains: Lists the domains a branch's Neon Auth may redirect to after sign-in.
  - list_branch_computes: Lists a branch's compute endpoints.
  - list_branches: Lists a project's branches with id, name, parent, and default flag.
  - list_credentials: Lists the scoped credentials issued on a branch, without secrets.
  - list_functions: Lists the functions on a branch.
  - list_functions_custom_domains: Lists a branch's custom domains and their targets.
  - list_incidents: Lists open Neon incidents and maintenance from neonstatus.com and the affected components and regions.
  - list_log_field_values: Lists the distinct values of one log field.
  - list_log_fields: Lists the low-cardinality log fields seen on a branch.
  - list_operations: Lists a project's operations.
  - list_organizations: Lists the organizations the user belongs to.
  - list_postgres_databases: Lists a branch's databases and their owners.
  - list_postgres_endpoints: Lists the compute endpoints of every branch in a project.
  - list_postgres_roles: Lists a branch's Postgres roles.
  - list_project_members: Lists organization members and their roles on an org-owned project.
  - list_project_permissions: Lists who has access to a project: each permission id, email, and grant date.
  - list_projects: Lists the projects in an organization, optionally filtered by name or id.
  - list_regions: Lists the regions you can create projects in.
  - list_slow_queries: Lists queries from pg_stat_statements, slowest mean execution time first.
  - list_snapshots: Lists a project's snapshots.
  - list_storage_buckets: Lists a branch's object storage buckets, inherited ones included.
  - list_storage_objects: Lists a bucket's objects on a branch, inherited ones included.
  - list_triggers: Lists a branch's function triggers, including inherited ones.
  - prepare_database_migration: Applies a schema change on a new temporary branch and returns a migration_id.
  - prepare_query_tuning: Runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE for a slow query on a new temporary branch and returns the plan, table schemas, and a tuning_id.
  - presign_storage_object: Returns a short-lived presigned PUT or GET URL for one object, with the headers to send.
  - provision_neon_auth: Enables Neon Auth on a branch and creates the neon_auth schema in its database.
  - provision_neon_data_api: Creates the Neon Data API, a REST interface over a database, on a branch.
  - query_logs: Returns a branch's log records, filtered by LogQL or structured filters.
  - query_loki_logs: Runs a LogQL range query on a branch's logs and returns Loki's response grouped by stream label.
  - recover_project: Recovers a project deleted in the last 7 days.
  - register_functions_custom_domain: Routes a domain you own to a function and returns the CNAME target.
  - reset_from_parent: Resets a branch to its parent's current state, discarding the branch's own changes.
  - reset_postgres_role_password: Sets a new random password for a Postgres role and returns it.
  - restart_postgres_endpoint: Restarts a compute endpoint by suspending and starting it.
  - restore_snapshot: Restores a snapshot into a new branch and waits until it is ready.
  - revoke_credential: Revokes a scoped credential.
  - rotate_auth_oauth_client_secret: Issues a new secret for a confidential OAuth client and returns it once.
  - rotate_credential: Replaces a scoped credential's secrets in place and returns them once.
  - rotate_realtime_secret: Replaces a branch's Realtime secret and waits until the old one stops working.
  - run_sql: Runs one SQL statement on a branch's database and returns its rows.
  - run_sql_transaction: Runs several SQL statements in one transaction and returns each one's rows.
  - search: Finds organizations, projects, branches, computes, and snapshots whose name or id contains the query, with ids for fetch.
  - search_docs: Searches neon.com docs, API reference, PostgreSQL tutorial, guides, FAQs, changelog, and blog and returns ranked pages with a slug for get_doc.
  - send_auth_test_email: Sends a test email through the branch's saved standard SMTP provider.
  - send_feedback: Sends anonymous feedback text to the Neon team.
  - set_default_branch: Makes a branch the project's default.
  - set_snapshot_schedule: Replaces a branch's automatic snapshot schedule.
  - start_postgres_endpoint: Starts a suspended compute endpoint.
  - suspend_postgres_endpoint: Suspends a compute endpoint, dropping its connections.
  - update_auth_allow_localhost: Sets whether a branch's Neon Auth accepts localhost origins.
  - update_auth_config: Sets the application name Neon Auth uses in its emails.
  - update_auth_email_and_password: Updates a branch's Neon Auth email and password sign-in.
  - update_auth_email_provider: Sets the email provider for Neon Auth's emails (Neon's shared sender or your SMTP).
  - update_auth_logs_export: Turns the export of a branch's Neon Auth events to Neon Platform logs on or off.
  - update_auth_oauth_client: Updates an OAuth client of Neon Auth's OAuth server.
  - update_auth_oauth_provider: Updates a social login provider on a branch's Neon Auth.
  - update_auth_oauth_server: Configures a branch's Neon Auth as an OAuth 2.1 server (oauth_provider plugin).
  - update_auth_plugins_magic_link: Updates the Neon Auth magic link plugin.
  - update_auth_plugins_organization: Updates the Neon Auth organization plugin.
  - update_auth_plugins_phone_number: Updates the Neon Auth SMS OTP plugin.
  - update_auth_user_role: Sets the roles of a Neon Auth user on a branch.
  - update_auth_webhooks: Replaces a branch's Neon Auth webhook configuration.
  - update_branch: Renames a branch, protects or unprotects it, or sets when it expires.
  - update_data_api: Updates the Neon Data API settings for a database and refreshes its schema cache.
  - update_function: Sets a function's display name.
  - update_postgres_database: Renames a database or changes its owner.
  - update_postgres_endpoint: Updates a compute endpoint's settings.
  - update_project: Updates a project's name, settings, default compute settings, or history retention.
  - update_snapshot: Renames a snapshot or changes when it expires.
  - update_trigger: Updates a function trigger.
- Search, kind `both`: (1) search: input `query` (string, min 3 chars, part of a name or id, or a compute endpoint host); result {results:[{id,title,url}]} (OpenAI search shape) for use with fetch; ranking: plain substring matching on name or id over Neon API list calls for projects, branches, endpoints, snapshots and organizations; runs on Neon's hosted MCP server against the Neon API. (2) search_docs: inputs `query` (1-500 chars), optional `categories` (docs, api, postgresql, guides, faqs, blog, changelog), optional `limit` (1-40, default 10); each hit holds title, url, slug, category, breadcrumb, heading, excerpt; the server POSTs to Neon's site search, a Neon Function at https://br-frosty-cell-a5smzg39-assistant.compute.c-1.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech/site-search (NEON_SITE_SEARCH_URL in lib/config.ts). Per Neon's own blog post (2026-10-26), that endpoint stores page chunks with embeddings (made through Neon AI Gateway) and tsvectors in Lakebase Postgres; common queries are answered from a cache of precomputed hybrid results (embedding search on a lakebase_ann index plus BM25 on a lakebase_bm25 index, merged with reciprocal rank fusion, then an LLM rerank); queries not in the cache are ranked by BM25 keyword search only, with no model call. The embedding and rerank model names are not stated. Both tools run on servers of the project, not on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. The OAuth consent and completion pages are web pages of the sign-in flow, not tool results.
- Prompts and resources: none. The server registers no prompts and no resources. The main authenticated route advertises the `resources` capability with listChanged false next to `tools`, but registers no resource; the docs-only route and mcp/server/index.ts declare only `tools`.
- Number of skills: 7 skills, in the neondatabase/agent-skills repository under skills/ (an identical copy under plugins/neon-postgres/skills/ for the neon-postgres plugin; also published as npm @neon/skills 3.0.10 and served at https://neon.com/docs/ai/skills/<name>/SKILL.md). Left out: evals/neon-postgres-egress-optimizer/.claude/skills/score-eval, a contributor eval skill.
- Skills:
  - neon: Overview of Neon's backend primitives around Lakebase Postgres (Auth, Object Storage, Functions, AI Gateway, Realtime); the start skill to choose Neon, set up the CLI or MCP server and follow the branch-first workflow, used when building an app or backend on Neon or when Neon or Lakebase Postgres is mentioned.
  - neon-postgres: Guides and best practices for Lakebase Postgres on Neon (connections, pooled vs direct, migrations, branching, autoscaling, scale-to-zero, restore, read replicas, egress optimization, Lakebase Search); used when the work is an existing DATABASE_URL, SQL, schema, inspect or search.
  - neon-auth: Adds authentication to a new app with Neon Auth (Managed Better Auth): sign-up, sign-in, OTP, magic links, organizations, OAuth, OAuth server for MCP, passkeys, MFA, trusted domains; used for 'add auth' or 'add login' and auth APIs in @neon/neon-js.
  - neon-realtime: Builds realtime, reactive apps and agents with live SQL queries on Lakebase Postgres; used when UI or agent state must update live from database rows, for optimistic mutations, or to replace polling.
  - neon-functions: Long-running serverless Node.js HTTP functions deployed onto a Neon branch with DATABASE_URL injected; used to host an API, streaming agent, WebSocket/SSE server, webhook handler, Discord bot, MCP server, or Function Triggers (cron, object-storage events).
  - neon-object-storage: S3-compatible object storage that branches with the database; used when a user wants buckets, file or blob storage, uploads or presigned URLs without a separate storage provider.
  - neon-ai-gateway: One API and one credential for LLMs and embedding models built into a Neon branch; used when a user wants to call an LLM, generate embeddings, add AI or an agent to an app, or route between model providers.
- What the skills point at: All four kinds. MCP server tools named in the skills: inspect_database, run_sql, explain_sql_statement, list_slow_queries, create_branch, describe_branch, list_branches, query_logs, query_loki_logs, list_log_fields, list_log_field_values, send_feedback, create_trigger, get_trigger, list_triggers, update_trigger, delete_trigger, get_auth_oauth_server, update_auth_oauth_server; server setup via `neon mcp`. CLI: neon init, neon mcp, neon skills update, neon deploy, neon env, neon claim, neon logs, neon functions, neon link, neon branches, neon auth, neon inspect db, neon connection-string. Files in the skill: references/*.md beside each SKILL.md (e.g. neon/references/logs-loki.md, …

#### NestJS
Checked: Skills: @nestjs/skills 0.1.1 (npm, published 2026-11-20T11:03:42Z; plugin.json 0.1.1), github.com/nestjs/agent-skills at commit 7f05f492c42b (2026-11-20T12:05:35+01:00). MCP server: NestJS Observe hosted MCP endpoint, no version number published; tool list as … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: One official MCP server: NestJS Observe MCP server at https://observe-api.nestjs.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, POST only, stateless; OAuth sign-in or a personal omcp_... bearer token, read-and-write or read-only; Pro plan and above). No version number or date published; checked as documented on 2026-11-20. Purpose: lets an agent query the production telemetry of the user's Observe projects (regressions per release, slow operations, error groups, traces, logs, jobs, SLOs, alerts, production rules) and set up a service. Not open source: the Observe SDK repo github.com/nestjs/observe holds no MCP server code; github.com/nestjs/mcp (@nestjs/mcp 0.0.4) is a module for building MCP servers in Nest apps, not a server for agents.
- Number of tools: 35 (Observe MCP server), counted from the documentation (server code is not public): 29 in the 'Available tools' table plus 6 under 'Setting up a service' (list_applications and 5 writing tools). docs.nestjs.com and observe.nestjs.com list the same 35 names. A read-only token is offered only the reading tools.
- Tools:
  - Source: documentation (server code not public).
  - list_projects - Lists every project the user is a member of, with team and application counts; used to resolve project ids.
  - get_project - Returns one project by id with the user's access level (read/write/admin) and subscription state.
  - search - Full-text search over the user's projects, applications, alert rules, SLOs and issues.
  - get_context_pack - Returns a ~2,500-token brief of one project to load before editing (busiest routes and jobs, hot methods, failing or slow outbound calls and statements, SLOs, quiet routes, production rules and how they held), as JSON and again as markdown for AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
  - get_method_impact - Returns the weight of one method, outbound call or statement before a change: calls and own time per minute, mean/max duration, error rate, last day vs. week, and the applications that run it.
  - find_regressions - Lists releases that made things worse: 5xx error rate and latency before vs. after each release boundary, classified better/worse/stable, with the operations each degraded.
  - get_release_verdict - Returns one release's verdict (regressed, changed, clean, or not enough data) with its evidence: traffic, outbound hosts, query shapes and methods added or removed, new error groups, quiet routes.
  - diff_release - Returns the statement shapes, outbound calls and NestJS methods whose calls per request or own time per call moved across one release boundary, ranked by added time.
  - verify_fix - Judges whether a release fixed an error group on that release's own requests: fixed, not fixed, too early, or insufficient data; writes nothing.
  - list_slow_operations - Lists the slowest HTTP operations in the window, ranked by p95, with volume.
  - get_operation_details - Returns one route's latency and error summary plus recent individual requests with duration, status and traceId.
  - get_trace - Resolves a traceId to every execution under it across services, requests and jobs, each with its span tree.
  - get_trace_logs - Returns every log line emitted under a traceId, in order.
  - list_error_groups - Lists errors grouped by fingerprint, ranked by count, with class, sample message and stack trace, first/last seen and introducing release.
  - get_error_details - Returns recent occurrences of one error class (message, status, user, traceId) plus a summary.
  - get_error_trend - Returns whether errors are growing or decaying over the window, classified as a direction.
  - get_affected_users - Returns which end users hit one error class and how often.
  - list_jobs - Lists background job performance per job name and queue: volume, duration and failure counts.
  - get_job_details - Returns duration and wait-time summaries for one job on one queue plus recent executions with status and traceId.
  - list_classes - Lists NestJS classes by own time, total time, calls and errors, as on the Services view.
  - get_class_methods - Returns the methods of one class with own/total time, calls and errors.
  - get_service_map - Returns who calls whom across the project: applications, queues, databases and external hosts, with calls, errors and average duration.
  - list_issues - Lists issues across the user's projects, newest first, filterable by project, status or limit.
  - get_issue - Returns one issue with its comments and activity.
  - get_incident_record - Returns an issue's incident record: what it was, start/end, introducing release, users reached, fixing release and verification, on one timeline.
  - list_slos - Lists a project's SLOs with current status and error-budget burn.
  - list_rule_violations - Returns each production rule over the window (violated, holding or unchecked), the traces checked and those that broke it, and newest violating traces.
  - list_alert_rules - Lists the alert rules across every project the user can see.
  - list_alert_events - Returns alert firing history, newest first, filterable by rule, project, state, severity and time window.
  - list_applications - Lists the applications of one project (to check before creating a duplicate).
  - create_project - Creates a project in an existing team or in a new team named after the project (writes).
  - create_application - Registers one NestJS service in a project; the name should match the SDK serviceId (writes).
  - create_api_key - Issues the key pair the SDK authenticates with; the secret is returned once (writes).
  - resolve_issue - Marks an issue resolved after a fix ships, starting fix verification; optional fixedInVersion (writes).
  - create_production_rule - Pins a production rule on one operation (what it may call and how often) and returns the sentence the rule is checked as (writes; Write access and paid plan).
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool: search. Searches the user's projects, applications, alert rules, SLOs and issues by full-text search. Input fields, result shape and the index or library behind the ranking are not documented. Runs on the project's server (hosted API at observe-api.nestjs.com), not on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Tools return JSON (get_context_pack also markdown) followed by a text block of dashboard links; no ui:// resource or image is documented.
- Prompts and resources: None documented. The docs name only server instructions sent at connect time (naming the order get_context_pack before edits, get_release_verdict / verify_fix / create_production_rule after a deploy); no MCP prompts or resources are listed. Server code is not public, so this cannot be checked against code.
- Number of skills: 6, in github.com/nestjs/agent-skills under skills/<name>/SKILL.md (with references/), also shipped as npm package @nestjs/skills 0.1.1 (installer bin nestjs-skills) and as Claude Code plugin nestjs from marketplace nestjs in the same repo. No contributor-only skills in the repo.
- Skills:
  - nestjs - Covers NestJS itself: starting a project non-interactively with the Nest CLI, the layout and module system, where the current docs are, and mistakes agents make that still pass tests; used when creating or extending a NestJS application.
  - nestjs-feature - Adds or changes HTTP endpoints: modules, controllers, services, request validation (Zod or another Standard Schema library with @Body({ schema }), or class-validator DTOs), status codes, error bodies, request IDs, versioning and Server-Sent Events; used when adding or changing endpoints.
  - nestjs-auth - Sign-in, sessions, bearer tokens, API keys and permissions with @nestjs/authentication and @nestjs/authorization (timing-safe password checks, global guard with @Public(), policies with @Can()); used when adding or changing authentication or authorization.
  - nestjs-data - Databases with @nestjs/drizzle and @nestjs/typeorm: registration, injection, schemas or entities, migrations, transactions and concurrency-safe writes; used when adding or changing persistence.
  - nestjs-testing - Unit, service and end-to-end tests with @nestjs/testing (Test.createTestingModule, overriding providers and guards, Supertest, test users, SSE, test databases, Vitest in ESM / Jest in CommonJS); used when writing, running or fixing tests.
  - nestjs-production - Production setup with first-party packages: @nestjs/config env validation, structured logs, observability with NestJS Observe (@nestjs/observe), @nestjs/terminus health checks, @nestjs/throttler, @nestjs/swagger, graceful shutdown and deployment behind a load balancer; used when preparing an app for production or adding any of these.
- What the skills point at: Web addresses: https://docs.nestjs.com/llms.txt and chapter .md pages (every skill and reference names its docs chapters; nestjs/references/docs-map.md maps topics to chapters). CLI commands: `npx @nestjs/cli new . --skip-git --package-manager npm`, `npx nest g module|controller|service <name> --no-spec`, `nest g resource` with `--type rest --crud`, `npx @nestjs/observe link` (with `--no-browser`), `npm ls @nestjs/core`, `npm view @nestjs/core version`, `npx vitest run`, `npx drizzle-kit generate|migrate`. MCP server: nestjs-production points to the Observe MCP server (https://observe-api.nestjs.com/mcp) for production questions, without naming its tools. No files in installed packages are …
