#### Next.js
Checked: next 16.4.6 (npm latest, checked 2026-11-20; newest canary 16.5.0-canary.58 published 2026-11-20 registers the same 9 /_next/mcp tools); next-devtools-mcp 0.4.0 (npm latest, published 2026-06-24; GitHub head 1e8dcfa, 2026-09-14, carries an unpublished 0.4.1 … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: Two official servers. (1) The built-in dev-server endpoint `/_next/mcp` (e.g. http://localhost:3000/_next/mcp), in the `next` package 16.4.6 (registered as McpServer name 'Next.js MCP Server', version '0.2.0'). It is on by default in `next dev` (config default `experimental.mcpServer: true`) and gives the running app's errors, routes, logs, metadata and compilation issues. (2) `next-devtools-mcp` 0.4.0 (npm, github.com/vercel/next-devtools-mcp, mcpName io.github.vercel/next-devtools-mcp), a stdio server that discovers running Next.js dev servers and forwards calls to their `/_next/mcp` tools. It also points the agent to the bundled docs and to the agent-browser CLI.
- Number of tools: `/_next/mcp` in next 16.4.6: 9 tools. 7 are always registered. `get_compilation_issues` and `compile_route` are registered only when the dev server provides a Turbopack project or a compileRoute function. `get_request_insights` is always registered but answers with an error unless experimental.requestInsights is set. next-devtools-mcp 0.4.0: 4 tools. Source for both counts: the code that …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (server.registerTool calls in next/dist/server/mcp/tools/*.js; tool metadata in next-devtools-mcp/dist/tools/*.js).
  - `/_next/mcp` (9):
  - get_project_metadata - returns the project's metadata, such as the project path and the dev server URL.
  - get_errors - returns the current error state of the dev server: Next.js global errors (e.g. next.config validation), browser runtime errors and build errors with source-mapped stack traces. It needs an active browser session.
  - get_page_metadata - returns runtime metadata about what contributes to the current page render, read from active browser sessions.
  - get_logs - returns the path of the development log file (<distDir>/logs/next-development.log), which the agent then reads itself.
  - get_server_action_by_id - takes actionId and looks it up in server-reference-manifest.json; returns the filename and the export name of that Server Action.
  - get_routes - scans the filesystem and returns every route that becomes an entry point, grouped by router (appRouter, pagesRouter); optional routerType 'app' | 'pages'.
  - get_request_insights - returns recent App Router request insights from the local span recorder (slow renders, server fetches, cache behavior, request timelines); optional requestId and htmlRequestId; needs experimental.requestInsights.
  - get_compilation_issues - builds the module graph for all routes and returns all compilation issues (resolve errors, missing modules, transform errors); Turbopack only, no browser session needed.
  - compile_route - compiles one route, given by routeSpecifier or path, without an HTTP request; returns { routeSpecifier, issues }, or an error when no route matches; Turbopack only.
  - next-devtools-mcp 0.4.0 (4):
  - nextjs_index - finds the running Next.js dev servers (optional port) and returns each server's port, PID and URL, with its MCP tools, their descriptions and their input schemas.
  - nextjs_call - calls one named `/_next/mcp` tool (port, toolName, optional args object) on a running dev server and returns its result.
  - nextjs_docs - does not fetch docs; it reads the installed Next.js version (optional topic and project_path) and returns JSON that points to node_modules/next/dist/docs/, with grep hints, or upgrade advice for versions before 16.
  - browser_eval - does not drive a browser; it checks whether the agent-browser CLI is installed (optional task) and returns install or usage instructions, such as `agent-browser skills get core --full`.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none. No tool searches. nextjs_docs takes an optional `topic` and only returns a grep command as a suggestion (`grep -ril "<topic>" node_modules/next/dist/docs`). The agent runs that command on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool returns a `ui://` resource or an image. browser_eval refers the agent to the agent-browser CLI, which the agent runs itself, including screenshots.
- Prompts and resources: none for both servers. next-devtools-mcp declares only `capabilities: { tools: {} }`. The `/_next/mcp` code calls only registerTool, with no registerPrompt or registerResource. The 0.3.x prompts and resources were removed (README: 'Migrating from 0.3.x').
- Number of skills: 6 skills for users, in the Next.js repository under `skills/` (github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills). They install with `npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill <name>` and are listed on skills.sh/vercel/next.js. They are not inside the npm package: the next 16.4.6 tarball has no SKILL.md. Not counted: the contributor skills in .agents/skills and .claude/skills (21 folders each, for example …
- Skills:
  - next-dev-loop - verifies Next.js runtime behavior after an edit to app code, so an agent confirms that a change works in a running app, using /_next/mcp (Next.js's view) and agent-browser (the browser's view); it needs a running `next dev`.
  - next-bundle-optimizer - audits and reduces the work a browser does on initial load; for slow route startup, oversized client bundles, duplicate browser dependencies, or features that can wait for interaction.
  - next-cache-components-adoption - turns on Cache Components and resolves the blocking routes they surface; for enabling or migrating (the `cacheComponents` flag), blocking-prerender / instant validation errors, the `cache-components-instant-false` codemod, or choosing between `export const instant = false` and a fix in place.
  - next-cache-components-optimizer - grows the UI that a route shows at once on a hard or soft navigation, by writing a failing @next/playwright instant() e2e test and working it to green one route at a time; it needs Next.js 16.3+ with Cache Components adopted.
  - next-partial-prefetching-adoption - turns on Partial Prefetching and works through its insights; for the `partialPrefetching` flag, `export const prefetch = 'partial'`, auditing `Link prefetch={true}`, keeping prefetched UI with instant() tests, and resolving the instant-link-prefetch-partial and instant-shell-url-data insights.
  - next-partial-prefetching-optimizer - after Cache Components and Partial Prefetching are adopted, sets what selected client navigations include before the click: it makes chosen URL-specific UI instant, lets reusable content wait for navigation, and chooses between default, viewport and intent prefetching; it needs Next.js 16.3+.
- What the skills point at: MCP server: next-dev-loop calls `/_next/mcp` directly over HTTP (tools/list, get_project_metadata, get_routes, get_errors, get_page_metadata, get_logs, get_server_action_by_id, get_compilation_issues), and other skills cite get_errors, get_request_insights (next-partial-prefetching-adoption, next-cache-components-adoption references) and get_compilation_issues. CLI: `next dev`, `next build` (including `next build --analyze` in next-bundle-optimizer), the agent-browser CLI, and the `cache-components-instant-false` codemod. Files in the installed package: `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (e.g. 01-app/02-guides/migrating-to-cache-components.md). Web: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/<slug> error …

Its source is in the nuxt/nuxt.com repository (server/mcp/, built with @nuxtjs/mcp-toolkit ^0.24.3), checked at main commit 70726bf (2026-11-20). It serves the nuxt.com docs (v3, v4 and v5), the deployment guides, the module directory, the blog, the changelogs of Nuxt and its official modules, and the Nuxters contributor data. The same repository also has a second handler, named 'admin' (server/mcp/admin.ts), with middleware requireMcpAdminToken; it is 'Authenticated MCP handler for the Nuxt team', not for consumers.
- Number of tools: 13 public tools on https://nuxt.com/mcp, counted from the code that registers them: the files in server/mcp/tools/{blog,changelog,deploy,docs,modules,nuxters}. The docs page in nuxt/nuxt (docs/3.guide/3.ai/1.mcp.md) lists only 10, because it leaves out search-documentation, list-nuxters and get-nuxter. The token-gated admin handler for the team has 13 more tools in server/mcp/tools/admin, each …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (nuxt/nuxt.com server/mcp/tools, main 70726bf). 13 tools:
  - 1. search-documentation: full-text search of the Nuxt v4 docs, the deploy guides, the hosted module docs and the blog. Input: query, plus scope (all, docs, deploy, modules or blog). Returns up to 6 best-matching sections, each with title, path, section, anchor URL and content.
  - 2. list-documentation-pages: lists docs pages (title, path and URL; plus description when a search term is given) for version 3.x, 4.x, 5.x or all, with an optional filter by words.
  - 3. get-documentation-page: returns the markdown of one docs page by path, optionally only the named h2 sections, truncated at 30,000 characters.
  - 4. get-getting-started-guide: returns the markdown of the 'Getting Started' introduction page for Nuxt 3.x, 4.x or 5.x, optionally only some sections.
  - 5. list-blog-posts: lists all blog posts with title, path, description, date, category, tags, authors, image and URL.
  - 6. get-blog-post: returns the full markdown of one blog post by path.
  - 7. list-deploy-providers: lists the hosting providers with title, path, description, category, nitroPreset, website, sponsor and URL.
  - 8. get-deploy-provider: returns the markdown deployment guide of one provider by path, optionally only some h2 sections.
  - 9. list-modules: lists up to 20 Nuxt modules from api.nuxt.com, with filters (search over name, description, npm name or supported provider; category), sorting (downloads, stars, publishedAt or createdAt) and an order. Each entry holds name, npm, description, category, links and downloads/stars or full stats (plus matchedProviders when the search matched a provider), and the result has totalMatches.
  - 10. get-module: returns the details of one module by slug or npm name: description, npm, repo, category, compatibility, providers, stats, a README cut at 8,000 characters, and the URL.
  - 11. get-changelog: returns the latest releases of nuxt/nuxt and the official modules (title, repo, tag, date, URL and markdown body cut at 4,000 characters), with an optional repo filter and a limit of 1 to 20 (default 5).
  - 12. list-nuxters: lists ranked Nuxt ecosystem contributors for a period (all, 30d, 12m or a year), optionally by country or username search, with limit 1 to 50 and offset. Returns rank, username, score, profile URL, totals and the available periods.
  - 13. get-nuxter: returns one contributor's stats by GitHub username and period: rank, score, merged PRs, issues, comments, reactions, links, country, maintained and contributed modules, blog posts, and the ranks of the other periods.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool search-documentation. Inputs: query (string, at least 2 characters: 'Keywords, API names, config keys or an error message excerpt') and scope (all | docs | deploy | modules | blog, default all). It returns up to 6 hits, with at most 2 per page and section text cut at 1,800 characters. Each hit holds title, path, section (the heading trail joined with ' › ', or 'Introduction'), url (path#anchor) and content. With no match it returns {results: [], hint}. Ranking: BM25 over the sections of the pages (k1 1.2, b 0.75, title weight 3, heading weight 2, an English stop-word list, word stemming and camelCase/underscore splitting in the tokenizer), in-house code in layers/nuxi/agent/lib/docs-index.ts. No embedding model is used. A section's score is multiplied by (0.5 + matched terms / query terms). The index is built from https://nuxt.com/llms.txt and the /raw/<path>.md page bodies, with an index TTL of one hour (INDEX_TTL_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000); the tool result is cached 30 minutes. Where it runs: on the nuxt.com server, not on the user's machine. The tool description itself says: 'Use keywords and API names, not full sentences'. list-documentation-pages and list-modules also filter by substring words.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Every public tool returns markdown text or JSON. No ui:// resource, registerAppResource or text/html;profile resource was found in server/, modules/ or layers/ of nuxt/nuxt.com at 70726bf.
- Prompts and resources: Resources (server/mcp/resources): - resource://nuxt-com/documentation-pages: a JSON list of all docs pages for v3.x, v4.x and v5.x (the code says 'across v3.x, v4.x, and v5.x'; the docs page says it 'defaults to v4.x'). - resource://nuxt-com/blog-posts: a JSON list of all blog posts. - resource://nuxt-com/deploy-providers: a JSON list of the deployment providers. Public prompts (server/mcp/prompts): - find-documentation-for-topic: finds the best docs for a topic. Input: topic, version. - deployment-guide: gives the deployment instructions for one hosting provider. Input: provider. - migration-help: gives steps to migrate between Nuxt versions. Input: fromVersion, toVersion. The admin handler has 5 more prompts (server/mcp/prompts/admin), for the team only: review-agent-chats, seo-opportunities, summarize-feedback, triage-problematic-pages and weekly-digest. The server also accepts an optional X-MCP-Tools HTTP header that limits the tools it exposes.

Its root AGENTS.md is a policy for contributing agents. - the nuxt@4.6.4 npm tarball: no file named skill, agents, claude or mcp. - nuxt/nuxt.com at 70726bf: exactly 7 SKILL.md files, all in layers/nuxi/agent/skills (debug-nuxt-com, ecosystem-usage, firehose-summary, seo-opportunities, …

The unreleased v5 branch (head 05424d9, 2026-11-20) is listed for reference only. The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: the remote HTTP endpoint https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp. The Nuxt UI documentation site serves it. It is not an npm package, and the @nuxt/ui 4.13.0 tarball holds no MCP or skill files. Its source is docs/server/mcp/ in nuxt/ui, built on @nuxtjs/mcp-toolkit (defineMcpHandler, defineMcpTool). Newest release: v4.13.0, 2026-11-18. Purpose: it gives AI assistants the documentation, metadata, examples, templates, icon search and migration guide of Nuxt UI components.
- Number of tools: 12 tools for https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp at v4.13.0. Source: the code that registers the tools, one defineMcpTool file each in docs/server/mcp/tools/, all returned by getMcpTools in docs/server/mcp/index.ts. The documentation page (repository source and live ui.nuxt.com raw Markdown) lists the same 12. A client can narrow the list with the X-MCP-Tools header. The unreleased v5 branch has 13 tool …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (docs/server/mcp/tools/*.ts at v4.13.0). All 12 tools are annotated readOnlyHint true.
  - 1. search-components: searches the component documentation pages by an optional `category` and an optional `search` term, which matches the name, title, keywords (alternate names such as "segmented control") and description. Returns {components:[name,title,description,category,keywords,path,url,links], total, filters}, ranked by score, or sorted by name when there is no search term.
  - 2. search-composables: finds composables by a case-insensitive substring match of `search` on the name, title and description, or lists all of them. Returns name, title, description, path and url, sorted by name, plus total.
  - 3. search-documentation: filters documentation pages by `search` (every term has to match the title, path or description) and an optional `section`, or lists all pages. Returns title, description, path, url and markdown_url, sorted by path, plus total.
  - 4. search-icons: searches one Iconify collection (`collection`, default lucide) for `query` with an optional `limit` (default 64). Returns icon names in the i-{prefix}-{name} format with a preview SVG URL, plus total.
  - 5. get-component: returns the Markdown documentation of one component (`componentName`), optionally only the `sections` usage, examples, api, theme or changelog. The result also holds the name, title, description, category, documentation_url and sections_returned.
  - 6. get-component-metadata: returns the structured props, slots and events of one component (compact props by default, raw recursive schemas with `full: true`). The result also holds the title, description, category and documentation_url.
  - 7. get-documentation-page: returns the Markdown of one documentation page by its `path`, optionally only the named h2 `headings`, as a string without metadata.
  - 8. list-templates: lists the Nuxt UI templates as full records with a total, optionally filtered by `framework`.
  - 9. get-template: returns one template record by its title, without case: description, framework, features, and links to its live preview and GitHub repository. It holds no setup steps and no code.
  - 10. list-examples: lists the names of all UI examples, without code.
  - 11. get-example: returns the source code of one example (`exampleName`, PascalCase) as a string.
  - 12. get-migration-guide: takes no parameters. Returns the full guide for migrating from the previous major version as Markdown, with its title, description, path and url.
- Search, kind `keyword`: search-components: inputs `category` (exact category, optional) and `search` (optional). Each result holds name, title, description, category, keywords, path, url and links. Ranking is a hand-written lexical score in docs/server/utils/searchComponents.ts (scoreComponent). An exact name or title match scores 100 and a containment match 60. An exact keyword scores 50, and a keyword prefix or multi-word keyword match 40. A description match scores 20. Each token of 3 or more characters adds 12, 8 or 3 for a word-boundary match in the name or title, a keyword, or the description. Results with a score of 0 are dropped; ties sort by name. The keywords hold alternate names from other ecosystems, such as "combobox" for InputMenu; this is word matching, not an embedding. search-composables: input `search`, a case-insensitive substring match on the name, title and description, sorted by name. search-documentation: inputs `search` and `section`. It uses listAgentPages from '#agent-discovery' (the nuxt-agent-discovery module), where every term has to match the title, path or description, and sorts the results by path. search-icons: inputs `query`, `collection` and `limit`. It forwards the query to the Iconify search API, a third-party server. All ranking runs on the server of the project (the ui.nuxt.com documentation site), except search-icons, which runs on Iconify's API. Nothing runs on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool names a ui:// resource or returns an image. search-icons returns preview SVG URLs as text strings only.
- Prompts and resources: Resources (5): resource://nuxt-ui/components, the complete list of v4 components with metadata and categories; resource://nuxt-ui/composables, the composables with the path, title and description of each; resource://nuxt-ui/documentation-pages, the complete list of documentation pages; resource://nuxt-ui/examples, the example names only, without code; resource://nuxt-ui/templates, the complete list of templates with categories. Prompts (3): find-component-for-usecase, to find the best Nuxt UI component for a use case (argument usecase); implement-component-with-props, to generate a complete component implementation with the right props and styling (arguments componentName and optional requirements); setup-project-with-template, a guide to setting up a new project with a Nuxt UI template (argument projectType).
- Number of skills: 1 released skill for consumers: skills/nuxt-ui/SKILL.md in the nuxt/ui repository (tag v4.13.0, branch v4). It is not in the npm package. The docs site also serves it at https://ui.nuxt.com/.well-known/skills/index.json, which lists only nuxt-ui. Installation is with `npx skills add nuxt/ui` (or `npx skills add https://ui.nuxt.com`) or the Cursor deep link. The unreleased v5 branch has 3: …
- Skills:
  - nuxt-ui: teaches the agent to build UIs with @nuxt/ui v4 (125+ accessible Vue components with Tailwind CSS theming). The agent uses it when it creates interfaces, customizes themes to match a brand, builds forms, or composes layouts such as dashboards, docs sites and chat interfaces. It has on-demand references: components.md, guidelines/ (component-selection, conventions, design-system, forms), layouts/ (chat, dashboard, docs, editor, landing) and recipes/ (auth, data-tables, navigation, overlays).
- What the skills point at: The skill points to the hosted MCP server https://ui.nuxt.com/mcp (with setup lines for Cursor and `claude mcp add`) and names its tools search-components, search-composables, search-icons, get-component, get-component-metadata and get-example. It points to generated theme files in the user's project, .nuxt/ui/<component>.ts (Nuxt) and node_modules/.nuxt-ui/ui/<component>.ts (Vue), and to its own reference files. It also gives the web address icones.js.org.

#### NVIDIA Elements
Checked: @nvidia-elements/cli 2.2.17 (npm latest, published 2026-11-07T05:56Z; MCP Registry io.github.NVIDIA/elements 2.2.17 isLatest, published 2026-11-09T14:45Z). - MCP servers: One official server. It runs as the `nve mcp` subcommand of the Elements CLI, npm package @nvidia-elements/cli, and is not part of @nvidia-elements/core. MCP Registry name: io.github.NVIDIA/elements. Newest version: 2.2.17 (npm 2026-11-07; registry entry 2026-11-09, status active, isLatest true). It runs over stdio. Purpose: it gives agents the Elements (nve-*) component APIs, tokens, icons, examples, lint validation and project scaffolding and setup.
- Number of tools: 16 tools by default, counted from the code that registers them. The server registers each @tool method whose support flag includes MCP: api 6, examples 3, packages 3, project 3 and cli 1. Two more tools, playground_validate and playground_create, register only when the environment variable ELEMENTS_PLAYGROUND_BASE_URL is set at runtime, which makes 18. Left out: examples_search (support None) and …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (projects/internals/tools/src/*/service.ts). Each name is built from <service>.<command> with dots and hyphens replaced by underscores.
  - 1. api_list: lists all Elements (nve-*) elements and attributes, returned as markdown or as JSON {elements, attributes}.
  - 2. api_get: returns the documentation of 1 to 3 named components or attributes (MAX_RESULT_LIMIT = 3; for example ["nve-button"]), as markdown or JSON. It looks each name up exactly and returns an error with a tip to use the list tool when no name is found.
  - 3. api_validate: checks HTML or JSON files (paths or globs) or supplied content with the recommended Elements lint rules, and returns a validation result with diagnostics and summary counts.
  - 4. api_imports_get: takes an HTML template and returns the ESM import paths that its nve-* elements need, as a string array.
  - 5. api_tokens_list: returns the semantic CSS custom properties (design tokens), each with name, value and description. An optional query filters them. The result is markdown or JSON, and the tool is linked to the ui://elements/tokens-list MCP App.
  - 6. api_icons_list: returns all icon names for nve-icon and nve-icon-button, as markdown or a JSON array, and is linked to the ui://elements/icons-list MCP App.
  - 7. examples_list: returns a summary list of the starter templates, patterns and examples ({id, summary}), as markdown or JSON.
  - 8. examples_get: returns the full template of one example or pattern by id, as markdown or JSON, and is linked to the ui://elements/example-preview MCP App.
  - 9. examples_render (MCP only): lints an ad-hoc nve-* HTML template in strict mode and returns {template, name, lintMessages}, or a tool error with the lint messages. It renders the template in the ui://elements/example-preview MCP App.
  - 10. packages_list: returns a string with the latest published versions of all Elements packages.
  - 11. packages_get: returns a string with the details of one named Elements package.
  - 12. packages_changelogs_get: returns the changelog of a named package, up to `limit` versions (default 10), as markdown or a JSON map.
  - 13. project_create: creates a new starter project of a given type in cwd and can start it. It returns a report. It is annotated destructive.
  - 14. project_setup: sets up or updates a project to use Elements. It configures MCP, adds the core dependencies and updates the packages to their latest versions, then returns a report. It is annotated destructive.
  - 15. project_validate: checks a project (application or library) for configuration issues, outdated dependencies or missing packages, and returns a health report.
  - 16. cli_upgrade (MCP only): downloads and installs the latest nve CLI through the shell or PowerShell bootstrapper, and returns a report. It is annotated destructive and open-world.
  - Only when ELEMENTS_PLAYGROUND_BASE_URL is set:
  - 17. playground_validate: lints an HTML template given inline or by path under the playground constraints, and returns the ESLint messages. Its description says to use it before playground_create.
  - 18. playground_create: creates a shareable playground URL from a valid HTML template (with a type, a name and an author), and returns the URL or the template errors.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none. The server exposes no search tool. ApiService.search has no @tool decorator, and ExamplesService.search is declared with support: ToolSupport.None, so neither reaches the server. The nearest thing is the optional `query` input of api_tokens_list. It filters tokens by a case-insensitive substring match on name, value or description, and the filter runs on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `mcp-apps`: The server declares the extension io.modelcontextprotocol/ui and three ui:// resources. Each published resource is a self-contained HTML file of about 1 MB in dist/mcp/ui/ of the 2.2.17 package that bundles the Elements themes, core and an MCP Apps client. None of them needs a dev server or another local process. (1) examples_get and examples_render use ui://elements/example-preview ('nve-mcp-examples-render'). The view shows the nve-* example or ad-hoc template live, themed to the host. For examples_get it fetches the template by calling examples_get back. When linting fails, it shows the lint messages instead. The user views and inspects it. (2) api_icons_list uses ui://elements/icons-list. The view is a searchable grid of icon previews with copyable <nve-icon name="..."></nve-icon> markup. (3) api_tokens_list uses ui://elements/tokens-list (the docs call it Token Explorer). The view groups tokens, previews their values, offers search, lets the user switch themes, and gives copyable var(--nve-*) references.
- Prompts and resources: Prompts (4; each loads the matching reference of the elements skill): 'artifact' (NVIDIA Artifact Template: create a standalone Elements UI artifact); 'doctor' (Elements Design System Doctor / Setup Check: verify setup and MCP configuration); 'create-project' (Initialize a new Elements Starter Project); 'migrate' (Migrate from Deprecated Elements APIs). Resources (3, all MCP App HTML): nve-mcp-examples-render at ui://elements/example-preview (renders example or ad-hoc templates); nve-mcp-api-icons-list at ui://elements/icons-list (icon picker); nve-mcp-api-tokens-list at ui://elements/tokens-list (token browser).
- Number of skills: 1 consumer skill, `elements` (SKILL.md plus references/artifact.md, doctor.md, integration.md and migration.md). Its source is .agents/skills/elements/ in the repository. It is bundled into the CLI and installed with `nve skills.install` (or --global for the current user); it can also be installed with `npx skills add https://github.com/nvidia/elements --skill elements`. The docs site publishes …
- Skills:
  - elements: the default skill for any UI work or work with NVIDIA Elements (nve-*): creating, editing, reviewing or debugging HTML, CSS, layout, theming, components, applications, prototypes, Claude Artifacts, Codex Sites pages and standalone UI artifacts. It sets Elements as the visual system, gives the lookup, write and validate workflow, and routes to its four references: artifact, integration, doctor and migration.
- What the skills point at: The skill points the agent to the CLI commands: nve api.list, api.get, api.validate, api.imports.get, api.tokens.list, api.icons.list, examples.list, examples.get, project.create, project.setup, project.validate, packages.list, packages.get, packages.changelogs.get and skills.install. It names the MCP server alias `nvidia_elements` and says most CLI commands have MCP tool equivalents; integration.md names the MCP tool `project_setup`. It also points to web addresses: https://nvidia.github.io/elements/llms.txt (fallback) and the docs. artifact.md points to the jsDelivr CDN bundles of @nvidia-elements/styles, themes and core.

The server exposes them only under conditions. Minimal mode is the default ('--minimal', default true) and hides 6 of them (nx_available_plugins, …
- Tools:
  - nx-mcp 0.25.4. The list comes from the registration code (libs/nx-mcp/nx-mcp-server/src/lib/tools/*.ts), with the README and the nx.dev reference as a cross-check.
  - 1. nx_docs: takes userQuery and returns up to 4 sections of the Nx docs that may answer it, wrapped in a prompt text.
  - 2. nx_available_plugins: returns a text list of the Nx plugins from the core team and the local plugins of the workspace (hidden in minimal mode).
  - 3. nx_workspace: returns a readable form of the project graph and nx.json, with any project graph errors; filter, select and pageToken inputs; structured content holds all projects (hidden in minimal mode).
  - 4. nx_workspace_path: returns the path of the workspace root as text (hidden in minimal mode).
  - 5. nx_project_details: takes projectName (with optional select and pageToken) and returns the configuration of that project, with targets in a compact text form, metadata and dependencies as JSON (hidden in minimal mode).
  - 6. nx_generators: returns the names and descriptions of all generators, from plugins and from the workspace (hidden in minimal mode).
  - 7. nx_generator_schema: takes generatorName and returns the full JSON schema of that generator and its examples.md where one exists (hidden in minimal mode).
  - 8. nx_current_running_tasks_details: returns the task IDs and status of the tasks of the running Nx CLI processes (needs an IDE connection).
  - 9. nx_current_running_task_output: takes taskId and optional pageToken and returns the terminal output of that task in 10000-character pages, newest first (needs an IDE connection).
  - 10. nx_visualize_graph: takes visualizationType (project, project-task or full-project-graph), projectName and taskName, opens that graph in the IDE through Nx Console, and returns a text confirmation (needs an IDE connection).
  - 11. ci_information: returns the status of the CI pipeline execution (CIPE) on Nx Cloud for the current branch or a given Nx Cloud URL, with its failed tasks and self-healing status; select gives raw JSON fields; has an output schema (needs Nx Cloud).
  - 12. ci_task_output: returns the terminal log of one CI task, found by runId or by searching the runs of the CIPE (needs Nx Cloud).
  - 13. update_self_healing_fix: applies or rejects a self-healing CI fix on Nx Cloud, found by aiFixId, short link or the current branch, and returns the result; not read-only (needs Nx Cloud). The README adds that it can request a rerun.
  - Hosted Nx Cloud MCP server: not confirmed.
- Search, kind `intent`: Tool nx_docs. Input: userQuery (string): 'The user query to get docs for. You can pass the original user query verbatim or summarize it.' The tool sends POST https://nx.dev/api/query-ai-embeddings with {messages:[{role:'user',content}]}. The endpoint (nrwl/nx, nx-dev/nx-dev/pages/api/query-ai-embeddings.ts) calls getTokenizedContext. That function embeds the query with OpenAI 'text-embedding-ada-002' and calls the Supabase RPC 'match_page_sections_2' (vector match with DEFAULT_MATCH_THRESHOLD and DEFAULT_MATCH_COUNT). One result is a page section with heading, longer_heading, content and similarity. The MCP tool keeps the first 4 sections and returns them as one text. The ranking runs on a server of the project (nx.dev and its Supabase database), not on the machine of the user.

It is a local stdio server that loads the user's Panda config through the compiler driver and serves the project's resolved design system (tokens, recipes, patterns, conditions, styles, config) plus a usage report of the project sources.
- Number of tools: 12 (@pandacss/mcp 2.6.0), counted from the code that registers the tools in packages/mcp/src/server.ts; the published dist/index.js of the 2.6.0 tarball contains the same 12 tool names, and the documentation page website/content/docs/get-started/mcp-server.mdx lists the same 12 tools.
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (packages/mcp/src/server.ts). Each tool returns JSON as text and reloads the config first if it changed on disk.
  - 1. get_tokens: returns the design tokens (categories, values with CSS variables, deprecated token names), optionally filtered by `category`.
  - 2. get_semantic_tokens: returns the semantic tokens of the theme with their conditional values (responsive, color modes), optionally filtered by `category`.
  - 3. get_recipes: returns the recipes and slot recipes with their variants, default values and usage examples, optionally filtered by `name`.
  - 4. get_patterns: returns the layout patterns with their properties and usage examples, optionally filtered by `name`.
  - 5. get_conditions: returns all conditions (breakpoints, pseudo-classes, color modes) with their CSS values and their definitions.
  - 6. get_keyframes: returns the keyframe animations defined in the theme.
  - 7. get_text_styles: returns the text style compositions for typography.
  - 8. get_layer_styles: returns the layer style compositions.
  - 9. get_animation_styles: returns the animation style compositions.
  - 10. get_color_palette: returns the color palettes and all color token values.
  - 11. get_config: returns the resolved Panda CSS configuration (paths, JSX settings, output options).
  - 12. get_usage_report: scans the project sources and returns usage of tokens, recipes, utilities, patterns and keyframes, unused configured names, source locations and diagnostics; input `scope` (all | tokens | recipes | utilities | patterns | keyframes); it sets isError when a diagnostic is an error or a parse error.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none. No tool takes a query; tools filter only by exact `category` or `name` and return an error listing the available names when the name is unknown.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. Every tool returns a single text content item holding JSON.

  - 2. countDocuments: counts documents in a collection, with an optional where clause.
  - 3. countVersions: counts document versions in a version-enabled collection, with an optional where clause.
  - 4. createDocuments: creates one or more documents, each with its own data or file (uploadReference, externalURL or base64), and returns the created documents.
  - 5. deleteDocuments: deletes documents in a collection by ID or where clause.
  - 6. duplicateDocument: duplicates a document from a source document ID.
  - 7. findDocuments: finds documents in a collection by an optional ID or where clause and returns them (paginated).
  - 8. findDistinct: returns the distinct values of one field path in a collection.
  - 9. findVersionByID: returns one document version, found by its version ID.
  - 10. findVersions: finds document versions, with an optional where clause.
  - 11. getCollectionSchema: returns the input schema and the LLM instructions to read before creating or updating documents in a collection.
  - 12. getUploadInstructions: prepares an upload for createDocuments or updateDocument. It does not upload bytes. It returns upload instructions (an HTTP request or a tool to call) and a file reference.

  - 19. unlock: unlocks a user account that was locked after failed login attempts.
  - 20. verify: verifies a user's email with a verification token.
  - 21. countGlobalVersions: counts the versions of a version-enabled global, with an optional where clause.
  - 22. findGlobal: returns a Payload global, found by its slug.
  - 23. findGlobalVersionByID: returns one version of a global, found by its version ID.
  - 24. findGlobalVersions: finds versions of a global, with an optional where clause.
  - 25. getGlobalSchema: returns the input schema and the LLM instructions to read before updating a global.
  - 26. restoreGlobalVersion: restores a global from a previous version.
  - 27. updateGlobal: updates a Payload global with the data given.

The code defines 83 browser tools, and filteredTools() drops the 11 marked skillOnly …

  - Source: the code that registers the tools (playwright-core coreBundle.js, 1.65.1 and 1.66.0-alpha-2026-11-18, with the same 83 names in both), checked against the generated README of @playwright/mcp 0.0.86. Each tool returns a text result, mostly Markdown sections with the generated Playwright code and, after actions, a page snapshot.
  - (A) Playwright MCP, 72 tools:
  - Default (core):
  - 1 browser_click: clicks an element by snapshot ref or selector (optionally a double click, a button or modifiers); returns the code and a snapshot.
  - 2 browser_close: closes the browser and all tabs.
  - 3 browser_console_messages: returns the console messages at or above a level, or saves them to a file.
  - 4 browser_drag: drags and drops between two elements.
  - 5 browser_drop: drops files or MIME-typed data onto an element.
  - 6 browser_emulate_media: emulates CSS media features (color scheme, reduced motion, forced colors, contrast, media type).
  - 7 browser_evaluate: evaluates a JavaScript function on the page or on an element and returns the result as text or to a file.
  - 8 browser_file_upload: uploads files to a file chooser, or cancels it.
  - 9 browser_fill_form: fills several form fields.
  - 10 browser_find: searches the page's accessibility snapshot for text or a regex and returns the matching nodes with context and refs.
  - 11 browser_handle_dialog: accepts or dismisses a dialog, with optional prompt text.
  - 12 browser_hover: hovers over an element.
  - 13 browser_navigate: navigates to a URL.
  - 14 browser_navigate_back: goes back in the history.
  - 15 browser_network_request: returns the full details (headers, body) of one request by index.
  - 16 browser_network_requests: returns a numbered list of the network requests, which can be filtered.
  - 17 browser_press_key: presses a key.
  - 18 browser_resize: resizes the browser window.
  - 19 browser_run_code_unsafe: runs a Playwright code snippet `async (page) => {...}` in the server process and returns its result.
  - 20 browser_select_option: selects options in a dropdown.
  - 21 browser_snapshot: captures the accessibility (ARIA) snapshot of the page or an element, optionally with boxes or to a file.
  - 22 browser_take_screenshot: takes a PNG, JPEG or WebP screenshot of the viewport, the full page or an element; saves it to a file and also returns it as an inline image when no filename is given.
  - 23 browser_type: types text into an editable element, optionally submitting.
  - 24 browser_wait_for: waits for text to appear or disappear, or for a time.
  - 25 browser_tabs: lists, creates, closes or selects tabs (optionally in an isolated context).
  - Opt-in config:
  - 26 browser_get_config: returns the final resolved configuration.
  - Opt-in network:
  - 27 browser_network_state_set: sets the network online or offline.
  - 28 browser_route: mocks requests that match a URL pattern (status, body, headers).
  - 29 browser_route_list: lists the active routes.
  - 30 browser_unroute: removes routes.
  - Opt-in storage:
  - 31 browser_cookie_clear: clears all cookies.
  - 32 browser_cookie_delete: deletes one cookie.
  - 33 browser_cookie_get: gets a cookie by name.
  - 34 browser_cookie_list: lists cookies, optionally filtered by domain or path.
  - 35 browser_cookie_set: sets a cookie with flags.
  - 36 browser_localstorage_clear: clears localStorage.
  - 37 browser_localstorage_delete: deletes a localStorage item.
  - 38 browser_localstorage_get: gets a localStorage item.
  - 39 browser_localstorage_list: lists the localStorage pairs.
  - 40 browser_localstorage_set: sets a localStorage item.
  - 41 browser_sessionstorage_clear: clears sessionStorage.
  - 42 browser_sessionstorage_delete: deletes a sessionStorage item.
  - 43 browser_sessionstorage_get: gets a sessionStorage item.
  - 44 browser_sessionstorage_list: lists the sessionStorage pairs.
  - 45 browser_sessionstorage_set: sets a sessionStorage item.
  - 46 browser_set_storage_state: restores cookies and localStorage from a file.
  - 47 browser_storage_state: saves the storage state to a file.
  - Opt-in devtools:
  - 48 browser_annotate: opens the Playwright Dashboard (a separate local process) in annotation mode, waits for the user's annotations, and returns the feedback and annotation boxes as text, with the annotated screenshot (PNG) and the ARIA snapshot (YAML) saved as files, not as inline images.
  - 49 browser_hide_highlight: removes a highlight overlay.
  - 50 browser_highlight: shows a persistent highlight overlay around an element.
  - 51 browser_resume: resumes a paused script, optionally step by step or to a file:line.
  - 52 browser_start_recording: starts recording the user's actions as Playwright code.
  - 53 browser_start_tracing: starts a trace recording.
  - 54 browser_start_video: starts a video recording.
  - 55 browser_stop_recording: stops the recording and returns the recorded actions as Playwright code.
  - 56 browser_stop_tracing: stops the trace recording.
  - 57 browser_stop_video: stops the video recording.
  - 58 browser_video_chapter: adds a chapter card to the video.
  - 59 browser_video_hide_actions: stops the action overlays.
  - 60 browser_video_show_actions: annotates later actions with callouts and a cursor.
  - Opt-in vision:
  - 61 browser_mouse_click_xy: clicks at coordinates.
  - 62 browser_mouse_down: presses a mouse button down.
  - 63 browser_mouse_drag_xy: drags between coordinates.
  - 64 browser_mouse_move_xy: moves the mouse to coordinates.
  - 65 browser_mouse_up: releases a mouse button.
  - 66 browser_mouse_wheel: scrolls the mouse wheel.
  - Opt-in pdf:
  - 67 browser_pdf_save: saves the page as a PDF file.
  - Opt-in testing:
  - 68 browser_generate_locator: returns a Playwright locator for an element, for use in tests.
  - 69 browser_verify_element_visible: checks that an element with a role and accessible name is visible.
  - 70 browser_verify_list_visible: checks that a list with the given items is visible.
  - 71 browser_verify_text_visible: checks that a text is visible.
  - 72 browser_verify_value: checks an element's value.
  - Plus dynamic tools: the WebMCP tools that the current page registers.
  - (B) Playwright Test Runner, 92 tools: the 9 below, plus the 72 above, plus the 11 skillOnly browser tools (browser_check: checks a checkbox or radio; browser_uncheck: unchecks one; browser_webmcp_list: lists the WebMCP tools that the page registers; browser_webmcp_call: calls a page WebMCP tool; browser_console_clear: clears the console messages; browser_press_sequentially: types text key by key; browser_keydown: presses a key down; browser_keyup: releases a key; browser_navigate_forward: goes forward in the history; browser_reload: reloads the page; browser_network_clear: clears the network requests). Here the browser tools are relayed to a paused test, and tools of type action, assertion or input take an added `intent` field. The 9 own tools:
  - planner_setup_page: sets up the page for test planning from a seed test file and a project.
  - planner_submit_plan: submits a structured test plan (overview, suites, tests, steps, expectations).
  - planner_save_plan: saves the test plan as a Markdown file.
  - generator_setup_page: sets up the page for a test from a plan and a seed file.
  - generator_read_log: returns the log of the performed test.
  - generator_write_test: writes the generated test code to a test file.
  - test_list: lists the tests.
  - test_run: runs tests by location and project and returns the output as text.
  - test_debug: runs one test by ID in debug mode, so that it pauses on errors.
- Search, kind `keyword`: browser_find (Playwright MCP, a core tool that is on by default). It does not search library docs. Inputs: text (a case-insensitive substring) or regex (case-sensitive, /…/flags allowed); maxResults; filename (to save the results to a file). One result is a matching node of the accessibility snapshot of the current page, with a few lines of context and its path from the root (it includes the element ref). Ranking: none by meaning; it matches strings or a regex in document order. It runs on the user's machine, in the local MCP server process. There is no documentation search tool.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: browser_take_screenshot: the agent gets the viewport, full page or element as an inline MCP image (when no filename is given, and unless imageResponses is "omit"), and the file is saved in the output directory. There is nothing to interact with. It needs the browser that the server starts or attaches to, which is a local process. browser_annotate (opt-in devtools): it spawns the Playwright Dashboard (lib/entry/dashboardApp.js) as a local process in annotation mode. The user draws annotations on the current page and submits them, and the tool returns the feedback text and the annotation boxes with text, and saves the annotated PNG and the ARIA snapshot as files. This view is a separate local app window, not an MCP Apps resource. No tool names a ui:// resource.
- Prompts and resources: none. The shared MCP server factory declares only the tools capability (with listChanged) and handles only the list-tools and call-tool requests. This applies to both server A and server B.
- Number of skills: 3 distinct skills. They live in playwright-core at lib/tools/skills/ (playwright-cli, playwright-component-testing, playwright-trace), and `npx playwright init-skills [--loop claude|agents]` installs all three. A second copy of playwright-cli ships in @playwright/cli 0.1.25 at skills/playwright-cli/ (installed with `playwright-cli install --skills`). That copy is a slightly newer text (identical …
- Skills:
  - playwright-cli: "Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests." The agent uses it to drive a browser through `playwright-cli` commands (open, goto, snapshot, click, fill, screenshot, network, storage, tracing, video, webmcp-list/webmcp-call, attach and others). It has references for tests, mocking, running code, sessions, storage state, test generation, tracing, video, PR attachments and element attributes.
  - playwright-component-testing: "Set up component testing with Playwright using a story gallery — scaffold stories and a gallery dev page driven by the built-in mount fixture, no dedicated component-testing runtime. Use when asked to test React or Vue components in isolation with Playwright, or to migrate off @playwright/experimental-ct-react / -vue."
  - playwright-trace: "Inspect Playwright trace files from the command line — list actions, view requests, console, errors, snapshots and screenshots." The agent uses it to debug a test trace .zip with `npx playwright trace …`.
- What the skills point at: The command line tool, not the MCP server. playwright-cli tells the agent to call `playwright-cli` commands (open, goto, snapshot, click, fill, type, press, screenshot, requests, route, cookie-*, localstorage-*, state-save/load, tracing-start/stop, video-start/stop, webmcp-list/webmcp-call, attach, run-code and others), or `npx playwright cli` as a fallback, and to install it with `npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest`. It also points to its own references/*.md files. playwright-trace calls `npx playwright trace open|actions|action|requests|request|console|errors|snapshot|attachments|close`. playwright-component-testing points to its references/ files (gallery-spec.md, react.md, vue.md, …
- Not confirmed: The exact shape of the dynamic WebMCP tools that server A exposes at runtime: the code shows that they come from the page (currentWebMCPTools), so they do not count as fixed tools. | Whether the test-runner server (B) is documented on playwright.dev. It is a hidden CLI command, and it was found only in the code and in the configs that init-agents writes. | The exact output format of each tool beyond its description and handler code. No tool was run.

#### PrimeTek (PrimeReact, PrimeVue, PrimeNG)
Checked: @primeng/mcp 22.1.5, @primevue/mcp 5.0.5, @primereact/mcp 11.2.3 (all published 2026-11-11, npm latest on 2026-11-20), shared core @primeuix/mcp 2.0.1 (2026-11-11); primefaces/primeui-plugins main at commit 06435556fab9eb948b46eb19f3718d754796270c … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: Three official servers, one for each library. All three are thin wrappers that call createPrimeMcpServer from the shared core @primeuix/mcp 2.0.1 (repository primefaces/primeuix-nextchapter, packages/mcp). (1) @primeng/mcp 22.1.5, bin primeng-mcp, repository primefaces/primeng-nextchapter packages/mcp, published 2026-11-11. (2) @primevue/mcp 5.0.5, bin primevue-mcp, repository primefaces/primevue-nextchapter packages/mcp, published 2026-11-11. (3) @primereact/mcp 11.2.3, bin primereact-mcp, repository primefaces/primereact-nextchapter packages/mcp, published 2026-11-11. Each one is a read-only server over stdio for the generated documentation, API data and examples that it bundles in its data/ folder (manifest.json, mcp-data.json, llms/). Node.js 22 or newer.
- Number of tools: 8 for @primeng/mcp, 8 for @primevue/mcp, 8 for @primereact/mcp. Source: the code that registers the tools, in the published dist/index.js of @primeuix/mcp 2.0.1 (eight registerTool calls; the wrappers contain no registerTool call). The core README and the PrimeVue documentation state the same eight.
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (registerTool in @primeuix/mcp 2.0.1 dist/index.js; the same eight tools in all three servers; annotations readOnlyHint true, destructiveHint false, idempotentHint true, openWorldHint false).
  - 1. list: "List generated components, guides, hooks, resources, examples, or modes." Input kind (components|guides|hooks|resources|examples|modes, default components), mode, limit (1-200, default 50), offset; returns {kind, total, limit, offset, items}.
  - 2. search: "Search generated component, guide, section, API, and example text." Input query, scope (all|components|guides|api|examples), mode, limit (1-50, default 10), offset; returns {query, total, results} with each result's type, title, description, resourceUri, publicUrl, matches, matchedTerms, nextCall and exampleSections.
  - 3. get_component: "Read generated component docs and metadata." Input component (or a batch 'components' of 1-10), mode, sections, includeApi, includeExamples, detail (compact|full); returns the component record or per-item batch results.
  - 4. get_guide: "Read generated guide docs and metadata." Input guide, mode, section, detail; returns the guide's name, title, description, route, resource URI, sections and, with detail full, the document text.
  - 5. get_example: "Return one source-backed example extracted from generated component docs." Input component, mode, section, variant; returns the code, its language, resourceUri, source and the available or suggested sections.
  - 6. get_setup: "Return source-backed setup or installation guidance from generated guide docs." Input environment, mode; returns the setup guide with its document, or valid environments and candidates.
  - 7. validate_usage: "Validate supplied component usage against generated component API metadata." Input component and code, mode (or a batch 'usages' of 1-10); returns valid and issues (codes such as invalid-enum-value, unknown-output), or per-item batch results.
  - 8. version: "Return server, docs data, tool, resource, and known manual metadata status." No input; returns server name and version, data schema/library/docs versions, generatedAt, sourceCommit, counts, the tool names and resource list.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool search. Input fields: query (string, required), scope (all|components|guides|api|examples, default all), mode (optional; for PrimeReact styled|tailwind|primitive|headless, inferred from query words when one matches), limit (1-50, default 10), offset. One result holds type (component, hook or guide), title, description, resourceUri, publicUrl where supplied, mode, matches (up to 5 snippets), matchedTerms, and for components nextCall (get_component arguments) and exampleSections. Ranking: a weighted word match over an in-memory index that the core builds lazily once per server instance from the bundled data. Fields and weights: name/title/route/mode/framework 8, description 4, section titles 3, API entries 3, document text 1. A whole-query substring hit adds 100 x weight; each matched query term adds the weight; a result needs a minimum share of matched terms (all for 1-2 terms, else at least 40 percent). Sort by score, then matched-term count, then title. No embedding model or external library is named in the code. It runs on the user's machine, in the local server process.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: Prompts (5, registered with registerPrompt, each with optional args component, goal, mode, and each telling the agent to read the llms.txt resource first): use_component "Use a PrimeUI component correctly in this app."; build_form "Build a form using PrimeUI form components."; theme_component "Customize a component with tokens, PT, classes, or styled mode."; migrate_primeui "Plan a PrimeUI version migration from source-backed docs."; audit_component_usage "Review app code for component API mismatches." Resources (base URI primeui://primeng, primeui://primevue or primeui://primereact): static index.json (MCP data index), llms.txt and llms-full.txt (generated documentation); resource templates component-docs (components/{component}.md, component Markdown docs), component-api (components/{component}/api.json, component API JSON), example-docs (examples/{component}/{section}/{variant}.md, source-backed examples), guide-docs (guides/{guide}.md, guide Markdown docs). For a library with modes (PrimeReact) the templates carry a {mode}/ segment.
- Number of skills: 20 skills for consumers, in the plugin marketplace repository github.com/primefaces/primeui-plugins (marketplace name primeui), under plugins/<lib>/skills/: 7 for PrimeNG, 7 for PrimeVue, 6 for PrimeReact (PrimeReact has no migration skill). The MCP npm packages contain no SKILL.md files. The PrimeVue documentation confirms the seven PrimeVue skills.
- Skills:
  - PrimeNG (plugins/primeng/skills):
  - 1. primeng-router: routes PrimeNG and Angular-specific PrimeUI work to exactly one focused PrimeNG skill; used first for PrimeNG requests, never for PrimeVue or PrimeReact.
  - 2. primeng-component-implementation: implements or discovers PrimeNG components in Angular code with MCP component metadata, routed examples, API resources and final usage validation; for components, templates, directives, forms, inputs, outputs and Table.
  - 3. primeng-setup-installation: sets up PrimeNG through standalone Angular ApplicationConfig, app.config.ts and providePrimeNG; for installation, environment aliases, providers and initial theme (NgModule setup unsupported).
  - 4. primeng-theming-customization: customizes PrimeNG with routed theming guidance; for presets, design tokens, styled or unstyled mode, Tailwind, pass-through and CSS layers.
  - 5. primeng-accessibility-icons: applies PrimeNG accessibility and icon guidance; for semantics, labels, focus, keyboard, PrimeIcons and custom icons.
  - 6. primeng-migration: migrates PrimeNG code with routed migration guidance; for supported version boundaries and deprecated-API cleanup.
  - 7. primeng-audit-troubleshooting: audits and troubleshoots PrimeNG code, repairs source-confirmed invalid Angular APIs, and diagnoses missing or duplicate MCP/plugin configuration with the PrimeUI doctor command.
  - PrimeVue (plugins/primevue/skills):
  - 8. primevue-router: routes PrimeVue and Vue-specific work to exactly one focused PrimeVue skill; never for PrimeNG or PrimeReact.
  - 9. primevue-component-implementation: implements or discovers PrimeVue components in Vue code with MCP metadata, routed examples and final usage validation; for components, pages, forms and directives.
  - 10. primevue-setup-installation: sets up PrimeVue in Vue, Vite or Nuxt apps; for installation, plugin or Nuxt module registration, initial theme and environment routing.
  - 11. primevue-theming-customization: customizes PrimeVue; for presets, design tokens, styled or unstyled mode, Tailwind, pass-through, slots, events and style APIs.
  - 12. primevue-accessibility-icons: applies PrimeVue accessibility and icon guidance.
  - 13. primevue-migration: migrates PrimeVue code with routed migration guidance and deprecated-API cleanup.
  - 14. primevue-audit-troubleshooting: audits and troubleshoots PrimeVue code and diagnoses MCP/plugin configuration with the PrimeUI doctor command.
  - PrimeReact (plugins/primereact/skills):
  - 15. primereact-router: routes PrimeReact work to exactly one focused skill after selecting a source-backed mode (styled, tailwind, primitive or headless); never for PrimeVue or PrimeNG.
  - 16. primereact-component-implementation: implements and discovers PrimeReact components or hooks with mode-scoped MCP metadata, examples and final validation.
  - 17. primereact-setup-installation: installs and configures PrimeReact with mode- and environment-scoped setup metadata; for React, Vite, Next.js, providers, aliases and CSS.
  - 18. primereact-theming-customization: customizes PrimeReact components and themes within one mode; for presets, tokens, Tailwind variants, primitive/headless styling and pass-through.
  - 19. primereact-accessibility-icons: applies mode-scoped PrimeReact accessibility and icon guidance.
  - 20. primereact-audit-troubleshooting: audits and troubleshoots PrimeReact code, repairs invalid mode-scoped APIs, and diagnoses MCP/plugin configuration with the PrimeUI doctor command.
- What the skills point at: The skills tell the agent to call the library's MCP server tools for all facts: get_component, get_example, search, list, get_guide, get_setup and validate_usage (with explicit call sequences and maximum call counts per scenario), and not to call version routinely. The three audit-troubleshooting skills also name a command line: primeui doctor --json --tool <tool> --library <lib>; the primeui command is the bin of the npm package @primeui/cli (1.2.7, 2026-11-16, "Command line tools for PrimeUI projects and assistant plugins"), which the PrimeVue docs also use for plugin install. Skills also tell the agent to inspect local project files (package.json, lockfile, app.config.ts, nuxt.config, …
- Not confirmed: The TypeScript source of @primeuix/mcp in primefaces/primeuix-nextchapter was not read; the tool list comes from the published dist/index.js and the README of 2.0.1. | Whether other official consumer skills exist outside primefaces/primeui-plugins (for example in the nextchapter library repositories) was not checked; the PrimeVue docs name only the seven plugin skills.

#### Prisma
Checked: Remote MCP server io.prisma/mcp server.json 1.1.0 (archived github.com/prisma/mcp, last commit 3cf8f9f 2026-10-26), with its tool list taken from the docs page read on 2026-11-20. Packages: prisma 8.0.0-rc.34 (npm latest, 2026-11-16) and prisma 7.10.1 (npm … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: (1) Remote hosted server https://mcp.prisma.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP; registry name io.prisma/mcp; server.json version 1.1.0). It manages Prisma Postgres databases, existing Prisma Compute apps and deployments, Object Storage and Composer topology, and it also searches the Prisma docs. You sign in with a Prisma account and pick a workspace. The server code is not public: the github.com/prisma/mcp repo is archived and holds only server.json, the README and a DXT wrapper (dxt/server/index.js only spawns the local `prisma mcp` CLI command). (2) The older local stdio server `prisma mcp` is a subcommand of the Prisma ORM CLI from 6.6 to 7.x. Its newest release is prisma 7.10.1 (2026-10-15, npm tag 'prev'). It runs Prisma ORM 7 migrate commands and Studio in the user's project. It is not in Prisma 8: no McpServer, registerTool or modelcontextprotocol string appears in the prisma@8.0.0-rc.34 package.
- Number of tools: Remote server mcp.prisma.io: 31 tools, counted from the documentation (the MCP tools reference page), because the source is not public. Local `prisma mcp` in prisma 7.10.1: 3 tools, counted from the code that registers them (three o.tool(...) calls in build/cli.js).
- Tools:
  - REMOTE SERVER (from the documentation, https://www.prisma.io/docs/ai/mcp-tools; 31 tools):
  - 1. fetch_workspace_details: fetches the details of the selected Prisma Postgres workspace.
  - 2. list_prisma_postgres_databases: returns a list of the Prisma Postgres databases in the user's workspace.
  - 3. create_prisma_postgres_database: creates a managed Prisma Postgres database and a new project.
  - 4. delete_prisma_postgres_database: permanently deletes a Prisma Postgres database by ID; it cannot delete a project's default database.
  - 5. list_prisma_postgres_connection_strings: returns the connection strings for a given database id.
  - 6. create_prisma_postgres_connection_string: creates a new connection string for a given Prisma Postgres database.
  - 7. delete_prisma_postgres_connection_string: deletes a connection string by its id.
  - 8. list_prisma_postgres_backups: lists the automated backups of a Prisma Postgres database.
  - 9. create_prisma_postgres_recovery: restores a Prisma Postgres database from a backup id into a new database.
  - 10. introspect_database_schema: reads the schema of a Prisma Postgres database and shows its structure.
  - 11. execute_sql_query: runs SQL that reads, modifies or deletes data in a Prisma Postgres database, without changing its schema.
  - 12. execute_prisma_postgres_schema_update: runs a schema update on a Prisma Postgres database by id.
  - 13. list_object_store_buckets: lists the Object Storage buckets in the workspace, optionally filtered by project id.
  - 14. create_object_store_bucket: creates a new Object Storage bucket in a project.
  - 15. delete_object_store_bucket: permanently deletes a bucket, all its objects and all its access keys.
  - 16. create_object_store_bucket_key: creates an S3-compatible access key for a bucket.
  - 17. delete_object_store_bucket_key: deletes a bucket access key, which stops working at once.
  - 18. search_prisma_documentation: answers a natural-language question about Prisma from the official docs and returns a cited answer with links to the docs.
  - 19. list_prisma_compute_apps: lists the Prisma Compute apps in the workspace, optionally filtered by project.
  - 20. list_prisma_compute_builds: lists builds, newest first, with optional project, branch and state filters.
  - 21. list_prisma_compute_deployments: lists the deployments of a Compute app, newest first.
  - 22. get_prisma_compute_deployment_logs: returns the runtime logs of a deployment, one page at a time.
  - 23. promote_prisma_compute_deployment: makes a running deployment the live version of an app.
  - 24. rollback_prisma_compute_app: makes an existing deployment live, and starts it first if it is stopped.
  - 25. start_prisma_compute_deployment: starts an existing deployment from a build that is already uploaded; it does not build or upload.
  - 26. stop_prisma_compute_deployment: stops a deployment and disconnects it from the public URL if it is live.
  - 27. delete_prisma_compute_deployment: permanently deletes a deployment, and stops it first if needed.
  - 28. delete_prisma_compute_app: permanently deletes an app; with deleteDeployments=true it also stops and deletes its deployments.
  - 29. set_prisma_compute_env_var: sets an environment variable for a project's production or preview environment, or overrides it for one preview branch; values are encrypted and never returned.
  - 30. delete_prisma_compute_env_var: permanently deletes an environment variable by ID.
  - 31. get_prisma_composer_topology: shows the saved connections between a project's Composer services and resources, with Console links and stored app URLs; it does not check whether the apps are running.
  - LOCAL `prisma mcp`, prisma 7.10.1 (from the code that registers the tools, build/cli.js; 3 tools). Each runs the Prisma CLI in the given projectCWD and returns its stdout and stderr as text:
  - 1. migrate-status: runs `prisma migrate status` and returns the state of the migrations in prisma/migrations compared with the _prisma_migrations table (input projectCWD).
  - 2. migrate-dev: runs `prisma migrate dev --name <name>`, which creates and applies a migration from schema changes and regenerates the artifacts (inputs name, projectCWD).
  - 3. Prisma-Studio: runs `prisma studio` to open Prisma Studio, a visual UI for the database data (input projectCWD).
  - (Note: the archived DXT manifest lists 7 older tool names, migrate-status, migrate-dev, migrate-reset, Prisma-Postgres-account-status, Create-Prisma-Postgres-Database, Prisma-Login and Prisma-Studio, for DXT version 0.1.0. The 7.10.1 code registers only 3.)
- Search, kind `intent`: Tool: search_prisma_documentation on the remote server. Input: a natural-language question; the docs do not publish the exact input field names. One result is a cited answer with links back to the Prisma docs, so the tool returns one generated answer rather than a ranked list. The source does not name the ranking or answer method (model, index or vendor). It runs on Prisma's hosted server (mcp.prisma.io), not on the user's machine.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool returns a ui:// resource or an image. The documented remote tools return text or data. The local 7.x tool Prisma-Studio runs `prisma studio`, which starts a local Studio process with its own browser UI, outside the MCP host. The tool returns only the command's text output.
- Prompts and resources: Local `prisma mcp` (7.10.1): none; the code registers only three tools and no prompt or resource. Remote server: not confirmed. The docs list only tools, and the source is not public.
- Number of skills: 14 skills for users: 11 in github.com/prisma/skills (installed with `npx skills add prisma/skills`; 2 of the 11 are deprecated compatibility names); 1 (prisma-8) shipped in each @prisma/orm-* package at package/skills/prisma-8 (the same SKILL.md in @prisma/orm-postgres, -sqlite, -mongo, -mysql and -mariadb 8.0.0-rc.24; only the metadata library line differs); 1 (prisma-composer-core-concepts) in …
- Skills:
  - 1. prisma-cli: a reference for the Prisma ORM 7 CLI (init, generate, migrate, db, dev, studio, mcp) for existing Prisma 7 apps; for setup or Prisma 8 the agent uses prisma-orm-setup instead.
  - 2. prisma-client-api: a Prisma Client API reference (model queries, filters, operators, client methods), used when the agent writes queries, CRUD, $transaction and similar code.
  - 3. prisma-compute: deploys and operates apps on Prisma Compute with the Prisma 8 CLI (prisma deploy, preview stages, git connect, service logs, rollback, env, domains), and helps port the removed prisma.compute.ts flow.
  - 4. prisma-database-setup: a deprecated compatibility name for prisma-orm-setup, used only when it is invoked by name.
  - 5. prisma-driver-adapter-implementation: a required reference for building or changing a Prisma ORM 7 SQL driver adapter (SqlDriverAdapter, Transaction, savepoints, DriverAdapterError).
  - 6. prisma-mongodb-upgrade: a decision and migration guide for MongoDB projects on Prisma 6, which have no path to v7, including the move to Prisma 8.
  - 7. prisma-orm-setup: sets up Prisma ORM, connects a database or repairs the connection of a Prisma 6, 7 or 8 app; new apps default to Prisma 8 and load the package-owned prisma-8 skill.
  - 8. prisma-postgres-setup: gets or reuses a Prisma Postgres database (including create-db, v0 and the Vercel Marketplace) and connects an app; it hands ORM configuration to prisma-orm-setup.
  - 9. prisma-postgres-upgrade: upgrades a PostgreSQL app from Prisma 6 or 7 to Prisma 8 in one pass and keeps the existing schema and data.
  - 10. prisma-postgres: a deprecated compatibility name for prisma-postgres-setup, used only when it is invoked by name.
  - 11. prisma-upgrade-v7: a migration guide from Prisma v6 to v7 that covers all breaking changes, used when the agent upgrades or meets v7 errors.
  - 12. prisma-8: everything for Prisma ORM 8 projects (@prisma/orm-postgres, -sqlite, -mongo): contract authoring, contract emit, migrations, db.orm/db.sql/db.query queries, db.ts and middleware, build tools, Supabase/RLS, dotted error codes, and upgrades within Prisma 8 of an app or an extension.
  - 13. prisma-composer-core-concepts: used when the agent deploys or manages an app that uses Prisma Composer: wiring services and Modules, running locally, testing composed services, and standing up or tearing down an environment.
  - 14. prisma-platform-core-concepts: used when the agent hosts, deploys or operates an app on the Prisma Platform: projects, branches, preview environments, services and versions, Postgres databases, buckets, env vars, domains, logs and the GitHub integration.
- What the skills point at: Files in the installed package: prisma-orm-setup tells the agent to run `prisma skills sync` and then read the synced prisma-8/SKILL.md (for example .agents/skills/prisma-8/SKILL.md). prisma-8 routes each task to bundled files such as references/quickstart.md, references/contract.md, references/migrations.md, references/queries.md, references/debug.md, references/upgrade-app.md and upgrading/app/upgrades/. The prisma/skills skills point to their own references/*.md. CLI commands: prisma-8 names prisma contract emit, db init, db update, migration plan, db migrate, db verify and db sign; prisma-compute names prisma deploy, prisma git connect, prisma service, and project env; …
