#### Pulumi (infrastructure as code)
Checked: MCP server: hosted at https://mcp.ai.pulumi.com/mcp, no version number published and no public source; tool list as the docs show it on 2026-11-20. Skills: github.com/pulumi/agent-skills at commit cd1011fcefe65a980b09a4810bf8506df436d572 (2026-11-17, still … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One current official server: the hosted remote Pulumi MCP server at https://mcp.ai.pulumi.com/mcp (streamable HTTP with OAuth, or a bearer token with an X-Pulumi-Org header). It has no version number; the docs were read on 2026-11-20. It is for querying stacks, resources, policy results and users in Pulumi Cloud, looking up provider schemas in the Pulumi Registry, giving AWS deploy instructions, and delegating tasks to Pulumi Neo. Historical: the local npm package @pulumi/mcp-server, latest 0.2.0 (2025-09-26), has tools named pulumi-registry-* and pulumi-cli-*. Its repository github.com/pulumi/mcp-server now returns 404, and the current setup guide does not mention the package. This record does not count it.
- Number of tools: 14 for the hosted server at https://mcp.ai.pulumi.com/mcp. The count comes from the documentation: 4 Pulumi Cloud tools, 4 task tools, 5 Registry tools and 1 code generation tool. No source code is public.
- Tools:
  - Source: documentation (the server is closed source).
  - 1. get-stacks: lists the stacks in your organization.
  - 2. resource-search: searches resources across all stacks with Pulumi resource search queries, such as `package:aws` or `-.tags:`, and returns the matching resources.
  - 3. get-policy-violations: lists the policy-as-code violations for your stacks.
  - 4. get-users: lists the members of your organization and their roles.
  - 5. neo-bridge: starts a Neo task in Pulumi Cloud, sends it follow-up messages, and approves or rejects its requests; returns a link to the task in the Pulumi Cloud console.
  - 6. neo-get-tasks: lists your organization's agent tasks and their status.
  - 7. neo-continue-task: checks the status of an existing task and returns its latest events.
  - 8. neo-reset-conversation: clears the server's tracked state for one task or for all tasks.
  - 9. list-resources: lists the resource types in a provider or module.
  - 10. list-functions: lists the functions in a provider or module.
  - 11. get-resource: returns a resource's properties and documentation.
  - 12. get-function: returns a function's inputs, outputs and documentation.
  - 13. get-type: returns the JSON schema for a type reference.
  - 14. deploy-to-aws: returns step-by-step instructions that the agent follows to analyze the application and write Pulumi code that deploys it to AWS.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool: resource-search. Input: a resource search query in Pulumi's field-based query syntax, for example `package:aws` or `-.tags:` (resources without tags). A result is a resource from the organization's stacks; the exact result fields are not documented on the MCP page. Matching runs on Pulumi Cloud's resource search, which needs the Essentials, Pro or Enterprise edition, and not on the user's machine. The docs name no ranking method, model or index. The server has no search over documentation.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No documented tool returns a ui:// resource or an image. neo-bridge returns only a link to the task in the Pulumi Cloud console.
- Prompts and resources: Prompts (6): deploy-to-aws, deploys application code to AWS by generating a Pulumi program; convert-terraform-to-typescript, converts Terraform HCL to a Pulumi TypeScript program; cdk-migration-plan, plans a migration from the AWS CDK to Pulumi; cdk-migration-automated, migrates a CDK app to Pulumi with automated conversion; cdk-migration-manual, migrates a CDK app to Pulumi by hand; cdk-migration-troubleshoot, troubleshoots a CDK-to-Pulumi migration. Resources: none are documented.
- Number of skills: 17 end-user skills in github.com/pulumi/agent-skills: 11 in pulumi/skills, 5 in migration/skills and 1 in delegation/skills. They install through Claude Code and Codex plugins (the combined `pulumi` plugin, whose plugin.json lists ./pulumi/skills, ./migration/skills and ./delegation/skills, holds all 17), a Gemini CLI extension, or `npx skills add`. The same repository has 2 more skills in …
- Skills:
  - End-user skills (17):
  - 1. pulumi-overview: the entry point for any task that creates, changes, inspects or destroys cloud infrastructure or SaaS configuration, including when Pulumi is not named; covers `pulumi do`, IaC projects and Pulumi Cloud, and routes to the specialized skills.
  - 2. pulumi-best-practices: loaded when writing, reviewing or debugging Pulumi TypeScript or Python programs (Output<T>, apply(), aliases, secrets and config, preview/up CI workflows, dependencies).
  - 3. pulumi-component: a guide for authoring ComponentResource classes, used when designing, building, adding multi-language support to, or distributing reusable components.
  - 4. pulumi-automation-api: loaded when the user wants to run Pulumi programmatically, embed it in an application, orchestrate several stacks in code, or use LocalWorkspace or inline programs.
  - 5. pulumi-esc: guidance on Pulumi ESC environments, secrets, configuration, OIDC short-term credentials and secret-store integrations.
  - 6. pulumi-debug-failed-operation: debugs a failed `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview` from the failure that Pulumi Cloud already recorded, finds the cause and fixes it.
  - 7. provider-upgrade: upgrades any Pulumi provider to a newer version and reconciles the resulting diff, checking for breaking changes and unexpected replacements.
  - 8. package-usage: tracks which stacks across an organization use a package and at which versions, for cross-stack audits and planning upgrades.
  - 9. pulumi-context-api: queries the Pulumi Context API graph for relationship, blast-radius and impact questions across an organization's infrastructure.
  - 10. pulumi-create-agent: creates a reusable Pulumi Agent with saved instructions, a role and selected integrations when the user asks to set one up.
  - 11. pulumi-setup-agent-automation: creates a schedule or event trigger for an existing Pulumi Agent, or pauses or resumes an automation.
  - 12. pulumi-terraform-to-pulumi: migrates Terraform or OpenTofu projects to Pulumi, translating HCL and/or importing Terraform state.
  - 13. pulumi-cdk-to-pulumi: migrates an AWS CDK application to Pulumi when the user asks for a migration.
  - 14. cloudformation-to-pulumi: converts, migrates or imports AWS CloudFormation stacks or templates into Pulumi programs.
  - 15. pulumi-arm-to-pulumi: converts or migrates Azure ARM or Bicep templates to Pulumi, including importing existing Azure resources.
  - 16. pulumi-migrate-from-discovered-stack: migrates a CloudFormation or ARM stack that Pulumi Cloud Discovery has already found, through the discovered-stacks API.
  - 17. pulumi-neo-handoff: hands the current thread to a new Pulumi Neo task as a one-way transfer, only when the user asks for it.
  - Not counted (package-maintenance, for provider authors): pulumi-upgrade-provider, which automates provider repository upgrades with the `upgrade-provider` tool; upstream-patches, which creates, amends, removes and rebases Terraform provider submodule patches with `./scripts/upstream.sh`.
- What the skills point at: The skills point to the Pulumi CLI and to web addresses, not to the Pulumi MCP server; a grep of the repository found none of its tool names or its address. (pulumi-create-agent and pulumi-setup-agent-automation mention MCP only as the external MCP integrations that a Pulumi Agent can select.) CLI commands: `pulumi api` (Pulumi Cloud REST endpoints, used in pulumi-debug-failed-operation and package-usage), `pulumi do` and `npx pulumi` (pulumi-overview), `pulumi env init/edit/set/get/open/run` (pulumi-esc), `pulumi neo` (pulumi-neo-handoff), and `pulumi preview`, `pulumi up`, `pulumi refresh`, `pulumi import` and `pulumi package`. For the migration skills, AWS CLI `aws cloudcontrol` commands …
- Not confirmed: The source code of the hosted MCP server: it is not public, so the tool count rests on the documentation only. | A version number or release date for the hosted MCP server. | The result fields and ranking method of resource-search; the docs name the query syntax but no ranking or index. | Whether the hosted server declares any MCP resources; the docs list none. | Whether the old @pulumi/mcp-server npm package is formally deprecated: npm shows no deprecation flag, but its repository returns 404 and the current docs do not mention it.

#### Qt
Checked: agent-skills repository at commit 062f7c9f0e16b7d2f66cd55e449a3ed85fba699e (2026-11-09), plugin qt-development-skills 1.8.1; Qt Documentation MCP registry version 0.4.0 (published 2026-11-09, isLatest true); QML Live Preview MCP server shipped with Qt 6.12 … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: Three official servers. (1) Qt Documentation MCP: hosted remote at https://qt-docs-mcp.qt.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP), registry name io.qt.qt-docs-mcp/qt-documentation, newest version 0.4.0 (2026-11-09); for looking up Qt documentation. The repository README and mcp/qt-documentation-mcp/README.md call it 'io.qt/qt-documentation-mcp', which differs from the registry name. (2) QML Live Preview MCP server (binary QmlPreviewMcpServer): local stdio server that ships with Qt 6.12 and later through the Qt Online Installer under 'Agentic Development Tools'; it starts a Qt Quick app with hot reload of QML edits. No version number other than 'Qt 6.12 or later'. (3) Qt Creator MCP Server (server name 'qt-creator-mcp-server'): an extension built into the Qt Creator IDE, open source in the qt-creator repository (src/plugins/mcpserver plus MCP support files in other plugins), version equal to the Qt Creator version, newest final release 20.0.2; it lets an agent control the IDE for editing files, building, running, testing and debugging projects. Not counted as servers of the Qt framework: the MCP servers of separate Qt Group products (Squish MCP, Coco MCP server preview, Axivion MCP, the MCP server inside Clate).
- Number of tools: Qt Documentation MCP: 2 (documentation; source not public, hosted). QML Live Preview MCP: 1 (documentation; binary only, no public source in the agent-skills repository). Qt Creator MCP Server: 64 at v20.0.2 (code that registers the tools: ToolRegistry::registerTool calls in src/plugins/mcpserver/mcpcommands.cpp 21, projectexplorer/mcpsupport.cpp 17, autotest/mcptools.cpp 5, …
- Tools:
  - Qt Documentation MCP (from the documentation):
  - qt_documentation_search: searches the Qt documentation by query or keywords, with optional version, intent, module, filter and max_results (1 to 10, default 3); returns a ranked list of matching documentation excerpts, each with a page filename that qt_documentation_read accepts.
  - qt_documentation_read: takes a filename from the search results (for example qobject.html) and an optional version; returns the full content of that page as text.
  - QML Live Preview MCP (from the documentation):
  - run-qmlpreview (README spelling; the blog spells it run_qmlPreview): takes the absolute path of an already built executable and starts the Qt Quick app with live preview (hot reload).
  - Qt Creator MCP Server v20.0.2 (from the code that registers the tools):
  - open_file: opens a file in Qt Creator, optionally at a line and column.
  - file_plain_text: returns the content of a file as plain text, also on remote devices.
  - set_file_plain_text: overwrites the content of a file with given text (does not save an open file).
  - save_file: saves a file in Qt Creator.
  - close_file: closes a file in Qt Creator.
  - search_in_file: searches a text pattern in one file and returns matches with line, column and text.
  - search_in_directory: searches a text pattern recursively in a directory and returns matches.
  - replace_in_file: replaces all matches of a pattern in one file.
  - replace_in_directory: replaces all matches of a pattern recursively in a directory.
  - list_open_files: lists the open files.
  - list_visible_files: lists the files visible in an editor.
  - list_sessions: lists the available sessions.
  - load_session: loads a session.
  - quit: quits Qt Creator.
  - get_current_session: returns the active session.
  - save_session: saves the current session.
  - execute_command: runs a command and returns exit code, standard output and error.
  - find_actions: finds IDE actions that match a query string.
  - call_action: calls an IDE action by its ID.
  - create_new_file: creates a new file at a path, optionally with text, and its parent directories.
  - reformat_file: reformats a file with Qt Creator's formatting rules.
  - build: builds the chosen or startup project, waits, and returns a verdict with error and warning counts and issues.
  - list_issues: lists current warnings and errors.
  - list_file_issues: lists current warnings and errors for one file.
  - run_project: runs the startup project, streams progress, and returns its output.
  - debug: starts a debug session for the startup project and returns once it has launched.
  - search_in_files: searches a text pattern in project files that match a file pattern.
  - replace_in_files: replaces a text pattern in project files that match a file pattern.
  - get_build_status: returns build progress and status.
  - find_files_in_projects: finds files that match a pattern in a project.
  - list_projects: lists the open projects.
  - list_build_configs: lists the build configurations.
  - switch_build_config: switches to a build configuration.
  - get_current_project: returns the active project.
  - get_current_build_config: returns the active build configuration.
  - known_repositories_in_projects: lists version-control repositories in the open projects.
  - project_dependencies: lists the dependencies of all projects.
  - get_run_configurations: returns the run configurations and which one is active.
  - run_tests: builds if needed and runs autotests, returning counts and failed and warning test names.
  - get_last_test_results: returns a summary of the most recent test run.
  - get_test_status: reports whether a test run is in progress and whether results exist.
  - get_test_details: returns status, failure message, location, duration and log of named tests.
  - list_tests: lists the test classes and functions that Autotest knows.
  - get_breakpoints: returns all breakpoints.
  - get_threads: returns the threads of the debug session.
  - select_thread: switches the current thread.
  - get_variables: returns the local variables of the current frame, optionally with watches.
  - get_variable: returns one variable by its iname, with children.
  - set_variable: changes the value of a variable.
  - add_watch_expression: adds a watch expression and returns its iname.
  - remove_watch_expression: removes a watch expression.
  - get_call_stack: returns the call stack.
  - select_frame: switches the current stack frame.
  - delete_breakpoint: deletes a breakpoint by ID.
  - add_breakpoint: adds a breakpoint.
  - debugger_step_over: steps over the current line.
  - debugger_step_in: steps into the next call.
  - debugger_step_out: steps out of the current function.
  - debugger_continue: resumes execution to the next breakpoint.
  - debugger_interrupt: pauses the running debuggee.
  - debugger_get_status: returns whether a session is active, its state and position.
  - evaluate_expression: evaluates an expression in the paused session and returns value and type.
  - stop_debug: stops the debug session.
  - get_qt_directory: returns the installation prefix, version, bin, header and library paths of the active kit's Qt.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: Qt Documentation MCP, tool qt_documentation_search. Inputs: query (string, for example "QTimer" or "signal slot"); keywords (array, 'multi-term OR matching'); at least one of query and keywords; version (default latest); intent (enum: api, tutorial, guide, concept, example, migration; a result-priority category, not a free-text intent); module; filter (all, class, qml, function, guide); max_results (1 to 10, default 3). One result: a documentation excerpt with a page reference (filename such as qobject.html); the full result schema is not documented. Ranking: the blog says it accepts 'a natural-language or keyword query' and queries 'an index built from Qt's official documentation corpus'; it names no model or library, so meaning-based ranking is not confirmed. Runs on Qt's hosted server qt-docs-mcp.qt.io. Qt Creator MCP Server: search_in_file, search_in_directory and search_in_files match a text pattern (with line, column and matched text per result) and find_files_in_projects matches a file pattern; find_actions matches IDE actions to a query string. These are word or pattern matches over the user's local files, run on the user's machine inside Qt Creator; they do not search documentation.
- User interface from a tool, kind `other`: run-qmlpreview (run_qmlPreview): the user sees the real Qt Quick app running in a native window on their machine, and QML edits are hot-reloaded into it; the user can use the running app and give the agent feedback on the live UI. It needs a local process: the tool starts the user's built executable (Qt 6.12 or later, built with QT_QML_DEBUG) through Qt's qmlpreview service. The documentation does not say that it returns a ui:// resource or an image. No tool of the Qt Documentation MCP or of the Qt Creator MCP Server v20.0.2 returns user interface (no tool returns an image or a ui:// resource in the registering code).
- Prompts and resources: Qt Creator MCP Server v20.0.2 (from code): no prompts. Resources: each file opened in an editor is added as a resource (name = file name, uri = file URL, removed when the editor closes); a resource template 'Local files' (file:///{path}, 'Access local files by URI'); one resource template per device (for example docker:// or ssh:// roots) to read files on that device; a fallback reads any file or lists any directory by URI. Qt Documentation MCP and QML Live Preview MCP: not confirmed; their documentation lists tools only and their source is not public.
- Number of skills: 13 skills, at skills/<name>/SKILL.md in github.com/TheQtCompanyRnD/agent-skills (public copy; the README points to Gerrit codereview.qt-project.org/qtai/qtaiskills as canonical). They ship as the Claude Code plugin qt-development-skills 1.8.1 (marketplace qt-skills-and-tools) and as the Gemini extension qt-ai-skills 1.8.1. All 13 are for users of Qt. Not counted: agents/cpp-review-agent.md and …
- Skills:
  - qt-cpp-review: runs deterministic linting (60+ rules), then deep-analysis agents, on Qt6 C++ code and reports high-confidence issues read-only; used when the user asks to review, check or audit Qt C++ code, or before a commit.
  - qt-qml-review: runs deterministic QML linting (48+ rules, optionally with system qmllint), then deep-analysis agents, on bindings, layout, loaders, delegates, states and performance, read-only; used when the user asks to review QML code, or before a commit.
  - qt-qml: applies QML best practices when writing, fixing, refactoring, optimizing or debugging QML code (not for purely conversational QML questions).
  - qt-canvas2d: applies Qt Canvas2D (Qt 6.12+) best practices for GPU-accelerated imperative 2D drawing in QML, including porting Qt Quick Canvas or HTML5 canvas code; used whenever Canvas2D or its types are the subject.

Purpose: creating, running and developing Quarkus applications from a coding agent (scaffolding, dev-mode lifecycle, proxy to the running app's Dev MCP server, extension skills, local semantic doc search, project update). Note: the running Quarkus app's own Dev MCP server is a separate, dynamic tool set that this server proxies; it is not counted here.
- Number of tools: 18 tools in Quarkus Agent MCP 1.2.15, counted from the @Tool(name=...) annotations in src/main/java (same 18 at main). The README tool reference lists 17 (it omits quarkus_update). When agent-mcp.mode is not dev, StartupObserver removes quarkus_searchTools, quarkus_callTool and quarkus_browser; with agent-mcp.tools.browser.enabled=false, BrowserToolFilter leaves quarkus_browser out of the list.
- Tools:
  - From the code that registers the tools (Quarkus Agent MCP 1.2.15):
  - 1. quarkus_create (CreateTools.java): creates a new Quarkus app (outputDir, groupId, artifactId, extensions, buildTool, quarkusVersion, platform BOM, noCode, noWrapper, port, profiles), generates AGENTS.md and auto-starts it in dev mode; returns the result with a skill index and a hint to call quarkus_skills.
  - 2. quarkus_update (UpdateTools.java): runs the Quarkus update tool (OpenRewrite recipes) on a project to a target stream, with dryRun and extra recipes; returns the update output or preview.
  - 3. quarkus_start (LifecycleTools.java): starts a Quarkus app in dev mode (Maven or Gradle auto-detected, port, profiles, extra args) and blocks until ready or failed; returns the status.
  - 4. quarkus_attach (LifecycleTools.java): attaches to an app already running in dev mode after checking its Dev MCP server answers; returns success or failure.
  - 5. quarkus_stop (LifecycleTools.java): stops a managed app (only detaches an attached app); returns confirmation.
  - 6. quarkus_restart (LifecycleTools.java): force-restarts a managed app and blocks until ready; returns the status.
  - 7. quarkus_browser (LifecycleTools.java): opens the app or the Dev UI in the local browser; returns confirmation text.
  - 8. quarkus_status (LifecycleTools.java): returns the state of an app (not started, starting, running with port, crashed or stopped).
  - 9. quarkus_logs (LifecycleTools.java): returns recent log lines (default 50) of a managed app.
  - 10. quarkus_list (LifecycleTools.java): lists all managed Quarkus instances with their status.
  - 11. quarkus_searchTools (DevMcpProxyTools.java): discovers tools on the running app's Dev MCP server, filtered by a case-insensitive query on name or description; returns the matching tools as JSON with their schemas.
  - 12. quarkus_callTool (DevMcpProxyTools.java): invokes a Dev MCP tool by name with JSON arguments on the running app; returns that tool's result.
  - 13. quarkus_skills (DevMcpProxyTools.java): returns coding skills (patterns, testing guidelines, configuration) for the project's extensions, read from extension JARs without the app running; the query (comma- or space-separated) filters skills by name or description, with an optional module; without query it lists the skills.
  - 14. quarkus_updateSkill (DevMcpProxyTools.java): creates or updates a global skill customization (enhance or override) in ~/.quarkus/skills/; returns confirmation.
  - 15. quarkus_saveSkill (DevMcpProxyTools.java): writes a composed extension skill as a standalone file to the project's .agent/skills/ (does not overwrite an existing local skill); returns the path.
  - 16. quarkus_searchDocs (DocSearchTools.java): semantic search over Quarkus and extension documentation matched to the project's Quarkus version; returns JSON chunks with score, text and metadata.
  - 17. quarkus_app_log (AppLogTools.java): enables, disables or reads file logging of a managed app; returns lines (default 100) or confirmation.
  - 18. quarkus_agent_log (AgentLogTools.java): enables, disables or reads the MCP server's own log file; returns lines (default 100) or confirmation.
- Search, kind `both`: (1) quarkus_searchDocs: inputs query (required, natural language), maxResults (default 4, max 50), projectDir (selects docs of the project's extensions and Quarkus version), extension (restricts to one extension). One result: score, text of a doc chunk, and metadata (title, repo_path, topics, categories, section_title, section_path, summary). Ranking: the query is embedded with BGE Small EN v1.5 (384 dimensions), 50 candidates matched by vector similarity in pgvector (min-score 0.82), then rescored by word matches of query terms in metadata (title +0.15, topics +0.15, repo_path +0.10, categories +0.10, section +0.08, summary +0.05; synonyms +0.12/+0.08), a +0.15 boost for modern REST guides and -0.50 penalties for legacy RESTEasy and internal docs. Where it runs: on the user's machine, in a Docker/Podman container started by the server (ghcr.io/quarkusio/quarkus-agent-pgvector:pg17 with an embedding server on port 9222; older versions use ghcr.io/quarkusio/chappie-ingestion-quarkus images), or an existing database given by AGENT_MCP_DOC_SEARCH_PG_HOST (agent-mcp.doc-search.pg-host). (2) quarkus_searchTools: inputs projectDir, query; a case-insensitive word filter on tool name or description over the running app's Dev MCP tools; runs locally. (3) quarkus_skills also filters skills by query tokens on name or description.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool returns an image or a ui:// resource (no ImageContent or ui:// in src/main/java). quarkus_browser only opens the app or the Dev UI in the user's local browser, needs the running dev-mode process, and returns text.
- Prompts and resources: none. No @Prompt, @Resource or @ResourceTemplate in src/main/java at 1.2.15. The server declares server instructions (quarkus.mcp.server.server-info.instructions) with workflows for new projects, existing projects and Spring Boot migration.

#### Quasar
Checked: @quasar/mcp 1.1.0 (npm, published 2026-09-22T08:16Z; 1.0.0 on 2026-09-17), the newest on 2026-11-20; it serves the docs of quasar 2.35.5 and @quasar/app-vite 3.10.4 (both newest on npm on 2026-11-20). Repo checked at quasarframework/quasar dev d4a958ce … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: One official server: npm package @quasar/mcp (bin quasar-mcp), newest version 1.1.0 (2026-09-22), source in the monorepo folder mcp/. It is a local stdio server that gives agents the Quasar documentation pages and component API of the exact quasar and @quasar/app-vite versions installed in the project, read offline from their dist/mcp and dist/api folders.
- Number of tools: 6 (@quasar/mcp 1.1.0). Source: the code that registers the tools, six server.registerTool calls in src/server.js; the README and the AI Agents docs page list the same six.
- Tools:
  - From the code that registers the tools (mcp/src/server.js, @quasar/mcp 1.1.0):
  - 1. list_pages: lists every documentation page available offline, giving route, title and approximate size, grouped by the installed package that ships it; it can filter to one package and can add one-line descriptions.
  - 2. search_docs: finds documentation pages by keywords and returns up to `limit` hits (default 5, max 50), each with route, title, size, description and the sections where the keywords occur.
  - 3. get_page: returns the markdown of one documentation page by route or quasar.dev URL, or only one section (by heading or #anchor), or only its outline of headings.
  - 4. list_api: returns the names of all API descriptors that get_api accepts (components such as QBtn, plugins such as Notify, directives such as Ripple, and utilities).
  - 5. get_api: returns the API of one Quasar component, plugin or directive as installed (props, slots, events, methods with types, defaults and descriptions), whole or for one part or one member, as markdown the way the site shows it or as raw JSON.
  - 6. check_updates: queries the npm registry and returns whether newer releases of quasar, @quasar/app-vite or @quasar/mcp exist, with a line on how to upgrade.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool search_docs. Inputs: query (string, keywords, e.g. "table pagination"), package (optional enum: quasar or @quasar/app-vite), limit (optional int 1-50, default 5), and app (only in a workspace with several Quasar apps). One result: page route, title, approximate size, the page's one-line description, and the list of sections where the terms occur. Ranking: hand-written lexical scoring in mcp/src/docs.js (searchDocs), no library and no model: query split into terms, a simple stemmer and prefix matching (min three characters); per term a subject score, the maximum of title (60 or 20), component names (60), description (10) and route (5), plus a mention score from headings (15) and body occurrences (log-scaled, capped at 12); mention scores are multiplied by an IDF-style weight log((pages+1)/pagesWith); every term must match. Runs on the user's machine, offline, over the markdown files in the project's node_modules.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none (every tool returns text content only; no ui:// resource, no image)
- Prompts and resources: none. The server registers no prompts and no resources (no registerPrompt or registerResource in src). It does send server instructions at initialization (buildInstructions): the installed versions served, missing packages, other workspace apps, a suggested workflow (search_docs, then get_page with section, get_api) and available updates.
- Number of skills: 0. The repository (dev d4a958ce) holds one SKILL.md, .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md, which is for maintainers (release notes and version bumps of the monorepo packages), so it is left out. The published packages quasar 2.35.5, @quasar/app-vite 3.10.4 and @quasar/mcp 1.1.0 contain no SKILL.md, and the AI Agents docs page names no skills; the consumer guidance is the MCP server, dist/mcp …
- Skills:
  - none (no consumer skills)
- What the skills point at: none (no consumer skills). For comparison only, the server's own instructions point the agent to its tools: 'Prefer these tools over memory or the web: the pages match the installed versions exactly.'

- MCP servers: Three official Redis MCP servers. (3) Redis Cloud remote MCP, address https://cloud.mcp.redis.io/mcp, hosted, no version (page dated 2026-11-10): manages the resources of a Redis Cloud account. The docs also name a local Redis Cloud MCP server and an MCP endpoint for each Agent Memory store. This record does not cover those two.

Its server source is not public. redis-mcp-server 0.5.1: 53, counted from the @mcp.tool() decorators in src/tools/*.py (rechecked: list 7, hash 7, misc 7, stream 7, query engine 6, pub_sub 5, json 3, set 3, sorted set 3, server management 3, string 2). …
- Tools:
  - REDIS DOCS MCP (source: documentation and the quoted tool descriptions; the server code is not public):
  - search(query): searches the Redis docs by free-text query and returns up to 8 matching pages (in fact sections), each with a snippet and a stable id.
  - fetch(id): returns the full text and metadata (title, canonical URL, body, topic/version/section) of one docs page or section, by an id from search or from ask's sources.
  - ask(question): answers a natural-language Redis question with a grounded prose answer and its source documents (sources[].id).
  - REDIS-MCP-SERVER 0.5.1 (source: the code that registers the tools, src/tools/*.py):
  - string: set(key,value,expiration) sets a string value with optional expiry; get(key) returns a string value.
  - hash: hset(name,key,value,expire_seconds) sets a hash field with optional expiry; hget(name,key) returns a field's value; hdel(name,key) deletes a field; hgetall(name) returns all fields and values as a dict; hexists(name,key) returns whether a field exists; set_vector_in_hash(name,vector,vector_field) stores a vector as a binary field; get_vector_from_hash(name,vector_field) returns a stored vector decoded from its blob.
  - json: json_set(name,path,value,expire_seconds) sets a JSON value at a path; json_get(name,path) returns the JSON value at a path; json_del(name,path) deletes the JSON value at a path.
  - list: lpush(name,value,expire) pushes values on the left; rpush(name,value,expire) pushes values on the right; lpop(name) removes and returns the first element; rpop(name) removes and returns the last element; lrange(name,start,stop) returns the elements in a range; llen(name) returns the list length; lrem(name,count,element) removes matching elements.
  - set: sadd(name,value,expire_seconds) adds a member; srem(name,value) removes a member; smembers(name) returns all members.
  - sorted set: zadd(key,score,member,expiration) adds a scored member; zrange(key,start,end,with_scores) returns a range of members, with scores if asked; zrem(key,member) removes a member.
  - stream: xadd(key,fields,expiration) adds an entry; xrange(key,count) reads entries; xdel(key,entry_id) deletes an entry; xgroup_create(key,group_name,start_id,mkstream) creates a consumer group; xgroup_destroy(key,group_name) destroys a consumer group; xreadgroup(key,group_name,consumer_name,count,block_ms,stream_id) reads entries through a consumer group; xack(key,group_name,entry_ids) acknowledges processed entries.
  - pub/sub: publish(channel,message) publishes a message; subscribe(channel) subscribes and returns a reusable subscription handle; psubscribe(pattern) subscribes by pattern and returns a handle; read_messages(subscription_id,timeout_ms,max_messages) returns pending messages for a subscription; unsubscribe(subscription_id) closes a subscription.
  - keys and misc: delete(key) deletes a key; type(key) returns the type of the value at a key; expire(name,expire_seconds) sets a key's expiry; rename(old_key,new_key) renames a key; scan_keys(pattern,count,cursor) runs one SCAN step and returns keys plus a cursor; scan_all_keys(pattern,batch_size) returns all keys that match a pattern over several SCAN steps; search_redis_documents(question) sends a question to the Redis docs search API (default https://redis.io/convai/api/docs/search) and returns a list of documentation results.
  - query engine: get_indexes() lists the search indexes in the database; get_index_info(index_name) returns an index's schema and info from FT.INFO; get_indexed_keys_number(index_name) returns how many keys an index holds; create_vector_index_hash(index_name,prefix,vector_field,dim,distance_metric) creates an HNSW vector index on hashes; vector_search_hash(query_vector,index_name,vector_field,k,return_fields) runs a KNN vector search over hashes and returns the matches; hybrid_search(query_vector,filter_expression,index_name,vector_field,k,return_fields) runs a KNN search combined with a filter expression.
  - server management: dbsize() returns the number of keys; info(section) returns server information and statistics; client_list() returns the connected clients.
  - (53 tools)
  - REDIS CLOUD REMOTE MCP (source: documentation):
  - search_tools: searches for the Redis Cloud tool that the agent needs and returns it (the docs give no result format).
  - call_tool: calls the Redis Cloud tool that search_tools found. It can view and create, update or delete Redis Cloud Essentials subscriptions and databases and Agent Memory stores; it can only view Redis Cloud Pro subscriptions and databases, plans, regions, payment methods and cloud accounts. Some changes return a task whose status the agent can check.
  - call_ui_tool: only for clients that support MCP Apps; opens interactive views such as Agent Memory store metrics.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: Docs MCP search: input `query` (free text). Up to 8 results; each holds a snippet, a page url and an id. Ids address sections or index windows, such as develop/clients/jedis/connect#sec:configure-a-connection-pool-w0. Results come back in relevance order. No source names the ranking method (model, index or library). The ranking runs on Redis's server (redis.io), not on the user's machine. The companion tool ask(question) takes natural language and is answered by a language model: the skill says query text from ask reaches "the model provider behind the gateway too". redis-mcp-server search_redis_documents: input `question` (a natural-language question). It sends a GET with q=question to MCP_DOCS_SEARCH_URL (default https://redis.io/convai/api/docs/search) and returns that API's JSON list of documentation results. The ranking runs on Redis's server and its method is not stated. The data tools vector_search_hash and hybrid_search run KNN over the user's own database, not over the docs.
- User interface from a tool, kind `mcp-apps`: call_ui_tool (Redis Cloud remote MCP only): the user sees interactive views, for example the metrics of an Agent Memory store. The docs do not say what the user can do in a view or name a ui:// resource. The server is hosted at cloud.mcp.redis.io and needs no local dev server. The Docs MCP and redis-mcp-server have no tool that returns user interface.
- Prompts and resources: redis-mcp-server 0.5.1: none. The code has no @mcp.prompt or @mcp.resource; FastMCP("Redis MCP Server") registers tools only. Redis Docs MCP: it sends server instructions ("Authoritative, up-to-date Redis documentation. Consult these tools for any question about Redis..."); its prompts and resources are not confirmed. Redis Cloud remote MCP: not confirmed. It uses MCP elicitation (form requests) to confirm changes, and its UI views imply MCP Apps resources, but the docs list none.
- Number of skills: 14, in github.com/redis/agent-skills under skills/ (the source). Copies are generated in plugins/redis-development/skills/ for the Claude Code, Codex/ChatGPT and Cursor plugin redis-development 1.7.0. All 14 serve users of Redis; none is for contributors. The redis.io page lists a skill named iris-development that is not in the repository.
- Skills:
  - redis-core: guides Redis data modeling (choosing String, Hash, List, Set, Sorted Set, JSON, Stream or Vector Set, and colon-separated key names); used when designing a data model, caching objects, building counters or leaderboards, or reviewing key naming.
  - redis-connections: guides client connections (pooling, multiplexing, pipelining, RESP3 client-side caching, avoiding slow commands, timeouts); used when configuring redis-py, Jedis, Lettuce or NRedisStack, or batching commands.
  - redis-search: guides Redis Search (FT.CREATE schemas, field types, DIALECT 2, FT.SEARCH/FT.AGGREGATE/FT.HYBRID, HNSW/FLAT vectors, hybrid retrieval, RAG, alias-based index updates, FT.PROFILE/FT.EXPLAIN); used when defining indexes, writing queries or troubleshooting slow or empty results.
  - redis-semantic-cache: guides LangCache semantic caching of LLM responses on Redis Cloud (search/set, similarity threshold, per-task caches, attributes); used when caching LLM completions or RAG answers.
  - redis-clustering: guides Redis Cluster and replication (hash tags, avoiding CROSSSLOT, reading from replicas); used when designing keys for a sharded cluster or debugging CROSSSLOT errors.
  - redis-security: guides security (requirepass and ACL users, TLS, least-privilege ACLs, bind and protected-mode, firewalls, disabling dangerous commands); used when deploying to production or auditing a deployment.
  - redis-observability: guides monitoring and triage (metrics, SLOWLOG, INFO, MEMORY DOCTOR, CLIENT LIST, FT.PROFILE, Redis Insight); used when setting up alerts, diagnosing regressions or profiling slow FT.SEARCH queries.
  - redis-docs-mcp: explains how to use and read the redis-docs MCP server (search/fetch/ask): section ids, metadata.version, corpus coverage, ask rate limits; used when those tools are available and the agent is about to look something up, or a result is confusing.
  - add-redis-iris: adds Redis Iris to an existing agent in any framework by detecting the framework and routing to the right product skill; used when the user asks for Iris or one of its products.
  - add-agent-memory: wires Redis Agent Memory into an agent (asks five questions, writes service.yaml, provisions with `iris agent-memory service create`, wires recall and write-back); used when the agent forgets users or the user asks for long-term memory.
  - add-agent-playbooks: adds Redis Iris Agent Playbooks (connect or provision a Playbook, publish FAQs and Skills, verify the first turn); used when approved answers or procedures live in prompts, retrieval or a semantic cache.
  - add-context-gateway: puts an agent's MCP servers behind one Redis Iris Context Gateway (provisions with `iris context-gateway`, sets cache and compression policies, repoints the agent, verifies with `tools list`/`tools call`); used when the agent configures many MCP servers or the user asks for tool caching.
  - add-intent-router: replaces hand-written routing with a Redis Iris Intent Router (writes intents.yaml, provisions with `iris intent-router service create`, loads intents, wires `router.match()`); used when the agent routes by keywords or an extra LLM call.
  - add-lens: adds Redis Iris Lens tracing so that each agent turn is one trace (installs redis-iris[llm-tracing], calls lens.init, opens lens.turn()); used when the user asks for tracing or observability, or asks why Lens traces are missing.
- What the skills point at: MCP server: redis-docs-mcp directs the agent to the redis-docs tools search, fetch and ask; add-agent-playbooks says "Use an available docs MCP". It serves a bundled Salt registry built from the Salt repository sources, for lookup, recommendation, translation, validation and migration work in consumer repos. Its source is not on main (2fa23b6, 2026-11-20 has no packages/mcp). It exists on the unmerged branches 'mcp' (482bb97, 2026-07-16) and 'mcp-eval' (6599072). No stable release exists, and the site does not document it.
- Number of tools: 5 tools for @salt-ds/mcp 0.0.0-snapshot-20260331141637, counted in the code that registers the tools (dist-es/mcp/src/server/registerTools.js and toolDefinitions.js in the published tarball). RAW_TOOL_DEFINITIONS defines 8 tools; TOOL_DEFINITIONS keeps only the 5 names in DEFAULT_TOOL_ORDER, and registerSaltTools registers only those. The three SUPPORT_TOOL_ORDER tools get_salt_entity, …
- Tools:
  - Taken from the code that registers the tools (toolDefinitions.js in the published snapshot 20260331141637). Each tool returns JSON as text plus structuredContent, with a top-level 'sources' array.
  - 1. get_salt_project_context: detects the local repo's framework, workspace shape, Salt package usage, repo instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md), layered project policy (.salt/team.json, .salt/stack.json) and likely runtime targets under an optional root_dir, and returns that context.
  - 2. choose_salt_solution: in recommendation mode (query) it recommends the best-fit Salt component, pattern, foundation or token for a described need; in comparison mode (names, 2 or more) it compares named Salt entities. It returns the decision, confidence, project_conventions_check, rule_ids, optional starter code and sources.
  - 3. analyze_salt_code: analyzes React and Salt source code (with an optional package_version or from/to_version) to validate usage, detect deprecated APIs and patterns, and suggest fixes and migration guidance. It returns issues, fix_candidates, confidence, rule_ids and sources.
  - 4. translate_ui_to_salt: translates non-Salt UI code, a description or a structured source_outline into Salt primitives, patterns and migration steps. It returns a Salt starter plan with post_migration_verification, visual_evidence_contract, optional starter code and sources.
  - 5. compare_salt_versions: explains Salt upgrade impact between from_version and an optional to_version (with package, component and change-kind filters), highlights breaking changes and deprecations, and returns the next migration actions with sources.
- Search, kind `keyword`: The server registers no dedicated search tool; the search tool discover_salt is defined but filtered out. The query-driven tool is choose_salt_solution (recommendation mode). Inputs: query, names, solution_type (auto|component|pattern|foundation|token), package, status, top_k (1-25), production_ready, prefer_stable, a11y_required, form_field_support, include_starter_code, view (compact|full). A result holds the recommended Salt entity with its score, matched terms, ship check, caveats, optional starter code, suggested follow-ups, confidence, rule_ids and sources. Ranking: recommendComponent scores each component with scoreQueryFields: the query is tokenized, and weights are added for an exact field match, a phrase substring match and each token substring match, plus a usage-semantics adjustment. No embedding model and no language model are used. The unregistered discover_salt / searchSaltDocs uses the MiniSearch library (minisearch ^7.2.0) over generated/page-search-index.json. All ranking runs on the user's machine, in the stdio process, over the bundled registry files in generated/.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: none. createServer.js calls only registerSaltTools; dist-es has no registerPrompt or registerResource calls. The server does declare 'instructions' text (buildSaltMcpInstructions), which among other points tells the agent to start with get_salt_project_context and maps the create, review, migrate and upgrade workflows to the five tools. The unmerged 'mcp' branch (482bb97, 2026-07-16) adds packages/mcp/src/server/registerResources.ts, but no published version contains it.

The server code is not public; the archived repository sanity-io/sanity-mcp-server holds only the deprecated local server. The count leaves out the Workflows tools that appear only where Workflows is enabled; the changelog names their functions (authoring …
- Tools:
  - Source: the documentation (https://www.sanity.io/docs/ai/mcp-server.md, 'Available tools'), because the server code is not public. 60 tools:
  - 1. dataset_assets_upload_from_web_chatgpt: uploads a ChatGPT web attachment or generated file to a Content Lake dataset; returns an operationId for assets_upload_status.
  - 2. dataset_assets_upload_from_url: starts an image or file upload from a public HTTPS URL to a dataset; returns an operationId.
  - 3. media_library_upload_from_url: starts an image, video or file upload from a public HTTPS URL to a Media Library, optionally as a new version of an asset; returns an operationId.
  - 4. media_assets_upload_from_url: deprecated; points to media_library_upload_from_url and does not start an upload.
  - 5. assets_upload_status: checks 1 to 20 uploads by operationId; returns asset IDs, URLs and references, and optionally full metadata.
  - 6. media_library_upload_from_file: prepares a one-use URL for uploading a local or private file up to 50 MiB to a Media Library; returns upload instructions.
  - 7. dataset_assets_upload_from_file: prepares a one-use upload URL for a file up to 50 MiB to a dataset; the POST response returns the document reference and an asset summary.
  - 8. get_schema: fetches the deployed schema for a project and dataset.
  - 9. list_workspace_schemas: deprecated; lists every deployed schema for a project and dataset, grouped by source, each with a schemaId.
  - 10. deploy_schema: deploys schema types directly to the cloud.
  - 11. undeploy_schema: removes a legacy MCP-managed schema from a named workspace, together with its MCP ownership record.
  - 12. schema_type_get: reads one type from the MCP-managed or Studio-deployed schema; returns the schemaVersion and an editable definition.
  - 13. schema_types_delete: removes one or more types from the dataset schema, with a dry run available.
  - 14. schema_fields_patch: adds, replaces or removes top-level fields on one document or object type.
  - 15. deploy_studio: deploys a hosted Studio bound to an MCP-managed schema; returns the studioUrl.
  - 16. create_documents: creates documents from structured content, as drafts, live-edit published documents or release versions.
  - 17. create_version: creates a version document (versions.{releaseId}.*) for a release.
  - 18. patch_documents: applies @sanity/client patch operations to up to 25 documents per call, saved to the draft or release version.
  - 19. query_documents: runs a GROQ query with params; returns complete results and rejects any result over 64 KiB.
  - 20. generate_image: starts async AI image generation for a document field (uses AI credits).
  - 21. transform_image: starts async AI transformation of an existing image (uses AI credits).
  - 22. get_document: fetches one document by its exact ID.
  - 23. documents_validate: validates documents against the deployed schema without changing them (beta).
  - 24. publish_documents: publishes one or more drafts by ID.
  - 25. unpublish_documents: unpublishes published documents back to drafts.
  - 26. discard_drafts: deletes drafts and keeps the published documents.
  - 27. version_discard: discards document versions from a release.
  - 28. list_organizations: lists the organizations the user can access.
  - 29. list_projects: lists the Sanity projects of the account.
  - 30. get_project_studios: returns the Studio applications linked to a project.
  - 31. create_project: creates a project with a dataset and API tokens.
  - 32. cors_origins_list: lists the CORS origins of a project.
  - 33. add_cors_origin: adds CORS origins to a project.
  - 34. cors_origins_delete: deletes a CORS origin from a project.
  - 35. whoami: returns the authenticated account (name, email, provider, MCP authentication method).
  - 36. list_datasets: lists the datasets of a project.
  - 37. create_dataset: creates a dataset with a name and access settings.
  - 38. update_dataset: changes a dataset's visibility and description.
  - 39. create_release: creates a release for grouping content changes, without scheduling it.
  - 40. list_releases: lists the releases of a dataset, active and scheduled by default.
  - 41. list_embeddings_indices: lists the embeddings indices of a dataset.
  - 42. semantic_search: performs a semantic search on an embeddings index.
  - 43. media_library_list: lists the Media Libraries of an organization; returns library IDs.
  - 44. media_library_get_schema: returns the document types of a Media Library, or the full fields of one type.
  - 45. media_library_query_documents: runs a GROQ query on a Media Library.
  - 46. media_library_get_document: fetches one Media Library document by its exact ID.
  - 47. media_library_create_documents: creates Media Library documents; only sanity.asset.collection documents can be created.
  - 48. media_library_patch_documents: edits an asset's title, aspects and cdnAccessPolicy, and collection metadata, within a safe subset.
  - 49. media_library_publish_documents: publishes asset drafts after validating them against the aspect definitions.
  - 50. media_library_discard_drafts: discards asset drafts.
  - 51. media_library_list_asset_references: lists the documents in the project datasets that reference a Media Library asset.
  - 52. media_library_link_assets: makes Media Library assets usable in project documents; returns field values to apply with patch_documents.
  - 53. usage_snapshot_get: returns metered usage totals for one billing period.
  - 54. usage_history_get: returns metered usage as daily, monthly or yearly data points.
  - 55. run_sanity_cli: runs a limited subset of Sanity CLI commands without a shell and returns their output.
  - 56. search_docs: searches the Sanity docs.
  - 57. read_docs: fetches one documentation article.
  - 58. list_sanity_rules: lists the available best-practice development rules.
  - 59. get_sanity_rules: loads specific best-practice development rules.
  - 60. give_sanity_feedback: submits feedback to Sanity about errors, gaps or unclear docs that the agent met.
- Search, kind `intent`: Two search tools. (1) semantic_search: 'Perform a semantic search on an embeddings index' of the user's dataset. It ranks by meaning, with an embeddings index; list_embeddings_indices lists the indices. Changelog v2.10.0 names a `limit` integer parameter. The other input fields, the content of a result and the embedding model are not documented. The search runs on Sanity's servers (the Embeddings Index of the project), not on the user's machine. (2) search_docs: 'Search Sanity docs', used together with read_docs, which reads one article. Its input fields, its result shape and its ranking method are not documented. It runs on Sanity's documentation backend: changelog v2.31.1 fixed 'an error when no results were returned', and the changelog cited by the first agent says it reports 'documentation backend timeouts'. The value 'intent' rests on semantic_search alone; whether search_docs ranks by meaning or by words is not confirmed.
- User interface from a tool, kind `mcp-apps`: The drafts widget, an MCP App introduced in v2.18.0 (2026-04-24, changelog 'Introducing MCP apps'). It was returned by create_documents_from_json and create_documents_from_markdown, in MCP hosts that support apps: Claude, ChatGPT and VS Code. What the user sees: previews of the created documents in a carousel or a table view. What the user can do: switch the view and follow direct links to each document in the Studio. v2.18.1 (2026-04-28) fixed its surface colour in ChatGPT and its image URLs. v2.21.0 (2026-06-10) renamed the JSON tool to create_documents and removed the Markdown tool; no later changelog and not the current tools page says whether create_documents still returns the widget at v2.46.1. It runs on the hosted server and needs no local dev server. The ui:// resource name is not published. No tool is documented as returning an image: generate_image and transform_image write to document fields asynchronously.
- Prompts and resources: not confirmed. The documentation lists no prompts or resources by name. The MCP Apps drafts widget (v2.18.0) implies at least one ui:// resource, but its name is not published. Changelog v2.12.0 says, of the removed get_context tool: 'Context information is now available through other tools and resources'. The server also carries built-in instructions, which the changelogs call the 'System prompt' (v2.13.0, v2.17.0) and the GA post calls '200+ lines of built-in instructions'; these are server instructions, not named MCP prompts.
- Number of skills: 10. They are in github.com/sanity-io/agent-toolkit under skills/*/SKILL.md. The same repository is packaged as the 'sanity' plugin for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex (.claude-plugin, .cursor-plugin, .codex-plugin, plugin.json), and the skills can be installed with `npx skills add sanity-io/agent-toolkit`. The repository has no contributor-only skills. It also holds 4 slash commands …

  - 1. sanity-best-practices: best practices and integration guides for schemas, GROQ, TypeGen, Visual Editing, images, Portable Text, Studio structure, localization, migrations, Functions, webhooks, Blueprints and framework integrations; used whenever an agent works with Sanity schemas, GROQ, previews or frontends, or reviews a Sanity codebase.
  - 2. content-modeling-best-practices: structured content modeling (schema design, reuse, references versus embedded objects, taxonomies); used when designing or refactoring content types or reviewing a page-shaped schema.

  - 9. sanity-migration: plans, implements and reviews migrations from other CMSes (AEM, Contentful, Strapi, WordPress and others) into Sanity; used when replatforming to Sanity.
  - 10. sanity-studio-upgrade: inspects the repository and produces a tailored Studio upgrade plan from v3 onward with only the breaking changes that apply; used when someone wants to bump or modernize a Studio or asks what will break.

- MCP servers: One official server for SAPUI5/OpenUI5: npm @ui5/mcp-server (repo github.com/UI5/mcp-server, mcpName io.github.UI5/mcp-server), newest 0.3.3 published 2026-11-10, stdio server named "UI5", for UI5 app development: guidelines, API reference, project info, scaffolding of apps and Integration Cards, UI5 linter and manifest validation. The 'ui5' plugin of UI5/plugins-coding-agents pins it as @ui5/mcp-server@0.3.3. Out of scope: the same GitHub org also publishes @ui5/webcomponents-mcp-server (github.com/UI5/webcomponents-mcp-server), which serves the separate UI5 Web Components project, not SAPUI5/OpenUI5; the ui5-modernization plugin configures the third-party chrome-devtools-mcp server.
- Number of tools: @ui5/mcp-server 0.3.3: 10 tools, counted from the code that registers them (src/registerTools.ts calls ten register functions, one per folder in src/tools). The README lists the same ten.
- Tools:
  - From the registering code (src/tools/*/index.ts and schema.ts):
  - 1. get_guidelines - returns the UI5 development guidelines as text; its description says it MUST be called once before any UI5 task.
  - 2. run_ui5_linter - runs UI5 linter on a project directory (optional filePatterns, optional fix to auto-fix), returns per-file messages (ruleId, severity, line, message) plus context: rule descriptions, migration guides and bundled documentation resources, and API references.
  - 3. get_api_reference - looks up a UI5 module or symbol by name (e.g. 'sap.m.Button', 'sap.m.Button#text') for the project's framework and version and returns its formatted API documentation (fetched as api.json from the UI5 CDN and cached).
  - 4. get_project_info - reads a local UI5 project and returns its name, type, framework (OpenUI5/SAPUI5), framework version, libraries and version support info (support status, LTS, latest version).
  - 5. create_ui5_app - scaffolds a new basic SAPUI5/OpenUI5 app in TypeScript or JavaScript at a base path (optional OData V4 service, entity set, properties, git init, npm install) and returns a text message with the final location, the generated files and app info (namespace, framework, version, OData URL, npm install status).
  - 6. get_version_info - returns version information for OpenUI5 or SAPUI5: all known versions with their support status and LTS flag.
  - 7. get_integration_cards_guidelines - returns the Integration Cards guidelines as text; must be called once before any Integration Card task.
  - 8. create_integration_card - creates a new UI Integration Card of a given type in a folder under a base path, with optional destinations, and returns a text message naming the location and the generated files.
  - 9. run_manifest_validation - validates a UI5 manifest.json against the UI5 Manifest schema and returns isValid plus Ajv error objects.
  - 10. get_typescript_conversion_guidelines - returns instructions for converting a UI5 project from JavaScript to TypeScript; must be called once before such a conversion.
- Search, kind `keyword`: get_api_reference. Inputs: projectDir (to find framework and version) and query (module or symbol name in dot or slash notation, optionally '#field'; characters < > ( ) " ' not allowed). It is an exact name lookup in an index of api.json files, not a ranked search: the normalized name is looked up, and if not found it splits at the last dot and retries to resolve a field (method, property, event, aggregation, etc.), following 'extends' to the parent class. A result is the formatted symbol (or several symbols of a module) with its API documentation. The api.json files are fetched from ui5.sap.com or sdk.openui5.org for the version and cached; the lookup runs on the user's machine. No embedding or language model.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool names a ui:// resource or returns an image; all return text, structured content or embedded text resources.
- Prompts and resources: none declared. The server declares only the tools capability; no registerPrompt or registerResource call exists in src. Bundled documentation is not served as MCP resources; it is embedded as 'resource' content items inside tool responses (converted to text when resources in responses are turned off).
- Number of skills: 29 skills on main (HEAD 2bab38d, 2026-11-19) of github.com/UI5/plugins-coding-agents, distributed as plugins: plugins/ui5/skills/ (9), plugins/ui5-modernization/skills/ (19), plugins/ui5-typescript-conversion/skills/ (1). The newest tagged release v0.1.9 (2026-10-16) holds 28: ui5-design-advisor is not in it. The @ui5/mcp-server repo has no SKILL.md for consumers.

#### Sentry (SDKs)
Checked: getsentry/toolkit (formerly getsentry/sentry-mcp) tag cli@0.50.0, commit b410e679d (2026-11-18), the newest tag on 2026-11-20: @sentry/mcp-server 0.50.0 (npm latest, published 2026-11-18T19:09Z) and the Sentry CLI 0.50.0 (npm package `sentry`, latest 0.50.0, … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: There is one official server codebase, packages/mcp-core in getsentry/toolkit (formerly getsentry/sentry-mcp), and it ships in three forms. (1) The hosted remote server at https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp (OAuth, Cloudflare Worker, package mcp-cloudflare). (2) `sentry mcp`, the stdio server inside the Sentry CLI (npm package `sentry` 0.50.0), which the README recommends. (3) The npm package @sentry/mcp-server 0.50.0 (npm latest, published 2026-11-18; tag cli@0.50.0), the same stdio server without the rest of the CLI, under the README heading 'Legacy'. Purpose: it gives a coding agent access to the user's Sentry organization (issues, events, traces, logs, monitors, alerts, projects, releases, Seer root-cause analysis) and to the Sentry docs.
- Number of tools: 74 tools in tools/list in the default (non-experimental) mode, counted from the code that registers them, for all three forms because they share mcp-core. Derivation: the catalog in tools/catalog/index.ts has 78 entries. EXPOSE_ALL_TOOLS = true exposes every catalog tool directly and removes the gateway tools search_sentry_tools and execute_sentry_tool. Three deprecated aliases are kept out of …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (tools/catalog/*.ts) and the generated toolDefinitions.json at tag cli@0.50.0. There are 74 tools.
  - add_issue_note: adds a comment (note) to an issue's activity feed.
  - add_team_to_project: grants a team access to a project and returns the project's teams.
  - analyze_issue_with_seer: runs Seer AI root-cause analysis on an issue and returns the root cause, the code locations and a suggested fix.
  - create_alert_rule: creates an Alert (notification workflow) that sends Slack, email, PagerDuty or other notifications.
  - create_dsn: creates an additional DSN (client key) for a project and returns its ID, name and DSN.
  - create_metric_monitor: creates a Metric Monitor with a static, percent-change or dynamic threshold.
  - create_monitor: creates a cron monitor for a scheduled job and returns the slug that check-ins use.
  - create_project: creates a project, provisions its DSN, and can link a repository; returns the project, the DSN and the supported signals with docs links.
  - create_team: creates a team and returns its ID, slug and name.
  - create_uptime_monitor: creates an HTTP uptime monitor for a URL.
  - delete_alert_rule: permanently deletes an Alert (notification workflow).
  - delete_metric_monitor: permanently deletes a Metric Monitor.
  - delete_monitor_environment: deletes one environment from a cron monitor.
  - delete_uptime_monitor: permanently deletes an uptime monitor.
  - find_alert_rules: finds Issue Alerts and Metric Monitor alerts with their conditions, actions, owner and environment.
  - find_dashboards: lists or searches dashboards by title and returns their IDs and titles.
  - find_dropped_events: returns the dropped and accepted event volume over time by outcome and reason (sampling, filters, rate limits, quota).
  - find_dsns: lists a project's DSNs (client keys).
  - find_metric_monitors: finds Metric Monitors and returns their IDs, queries and connected Alerts.
  - find_monitors: finds cron monitors with their status, schedule, owner, project and environment state.
  - find_organizations: lists or searches accessible organizations and returns the slug, region URL and web URL.
  - find_projects: lists or searches projects in an organization and returns project slugs.
  - find_related_issues: finds related issues (likely duplicates, errors in the same trace, issues behind a metric alert), with the reason each is related.
  - find_releases: lists or searches releases with their dates, new issue count, last commit and last deploy.
  - find_teams: lists or searches teams and returns the slug and ID.
  - find_uptime_monitors: finds uptime monitors and returns the URL, status, interval, owner and project.
  - get_agent_conversation_details: returns the transcript of one agent (AI) conversation, with its messages, tool calls, and trace and span IDs.
  - get_alert_options: lists the notification actions, integrations, conditions and sources that an Alert can use.
  - get_alert_rule: returns one alert rule by ID or name, with its triggers, conditions, actions, monitors and scope.
  - get_dashboard_details: returns one dashboard's widgets, saved queries, filters and layout.
  - get_doc: fetches the full markdown of a Sentry documentation page.
  - get_event_attachment: lists or downloads an event's attachments (screenshots, log files, minidumps).
  - get_event_stacktrace: returns the full stack trace of one thread in an event.
  - get_issue_activity: returns an issue's activity feed and comments.
  - get_issue_breadcrumbs: returns the breadcrumb trail of an issue event.
  - get_issue_details: returns one issue's title, status, counts, an event with its stack trace, the Seer root cause, the suspect commit, linked tickets and replays.
  - get_issue_tag_values: returns the tag value distribution of an issue (browser, environment, release, URL and others).
  - get_issue_user_reports: returns the legacy User Reports and crash-report feedback of an issue.
  - get_latest_base_snapshot: returns an app's latest baseline UI screenshots from preprod snapshots, as file names and descriptions.
  - get_metric_monitor_details: returns a Metric Monitor's query, dataset, detection mode, thresholds and connected Alerts.
  - get_monitor_details: returns a cron monitor's schedule, status, environments, recent check-ins and statistics.
  - get_profile: analyzes the aggregated CPU profiles (flamegraph) of a transaction: hot paths, p75/p95/p99 per function and regressions.
  - get_profile_details: inspects one profile by ID or URL: its transaction, trace, runtime and top frames.
  - get_release_details: returns one release's projects, deploys, environments, commits and, optionally, release health.
  - get_replay_details: returns a session replay summary and a timeline of user actions, console errors and failed requests.
  - get_sentry_mcp_info: returns the version and details of the running Sentry MCP server.
  - get_sentry_resource: fetches an issue, event, trace, span, conversation, replay, monitor, dashboard or snapshot by URL or ID.
  - get_snapshot: returns a preprod snapshot comparison (visual regression) with its changed images and the percentage of pixels that differ.
  - get_snapshot_image: returns one current, previous or diff image from a snapshot, as an image (a preview, or full resolution on request).
  - get_span_details: returns one span's attributes, timing, errors and child spans.
  - get_trace_details: returns an overview of one trace: statistics, a span breakdown and a link.
  - get_uptime_monitor_details: returns an uptime monitor's URL, interval, thresholds and recent HTTP check results.
  - link_issue: links an external ticket or a pull request to an issue by URL.
  - onboarding_status_update: reports the progress of one stage of an SDK setup to Sentry's agentic onboarding UI.
  - remove_team_from_project: revokes a team's access to a project.
  - search_agent_conversations: searches agent conversations and returns one summary row (cost, tokens, previews) for each conversation.
  - search_docs: searches the Sentry documentation and returns page paths, URLs, relevance scores and snippets.
  - search_errors: searches error events and returns events, counts and aggregates.
  - search_issue_events: searches the individual events of one issue, in natural language or Sentry syntax.
  - search_issues: searches issues in natural language or Sentry syntax and returns them with status, counts, users, assignee, and first and last seen.
  - search_logs: searches application logs and returns lines, counts and aggregates.
  - search_metrics: searches metrics (counters, gauges, distributions) and returns values, percentiles and trends.
  - search_profiles: searches transaction and continuous profiles and returns profile IDs.
  - search_replays: searches session replays by rage clicks, dead clicks, pages, errors or users and returns a list of replays.
  - search_traces: searches traces and spans for latency, throughput and slowness, and returns events, counts and aggregates.
  - submit_feedback_to_sentry_team: sends a report about friction with the MCP server to its maintainers.
  - unlink_issue: removes a linked external ticket or pull request from an issue.
  - update_alert_rule: updates an Alert's name, status, owner, triggers, actions or connections.
  - update_dsn: renames a DSN, activates or deactivates it, or changes its rate limit or Loader Script options.
  - update_issue: resolves, ignores or reopens an issue, assigns it, or changes its priority.
  - update_metric_monitor: updates a Metric Monitor's query, conditions, name, owner, status or Alerts.
  - update_project: renames a project, or changes its slug or platform.
  - update_uptime_monitor: updates an uptime monitor's URL, interval, timeout, method, headers, body, status or thresholds.
  - whoami: identifies the authenticated Sentry user by name and email.
  - (Not in the count: search_attributes, which is experimental only; the deprecated aliases search_events, search_ai_conversations and get_ai_conversation_details; and the gateway tools search_sentry_tools and execute_sentry_tool, which are disabled while EXPOSE_ALL_TOOLS is true.)
- Search, kind `intent`: search_docs takes the inputs query (2 to 200 characters, natural language), maxResults (1 to 10, default 3) and guide (an optional platform or platform/guide filter). Each result holds path (to pass to get_doc), url, relevance (a score from 0 to 1) and snippet (only the first 3 results have one). Ranking: the tool sends a POST to /api/search on https://mcp.sentry.dev, also from the stdio forms, where context.mcpUrl defaults to that host. That route calls Cloudflare AutoRAG (AI Search) on the index 'sentry-docs' with score_threshold 0.2 and a folder filter for the guide. The ranking therefore runs on a Sentry-operated server (Cloudflare Workers AI), not on the user's machine. The embedding model is not named in the source. Other searches are not documentation searches: search_issues, search_issue_events and the search_errors, search_logs and other event searches accept natural language and can repair or translate the query with an embedded LLM agent (internal/agents with Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenRouter providers) into Sentry search syntax, and the Sentry API then filters the user's data. The gateway tool search_sentry_tools (disabled in 0.50.0) ranks tools by word scoring (scoreTool in catalog-runtime/search.ts).
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: get_snapshot_image returns an MCP image content block: the current, previous or diff screenshot of a preprod snapshot, as a preview or at full resolution when imageResolution=full, with text labels. get_event_attachment returns an image content block when an event attachment is an image (for example a screenshot sent with an error report); other binary attachments come back as embedded resources. Both are static images that the user can only view; there is no interactive view. They fetch from the Sentry API and need no dev server or local process. No code has a `ui://` resource, MCP Apps or the OpenAI Apps SDK (a search for 'ui://', 'text/html+skybridge' and 'openai/outputTemplate' found nothing).
- Prompts and resources: none. A search of packages/ and apps/ at cli@0.50.0 found no registerPrompt, registerResource, ListPrompts or ListResources. buildServer registers only tools, with the capability tools.listChanged set to false, and gives server instructions through buildServerInstructions.
- Number of skills: 9. Eight skills in getsentry/sentry-for-ai under src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, which a build distributes as plugins (getsentry/agent-plugin, plugin-claude, plugin-cursor, plugin-codex, plugin-copilot, plugin-antigravity, plugin-grok) and also serves at skills.sentry.dev. One skill, sentry-cli, in getsentry/toolkit under packages/cli/plugins/sentry-cli/skills/sentry-cli/SKILL.md (version 0.50.0), …
- Skills:
  - sentry-get-started: a guided entry point that orients the user to their current Sentry setup and, for a new project, sets Sentry up end to end (provision a project, install the SDK, confirm that telemetry arrives); it sends other intents to the right skill.
  - sentry-instrument: detects the platform, installs and initializes the SDK, and wires up any signal (errors, tracing, logging, metrics, profiling, replay, feedback, crons, uptime, AI/LLM monitoring); the agent uses it to add Sentry or to capture more than errors.
  - sentry-debug-issue: finds a Sentry issue by link, ID or search, pulls its context, optionally runs Seer, applies the fix and resolves the issue with a `Fixes PROJECT-NAME-12A` commit or PR; the agent uses it to work on a known error.
  - sentry-fix-stack-traces: uploads source maps or debug files (dSYM, ProGuard/R8, NDK, Dart maps, .NET PDBs); the agent uses it when frames show minified names, hex addresses or 'unknown'.
  - sentry-create-alert: creates Sentry alerts with the workflow engine API (email, Slack, PagerDuty, Discord); the agent uses it when asked to create alerts or notifications.
  - sentry-otel-exporter-setup: configures the OpenTelemetry Collector with the Sentry exporter for multi-project routing; the agent uses it when it sets up OTel with Sentry.
  - sentry-setup-releases: sets up releases and deploy tracking, suspect commits and code mappings; the agent uses it when asked to track deploys, or when issues show an unknown release or no suspect commit.
  - sentry-snapshots-cocoa: does the full Sentry Snapshots setup for Apple/Cocoa projects (SnapshotPreviews, uploads, GitHub Actions, selective snapshot testing); the agent uses it for Apple snapshot testing.
  - sentry-cli: a guide to the Sentry CLI; the agent uses it when the user asks about viewing issues, events, projects or organizations, making API calls, or authenticating through the CLI.

- Tools:
  - shadcn-vue (from the code that registers the tools, packages/cli/src/mcp/index.ts and the formatters in packages/cli/src/mcp/utils.ts):
  - 1. get_project_registries: takes no input fields; reads components.json in the working directory and returns text that lists the configured registry names with example `view` commands, or a text message to run init when no components.json or registries exist.
  - 2. list_items_in_registries: takes registries[], optional limit, offset and cwd; returns a paginated text list of the items in those registries (name, type, description, registry, add command).
  - 3. search_items_in_registries: takes registries[], query, optional limit and offset; fuzzy-matches the query against item names and descriptions and returns the same paginated text list of matches.
  - 4. view_items_in_registries: takes items[] with registry prefix (e.g. '@shadcn/button'); returns for each item its name, description, type, the number of its files, and its dependencies and devDependencies (not the file contents).
  - 5. get_item_examples_from_registries: takes registries[] and query (e.g. 'accordion-demo'); fuzzy-searches the registries with the query, fetches the matching items and returns the content of their files as code blocks.
  - 6. get_add_command_for_items: takes items[]; returns the CLI command string `npx shadcn-vue@latest add <items>` (with the project's package runner) without running it.
  - 7. get_audit_checklist: takes no input fields; returns a fixed markdown checklist to verify added components (imports, next/image config, dependencies, lint, TypeScript errors, use the Playwright MCP).
  - shadcn-svelte: no-server.
- Search, kind `keyword`: shadcn-vue: tool search_items_in_registries (get_item_examples_from_registries uses the same searchRegistries function). Input fields: registries (array of registry names, e.g. ['@shadcn','@acme']), query (string), limit (optional number), offset (optional number). One result line holds the item name, type, description, registry and its add command; the response adds pagination (total, offset, limit). Ranking: fuzzy text matching with the fuzzysort library (^4.0.2) over the keys name and description, threshold 0, in packages/cli/src/registry/search.ts. It runs on the user's machine inside the CLI process; the registry indexes are fetched from the registry servers (useCache: false), then matched locally. shadcn-svelte: none (no server).
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. All seven shadcn-vue tools return only content of type 'text'; no ui:// resource and no image. shadcn-svelte has no server.
- Prompts and resources: shadcn-vue: none. The server declares the capability `resources: {}` but registers no resources handler and no prompts; only ListToolsRequestSchema and CallToolRequestSchema handlers exist. shadcn-svelte: no server.

- Skills:
  - shadcn-vue: shadcn-vue: manages shadcn-vue components and projects (adding, searching, fixing, debugging, styling, composing UI) and provides project context, component docs and examples; an agent uses it when working with shadcn-vue, component registries, presets or --preset codes, or any project with a components.json file.

Checked: npm package shadcn 4.23.0 (latest dist-tag, published 2026-10-27T12:33:51Z); source repository shadcn-ui/ui main at commit 45bbf9ba23c9c0f63d38887947e5fb06f59c7da3 (2026-11-20), packages/shadcn/package.json version 4.23.0.
