- MCP servers: One official server: the `mcp` subcommand of the npm package `shadcn` (the CLI), version 4.23.0 (2026-10-27), started as a stdio server with `npx shadcn@latest mcp`. `shadcn mcp init` writes the client config. The server names itself "shadcn" with internal version "1.0.0". It lets an AI assistant browse, search, view and install items from the shadcn registry and from registries configured in components.json.
- Number of tools: 7 (shadcn mcp). Counted from the registerTool calls in packages/shadcn/src/mcp/index.ts on main. The published 4.23.0 dist also has exactly these 7 registerTool calls.
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (packages/shadcn/src/mcp/index.ts).
  - 1. get_project_registries: reads components.json in the working directory and returns the names of the configured registries as text, with example `shadcn view` commands. If no components.json exists, it returns a fix-it message. No input.
  - 2. list_items_in_registries: lists items from the given registries, or from all configured registries, with optional type filter, limit (default 100) and offset. It returns a paginated text list: name, type, description, registry and an add command for each item.
  - 3. search_items_in_registries: fuzzy-searches item names, titles and descriptions in the registries for a query (with optional types, limit and offset). It returns the same paginated list format with add commands.
  - 4. view_items_in_registries: takes item names with a registry prefix (for example @shadcn/button) and returns each item's name, description, type and full file contents.
  - 5. get_item_examples_from_registries: searches the registries for demo or example items that match a query (for example 'accordion-demo'), then returns their full implementation code with dependencies.
  - 6. get_add_command_for_items: takes prefixed item names and returns the shadcn CLI `add` command string for them, using the project's package runner.
  - 7. get_audit_checklist: no input. It returns a fixed markdown checklist to verify components after they are added or generated: imports, next/image remotePatterns, installed dependencies, lint, TypeScript, and use of the Playwright MCP.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool search_items_in_registries. Inputs: query (string, required); registries (optional string[], for example ['@shadcn','@acme']; if omitted, all registries in components.json); types (optional string[], item types); limit (optional number, default 100, 0 for no limit); offset (optional number). One result: item name, type, description, registry, and an add command (`npx shadcn@latest add <registry/item>`), under a header 'Found N items matching "q"' with a pagination range. Ranking: the fuzzysort library (fuzzysort.go with keys name, title, description, threshold -10000) runs on the user's machine over item indexes fetched from each registry. Exception: when the query targets a single 'dynamic' registry that returns its own pagination, the registry server filters and ranks, and the CLI returns its items verbatim. get_item_examples_from_registries uses the same searchRegistries function to find example items.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. All seven tools return only text content (textResult or errorResult).
- Prompts and resources: none. The server declares only the capabilities logging and tools (listChanged: false). There are no registerPrompt or registerResource calls in packages/shadcn/src or in the 4.23.0 dist.
- Number of skills: 2. Both are in the top-level skills/ directory of the GitHub repository shadcn-ui/ui (skills/shadcn and skills/migrate-radix-to-base), not in the npm package. Users install them with `npx skills add shadcn/ui`. There are no other SKILL.md files in the repository.
- Skills:
  - 1. shadcn: manages shadcn components and projects (adding, searching, fixing, debugging, styling and composing UI, including chat interfaces) and provides project context, component docs and usage examples. It applies in any project with a components.json, for shadcn/ui, registries, presets and --preset codes, 'shadcn init', and for building a design system from a DESIGN.md or brand spec. It is marked user-invocable: false.

Its allowed-tools are limited to Bash(npx|pnpm dlx|bunx --bun shadcn@latest *). Web addresses: the URLs that `docs` returns (ui.shadcn.com). migrate-radix-to-base runs `npx shadcn@latest info --json` and fetches `https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/<style>/<component>.json` and `.../base-<style>/<component>.json`. Package files: it reads `node_modules/@base-ui/react/**/*.d.ts`. MCP: the shadcn skill folder holds mcp.md, which …

- Tools:
  - A) @shopify/dev-mcp 1.19.0, from the code that registers the tools (5):
  - 1. learn_shopify_api: the mandatory first call. It takes api (an enum of Shopify APIs such as admin, functions, polaris-app-home, polaris-admin-extensions, liquid, hydrogen, onboarding topics), an optional version, conversationId, model and user_prompt. It returns a new or reused conversationId, the resolved API version and that API's bundled instruction file (data/mcp-instructions/<api>.md) as text.
  - 2. search_docs_chunks: searches shopify.dev with a natural-language prompt, optionally filtered by api_name and version and limited by max_num_results. It returns a JSON array of documentation chunks with code examples.
  - 3. validate: validates code generated or edited in the turn (GraphQL operations for one API, or Polaris/UI-extension components in JSX/TSX/HTML, with extensionTarget for extension surfaces) against the bundled schemas and component references. It returns a per-block validity report naming hallucinated types, fields, components, props or values.
  - 4. validate_theme: takes absoluteThemePath and filesCreatedOrUpdated, then runs Theme Check over Liquid and supporting theme files in a local theme directory. It returns the errors and suggested fixes. It is registered only when LIQUID_VALIDATION_MODE is not "partial".
  - 5. feedback: records a once-per-turn scorecard (overall up/down/mixed; docsContext, schemaValidation, apiVersion and codegen as worked/partial/failed/not_used; a comment) and sends it to Shopify telemetry. It returns "ok" (or a note that feedback is already recorded).
  - B) Hosted connectors, from the documentation (Claude connector help page, 43; the ChatGPT plugin page adds item 44). The pages do not name the server address; the list is attributed to setup.shopify.com/mcp by inference:

  - 3. create-collection: creates a manual or smart collection and publishes it to the online store.
  - 4. create-digital-product: creates a draft digital product for an uploaded file.
  - 5. create-digital-product-from-link: creates a draft digital product that delivers a link.
  - 6. create-discount: creates a percentage-off discount code.
  - 7. create-product: creates a product with variants, options and inventory tracking.
  - 8. create_store: creates a store from a business description before sign-up and returns a link to view it.
  - 9. find-sample-product: returns sample products for a named category for the user to browse and add.
  - 10. generate-business-names: returns suggested store names, each with a save/rename/signup link.
  - 11. generate-domain-names: returns available domain names, each with a purchase link.
  - 12. get-collection: returns one collection's title, description, image, products and rules.
  - 13. get-digital-product: returns one digital product's title, description, price, status and cover image.
  - 14. get-inventory-levels: returns stock for every variant of a product across locations.
  - 15. get-order: returns one order's line items, fulfillment status, shipping address and tracking.
  - 16. get_preview_store_links: returns a new link to view an unsaved store and a link to save it.
  - 17. get-product: returns one product's title, status, vendor, variants, images, tags and inventory.
  - 18. get-shop-info: returns the connected store's name, domain, email, plan, currency, time zone and country.
  - 19. get_uploaded_files: returns the files uploaded in the chat.
  - 20. graphql_mutation: makes a change through the Admin API to a part of the store that has no dedicated action.
  - 21. graphql_query: reads data through the Admin API from a part of the store that has no dedicated action.
  - 22. graphql_schema: returns the parts of the Admin API that a request can use.
  - 23. list-customers: returns customers with name, email, phone, order count and total spend.
  - 24. list-orders: returns recent orders with customer, totals, and payment and fulfillment status.
  - 25. open-digital-products-install: displays an Install button that opens the admin to install the Digital Products app.
  - 26. publish-digital-product: activates a digital product and requests its Online Store listing.
  - 27. run-analytics-query: runs a ShopifyQL query against the store's analytics data.
  - 28. search_collections: searches collections by keyword or by a filter such as title or collection type.
  - 29. search_docs_chunks: searches Shopify's documentation for an answer to a platform question.
  - 30. search_products: searches the catalog by keyword or by a filter such as price, tag or status.
  - 31. set-inventory: sets the available quantity for an item at one location, with a reason.
  - 32. switch-shop: switches to another store the user owns and asks for authorization.
  - 33. test-digital-products-connection: checks that the store can reach the Digital Products app.
  - 34. theme_bash: reads and edits theme files; the edits stay pending until committed.
  - 35. theme_commit: saves pending theme edits as a new theme version.
  - 36. theme_publish: publishes a theme after the user confirms.
  - 37. theme_screenshot: displays a screenshot of a store page, including pending theme edits.
  - 38. update-collection: updates a collection's title, description, image, sort order or rules.
  - 39. update-product: updates a product's title, description, status, images, variant prices or SKUs.
  - 40. upload-digital-product-file: opens a file picker to attach the downloadable file to a digital product.
  - 41. upload-digital-product-media: opens a file picker to add a cover image to a digital product.
  - 42. upload_file: opens an upload box in the chat to add images and other files.
  - 43. validate_graphql_codeblocks: checks an Admin API request for errors before it runs.
  - 44. upload-image (ChatGPT plugin page only): uploads a photo to Shopify and returns a hosted address that a product can use.
- Search, kind `intent`: Dev MCP tool search_docs_chunks. Inputs: prompt (the natural-language query; the description says it takes the user prompt), max_num_results (optional), api_name (optional filter, such as admin or polaris-admin-extensions), version (optional API version). The handler also passes conversationId. It sends POST https://shopify.dev/assistant/search with {query, max_num_results, conversation_id, api_name, api_version} and returns the JSON array of documentation chunks as text. One result is a chunk of a shopify.dev page with its text or code examples; for Hydrogen at 2026-10 and later, the client drops legacy Hydrogen chunks. Ranking runs on Shopify's server (shopify.dev), not on the user's machine (a SHOPIFY_DEV_LOCAL_SERVER_URL override exists only for source builds). The client has two backends: the legacy backend (USE_LEGACY_SEARCH=true) sends the header X-Shopify-Dev-Use-OpenAI-Search: true; the default "new" backend does not name its ranking method. If one backend fails, the client retries the other. The hosted connectors also have search_docs_chunks ("Searches Shopify's documentation for an answer to a question about the platform"), plus search_products and search_collections ("by keyword, or by a filter") over store data. The intent value rests on the natural-language prompt input and the OpenAI-search flag of the legacy backend; the model or index of the default backend is not stated.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: Dev MCP: no tool returns user interface (all five return text). Hosted connectors: (1) theme_screenshot shows a screenshot of a store page, including pending theme edits; no local process is needed, because Shopify hosts the store. (2) upload_file opens an upload box in the chat, where the user uploads images and other files (up to 20 MB each). (3) upload-digital-product-file and upload-digital-product-media open a file picker in the chat; the browser uploads the file directly to Shopify. (4) open-digital-products-install shows an Install button that opens the Shopify admin. (5) find-sample-product shows sample products that the user can browse and add. (6) run-analytics-query results are returned "as tables and charts". (7) In ChatGPT only, a Shopify panel opens beside the conversation with fields and controls the user edits directly (for example the title, description and price of a drafted product) and stays in sync with the conversation; pinned Shopify shows a home screen with a store summary and task cards. None of these needs a local process. The documentation does not say whether these in-chat views are MCP Apps (ui://) resources or OpenAI Apps SDK widgets, so mcp_ui_kind counts only the confirmed screenshot.

  - 8. docs-show (docs): takes `id` (plus `storybookId` with several sources) and returns the documentation of one component or docs entry: its first stories with code snippets and story IDs, and the TypeScript prop definitions. On a miss, 10.6.8 returns a not-found message that points to docs-list; 11.0.0-beta.3 returns up to 5 suggested entries.
  - 9. docs-show-story (docs): takes `storyId`, or componentId + storyName, and returns the full documentation and code of one story.
- Search, kind `no-search`: none. No tool takes a query. In 11.0.0-beta.3 (and `next`), docs-show has a fallback: when an id misses, suggestEntries returns up to 5 entries ranked by shared word tokens of the id and the names. This is word matching on the machine of the user, inside the Storybook dev server, not a search tool. 10.6.8 has no such fallback.
- User interface from a tool, kind `mcp-apps`: stories-preview: the tool sets `_meta.ui.resourceUri` to ui://stories-preview/preview.html. The view shows one article per story, with a heading '<title> - <name>' and the live story in an iframe from the Storybook `iframe.html?id=...`, resized to the story height. The user can view and interact with the rendered story; the app script also uses the ui/open-link and ui/message calls. Hosts without MCP Apps get links to the stories. The view needs the running Storybook dev server: the iframe src and the CSP domains are the dev-server origin. review-create returns no MCP UI; it returns a URL of the review page in the running Storybook.
- Prompts and resources: Resources: one, ui://stories-preview/preview.html ('App resource for the Preview Stories tool', the HTML of the MCP App), registered only when the dev toolset is enabled. Prompts: none; the 10.6.8 and 11.0.0-beta.3 bundles contain no prompt registration. The server also sends `instructions`, built by buildServerInstructions from the enabled toolsets.
- Number of skills: 7. They are in the separate repository storybookjs/skills, on the `next` branch and the tags v11.0.0-alpha.1 to v11.0.0-beta.3, at skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Six of them require Storybook 11.0 or a prerelease of it; storybook-init has no such prerequisite and installs the 11.0 prerelease when the stable release is below 11.0. The `main` branch has no skills.
- Skills:
  - 1. component-docs: 'Look up the components of a project with Storybook, with their props and usage examples, to reuse existing components instead of building duplicates or to answer a question about a component's props, API, or usage.'
  - 2. storybook-init: 'Use when adding Storybook to a project that has no `storybook` dependency yet.'
  - 3. storybook-setup: 'Use this skill when Storybook is already installed and the user wants it set up for the project, with a working `preview` file and stories for its real components. To write or update the stories of a component, use write-stories instead.'
  - 4. storybook-upgrade: 'Use this skill when Storybook exists but needs an upgrade.'
  - 5. test-stories: 'Run the Storybook story tests of a project, with their accessibility checks, and fix what fails.'
  - 6. ui-review: 'Publish a Storybook review that shows the user the stories a UI change affects, or the components and stories they ask to see.'
  - 7. write-stories: 'The rules for writing Storybook stories in a project. They cover which states get a story, the imports, play functions, and mocks for network requests and modules.'
- What the skills point at: Each skill is a thin stub that points to the installed command line tool. component-docs, write-stories, test-stories and ui-review say to run `npx storybook skills <name>`; storybook-setup says to run `npx storybook skills setup`; the agent follows the output. That output is built in code/core/src/cli/skills/content/ of the storybook package (present in the 10.6.8 dist at dist/cli/skills/content). It names CLI commands such as `npx storybook tools docs list`, `docs show`, `docs show-story`, `stories changed`, `stories find-by-component`, `test run`, `review create` and `stories preview`. With `--mcp`, the same text names the MCP tools docs-list, docs-show, docs-show-story, stories-changed, …
- Not confirmed: The full text that `npx storybook skills <name>` prints at runtime: not run; known only from its builder source. | Whether the storybookjs/skills repository has a release of skills for Storybook 10.x: only 11.0 tags and an empty main branch exist.

  - 1. stripe_api_search: searches for Stripe API methods by keyword and returns matching methods.
  - 2. stripe_api_details: returns detailed parameter information for one Stripe API method.
  - 3. stripe_api_read: reads data with any supported Stripe API GET method and returns the API response.

  - 8. get_balance_summary (Treasury, public preview): displays an interactive balance summary across the Stripe balance and Treasury accounts.

  - 11. setup_recipient (Treasury): sets up a recipient account for sending money from a Treasury account.
  - 12. transfer_money (Treasury): transfers money between supported Stripe balances (human confirmation).
  - 13. search_stripe_documentation: searches the Stripe documentation for the given question and language.
  - 14. stripe_implementation_planner: guides the user through Stripe products to accept payments, sell online, set up billing or build an integration.
  - 15. send_stripe_feedback: shares feedback about Stripe's products.

- Tools:
  - Source: registration code at tag mcp-server-supabase-v0.19.0 (not the docs). mcp-server-supabase (41):
  - [docs] search_docs — searches the Supabase documentation with a GraphQL query (searchDocs etc.) against the Content API; returns the GraphQL result.
  - [account] list_organizations — lists the organizations the user belongs to.
  - [account] get_organization — gets one organization's details, including its subscription plan.
  - [account] list_projects — lists all the user's Supabase projects, to help find the project ID.

  - [account] get_cost — gets the cost of creating a new project or branch in an organization.

  - [account] pause_project — pauses a project.

  - [database] apply_migration — applies a DDL migration to the database (destructive statements may need confirmation).

  - [debugging] get_logs — gets a project's logs by service type for a window of 24 hours or less (hidden when query_logs is available).

  - [functions] deploy_edge_function — deploys or replaces an Edge Function.
  - [functions] create_edge_function_secret — creates or updates an Edge Function secret; the user enters the value in the dashboard through a URL elicitation.
  - [branching] create_branch — creates a development branch (with cost confirmation) and applies migrations to it; linked to the ui://supabase/create-branch view.
  - [branching] list_branches — lists development branches with their status.
  - [branching] delete_branch — deletes a development branch.
  - [branching] merge_branch — merges a branch's migrations and Edge Functions into production.
  - [branching] reset_branch — resets a branch's migrations, discarding untracked changes.
  - [branching] rebase_branch — runs newer production migrations on a branch.
  - [storage] list_storage_buckets — lists a project's storage buckets.
  - [storage] get_storage_config — gets a project's storage config.
  - [storage] update_storage_config — updates a project's storage config.

  - [notebooks] get_notebook — gets one notebook with its cells.
  - [notebooks] run_notebook — runs a notebook's query cells in order and returns each cell's rows, error or skipped reason.
  - [notebooks] delete_notebook — deletes a notebook for everyone (may need confirmation).
  - [feedback] submit_feedback — sends feedback on Supabase tools or docs to the Supabase team and returns a delete token.

- Search, kind `both`: Tool: search_docs. Input: graphql_query (string), a GraphQL query against the Supabase Content API. The tool description embeds the GraphQL schema and gives the example `{ searchDocs(query: "row level security", limit: 5) { nodes { title href content } } }`. Output: { result }, the GraphQL result. Each searchDocs node is a SearchResult with title, href and content (Guide, SDK reference, CLI reference, Management API reference or Troubleshooting types). Ranking runs on Supabase's servers, not on the user's machine. The resolver calls SearchResultModel.searchHybrid. It embeds the query with OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002, then calls the Postgres RPC search_content_hybrid (or search_content_hybrid_nimbus) with query_text and query_embedding, so the ranking combines text and vector. It appends up to 5 results (KB_RESULTS = 5) from the knowledge-base search at https://supabase.com/kb/api/search.

The server needs the experimentalApps option (experimental_apps=true on the HTTP query), and the client must advertise the MCP Apps extension. (1) create_project → ui://supabase/create-project. The user sees live provisioning progress for the new project: a summary with its name, ref and region, and step status. When the project is ready, the view offers an 'Open in Studio' button (the host opens the link) and copy fields for the Project URL, the publishable key and the Studio link. The view polls by calling server tools. (2) create_branch → ui://supabase/create-branch, with live setup progress for a branch and similar ready actions. Both views are React apps in packages/mcp-ui (private, never published), inlined as single HTML files. They make no network requests (empty CSP connectDomains) and need no local dev server or other local process.

Resources exist only when MCP Apps are on: ui://supabase/create-project ('Create project view', for live provisioning progress of create_project) and ui://supabase/create-branch ('Create branch view', for live setup progress of create_branch). With apps off, getResources returns []. The server also sends an instructions string with usage guidelines. It points to `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` and to the Supabase CLI. mcp-server-postgrest: one resource, postgrest:///spec ('OpenAPI spec', the OpenAPI spec of the PostgREST API), and no prompts.

The repo's .claude-plugin/marketplace.json ('supabase-agent-skills') ships them as plugins 'supabase' and 'postgres-best-practices'. The docs page 'Agent Skills' lists the same two under 'Available skills', and the 'Supabase Plugin …
- Skills:
  - supabase — an umbrella skill 'Use when doing ANY task involving Supabase'. It covers the Supabase products (Database, Auth, Edge Functions, Realtime, Storage, Vectors, Cron, Queues), supabase-js and @supabase/ssr in SSR frameworks, auth issues, the CLI and MCP server, schema changes and migrations, security audits, Postgres extensions, and debugging and log queries. #### Svelte and SvelteKit
Checked: @sveltejs/mcp 0.1.31 (npm latest, published 2026-11-17T14:15:37Z); sveltejs/ai-tools main at commit f9d22f2f7f7cd5e4596eef5d108a69ac8f0dd48d (2026-11-17). The local package and the hosted server at mcp.svelte.dev register the same server object from the … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: There are two ways to reach one server, both built from the same server object in packages/mcp-server. (1) Local stdio: the npm package @sveltejs/mcp 0.1.31, published 2026-11-17, started with `npx -y @sveltejs/mcp`. Its purpose is official Svelte and SvelteKit documentation plus static analysis of Svelte code. The same package is also a CLI with the commands list-sections, get-documentation and svelte-autofixer. (2) Hosted remote: https://mcp.svelte.dev/mcp, from apps/mcp-remote, which imports `server` from '@sveltejs/mcp-server' and serves it over HTTP with SSE disabled. The server describes itself as "The official Svelte MCP server implementation".
- Number of tools: 4 for the local stdio server and 4 for the hosted remote server, because they register the same server object. The count comes from the code that registers the tools: packages/mcp-server/src/mcp/handlers/tools/index.ts exports four registration functions, and setup_tools runs each export. The published tarball of @sveltejs/mcp 0.1.31 registers the same four names. The documentation page "Tools" …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (handlers/tools/*.ts). The list applies to both servers.
  - 1. list-sections: lists all Svelte 5 and SvelteKit documentation sections, fetched from https://svelte.dev/docs/experimental/sections.json. It returns text lines of the form "- title: …, use_cases: …, path: …", with an intro and an outro telling the agent to call get-documentation next.
  - 2. get-documentation: takes `section` (one string or an array of strings: a title such as "$state" or a path such as "cli/overview"). For each matching section it fetches the llms.txt version from svelte.dev and returns the full Markdown under a "## <title>" heading. For a name that does not match, it returns similar sections, or the full section list when nothing is similar.
  - 3. svelte-autofixer: takes `code`, `desired_svelte_version`, an optional `async` and an optional `filename`. It runs compile checks, the project's own AST autofixer visitors and ESLint over a Svelte component or module (in stdio mode `code` may be a file path), and returns structured content {issues[], suggestions[], require_another_tool_call_after_fixing}.
  - 4. playground-link: takes `name`, `tailwind` and `files` (a record of file names to file contents, which must include App.svelte). It encodes the files with gzip and base64 into the hash of a https://svelte.dev/playground URL. It returns {url} as text and as structured content, plus an embedded MCP-UI resource (externalUrl) that points to the /playground/embed URL.
- Search, kind `keyword`: The server has no dedicated search tool. The search behaviour sits inside get-documentation. Input: `section` (a string or an array of strings). It first matches exactly: a title compared without case, the slug, or the URL. For a name that does not match, it falls back to substring matching on the title, the slug and the use_cases text. Each fallback result is a line "- title: …, section: …" under "N similar results for …", followed by "Section not found". It uses no embedding model and no language model at query time. The matching runs in the server process: on the user's machine for the stdio package, and on the project's server for mcp.svelte.dev. The section index is fetched from svelte.dev/docs/experimental/sections.json. Separately, list-sections hands the agent the use_cases keywords so that the model itself chooses sections by intent. The bundled src/use_cases.json summaries are used whenever the svelte.dev metadata gives no use_cases.
- User interface from a tool, kind `mcp-apps`: playground-link. It registers the resource ui://svelte/playground-link (HTML built with @mcp-ui/server createUIResource, with the mcpApps adapter enabled) and points to it from the tool's _meta.ui.resourceUri. In the tool result it also embeds an MCP-UI resource of type externalUrl. What the user sees: an iframe that loads the svelte.dev playground embed (https://svelte.dev/playground/embed#<encoded files>), with a "Loading playground..." placeholder first, at a preferred frame size of 100% by 1200px. What the user can do: whatever the hosted svelte.dev playground embed allows (the iframe is granted clipboard-write). The source says the purpose is "to quickly check the code in the playground"; the exact controls of the embed were not confirmed. Local process: none. The view loads from svelte.dev (the CSP allows https://svelte.dev) and needs no local dev server.
- Prompts and resources: Prompts (1): svelte-task (title "Svelte-Task-Prompt", argument `task`). It tells the model which documentation sections exist and how to use get-documentation, the svelte-autofixer loop and playground-link. Resources (2): (a) the resource template Svelte-Doc-Section, URI svelte://{/slug*}.md, "A single documentation section". It lists every documentation section and returns that section's llms.txt text; the documentation calls it "doc-section". NuGet .NET tools, version 2.0.0: Syncfusion.Blazor.MCP (registry name com.syncfusion/syncfusion-blazor-mcp in .mcp/server.json), Syncfusion.AspNetCore.MCP, Syncfusion.AspNetMvc.MCP, Syncfusion.Maui.MCP, Syncfusion.WPF.MCP, Syncfusion.WinForms.MCP, Syncfusion.WinUI.MCP, Syncfusion.UWP.MCP and Syncfusion.DocumentSdk.MCP. They exist to search the Syncfusion documentation for the agent's platform. Each one needs a Syncfusion API key in Syncfusion_API_Key or Syncfusion_API_Key_Path.
- Number of tools: Each of the 14 servers has 1 tool: react-mcp 1, angular-mcp 1, vue-mcp 1, javascript-mcp 1, typescript-mcp 1, Blazor.MCP 1, AspNetCore.MCP 1, AspNetMvc.MCP 1, Maui.MCP 1, WPF.MCP 1, WinForms.MCP 1, WinUI.MCP 1, UWP.MCP 1, DocumentSdk.MCP 1. The npm counts come from the code that registers the tools (dist/index.js, `[new a].forEach(o=>p.register(o))`, where a single class sets up search_docs; the …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools in the published npm packages (bundled dist/index.js, not a public repository), and for NuGet the strings in the compiled DLLs. Every server: search_docs. It takes `query` (string) and sends {platform, tool, query} with the API-Key header by HTTPS POST to https://helpbot.syncfusion.com/api/documents/search. When the query does not name the platform, it adds the platform name to the query. It returns one text block: "Documentation Search Results for \"<query>\"" followed by the service's response serialized as JSON. Descriptions: npm and Blazor say "Search Syncfusion <Platform> documentation for specific component/control features, API references, configuration details, and troubleshooting information." MAUI, WPF, WinForms, WinUI, UWP and DocumentSdk say "The SearchDocs helps you with Syncfusion UI for <Platform> development questions and provides documentation references." These six DLLs also hold a `components` string and the description "Retrieve the components list information from the user query make sure to separate components using , .", which suggests a second parameter. This is not confirmed from the binaries. The React docs say an earlier tool, `#sf_react_assistant`, was renamed to search_docs, and an earlier `#sf_react_ui_builder` was removed from the server.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: Tool search_docs. Input: `query` (string), described as "query for searching documentation, features, or real-world use cases (e.g. 'DataGrid sorting', 'DatePicker events', 'Chart configuration')". The six desktop and DocumentSdk servers may also take `components`; this is not confirmed. One result: the hosted service's response body, either a string or JSON, put under "Documentation Search Results for ...". The client does not define a result structure. Ranking runs on a Syncfusion server: POST https://helpbot.syncfusion.com/api/documents/search with body {platform, tool:'<platform>-mcp', query}, a 20-second timeout and the API key in the header. The local package does no ranking. The code and the docs do not name the ranking method, model or index. The docs show natural-language questions as queries (README example: "#search_docs Create a Syncfusion React Grid with paging, sorting, and filtering enabled.").
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: none. The npm bundle calls only registerTool (once), with no registerPrompt or registerResource. The NuGet DLLs have no McpServerPrompt, McpServerResource, WithPrompts or WithResources references; they have only WithTools and one SearchDocsTool (per the first reader's DLL string read; not re-read here).

#### Telerik and Kendo UI
Checked: Rechecked on 2026-11-20. MCP packages at their newest releases: npm @progress/kendo-react-mcp 1.12.1 (2026-11-12), @progress/kendo-angular-mcp 1.11.1 (2026-11-12), @progress/kendo-jquery-mcp 1.11.0 (2026-10-22); NuGet Telerik.Blazor.MCP 1.13.0, … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: 14 official MCP servers, one for each product, all stdio. They are published by Progress and are not open source: each npm package ships one bundled dist/index.js, and each NuGet package ships compiled DLLs (tools/net10.0/any). The servers send their queries to Progress's hosted gRPC service at contextapi.telerik.com:443, and each one needs a Telerik license. (1) npm @progress/kendo-react-mcp 1.12.1, 2026-11-12, bin kendo-react-mcp. Server name "kendo-mcp" (title "Kendo MCP Server"). The KendoReact Agentic UI Generator and its assistants. (2) npm @progress/kendo-angular-mcp 1.11.1, 2026-11-12, bin kendo-angular-mcp. Server name "kendo-mcp". Kendo UI for Angular, with the same tool set as React. (3) npm @progress/kendo-jquery-mcp 1.11.0, 2026-10-22. Server name "kendo-and-kendo-resources". Kendo UI for jQuery: it answers documentation questions and upgrades projects. (4) NuGet Telerik.Blazor.MCP 1.13.0. server.json name io.github.telerik/telerik-blazor-mcp. "MCP server providing Telerik Blazor component knowledge and UI-generation capabilities." (5) NuGet Telerik.ASPNETCore.MCP 1.4.0. "Telerik ASP.NET Core MCP Orchestrator enables syntax-aware agentic UI generation". (6) NuGet Telerik.ASPNETCoreHtml.MCP 1.7.0. A documentation assistant for the ASP.NET Core HTML Helpers. (7) NuGet Telerik.ASPNETCoreTag.MCP 1.7.0. A documentation assistant for the ASP.NET Core TagHelpers. (8) NuGet Telerik.AspNetMvc.MCP 1.7.0. A documentation assistant for ASP.NET MVC. (9) NuGet Telerik.Ajax.MCP 1.6.0. A documentation assistant for ASP.NET AJAX. (10) NuGet Telerik.WinForms.MCP 1.9.0. WinForms documentation, migration from the standard Microsoft controls, and version upgrades. (11) NuGet Telerik.WPF.MCP 1.10.0. WPF documentation and upgrade analysis. (12) NuGet Telerik.MAUI.MCP 1.9.0. .NET MAUI documentation and upgrade analysis. (13) NuGet Telerik.Reporting.MCP 1.8.0. Telerik Reporting documentation. (14) NuGet Telerik.DPL.MCP 1.8.0. Document Processing Libraries documentation. The plugins in telerik/ai-plugins wrap only five of these servers: React and Angular (`npx @progress/kendo-<x>-mcp@latest`), and Blazor, WinForms and WPF (`dnx <id> --yes`). Each plugin sets PLUGIN_MODE=1.
- Number of tools: 60 in total. The count for each server, read from the tool-registration code in the published package: - kendo-react-mcp: 9 - kendo-angular-mcp: 9 - kendo-jquery-mcp: 2 - Telerik.Blazor.MCP: 11 - Telerik.ASPNETCore.MCP: 12 - Telerik.ASPNETCoreHtml.MCP: 1 - Telerik.ASPNETCoreTag.MCP: 1 - Telerik.AspNetMvc.MCP: 1 - Telerik.Ajax.MCP: 1 - Telerik.WinForms.MCP: 7 - Telerik.WPF.MCP: 2 - …
- Tools:
  - Source: the registration code in each published package. For npm, the bundles. For the .NET servers, the McpServerTool Name and Description attributes, decoded from the DLL metadata.
  - KendoReact (9). Angular has the same tools, with kendo_angular_assistant in place of kendo_react_assistant:
  - kendo_ui_generator: the orchestrator (userIntent and confidence numbers). It returns a step-by-step plan that names which assistant tools to call, in what order, with a workflowId.
  - kendo_react_assistant: an orchestrator for "assistant" access. It returns a plan to gather component documentation and icon suggestions.
  - kendo_layout_assistant: takes a prompt and returns Kendo Design System CSS utility classes from the CssUtilsSearch service.
  - kendo_style_assistant: takes a natural-language style prompt and returns generated CSS variables from the hosted GenerateTheme "external style agent".
  - kendo_icon_assistant: takes a query and a limit. It returns matching icons from the Telerik Icons library.
  - kendo_component_assistant: takes a query and a component. It returns 3 documentation matches from the hosted Query service.
  - kendo_getting_started_assistant: takes projectName, createNewProject and theme. It returns setup instructions, for example `npx kendo react create vite <name> --theme=...`.
  - kendo_accessibility_assistant: takes a query and a component, with optional general WCAG 2.2 AA guidelines. It returns accessibility API matches.
  - kendo_upgrade_assistant: takes workingDirectory, packageNames and skipInstall. It runs `kendo migrate ... --codemods --force --ai-mode` in the project and returns the CLI output and the upgrade status.
  - Kendo UI for jQuery (2):
  - kendo_jquery_assistant: takes query, component and queryInvolvesIcons. It returns documentation matches, and icon matches when queryInvolvesIcons is set.
  - kendo_jquery_upgrade_assistant: takes workingDirectory, fromVersion and toVersion. It runs `kendo migrate @progress/kendo-ui --codemods --force --ai-mode --no-install --from <v> --to <v>` and returns the output.
  - Telerik.Blazor.MCP (11):
  - telerik_ui_generator: the orchestrator. It returns an execution plan.
  - telerik_blazor_assistant: returns a plan to discover components and icons.
  - telerik_component_assistant: answers questions with documentation.
  - telerik_layout_assistant: returns Kendo Design System CSS utilities.
  - telerik_style_assistant: generates CSS variables through the external style service.
  - telerik_icon_assistant: searches Telerik Icons.
  - telerik_accessibility_assistant: returns WCAG 2.2 AA and component guidance.
  - telerik_getting_started_assistant: creates a BlazorWasm, BlazorServer or BlazorWebApp project and returns setup guidance.
  - telerik_validator_assistant: takes a .razor path and "Returns a list of invalid properties that don't exist on the component."
  - telerik_upgrade_assistant: takes a path, a target version and dryRun. It upgrades Telerik.UI.for.Blazor and migrates the affected APIs in the files.
  - telerik_localization_assistant: modes preview, apply, translate and status, for .resx localization.
  - Telerik.ASPNETCore.MCP (12):
  - telerik_ui_generator: "Returns an implementation checklist with required components, layout, data binding, and syntax guidance."
  - telerik_layout_assistant: returns layout guidance and CSS utilities.
  - telerik_icon_assistant: returns icon recommendations.
  - telerik_component_assistant: returns syntax-aware API details, configuration and markup examples for one component.
  - telerik_validator_assistant: checks the .cshtml files and returns PASSED or FAILED with findings.
  - telerik_style_assistant: returns theme and CSS-variable guidance.
  - telerik_accessibility_assistant: returns WCAG guidance.
  - telerik_getting_started_assistant: returns setup steps for a new project.
  - telerik_tools_info: returns the usage rules and sequencing for all the tools.
  - telerik_upgrade_assistant: upgrades the project to the latest package.
  - telerik_databinding_assistant: returns guidance on DataSource transport and ToDataSourceResult.
  - telerik_jquery_config_assistant: returns client-side jQuery guidance.
  - One documentation tool each (query and component in, documentation matches out):
  - telerik-aspnetcorehtml-assistant (ASPNETCoreHtml)
  - telerik-aspnetcoretag-assistant (ASPNETCoreTag)
  - telerik-aspnetmvc-assistant (AspNetMvc)
  - telerik_ajax_assistant (Ajax)
  - telerik-reporting-assistant (Reporting, with a reportingArea field)
  - telerik-dpl-assistant (DPL, with component and target framework fields)
  - Telerik.WinForms.MCP (7):
  - telerik_winforms_assistant: answers questions with documentation.
  - telerik_get_migration_plan: returns the migration workflow, the rules and the anti-patterns.
  - telerik_analyze_project: reads a .csproj and returns the framework, the project style and the Telerik references.
  - telerik_add_package_reference: returns package installation instructions.
  - telerik_convert_file: converts a .cs or .vb file to RadControls with Roslyn, and writes it unless dryRun is set.
  - telerik_get_theme_setup: returns the theme configuration.
  - telerik_upgrade_assistant: analyzes the project with the Telerik CLI and reports breaking API changes with file, line and old/new signature.
  - Telerik.WPF.MCP (2):
  - telerik-wpf-assistant: answers questions with documentation.
  - telerik-upgrade-assistant: analyzes a .csproj for breaking changes between Telerik versions.

- Search, kind `intent`: - Example tool: kendo_component_assistant. Its inputs are workflowId (optional), query ("The query to search for.") and component (an enum of the component names, with General as the default). - Request: the gRPC Query call with lib_name (react), text_matches_count 3, code_matches_count 0 and allowed_types ["documentation"]. - Result: the documentation text chunks that the service returns, joined into one text block, plus component instructions. - The other search tools use other RPCs of the same service: - icon assistants: IconsSearch (query, limit) - layout assistants: CssUtilsSearch - accessibility assistants: GetApiRefMatches with filter type accessibility - kendo_jquery_assistant: Query, with allowed_types ["documentation","icons"] when queryInvolvesIcons is set. - Where the ranking runs: on Progress's server (ContextQueryService at contextapi.telerik.com:443), not on the user's machine. - How it ranks: the Kendo jQuery documentation tells users to optimize the query "for vector embeddings", which points to an embedding index. The embedding model and the index are not named. The client bundle contains no embedding code.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none
- Prompts and resources: Telerik.WinForms.MCP 1.9.0 is the only server that declares prompts and resources. Resources: - telerik://templates/app.config ("App.config Template", application/xml): a sample App.config that sets the default Telerik theme. - telerik://templates/program.cs ("Program.cs Template", text/x-csharp): a sample Program.cs that sets up the theme in code. - telerik://templates/nuget.config ("NuGet.config Template", application/xml): a sample NuGet.config with the Telerik feed. Prompts: - migrate-project ("Migrate WinForms Project to Telerik"): migrates a whole app and backs up each file as .bak. - migrate-project-dryrun ("Migrate WinForms Project to Telerik (Dry Run)"): the same migration, with each change reviewed before it is written. - convert-file ("Convert Single File to Telerik"): converts one file. All the other servers declare none. The npm bundles have no registerPrompt or registerResource calls, and the other DLLs have no McpServerPromptAttribute or McpServerResourceAttribute.

#### Terraform (HashiCorp, also Packer)
Checked: terraform-mcp-server 1.4.1 (newest release; git tag v1.4.1; releases.hashicorp.com build 2026-10-23T21:30:42Z; server.json "version": "1.4.1"). Tags on 2026-11-20 end at v1.4.1. main re-read at b4c8016 (2026-11-20): CHANGELOG has an Unreleased section and a … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: There are two official servers, both built from one codebase. (1) terraform-mcp-server: a Go server from github.com/hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server, newest release 1.4.1 (2026-10-23). It ships as the Docker image docker.io/hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server:1.4.1, as binaries on releases.hashicorp.com and through go install, with the registry name io.github.hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server. It gives AI models real-time access to Terraform Registry provider docs, modules and policies, and to HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise workspaces. (2) The remote Terraform MCP server at https://mcp.terraform.io/mcp, hosted by HashiCorp and in beta. It runs the same server for HCP Terraform users (US organizations only) and needs an HCP Terraform API token on every request, including the public registry tools. No separate official MCP server for Packer was found.
- Number of tools: terraform-mcp-server 1.4.1: 61 tools, counted from the code that registers them (61 {Name: ...} entries in the AllTools list in pkg/toolsets/registry.go). By default only the 9 tools of the registry toolset are on; the other tools need the toolsets flag, and most need a TFE token. On main (unreleased, b4c8016 on 2026-11-20) AllTools has 68 entries: a new search toolset adds 7 tools. Remote server …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools in v1.4.1 (pkg/toolsets/registry.go AllTools; pkg/tools/registry/*.go and pkg/tools/tfe/*.go, mcp.NewTool with WithDescription). There are 61 tools.
  - Registry toolset (public registry, no token):
  - 1 search_provider_docs: takes a provider name and namespace, a service_slug and a document type; returns a list of matching provider documents (providerDocID, title, category, description) for get_provider_details.
  - 2 get_provider_details: returns the full documentation of one provider document by provider_doc_id.
  - 3 get_latest_provider_version: returns the latest version of a provider in the public registry.
  - 4 get_provider_capabilities: returns what a provider supports (resources, data sources, functions, guides, actions).
  - 5 search_modules: searches the public registry for modules by a query; returns module_id, name, description, downloads, verified and published date.
  - 6 get_module_details: returns current documentation of one module (inputs, outputs, examples) by module_id.
  - 7 get_latest_module_version: returns the latest version of a module in the public registry.
  - 8 search_policies: searches registry policies by a query string; returns matching policies with terraform_policy_id.
  - 9 get_policy_details: returns the documentation of one registry policy by terraform_policy_id.
  - Registry-private toolset (needs a TFE token):
  - 10 search_private_modules: lists or searches the private modules of an HCP Terraform or TFE organization.
  - 11 get_private_module_details: returns the details of one private module (inputs, outputs, dependencies, versions, usage examples, submodules).
  - 12 search_private_providers: lists or searches the private providers of an organization.
  - 13 get_private_provider_details: returns usage, permissions and available versions of one private provider.
  - Terraform toolset (HCP Terraform or TFE, needs a token):
  - 14 whoami: returns the identity of the user or service account behind the current token.
  - 15 get_token_permissions: returns the permissions of the current token in an organization.
  - 16 list_terraform_orgs: lists all organizations, with pagination.
  - 17 list_terraform_projects: lists all projects, with pagination.
  - 18 create_project: creates a project in an organization.
  - 19 get_project: returns the details of a project by ID.
  - 20 delete_project: deletes an empty project by ID (needs ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS).
  - 21 list_teams: lists the teams of an organization with ID, name, visibility and member count.
  - 22 get_team: returns one team with its members, organization access and SSO settings.
  - 23 create_team: creates a team in an organization.
  - 24 add_team_member: adds one member to a team by username or membership ID.
  - 25 grant_team_access: gives a team access to a workspace or a project and returns the access grant.
  - 26 delete_team: deletes a team permanently, with its memberships and access grants (needs ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS).
  - 27 list_workspaces: searches and lists workspaces with name, tag or query filters; returns short summaries.
  - 28 get_workspace_details: returns the configuration, variables and state information of one workspace.
  - 29 create_workspace: creates a workspace in an organization.
  - 30 create_no_code_workspace: creates a workspace from a no-code module and asks the user for the module's variables through MCP elicitation.
  - 31 update_workspace: updates the configuration of a workspace.
  - 32 delete_workspace_safely: deletes a workspace only when it manages no resources (needs ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS).
  - 33 force_unlock_workspace: unlocks a locked workspace (needs ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS).
  - 34 list_runs: lists or searches the runs of a workspace, with filters.
  - 35 get_run_details: returns the details of one run.
  - 36 get_run_comments: returns the ID and text of each comment on a run.
  - 37 create_run: creates a run in a workspace. It has plan_and_apply, refresh_state, plan_only and allow_empty_apply; auto_approve and is_destroy only when ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS is true.
  - 38 action_run: applies, discards or cancels a run (needs ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS).
  - 39 get_plan_details: returns the details of one plan.
  - 40 get_plan_logs: returns the logs of one plan.
  - 41 get_plan_json_output: returns the structured JSON of a plan (resource changes, attribute values before and after, metadata).
  - 42 get_apply_details: returns the details of one apply.
  - 43 get_apply_logs: returns the logs of one apply.
  - 44 get_sentinel_mock: exports and downloads the Sentinel mock bundle of a plan, for testing policies.
  - 45 list_workspace_variables: lists the variables of a workspace.
  - 46 create_workspace_variable: creates a variable in a workspace.
  - 47 update_workspace_variable: updates a variable in a workspace.
  - 48 list_variable_sets: lists the variable sets of an organization.
  - 49 create_variable_set: creates a variable set.
  - 50 create_variable_in_variable_set: creates a variable in a variable set.
  - 51 delete_variable_in_variable_set: deletes a variable from a variable set.
  - 52 attach_variable_set_to_workspaces: attaches a variable set to one or more workspaces.
  - 53 detach_variable_set_from_workspaces: detaches a variable set from one or more workspaces.
  - 54 create_workspace_tags: adds tags to a workspace.
  - 55 read_workspace_tags: returns all tags of a workspace.
  - 56 attach_policy_set_to_workspaces: attaches a non-global policy set to one or more workspaces.
  - 57 list_workspace_policy_sets: returns the policy sets that apply to a workspace, directly attached and global.
  - 58 list_stacks: lists the Stacks of an organization, with pagination.
  - 59 get_stack_details: returns the details of one Stack.
  - 60 list_state_versions: lists the state versions of a workspace.
  - 61 get_state_version: returns one state version by ID, or the latest one of a workspace.
  - Unreleased on main, not in 1.4.1: get_search_list_resource_schemas, generate_search_query_configuration, execute_search_query, get_search_query_status, get_search_query_summary, prepare_import and verify_import_plan, for Terraform Search and import. The Unreleased section also changes create_no_code_workspace on the official-SDK server to ask through an input request instead of a server-initiated elicitation.
- Search, kind `keyword`: search_provider_docs takes provider_name, provider_namespace, service_slug, provider_document_type (one of resources, data-sources, functions, guides, overview, actions, list-resources) and an optional provider_version. It gets the provider's document list from the registry API and keeps the documents whose slug, or provider_name_slug, holds the lowercase service_slug (utils.ContainsSlug, a substring regex). Each result holds providerDocID, Title, Category and Description. search_modules takes module_query and current_offset and calls the public registry endpoint modules/search?q=...&offset=. Each result holds module_id, Name, Description, Downloads, Verified and Published. The tool description tells the agent to choose a match by name similarity, description, verified status and downloads. search_policies takes policy_query and keeps the policies whose title or name holds the query (ContainsSlug); it returns terraform_policy_id values. search_private_modules takes terraform_org_name, an optional search_query, page_size and page_number; search_private_providers takes terraform_org_name, an optional search_query, registry_name, page_size and page_number. The search_query goes to the HCP Terraform or TFE API as the Search list option. The substring matching runs in the server process: on the user's machine for a local server, or on HashiCorp's host for mcp.terraform.io. The module search and the private searches rank on the Terraform Registry and HCP Terraform or TFE APIs. The code names no embedding or semantic model.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. No tool returns a user interface. The nearest thing is create_no_code_workspace: it asks the user for the module's variables through an MCP elicitation form that the host shows. That is a form the host draws, not a view from a ui:// resource.
- Prompts and resources: Prompts: none (no AddPrompt or NewPrompt in v1.4.1). Resources: two. (1) /terraform/style-guide, "Terraform Style Guide": fetches style.mdx of the Terraform language docs as markdown. (2) /terraform/module-development, "Terraform Module Development Guide": fetches the module-development pages (index, composition, structure, providers, publish, refactoring) as markdown. Resource template: registry://providers/{namespace}/name/{name}/version/{version}, "Provider details": returns the docs of one Terraform provider as markdown. Both the mark3labs server (pkg/resources) and the official-SDK server (pkg/mcp-official/resources) register all three.
- Number of skills: 20 skills in the separate repository github.com/hashicorp/agent-skills, which is also a Claude Code and Codex plugin marketplace named hashicorp. 16 are under plugins/terraform/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and 4 under plugins/packer/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. All 20 are for users of Terraform and Packer: configuration authors, module and provider authors, and image builders. None are contributor-only …
- Skills:
  - Terraform plugin:
  - 1 azure-verified-modules: requirements and best practices of Azure Verified Modules (AVM); used when the agent creates or reviews Azure modules that need AVM certification.
  - 2 new-terraform-provider: scaffolds a new provider with the Plugin Framework (layout, go module, main.go, provider.go); used when the user starts a terraform-provider-* project.
  - 3 provider-actions: implements provider actions with the Plugin Framework; used when the agent develops imperative operations that run at lifecycle events.

  - 12 terraform-policy: writes, tests or converts Terraform Policy files (.policy.hcl, .policytest.hcl, Sentinel to tfpolicy).
  - 13 terraform-search-import: finds existing cloud resources with Terraform Search queries and bulk-imports them; used when unmanaged infrastructure comes under Terraform.
  - 14 terraform-stacks: guide to Terraform Stacks (.tfcomponent.hcl, .tfdeploy.hcl); used when the agent creates, changes, validates or troubleshoots Stack configurations.
  - 15 terraform-style-guide: generates HCL that follows HashiCorp's official style conventions; used when the agent writes, reviews or generates Terraform configurations.
  - 16 terraform-test: guide to writing and running Terraform tests (.tftest.hcl, run blocks, assertions, mocks); used when the agent creates tests or troubleshoots them.

  - 19 push-to-registry: pushes Packer build metadata to the HCP Packer registry to track the image lifecycle.
  - 20 windows-builder: builds Windows images with Packer, WinRM and PowerShell provisioners, for AWS, Azure or VMware.

#### Trigger.dev
Checked: trigger.dev CLI 4.8.8 and @trigger.dev/sdk 4.8.8 and @trigger.dev/convex 4.8.8 (npm; trigger.dev 4.8.8 modified 2026-11-20T12:07:15Z, the newest version). The remote MCP server was read from the main branch of github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev at commit … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: Two official servers. (1) The CLI MCP server, in the npm package `trigger.dev` 4.8.8 (2026-11-20). It is a stdio subcommand: `npx trigger.dev@latest mcp`, server name "trigger". It automates the user's Trigger.dev projects from the local machine (deploy, dev server, profiles, runs, queries) and searches the docs. Flags: -p/--project-ref, --dev-only, --readonly, --log-file and --install. (2) The remote MCP server at https://mcp.trigger.dev/mcp, which uses HTTP and OAuth. Its code is in the open-source webapp, apps/webapp/app/mcp, read at main 3b0ec98 on 2026-11-20. It reads and manages projects, runs, logs, bulk actions and webhooks without a local install. The docs say each state-changing tool needs the user's approval in the dashboard. In the code, send_agent_message, close_agent_chat and submit_feedback are exempt (`confirm: false` / `approval: "none"`), so those three run without approval. The search_docs tool of both servers forwards the query to a third MCP endpoint, https://trigger.dev/docs/mcp (tool search_trigger_dev). Neither the code nor the docs present that endpoint as a server for users, so it is not counted.
- Number of tools: CLI server: 55, counted from the code that registers the tools (the `tools` array in registerTools, dist/esm/mcp/tools.js, 4.8.8). The count drops to 54 when telemetry is off (--skip-telemetry or TRIGGER_TELEMETRY_DISABLED), because submit_feedback is then hidden. --readonly hides the 23 tools in WRITE_TOOLS. config.js also defines metadata for get_tasks, but no code registers it. Remote server: …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools. For the CLI, descriptions come from dist/esm/mcp/config.js (4.8.8). For the remote server, they come from apps/webapp/app/mcp/tools/*.server.ts.
  - A. CLI server (55):
  - search_docs - Sends a query to the Trigger.dev docs search and returns matching content with titles and links to doc pages.
  - submit_feedback - Sends the agent's report of a problem with the MCP server, SDK or docs to Trigger.dev and returns a confirmation.
  - list_orgs - Lists the user's organizations, with slugs and IDs.
  - list_projects - Lists the user's projects, used to find a projectRef.
  - create_project_in_org - Creates a new project in an organization.
  - initialize_project - Creates a project in a chosen org (or reuses the ref in an existing trigger.config.ts) and returns the manual setup guide, fetched from trigger.dev/docs/manual-setup.md, with the project ref and dev secret key filled in, for the agent to follow; it writes no files itself.
  - get_current_worker - Returns the current worker: its version and the slugs of its registered tasks.
  - get_task_schema - Returns the payload schema of one task.
  - trigger_task - Triggers a task run in the background and returns the run.
  - list_runs - Lists a project's runs, with filters.
  - get_run_details - Returns a run's details and a paginated trace.
  - get_span_details - Returns one span of a trace: timing, attributes, errors, and the model, tokens and cost for AI spans.
  - wait_for_run_to_complete - Waits up to a timeout (60 s by default) and returns the run's final or current state.
  - cancel_run - Cancels a run.
  - replay_run - Creates a new run of the same task from the original run's payload and options, with optional overrides.
  - deploy - Deploys a project and reports progress (a long-running operation).
  - list_deploys - Lists a project's deploys.
  - list_preview_branches - Lists a project's preview branches.
  - get_query_schema - Returns the columns, types and allowed values of a TRQL table (runs, metrics, llm_metrics).
  - query - Runs a TRQL (SQL-style) query against runs, metrics and LLM usage data and returns the result.
  - list_dashboards - Lists the built-in and custom dashboards, with their widgets.
  - run_dashboard_query - Runs the query of one dashboard widget and returns the result.
  - create_dashboard - Creates a custom metrics dashboard with TRQL widgets and returns its id.
  - set_dashboard_widgets - Replaces every widget on a custom dashboard and can rename it.
  - whoami - Shows the authenticated user, active CLI profile, email and API URL.
  - list_profiles - Lists the configured CLI profiles and marks the active one.
  - switch_profile - Switches the active CLI profile, and with it the account and API URL, for the session.
  - start_dev_server - Starts `trigger dev` in the background and waits up to 30 s for the worker to be ready.
  - stop_dev_server - Stops the running dev server.
  - dev_server_status - Returns the dev server's state and recent log lines.
  - list_prompts - Lists the managed prompts: slug, current version, override status, version count.
  - get_prompt_versions - Lists a prompt's versions with labels, source, model and content.
  - promote_prompt_version - Makes a code-sourced prompt version the current version.
  - create_prompt_override - Creates a dashboard override that takes precedence over a prompt's code version.
  - update_prompt_override - Updates the active override of a prompt.
  - remove_prompt_override - Removes the active override, so the prompt reverts to the code version.
  - reactivate_prompt_override - Makes an earlier dashboard version the active override again.
  - list_agents - Lists the chat agents (chat.agent / chat.customAgent tasks) in the current worker.
  - start_agent_chat - Starts a conversation with a chat agent and returns a chatId.
  - send_agent_message - Sends a message to an agent chat and returns the full response text.
  - close_agent_chat - Closes an agent chat.
  - read_session_channel - Reads records from a session's realtime stream (a side channel or the chat transcript) and returns them with a cursor.
  - write_session_channel - Appends one record to the `in` stream of a session's named side channel.
  - get_report - Returns an interpreted report (currently 'health') as text with sparklines, a verdict and a suggested next action.
  - list_alert_capabilities - Lists what a monitoring alert can watch, with tunable parameters.
  - list_alerts - Lists monitoring alerts, filtered by lifecycle or attention.
  - create_alert - Creates a monitoring alert.
  - resolve_alert - Resolves an alert that needs attention, which re-arms it.
  - list_webhook_endpoints - Lists the hosted webhook endpoints: id, source, status, URL and whether a secret is set.
  - get_webhook_endpoint_details - Returns an endpoint's details, its subscribers with their filters, and a setup prompt.
  - list_webhook_deliveries - Lists recent webhook deliveries, newest first, filtered by endpoint and status.
  - get_webhook_delivery - Returns one delivery: its status, error, the outcome at each subscriber, and the event body and headers.
  - replay_webhook_delivery - Replays a stored webhook event as a new delivery.
  - generate_webhook_secret - Generates a new signing secret for an endpoint and returns it once.
  - set_webhook_secret - Stores the signing secret or public key that a provider issued for an endpoint.
  - B. Remote server (67). It has every CLI tool above with the same name and purpose except the 8 CLI-only tools: deploy, start_dev_server, stop_dev_server, dev_server_status, whoami, list_profiles, switch_profile and initialize_project. That leaves 47. It adds these 20:
  - list_run_tags - Lists, in alphabetical order, the tags on runs created in a period.
  - read_run_stream - Reads the output or input stream records of a run, or lists its output stream keys, with a cursor.
  - search_logs - Searches an environment's logs, newest first, by text, level, task, run and period, and returns a page with a cursor.
  - get_log - Returns one log entry in full, with its attributes.
  - reset_run_idempotency_key - Clears a run's idempotency key.
  - update_run_metadata - Replaces or edits by key the metadata of an unfinished run.
  - add_run_tags - Adds tags to a run.
  - reschedule_run - Changes when a delayed run starts.
  - list_bulk_actions - Lists bulk actions (cancel or replay of many runs), newest first.
  - get_bulk_action - Returns a bulk action's type, status, run counts, selection and times.
  - create_bulk_action - Cancels or replays many runs, selected by IDs or a filter.
  - abort_bulk_action - Stops a bulk action that is in progress.
  - search_webhook_endpoints - Searches webhook endpoints, including per-tenant ones, by subscriber, source, status and text, and returns up to 50 per page.
  - get_task_webhook - Returns a webhook task's file path, creation time and subscribed endpoints with their filters.
  - list_webhook_waiters - Lists the runs that wait on a webhook endpoint (waitpoints), soonest expiry first.
  - remove_webhook_secret - Removes an endpoint's signing secret.
  - generate_webhook_verify_token - Generates a new URL verification token for an endpoint and returns it once.
  - pause_webhook_endpoint - Pauses a hosted webhook endpoint, so its URL answers 404.
  - resume_webhook_endpoint - Resumes a paused endpoint.
  - cancel_webhook_waiter - Cancels a waiter, so the runs that wait on it resume with WebhookWaiterCancelledError.
- Search, kind `not confirmed`: search_docs (both servers). Input: { query: string }. The documented examples are natural-language questions, such as "How do I create a scheduled task?". The tool does not rank results itself. It sends a JSON-RPC tools/call for `search_trigger_dev` to the hosted endpoint https://trigger.dev/docs/mcp. The CLI file that does this is named mintlifyClient.js, so the endpoint is the Mintlify-hosted docs MCP. The tool returns that endpoint's result content unchanged. The tool description says the search "returns contextual content with titles and direct links to the documentation pages". The remote server caps the result at 20,000 characters (MAX_RESULT_CHARS) and fences it as untrusted (fenceUntrusted). Ranking therefore runs on a hosted server, not on the user's machine. Neither source names the ranking method (semantic or keyword). Other search tools, on the remote server only: search_logs filters logs by text, level, task, run and time period (newest first, one page per call, with a cursor); search_webhook_endpoints filters by subscriber, source, status and text in the id, tenant id or external ref (up to 50 per page). Both filter on fields and text, and neither ranks by meaning.

It has the optional arguments key, environment and period, with completions, and tells the agent to call get_report and show the health report unchanged. A code comment says Claude Code renders it as /mcp__trigger__report. The CLI server declares no resources. Remote server: no prompts and no resources; it declares only the tools capability.

- Skills:
  - @trpc/server:
  - 1. trpc-router: entry point for all tRPC skills, a decision tree that routes by task (init, routers, procedures, client, adapters, subscriptions, React Query, Next.js, links, middleware, validators, errors, caching, FormData, OpenAPI, multiple services) with a minimal working server and client.
  - 2. server-setup: set up a tRPC server with initTRPC.context().create(), routers, query/mutation procedures, base procedures, createContext, the exported AppRouter type, nested/merged routers and lazy().
  - 3. middlewares: create and compose middleware with t.procedure.use(), extend context via opts.next({ ctx }), reuse with .concat()/.unstable_pipe(), base procedures, getRawInput(), for authorization, logging and timing.
  - 4. validators: configure .input()/.output() validation with Zod, Yup, Superstruct, ArkType, Valibot, Effect, Standard Schema or custom functions; invalid input gives BAD_REQUEST, invalid output INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.
  - 5. error-handling: throw TRPCError with codes, configure errorFormatter, per-procedure .errors(), global onError, getHTTPStatusCodeFromError(), stack traces with isDev.
  - 6. auth: JWT/cookie authentication and authorization via createContext, middleware context narrowing, protectedProcedure, client Authorization headers, WebSocket connectionParams and SSE auth; UNAUTHORIZED vs FORBIDDEN.
  - 7. server-side-calls: call procedures from server code with t.createCallerFactory()/router.createCaller(ctx) for integration tests, internal logic and custom endpoints; error handling; do not use a caller inside another procedure.
  - 8. caching: set HTTP cache headers on query responses via the adapter's responseMeta for CDN/browser caching, with batching, streaming and auth caveats, and the Next.js App Router pattern.
  - 9. non-json-content-types: handle FormData, file uploads, Blob, Uint8Array and ReadableStream inputs in mutations with octetInputParser and splitLink/isNonJsonSerializable(); keep body parsers off tRPC routes.
  - 10. subscriptions: real-time streams with async generator subscriptions, SSE via httpSubscriptionLink (recommended) or WebSocket via wsLink/applyWSSHandler, tracked() for reconnection, ping config, AbortSignal, and consuming on the client.
  - 11. service-oriented-architecture: split a backend into several services with custom routing links on the first path segment, a faux gateway router for the AppRouter type, and a shared server-lib package.
  - 12. adapter-standalone: mount tRPC on the Node.js HTTP server with createHTTPServer(), createHTTPHandler(), createHTTP2Handler(), basePath and CORS.
  - 13. adapter-express: mount tRPC as Express middleware with createExpressMiddleware(), with context options and the body-parser caveat for FormData/binary inputs.
  - 14. adapter-fastify: mount tRPC as a Fastify v5+ plugin with fastifyTRPCPlugin, prefix, trpcOptions, WebSocket subscriptions with useWSS and @fastify/websocket, maxParamLength.
  - 15. adapter-aws-lambda: deploy on AWS Lambda with awsLambdaRequestHandler() for API Gateway v1/v2 and Function URLs, and response streaming with awsLambdaStreamingRequestHandler().
  - 16. adapter-fetch: deploy on WinterCG edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy, Vercel Edge, Astro, Remix, SolidStart) with fetchRequestHandler().

Checked: turbo 2.11.13 (npm latest; registry modified 2026-11-19; canary 2.11.14-canary.2). Repository vercel/turborepo main at commit 99233190d0dd77d9ae6ea897297a5adc20244ef6 (2026-11-19). The docs app pins @vercel/geistdocs 2.16.0 (apps/docs/package.json and … The second agent's verdict: corrected.

- MCP servers: There is no MCP server in the turbo package and no MCP command in the CLI. The Turborepo docs site has one remote MCP endpoint: the route apps/docs/app/api/mcp/route.ts, served at https://turborepo.dev/api/mcp (basePath is undefined). It is a documentation-search server built with createMcpRoute from @vercel/geistdocs 2.16.0 and enabled by webmcp: { enabled: true } in apps/docs/lib/geistdocs/config.tsx. The maintainers added it in PR #14828, 'feat: Enable WebMCP for Turborepo docs', commit af866e51, 2026-10-20. In code, the server reports serverInfo name = the site title and version "1.0.0". The Turborepo docs do not mention this endpoint: guides/ai.mdx names the agent skill, AGENTS.md guidance, `turbo docs` and Markdown docs, but no MCP. examples/with-mcp-servers is an example monorepo, not a server for Turborepo. Not connected to, so whether it is live is not checked.
- Number of tools: 1 for the remote server at turborepo.dev/api/mcp. Source: the code that registers the tools, one server.registerTool call in @vercel/geistdocs 2.16.0 dist/routes/mcp.js. The geistdocs WebMCP feature has two more tools, read_current_page and ask_ai, but both run only in the browser and are not part of /api/mcp; ask_ai is also opt-in and Turborepo does not set webmcp.askAI.
- Tools:
  - From the code that registers the tools (@vercel/geistdocs 2.16.0, dist/routes/mcp.js):
  - search_docs: searches the Turborepo documentation for a query (1 to 500 characters) in a locale (en or cn, default en) and returns one text content item holding a JSON array of search entries (page entries, each followed by up to two matching section snippets, each with a url, a type and content); the description calls these titles, excerpts and page URLs. Annotated readOnlyHint: true.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool: search_docs. Inputs: query (string, trimmed, 1 to 500 characters) and locale (enum of the site languages en and cn, default en). search_docs calls the docs site's /api/search handler in-process (createSearchRoute from geistdocs, over the docs and OpenAPI sources). The handler runs two fumadocs-core createI18nSearchAPI searches over Orama: a 'simple' page search with boosts title 8, keywords 6, description 2, content 1, threshold 1, tolerance 0, and an 'advanced' section search. rankSearchResults then puts exact and relaxed title and keyword matches first, keeps English page hits only when every query term prefixes a word of the page, and returns at most 20 pages, each followed by at most 2 section snippets sorted by term coverage. One result entry is a fumadocs search entry with url, type (page, heading or text) and content (plus fields such as id and breadcrumbs passed through). For cn it uses the Orama Mandarin tokenizer. No embedding or language model is involved. Ranking runs on the project's server, the Next.js docs deployment at turborepo.dev, not on the user's machine. The route's 'mode=vector' branch only returns the same Orama section search, and search_docs does not set it.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. search_docs returns JSON text. The remote server declares no ui:// resource and returns no image.
- Prompts and resources: none. The route registers one tool and no prompts or resources; its server options set maxSubscriptions: 0 and experimental_webMcp tools ["search_docs"]. geistdocs also has a discovery manifest route (createMcpManifestRoute, /.well-known/mcp.json), but Turborepo does not use it: its agent config in apps/docs/geistdocs.tsx lists no mcp.servers, and apps/docs/app has no .well-known route.
- Number of skills: 2 skills for users of Turborepo, in the skills/ folder of the vercel/turborepo repository: skills/add/SKILL.md (added 2026-11-12, PR #15014) and skills/turborepo/SKILL.md. Users install them with `npx skills add vercel/turborepo`. The docs mention only the turborepo skill ('the Turborepo Skill'). No other SKILL.md exists in the repository.
- Skills:
  - add: adds Turborepo to an existing repository in any toolchain Turborepo supports; an agent uses it when asked to add, introduce or set up Turborepo or turbo in a repository that does not use it yet.
  - turborepo: configures and troubleshoots Turborepo repositories, sending the agent to the docs bundled in the installed turbo package; an agent uses it when it works with turbo.json, task pipelines, caching, Remote Cache, the turbo CLI, filtering, environment variables, package boundaries, monorepo structure or CI workflows.
- What the skills point at: The turborepo skill points to files in the installed package: node_modules/turbo/docs/README.md, then the pages under docs/, and gives `node -p "require.resolve('turbo/package.json')"` to find the package. The add skill points to turborepo.dev pages (/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository, /docs/crafting-your-repository/configuring-tasks, /docs/reference/configuration, /docs/reference/package-configurations, and toolchain guides /docs/guides/tools/rust, /python, /go); once turbo is installed it prefers the bundled docs/README.md, and it uses the CLI command `turbo run <task> --dry` to check the result. Neither skill names an MCP server.
- Not confirmed: Whether https://turborepo.dev/api/mcp is live on the deployed site: neither reader connected to it. | Whether the maintainers count the docs-site endpoint as an official MCP server: the Turborepo docs do not mention it. | Every field of one search entry beyond url, type and content: the rest passes through from the fumadocs/Orama response and was not traced field by field.

#### Untitled UI React
Checked: Hosted MCP server at https://www.untitledui.com/react/api/mcp has no published version; its documentation page was read again on 2026-11-20. Repositories read at HEAD: untitleduico/react bff7606 (2026-11-18), untitledui-nextjs-starter-kit 29937f0 … The second agent's verdict: confirmed.

- MCP servers: One official server, the Untitled UI MCP server. It is a remote HTTP server at https://www.untitledui.com/react/api/mcp. No version is published, and the documentation was read on 2026-11-20. It lets an agent search, browse and install Untitled UI React components, page templates and icons: its tools return a CLI install command. It is closed source and hosted by Untitled UI.
- Number of tools: 7, counted from the documentation. The server code is not public.
- Tools:
  - Taken from the documentation; the server code is not public.
  - search_components: finds components for a query in natural language, with optional category_filter, limit and key. Each result holds an AI-generated description, a screenshot URL, key features and a match reason.
  - list_components: lists all components, filtered by category (base, application, marketing, foundations, shared-assets) and paged with skip and limit (defaults 0 and 100).
  - get_component: returns one component and its CLI install command.
  - get_component_bundle: returns the install command for several components at once.
  - get_page_templates: lists or searches complete page templates by query, page_type, category, layout and limit. Each template holds a description, a section breakdown, its hero style, its UI elements and a screenshot URL.
  - get_page_template_files: takes a template name from get_page_templates and returns the CLI install command for that page template. PRO only.
  - search_icons: finds icons by name or keyword, to confirm that an icon exists and to get its correct import name.
- Search, kind `both`: search_components takes query (required), category_filter, limit (default 20) and key. Each result holds an AI-generated description, a screenshot URL, key features such as avatar-upload, and a match reason. With PRO authentication, it ranks by meaning with 'multimodal AI embeddings' built from the text description and the screenshot of each component. The source does not name the model. Without authentication, it scores keyword matches on names and descriptions, and hides PRO components. get_page_templates takes query, page_type, category, layout, limit (default 10) and key. With a query and PRO authentication, it ranks by semantic relevance; page templates are PRO-only. search_icons searches by name or keyword; its input fields are not documented. All ranking runs on the Untitled UI server, because the server is remote and hosted.
- User interface from a tool, kind `none`: none. The documentation names no ui:// resource and no image content. search_components and get_page_templates return a screenshot URL as text in each result, not a rendered view or an image.
