One server, maintained by the vitejs organization: the Vite DevTools MCP endpoint. The experimental package @vitejs/devtools 0.8.3 (2026-11-15) mounts it in the running Vite dev server at '<base>__mcp', with base DEVTOOLS_MOUNT_PATH '/__devtools/'. It is a Streamable-HTTP endpoint over the agent tools of every mounted devframe; it lets an agent inspect and drive the live DevTools hub (RPC functions, commands, shared state, messages, terminals). The MCP code (mountMcpHttp, buildMcpServerFromContext) comes from the dependencies @devframes/hub and @devframes/agentic (direct dependencies of @vitejs/devtools, ^1.3.5), published from github.com/devframes/devframe; npm maintainer antfu. The server is named 'devframes-hub' with version '0.0.0', because @vitejs/devtools passes no `name` or `version` to initHub. With the default mcp: 'auto', the hub mounts the route through loadAutoMcpAdapter once an agent surface exists.
- Number of tools: Vite DevTools MCP endpoint: 11 tools with the default setup. That is 10 agent-flagged RPC functions from the three built-in devframes that @vitejs/devtools mounts (inspect 4, messages 1, terminals 5), plus the built-in devframe_state_read. Source: the code that registers the tools. The list is dynamic: it grows with each agent-flagged RPC function or agent-flagged hub command that an integration …
- Tools:
  - Source: the code that registers the tools (the tools/list handler in @devframes/agentic build-server.ts, and the RPC definitions in the plugin packages, version 1.4.0). Wire names come from toAgentToolName, which turns each run of characters outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] (here ':') into '_'.
  - 1. devframes_plugin_inspect_describe-agent: describes the agent surface of the devframe and returns the manifest of tools and resources, with titles, descriptions, safety hints and schemas (read-only).
  - 2. devframes_plugin_inspect_list-commands: lists every command registered on the hub commands host, with id, title, description, category, whether it has a handler, and its children (read-only).
  - 3. devframes_plugin_inspect_list-functions: lists every RPC function registered on the connection, with name, type, JSON-serializable and snapshot flags, argument and return schemas, and agent exposure (read-only).
  - 4. devframes_plugin_inspect_list-state-keys: returns the sorted keys of all shared-state entries that the connection publishes (read-only).
  - 5. devframes_plugin_messages_list: lists the hub message feed (diagnostics, notifications and tool output entries with level, category, labels and positions); takes an optional `since` argument.
  - 6. devframes_plugin_terminals_list: lists the current terminal sessions with status, mode and command, and returns an array of session info (safety read).
  - 7. devframes_plugin_terminals_spawn: spawns a new terminal session from a preset id, or from a command and a mode, and returns the session info (safety action).
  - 8. devframes_plugin_terminals_terminate: terminates the running process of a session and keeps the session and its scrollback (safety destructive).
  - 9. devframes_plugin_terminals_remove: kills a terminal session and discards its process, stream and scrollback (safety destructive).
  - 10. devframes_plugin_terminals_clear-exited: discards every stopped (exited or errored) terminal session and leaves running sessions alone (safety destructive).
  - 11. devframe_state_read: built-in; called with no key it returns the list of shared-state keys, and with a key it returns that value as JSON (read-only).
  - Conditional: devframe_agent_list-clients ('List connected browser tabs') appears only while a browser tab has synced browser agent tools; no vitejs integration registers such tools in 0.8.3.

  - 3. get_directive_api_by_version: returns the web-types JSON entry for one directive (e.g. v-ripple) for a version.

  - 9. get_release_notes_by_version: returns the release notes for one or more versions (default latest).
  - 10. get_vuetify_one_installation_guide: returns the README of the @vuetify/one package from GitHub.
  - 11. get_upgrade_guide: returns the raw upgrade guide markdown between major versions (v1.5 to v2, v2.7 to v3, v3 to v4).
  - 12. get_upgrade_plan: returns a structured, multi-hop upgrade plan for from/to versions, with tooling recommendations, effort estimates and a rule index per hop.
  - 13. get_upgrade_rules: returns machine-actionable migration rules (detect.grep patterns, replace mappings, codemod hints, revert snippets), filterable by ids, category or component.
  - 14. get_migration_receipt_schema: returns the MigrationReceipt schema and batch envelope that agents must use to report migration findings.
  - 15. get_v4_breaking_changes: (marked DEPRECATED in favour of get_upgrade_rules) returns Vuetify 4 breaking changes with migration guidance, optionally by category.
  - 16. get_v3_breaking_changes: returns Vuetify 2 to 3 breaking changes by category (setup, layout, theme, components, gotchas, ...), with before/after snippets for high-pain categories.
  - 17. get_v2_to_v3_component_map: returns each v2 component with its v3.13 status (core, renamed, removed, replaced), notes and issue links.
  - 18. get_v3_upgrade_playbook: returns the ordered phases of a v2 to v3 upgrade (baseline e2e, Vue 3 prerequisite, bundler/Nuxt, eslint --fix, component map, breaking-change scan).
  - 19. get_v3_upgrade_baseline_recipe: returns a Playwright recipe to snapshot the app before the upgrade (upgrade-baseline/) and re-run after (upgrade-after/).
  - 20. get_vuetify0_installation_guide: returns the README of @vuetify/v0 from GitHub.
  - 21. get_vuetify0_package_guide: returns the package-specific documentation of @vuetify/v0 from GitHub.

  - 23. get_vuetify0_component_list: returns the list of @vuetify/v0 headless components.
  - 24. get_vuetify0_composable_guide: returns the documentation and source code of one @vuetify/v0 composable (category + name).
  - 25. get_vuetify0_component_guide: returns the documentation and source code of one @vuetify/v0 component.
  - 26. get_vuetify0_exports_list: returns the subpath exports of @vuetify/v0.

  - 3. close_session: closes the session, or with detach: true disconnects and leaves it running.
  - 4. launch_chrome: launches Chrome with remote debugging and a temporary profile, so that start_session with attach: true can connect.
  - 5. emulate_device: emulates a phone or tablet in a BiDi browser session (viewport, DPR, user agent, touch), lists presets, or resets.
  - 6. navigate: loads a URL in the current tab and waits for the load event.
  - 7. switch_tab: switches to a tab by handle or 0-based index.
  - 8. switch_frame: switches into an iframe or back to the top page and returns the frame's elements.
  - 9. scroll: scrolls the page up or down by a pixel amount (browser only).
  - 10. click_element: clicks an element and, on web pages, returns what changed (new elements with refs, or the new page).
  - 11. set_value: replaces the text of an input or textarea and, on web pages, returns what changed.
  - 12. select_option: selects an option of a <select> by its text and returns what changed.
  - 13. press_key: presses a key or key combination in the focused element and returns what changed.
  - 14. perform_actions: runs several actions in one call (for example, fill a form and submit it) and returns what each one changed.
  - 15. snapshot: returns the page or app screen as an accessibility tree with refs (button "Save" [ref=e3]), with options find, full, scope and viewport.
  - 16. set_cookie: sets a browser cookie on the active session.
  - 17. delete_cookies: deletes all cookies or one cookie by name.
  - 18. tap_element: taps an element or screen coordinates on mobile and returns what changed.
  - 19. swipe: performs a full-screen swipe gesture on mobile.
  - 20. drag_and_drop: drags an element to another element or by an x/y offset on mobile.
  - 21. switch_context: switches between the native and webview contexts of a hybrid mobile app.
  - 22. rotate_device: rotates a mobile device to portrait or landscape.
  - 23. hide_keyboard: dismisses the on-screen keyboard on mobile.
  - 24. set_geolocation: overrides the GPS coordinates of the session.
  - 25. execute_script: runs JavaScript in the page and returns its value, or on Appium runs a "mobile: <command>".
  - 26. execute_electron_script: runs JavaScript in the Electron main process.
  - 27. mock: configures a session-scoped mock of network requests (BiDi) or Electron API functions.
  - 28. get_mock_calls: returns the recorded call arguments of a mock.
  - 29. manage_mock: clears, resets or restores a mock.
  - 30. trigger_electron_deeplink: triggers a deeplink through the active Electron app.
  - 31. get_elements: returns the interactable elements of the current page with selectors, text and bounding boxes, with filters and pagination.
  - 32. open_web_extension: installs a web extension through WebDriver BiDi and opens one of its extension pages.
  - 33. list_apps: lists the apps uploaded to a cloud provider (BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, TestMu, TestingBot, Digital.ai).
  - 34. upload_app: uploads a local .apk or .ipa to a cloud provider and returns its app URL for start_session.
  - 35. query_docs: searches the official WebdriverIO documentation and returns the best excerpts with title, section trail, path and score (or the full pages with fullPage).
  - 36. get_screenshot: takes a screenshot of the page or screen and returns a base64 image, resized and compressed.
  - 37. get_accessibility_tree: returns the accessibility tree of the page with roles, names and selectors (web contexts), with role filters and pagination.
  - 38. get_tabs: lists all browser tabs with handle, title, URL and which one is active.
  - 39. get_contexts: returns the available automation contexts (NATIVE_APP, WEBVIEW_*) and the active one on mobile.
  - 40. get_app_state: returns the state of a mobile app (not installed, not running, background or foreground).
  - 41. get_cookies: returns all cookies of the session, or one cookie by name.
  - 42. enable_tools: lists more tool groups (mocks, cookies, device, extensions, attach, elements, cloud-apps) and returns the names it added.
- Search, kind `keyword`: Tool query_docs. Input fields: query (string, 2-3 keywords), limit (integer 1-20, default 5), fullPage (boolean, default false). A result is TOON-encoded { query, hits } with these fields for each hit: title, trail (section path), path, score, and excerpt (the full page, capped, when fullPage is true). Ranking: its own BM25 in docs-index.ts (k1 1.2, b 0.75) over three weighted fields (FIELD_WEIGHTS [1.0, 0.4, 1.0]: whole tokens, camelCase parts, page title plus section trail). It demotes pages under /docs/mcp/ unless the query contains 'mcp'. No embedding model and no third-party search library. Ranking runs on the user's machine, in the server process. The corpus is https://webdriver.io/llms-full.txt, fetched over the network and cached in ~/.wdio-mcp (or WDIO_MCP_CACHE_DIR) for 24 hours, with an ETag (If-None-Match) check.
- User interface from a tool, kind `image`: get_screenshot: the user sees a screenshot of the current page or app screen as a base64 image, resized and compressed. The image is not interactive. It needs a live session that the MCP server drives: a browser, Electron app, or Appium mobile device, local or in a cloud. The resource wdio://session/current/screenshot returns a screenshot too. No tool names a ui:// resource (grep for ui:// in src at v4.1.0 finds nothing).
- Prompts and resources: Prompts: none (no registerPrompt in src; server capabilities declare only tools and resources). Resources (22 registerResource calls in src/server.ts, lines 217-240, at v4.1.0): - sessions (wdio://sessions): JSON index of all sessions with metadata and step counts. - session-current-steps (wdio://session/current/steps): JSON step log of the active session. - session-current-code (wdio://session/current/code): generated WebdriverIO JS code for the active session. - session-steps (wdio://session/{sessionId}/steps): step log of one session. - session-code (wdio://session/{sessionId}/code): generated code of one session. - session-current-logs (wdio://session/current/logs): logs, console errors, network events and crash reports. - browserstack-local-binary (wdio://browserstack/local-binary): BrowserStack Local download and setup instructions. - saucelabs-local-binary (wdio://saucelabs/local-binary): Sauce Connect Proxy download and setup. - testmu-local-binary (wdio://testmu/local-binary): TestMu Tunnel download and setup. - testingbot-local-binary (wdio://testingbot/local-binary): TestingBot Tunnel download and setup. - session-current-capabilities (wdio://session/current/capabilities): raw capabilities that the driver accepted. - session-current-elements (wdio://session/current/elements): interactable elements with selectors. - session-current-accessibility (wdio://session/current/accessibility): accessibility tree of the page. - session-current-screenshot (wdio://session/current/screenshot): screenshot of the current page. - session-current-cookies (wdio://session/current/cookies): cookies of the session. - session-current-app-state (wdio://session/current/app-state/{bundleId}): app state for a bundle ID. - session-current-contexts (wdio://session/current/contexts): available contexts. - session-current-context (wdio://session/current/context): active context. - session-current-geolocation (wdio://session/current/geolocation): current device geolocation. - session-current-tabs (wdio://session/current/tabs): browser tabs. - docs-index (wdio://docs/index): every docs page as title, path and slug. - docs-page (wdio://docs/page/{slug}): full markdown of one docs page, truncated at PAGE_CHAR_CAP characters.
- Number of skills: 2 consumer skills. (1) wdio-session: in webdriverio/webdriverio at packages/wdio-session/src/skill/SKILL.md, published in @wdio/session 10.2.0 as package/src/skill/SKILL.md. An identical copy is in packages/create-wdio/templates/wdio-session/SKILL.md, published in create-wdio 10.2.0 as package/templates/wdio-session/SKILL.md (identical to main). `npx wdio session skill --install .` or `npm init …
- Skills:
  - wdio-session: from its description, it drives browsers, mobile apps and desktop apps with WebdriverIO from the shell (`npx wdio session`) to explore UI, verify changes and write tests. An agent uses it to see or drive a real app, check a change, or turn steps into a spec.
  - wdio-v10-migration: it migrates a test suite from WebdriverIO v9 to v10. An agent uses it when the user asks to upgrade WebdriverIO, the @wdio packages, or a v9 config, spec or page object to v10.
- What the skills point at: wdio-v10-migration points to a web address, the migration guide https://webdriver.io/docs/v10-migration.md, which the agent must fetch and follow. It also links the expect-webdriverio migration docs and the driver upgrade notes on GitHub, and tells the agent to install and run the @wdio/codemod package (npm install jscodeshift @wdio/codemod; npx jscodeshift -t ./node_modules/@wdio/codemod/v10 ./e2e/). wdio-session points to the command line tool `npx wdio session` (open, click, fill, select, check, snapshot, find, read, get, wait, navigate, exec, export, resume, doctor, close and more), and to `npx wdio session <action> --help` for the details. Neither skill names the MCP server or its …
